ask-prompt-no-template-placeholders.text: `build_ask_prompt` never leaves `{{` or `}}` template markers in the generated prompt string — all placeholders are resolved before output.

ask-prompt-tools-section-overrides-defau.text: A caller-supplied `tools_section` fully replaces the default prompt tools block, including removing the default `"one tool available"` wording.

ask-requires-sources-db-for-dual-mode.text: `ask` raises `ValueError` at the top if `dual=True` and `sources_db is None`.

ask-search-source-chunks-uses-stopword-f.text: _search_source_chunks tokenizes the question, filters stop words, runs an OR query against the rag_fts.db SQLite FTS5 index, and returns markdown with filename and section headers.

ask-simple-mode-skips-llm-when-no-contex.text: `ask(..., simple=True)` returns `NO_BELIEFS_MSG` without invoking the LLM when there are no matching beliefs and no matching source documents.

ask-simple-mode-uses-depth-2-markdown-se.text: `ask()` in `simple=True` mode calls `api.search(format="markdown", depth=2)` for the initial belief context.

ask-source-chunk-search-default-top-k-10.text: `_search_source_chunks(question, sources_db, top_k=10)` defaults to returning the top 10 source document chunks.

ask-source-chunks-persist-across-tool-it.text: Source document content included in the initial ask prompt is re-included in all subsequent prompts after tool-call round-trips, ensuring the LLM retains source context across the entire multi-turn loop.

ask-source-docs-persist-across-tool-roun.text: In the agentic `ask` loop, source document content included in the prompt persists across tool-call rounds.

ask-sources-can-satisfy-query-without-be.text: When `sources_db` is provided, source-document search results alone can produce an answer even when belief search returns no matches; with neither belief nor source matches, `ask()` returns `NO_BELIEFS_MSG`.

ask-sources-db-failure-silently-degrades.text: If the `sources_db` SQLite file is missing or corrupt, `_search_source_chunks` catches `OperationalError`/`DatabaseError` and returns empty string, degrading to belief-only mode without user-visible errors.

ask-stop-word-fallback-ensures-nonempty-.text: `_search_source_chunks` strips stop words from the question before building the FTS5 query, but falls back to all words longer than 1 character if every word is a stop word — ensuring the query is never empty

ask-strips-claudecode-env.text: `_invoke_claude` removes the `CLAUDECODE` environment variable to prevent recursive invocation when running inside Claude Code.

ask-tool-call-budget-is-three.text: The agentic `ask` loop permits at most 3 tool-call rounds before forcing synthesis via `build_final_prompt` (no tool definition), resulting in exactly 4 LLM invocations maximum.

ask-tool-call-parsing-is-line-based-json.text: Tool calls are detected by scanning each line of the LLM response for valid JSON with a `"tool"` key; multi-line JSON objects are silently missed.

ask-tool-loop-bounded-at-three.text: Covered by existing `ask-has-tiered-query-modes` which already states "bounded 3-iteration tool loop."

ask-tool-loop-bounded-to-three-rounds.text: `ask()` in default full mode performs at most three tool-call rounds before final synthesis; on final-synthesis timeout, error, or another tool call, it falls back to accumulated belief/search context.

ask-tool-loop-capped-at-three.text: The LLM synthesis loop runs at most `MAX_ITERATIONS` (3) rounds, with `FINAL_TURN_INSTRUCTION` appended on the last iteration to force a final answer.

ask-tool-loop-max-three-rounds.text: Covered by existing `ask-has-tiered-query-modes` which already describes the "bounded 3-iteration tool loop."

ask-tool-loop-status-messages-use-stderr.text: Status messages in ask.py are written to stderr so they do not pollute the answer written to stdout.

ask-tool-results-replace-context-only-if.text: Tool-loop search results replace `beliefs_context` only when non-empty and not `"No results found."`; empty tool results are recorded in `tool_history` but do not overwrite the current context.

ask-treats-none-as-no-tool-call.text: The ask loop checks `tool_call is None` at `reasons/ask.py:516` and `if extract_tool_call(response)` at `:561`, so a parse miss is indistinguishable from an absent tool call.

ask-unknown-tool-returns-raw-response.text: When the LLM emits an unrecognized tool name, `ask()` returns the raw LLM response without crashing.

ask-unknown-tool-treats-as-final-answer.text: In the ask tool loop, if the LLM response is not valid JSON with a recognized `"tool"` key (unknown tool name or non-JSON text), it is treated as the final answer and returned immediately rather than triggering a loop iteration.

ask-uses-text-based-tool-protocol.text: `ask.py` implements tool use by parsing JSON lines with a `"tool"` key from LLM text output, not Claude's native tool-use API, because it invokes `claude -p` (pipe mode) which doesn't support function calling.

assert-flips-truth-without-removing-just.text: The `assert` command only flips a node's truth value to IN without removing or invalidating existing SL justifications; if a justification is structurally invalid (e.g., from import-beliefs contextual dependencies), the node will revert to OUT on next recompute, and `convert-to-premise` is the required workaround.

assert-node-propagates-outlist-changes.text: Asserting an outlist node recomputes dependent nodes and includes them in the returned `changed` set.

assert-retract-changed-set-includes-outl.text: `assert_node` and `retract` propagate through outlist dependencies and include affected dependent node IDs in their returned `changed` set.

assert-retract-is-idempotent.text: Retracting an already-OUT node or asserting an already-IN node returns an empty `changed` list with no cascading side effects, ensuring repeated calls are no-ops.

assign-topics-groups-unmatched-under-oth.text: `_assign_topics` groups node IDs matching a topic under that topic, places all non-matching IDs under `"Other"`, and returns `{}` for an empty node list.

assign-topics-parses-id-segments.text: `_assign_topics` splits node IDs on `[-._:]`, drops tokens of length ≤ 2, and matches the first segment against the topic set.

atomicity-is-backend-independent.text: Both storage backends enforce atomic isolated operations through backend-appropriate mechanisms: the SQLite backend uses context-managed load/save with write-flag gating and per-function transaction scope, while PostgreSQL uses per-method transactions with composite-key multi-tenancy — achieving the same transactional guarantee at different architectural levels

justifications.label: Context-managed SQLite atomicity and per-method PostgreSQL transactions are backend-specific implementations of the same isolation guarantee

auto-k-default-and-clamp-semantics.text: `_auto_k(n)` defaults to `max(2, n // 5)`; `max_k` caps that auto-derived value, while explicit `n_clusters` wins and is clamped to `n`.

auto-k-floor-is-two.text: `_auto_k` never returns fewer than 2 clusters regardless of input size (using the `n // 5` heuristic), unless clamped by `n` itself when there are fewer beliefs than clusters.

auto-k-formula-is-n-div-5-capped-at-20.text: The `_auto_k` helper computes a default cluster count as `min(n // 5, 20)` with a floor of 2; an explicit `n_clusters` override is capped at `n_beliefs`, and a separate `max_k` parameter provides an additional upper bound.

auto-k-is-n-over-5-capped.text: `_auto_k(n)` defaults to `max(2, n // 5)`, `max_k` caps that default, and an explicit `n_clusters` overrides it but is clamped to `n`.

auto-k-max-k-caps-cluster-count.text: `_auto_k` caps the computed cluster count at `max_k` and clamps an explicit `n_clusters` value to the number of beliefs.

auto-retract-respects-dry-run.text: The `--auto-retract` flag in the `review-beliefs` CLI is gated by `--dry-run`: when dry-run is active, findings are displayed but no database mutation occurs, even for beliefs flagged as invalid.

automated-sync-achieves-full-lifecycle-c.text: Automated repeated sync safely reconciles external beliefs with complete lifecycle coverage including full source staleness detection — idempotent cascade-preserving sync combined with conservative staleness gating ensures no lifecycle gap between sync runs.

justifications.label: idempotent sync + staleness gate = full lifecycle coverage, gated on silent missing-file handling

autonomous-convergence-preserves-trust-b.text: The system simultaneously achieves autonomous self-maintenance (converging to deterministic stable states while actively detecting and resolving inconsistencies) AND comprehensive boundary enforcement (architectural trust through self-containment and information flow control through authorization and budget constraints) — convergence never requires relaxing defensive controls, and boundary enforcement never prevents convergence.

justifications.label: Autonomy and control are co-achievable — the system converges within its trust boundaries rather than needing to relax them

metadata.retract_reason: Invalid: non-interference is unstated compositional property

autonomous-convergence-produces-document.text: The system's autonomous convergence to evaluation-invariant equilibria generates consistently identifiable artifacts with deterministic traceable history at every step — every equilibrium state is not merely stable and transformation-invariant but fully explainable through its documented convergence path.

justifications.label: Evaluation-invariant convergence (depth-7) combined with consistent referenceability (depth-7) yields equilibria that are both mathematically correct and operationally explainable

backend-agnostic-operational-assurance.text: The system's comprehensive operational assurance — spanning temporal self-correction, end-to-end reliability, and external control — holds identically across both storage backends with equivalent safety guarantees, provided PgApi achieves full API parity with the SQLite path.

justifications.label: Full operational assurance across backends requires complete PgApi API coverage

backend-independent-self-correction.text: The complete self-correction pipeline — contradiction resolution through dependency-directed backtracking, staleness detection through source hash comparison, and ongoing belief currency management — operates identically across all storage backends, making the system's self-maintaining properties a deployment-independent guarantee rather than a backend-specific capability.

justifications.label: Self-correction relies on operations that PgApi has not yet fully implemented; once PgApi achieves complete API coverage, self-correction becomes backend-independent

backend-kwargs-exits-on-pg-without-domai.text: `_backend_kwargs` calls `sys.exit(1)` if `--pg` (or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`) is set without any `--domain-id` / `--project-id` / env fallback.

backend-kwargs-precedence-cli-over-env.text: `_backend_kwargs` resolves PostgreSQL configuration with CLI arguments taking precedence over `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` and `REASONS_PROJECT_ID`, and defaults to `{"db_path": args.db}` when no PG configuration is present.

backend-kwargs-reads-env-var-fallbacks.text: `_backend_kwargs` reads `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` and `REASONS_DOMAIN_ID` environment variables as fallbacks when the corresponding `--pg` / `--domain-id` flags are not provided, enabling shell-level configuration without repeating flags on every invocation.

backfill-hashes-can-silently-hash-cycles.text: `backfill_hashes` calls `compute_content_hash` for every missing justification hash, so cyclic justifications can be assigned normal-looking hashes (`reasons/merkle.py:130-146`).

backfill-hashes-only-fills-missing-hashe.text: `backfill_hashes` computes only missing `text_hash`/`content_hash` values and leaves existing hashes untouched.

backfill-hashes-repairs-missing-hash-row.text: `api.backfill_hashes` repairs missing node `text_hash` and justification `content_hash` values and reports `nodes_updated`/`justifications_updated` counts.

backfill-requires-missing-hashes.text: `api.backfill_hashes()` fills empty `text_hash`/`content_hash` fields and reports `nodes_updated` and `justifications_updated`; afterward `check_integrity` reports zero missing hashes.

backtracking-retracts-least-entrenched.text: `add_nogood` resolves contradictions via dependency-directed backtracking: `find_culprits` traces to premises, scores by `_entrenchment`, and retracts the least-entrenched premise to minimize disruption.

basis-controls-review-tier-in-prompt.text: `PROPOSE_UPDATE_PROMPT` annotates only `basis` values with accept/review language ("cheap to accept" for `source-divergence`, "needs scrutiny" for `prior-knowledge`), making `basis` the intended auto-accept/manual-review axis.

batch-failures-do-not-abort-propose-upda.text: Exceptions from `invoke_model`, parsing, or the `on_batch` callback are caught per batch and logged as `WARN` to stderr; remaining batches still execute.

batch-failures-do-not-abort-review.text: A `_process_batch` exception inside either the serial loop or a parallel `future.result()` is caught, logged to stderr, and does not stop remaining batches.

batch-fault-isolation-is-universal-acros.text: Both LLM-facing batch operations — derive proposal application (try/except per proposal with error accumulation) and belief review (silent skip on per-batch LLM failure) — isolate faults at the individual item level, preventing any single bad item from aborting the entire batch.

justifications.label: Both batch processing paths independently implement per-item error isolation, establishing it as a cross-cutting system pattern

belief-consistency-spans-structural-and-.text: The system maintains belief consistency through two complementary mechanisms targeting different quality dimensions: deduplication resolves structural redundancy (merging equivalent beliefs while preserving topology with user-editable auditable plans), while contradiction management resolves semantic inconsistency (traceable dependency-directed backtracking with consistent nogood IDs and minimal-disruption culprit selection).

justifications.label: Structural dedup and semantic contradiction resolution are complementary consistency mechanisms

belief-currency-is-actively-managed.text: The system actively manages belief currency bidirectionally: the production-ready derive pipeline safely introduces new beliefs through defensive validation, while the staleness CI gate detects drift in existing beliefs against source material — together preventing both unsafe additions and undetected obsolescence.

justifications.label: New-belief derivation plus existing-belief drift detection yields bidirectional currency assurance

belief-modification-is-bidirectionally-c.text: Belief modification is complete in both directions: contradictions that create truth changes are resolved through traceable dependency-directed backtracking with consistent nogood IDs, AND defeats that suppress truth values reverse automatically through BFS propagation with surgical restoration hints — no truth change is either irresolvable or irreversible without full traceability.

justifications.label: Bidirectional completeness — creating and undoing modifications are both complete and traceable

belief-replacement-is-topology-safe-and-.text: Both belief replacement mechanisms achieve topology safety and view consistency: supersession operates through reversible outlist semantics with gated view exclusion of superseded nodes, while deduplication rewires all justification references (both antecedent and outlist) to the most-connected survivor with user-auditable plans — ensuring the dependency graph remains structurally sound and consumers see a clean non-redundant belief set regardless of which replacement mechanism was used.

justifications.label: Two independent belief replacement mechanisms both achieve the same dual guarantee, establishing a system-wide replacement invariant

belief-revision-covers-all-cases-uniform.text: The belief revision system handles normal beliefs and all edge cases (premises from absent justifications, asymmetric missing-node semantics, vacuously valid empty antecedents) through the same minimal mechanisms (outlist defeat and dependency-directed backtracking) — no edge case requires special-case logic.

justifications.label: Uniform edge-case semantics mean the two minimal revision primitives never need special-case dispatch — edge cases are just ordinary cases

belief-revision-is-comprehensive-and-min.text: The system handles all forms of belief revision through two complementary minimal mechanisms: the outlist primitive provides a single reversible defeat mechanism for challenges, kill-switches, and supersession, while dependency-directed backtracking resolves detected contradictions by retracting the least-entrenched premise with minimal disruption.

justifications.label: depth-3 — defeat (proactive, via outlist) and contradiction resolution (reactive, via backtracking) are orthogonal subsystems that together cover all belief revision scenarios

belief-revision-is-fully-reliable.text: The complete belief revision pipeline — outlist-based defeat for proactive retraction plus dependency-directed backtracking for reactive contradiction resolution — produces correct, consistent, auditable results with deterministic propagation settling all consequences.

justifications.label: depth-3, gated — dangling dependents could crash propagation mid-cascade (violating the determinism guarantee), and append-only nogood IDs could collide if nogoods are ever deleted (corrupting the contradiction audit trail)

belief-source-metadata-is-file-level.text: Belief source tracking uses flat file-level pointers (source path + source_hash) with no structural awareness of where within a document the claim originated — section, page, or paragraph level provenance is not supported.

belief-text-truncated-at-200-chars.text: `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check` truncates any belief text longer than 200 characters, appending `...` as a suffix, to keep LLM prompts bounded.

belief-type-defaults-from-justifications.text: Without `beliefs_type` metadata, `export_markdown` emits `DERIVED` for nodes with justifications and `OBSERVATION` otherwise.

beliefs-section-excludes-derived-nodes.text: `_build_beliefs_section` only lists nodes that are `IN` and not in the derived set; derived nodes are listed separately.

beliefs-section-omits-empty-agent-and-lo.text: `_build_beliefs_section` omits the `Agent:` section when `agents=None` and omits `Local beliefs` when there are no local beliefs.

beliefs-type-lookup-is-case-insensitive.text: `beliefs_type` is uppercased before the table lookup, so `"axiom"` and `"AXIOM"` both score `90`.

beliefs-type-metadata-overrides-default-.text: If a node's metadata contains `beliefs_type`, that string replaces the default type label (`OBSERVATION` for premises, `DERIVED` for justified nodes) in the `### <id> [<status>] <TYPE>` header.

bidirectional-modification-achieves-topo.text: Bidirectional belief modification — contradiction resolution through traceable backtracking and defeat reversal with guided recovery — achieves topology-complete truth changes that are robust across all graph states, ensuring both directions of modification propagate through the complete dependency graph including under adverse conditions.

justifications.label: Bidirectional completeness (both directions of truth change are handled) combined with topology completeness (all reachable nodes are updated) ensures no modification direction leaves orphaned state

bidirectional-modification-is-richly-gov.text: Every bidirectional belief modification — contradiction resolution through traceable backtracking and defeat reversal with guided recovery — operates within richly-governed exception-safe revision that manages state beyond binary truth values, so every modification in either direction produces metadata-enriched recoverable state changes within a deterministic lifecycle.

justifications.label: Bidirectional modification achieves topology within deterministic lifecycle; rich governance adds exception-safe metadata management — combining yields fully characterized bidirectional operations

bidirectional-modification-within-determ.text: Bidirectional belief modification — contradiction resolution through traceable backtracking and defeat reversal with guided recovery — achieves topology completeness within a deterministic architecturally-grounded lifecycle framework that monitors every modification path from creation through maintenance.

justifications.label: Topology-complete bidirectional modification composes with deterministic lifecycle management — every bidirectional change (forward contradiction resolution and backward defeat reversal) operates within a monitored predictable lifecycle

bidirectional-modifications-achieve-full.text: Bidirectional belief modifications — contradiction resolution through traceable backtracking and defeat reversal with guided recovery — simultaneously achieve all three governance dimensions: rich revision governance extending beyond binary truth, exception-safe recoverability across all failure modes, and topology-complete metadata propagation through the full dependency graph.

justifications.label: bidirectional modifications unify rich governance, exception safety, and topology-complete metadata

blocker-entries-require-text-and-gated-l.text: Each entry in `gated_data["blockers"]` is consumed as an object containing `text` and a `gated` list of objects with `id` and `text`.

blocker-in-causes-gated-belief-out.text: If an outlist blocker is `IN` and no alternative justification remains, the gated belief can flip from `IN` to `OUT`.

bootstrap-bypasses-incremental-propagati.text: Both persistence loading and import construct the full node graph before truth maintenance — load trusts stored truth values and skips propagation entirely, while import adds all nodes then propagates via recompute_all — sharing a bulk-construction pattern that avoids per-node incremental propagation.

justifications.label: Both subsystems separate graph construction from truth maintenance for efficiency and correctness during bulk operations

both-backends-support-safe-hypothetical-.text: Both storage backends enable hypothetical what-if reasoning without permanent mutation: PgApi performs real mutations inside a transaction then rolls back, while the in-memory backend uses write-flag gating to discard speculative changes after analysis

justifications.label: Transaction rollback (PgApi) and write-flag gating (SQLite) achieve the same safe-simulation guarantee through backend-appropriate mechanisms

both-revision-paths-preserve-system-inva.text: Both forms of belief modification — reactive contradiction resolution (backtracking to least-entrenched premise, skipping retracted nodes) and proactive dialectical challenge (irreversible premise transformation with inherited outlist semantics) — preserve system invariants despite operating through fundamentally different mechanisms, confirming that invariant preservation is architectural rather than mechanism-specific.

justifications.label: Two independent revision mechanisms both preserve invariants — safety is structural, not incidental

budget-check-reserves-footer-space.text: `_over_budget` adds `footer_tokens` to every line check so the closing token-count line always has reserved room.

budget-enforcement-is-efficient-across-p.text: All budget-constrained operations — compact output distillation and derive belief allocation — achieve computationally efficient tracking with representation-safe minimum bounds, ensuring budget enforcement never becomes a performance bottleneck.

justifications.label: Compact uses O(1) per-line char tracking; derive uses O(N) linear accumulation with floor-5 guarantee — both avoid quadratic costs

budget-floor-is-five.text: `_build_beliefs_section` guarantees local beliefs get at least 5 slots regardless of agent count, enforced by `max(5, max_beliefs - count)`

budget-section-graceful-emptiness.text: This claim (zero beliefs/agents/locals handled without raising) is a trivial consequence of any well-written loop over empty collections and does not represent a non-obvious invariant or architectural constraint a developer needs to know.

build-ask-prompt-appends-tool-history-se.text: When `tool_history` is provided, `build_ask_prompt()` appends an 'Additional search results' section containing prior queries and their results.

build-ask-prompt-includes-search-beliefs.text: `build_ask_prompt()` always includes the `search_beliefs` tool definition so the LLM knows it can request additional searches.

build-beliefs-section-headers-are-regex-.text: `_build_beliefs_section` emits headers matching `Local beliefs (N beliefs, showing M)` and `Agent: <name> (N beliefs, showing M)`, which tests parse as an output contract.

build-beliefs-section-safe-on-empty-or-m.text: `_build_beliefs_section` returns a string without crashing for an empty network or when the agents mapping references nonexistent node IDs.

build-justifications-falls-back-to-bare-.text: When a claim has zero `raw_justifications`, `_build_justifications` produces a single `Justification(type="SL", antecedents=[], outlist=[inactive_id])` as a fallback, ensuring even premise nodes are wired into the kill-switch cascade.

build-mcp-instructions-concatenates-brid.text: `_build_mcp_instructions` concatenates instructions from multiple MCP bridges and returns an empty string when no instructions are provided.

build-meta-computes-now-once.text: `build_meta` computes the current UTC timestamp once per call and uses it for `updated_at` and for `created_at` only when `created_at` is falsy.

build-meta-computes-now-once-per-call.text: `build_meta()` computes the current UTC timestamp once per call and uses that same value for `updated_at` and for `created_at` when `created_at` is falsy.

build-meta-default-project-name-is-empty.text: `build_meta()` called with no arguments returns an empty-string `project_name`, distinct from the file-derived default used by `init_db`.

build-meta-does-not-order-created-at-and.text: `build_meta()` does not validate or enforce that `created_at` is less than or equal to `updated_at`.

build-meta-does-not-validate-inputs.text: `build_meta` performs no runtime validation of `project_name`, `node_count`, or `created_at`.

build-meta-generator-fallback-is-unknown.text: `_get_generator` catches `Exception` from `importlib.metadata.version` and returns `ftl-reasons/unknown` on failure.

build-meta-import-unused.text: `build_meta` is imported from `reasons.metadata` but never referenced in this file.

build-meta-populates-generator-via-get-g.text: `build_meta()` calls `_get_generator()` when constructing the `"generator"` metadata field.

build-meta-preserves-created-at.text: A truthy `created_at` argument is copied verbatim; falsey values are replaced with the current UTC timestamp.

build-meta-preserves-truthy-created-at.text: `build_meta` copies any truthy `created_at` value unchanged and replaces only falsy values with the current timestamp.

build-meta-refreshes-updated-at.text: `updated_at` is always regenerated using `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` with seconds precision.

build-meta-returns-fixed-six-key-dict.text: `build_meta()` always returns a flat dict with exactly six keys — `schema_version`, `project_name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `node_count`, `generator` — no more, no fewer, and consumers can rely on this shape without defensive `.get()` calls.

build-meta-returns-fresh-mutable-dict.text: `build_meta()` returns a new mutable `dict` on every call and does not mutate its arguments or module-level state.

build-meta-returns-six-fields.text: `build_meta` returns a dict with exactly `schema_version`, `project_name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `node_count`, and `generator`.

build-meta-timestamps-use-second-precisi.text: `build_meta()` timestamps use `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")`, so they omit microseconds and include the `+00:00` UTC offset.

build-prompt-validates-custom-templates.text: `build_prompt` raises `ValueError("unknown placeholder")` for unrecognized `{fields}` and `ValueError("malformed braces")` for unclosed braces in custom prompt templates

build-tools-section-always-includes-sear.text: `_build_tools_section` always includes the built-in `search_beliefs` tool in its output regardless of whether MCP bridges are provided — it is the baseline tool present in every ask prompt.

build-tools-section-handles-empty-params.text: For a tool whose input schema has empty `properties`, `_build_tools_section` emits a JSON example without a trailing comma after the tool name.

build-tools-section-merges-all-bridges.text: `_build_tools_section` merges tool descriptors from all provided MCP bridges together with the built-in `search_beliefs` tool.

build-wiki-always-writes-index-md.text: `build_wiki` creates `index.md` even when there are no beliefs, and that page contains `"No beliefs found"` for an empty database.

build-wiki-cluster-label-collisions-get-.text: When cluster mode derives a page label already used by another cluster, `build_wiki` appends `-{cluster_id}` to make the label unique.

build-wiki-cluster-labels-derived-from-i.text: Cluster page labels are chosen as the most frequent non-stopword token after splitting member ids on `[-._:]`, with a `cluster-{id}` fallback and `-{id}` collision suffixing.

build-wiki-defeater-rendering-reverse-ou.text: `_format_node` renders “Defeated by” by scanning each justification's `outlist`, looking up those nodes, and keeping only nodes whose `metadata["defeats_node"]` equals the rendered node ID.

build-wiki-does-not-mutate-database.text: `build_wiki` opens the network read-only and never writes to the SQLite database.

build-wiki-does-not-perform-grouping.text: `build_wiki` receives the `groups` dict fully formed; it never calls `_assign_topics` itself.

build-wiki-does-not-support-postgresql.text: `build_wiki` has no `pg_conninfo`/`domain_id` parameters, unlike most sibling functions in `reasons/api.py`, so it is SQLite-only.

build-wiki-duplicate-node-membership-las.text: If the same node ID appears in multiple groups, `node_to_page` is built by walking groups in order, so the node is linked to the last group's page without error.

build-wiki-empty-network-produces-placeh.text: When the filtered node set is empty, `build_wiki` creates `output_dir`, writes a single `index.md` containing `*No beliefs found.*`, and returns `{"pages": 0, "total_nodes": 0}` without invoking `_build_wiki`.

build-wiki-failure-can-leave-partial-out.text: `build_wiki` has no try/except around `_build_wiki`, so a mid-write failure can leave partial output on disk.

build-wiki-falls-back-on-llm-errors.text: When `model` is supplied, `build_wiki` uses `generate_wiki_page`, but a `RuntimeError` from generation does not prevent static `_format_node` Markdown from being written.

build-wiki-is-dependency-leaf.text: `build_wiki.py` is imported only by `reasons/api.py` and test files; no other `reasons/*.py` runtime module depends on it, placing it at a leaf of the internal dependency graph.

build-wiki-is-sqlite-only.text: `build_wiki` in `reasons/api.py` accepts only `db_path` and has no `pg_conninfo` parameter, so it cannot route to the PostgreSQL backend.

build-wiki-linkify-longest-first-prevent.text: `_linkify` sorts node IDs by length (longest first) before substitution to prevent a shorter ID like `node-alpha` from consuming the prefix of `node-alpha-extended`, and skips same-page references to avoid self-links.

build-wiki-linkify-skips-current-page.text: `_linkify` skips IDs whose target page equals the current page, leaving intra-page references as literal text while still linking cross-page IDs.

build-wiki-llm-failure-falls-back-to-tem.text: When `generate_wiki_page` raises any exception during LLM-based wiki generation, `build_wiki` silently falls back to template rendering and still produces valid output.

build-wiki-parallel-requires-model.text: The parallel branch is only entered when **both** `model` is truthy and `parallel > 0`; `parallel > 0` with `model=""` degrades to the static renderer.

build-wiki-prompt-omits-outlist-and-meta.text: `_format_beliefs_for_prompt` emits only status, text, dependency, and support summary for the LLM; unlike `_format_node`, it does not walk outlists or metadata.

build-wiki-reserved-index-slug-rewritten.text: A topic label that slugifies to `index` is rewritten to `index-topic` so it cannot overwrite the generated `index.md`.

build-wiki-returns-page-count-dict.text: `build_wiki` returning `{"pages": int, "total_nodes": int}` is a minor API signature detail unlikely to change semantics independently of the broader build_wiki contract already captured by other beliefs.

build-wiki-slug-collision-produces-disti.text: Two topics that slugify to the same filename produce two distinct output files rather than silently overwriting each other; the index page is also always created even for an empty database.

build-wiki-swallows-llm-errors.text: LLM generation failures in `build_wiki` are caught, logged to stderr as `WARN`, and the page falls back to raw markdown rendering.

build-wiki-swallows-node-detail-errors.text: `KeyError` and `PermissionError` from `show_node` are caught and ignored, meaning `node_details` can be a strict subset of `groups`' referenced ids.

build-wiki-swallows-show-node-errors.text: `build_wiki` catches and ignores `KeyError` and `PermissionError` from `show_node`, so a node can appear in `groups` without a corresponding `node_details` entry.

build-wiki-topic-assignment-is-prefix-ba.text: `_assign_topics` maps each node to the first topic whose key is a prefix of the node ID; nodes matching no topic go to "Other" and are never dropped.

build-wiki-topic-labels-bypass-visibilit.text: The `cluster=False` branch calls `topics(limit=max_topics, db_path=db_path)` without `visible_to` or `status`, so topic vocabulary is derived from the entire network even when the requesting caller has restricted access tags.

build-wiki-topic-labels-ignore-status-an.text: In topic mode `build_wiki` calls `topics()` without `status` or `visible_to`, so topic labels are derived from all nodes even though grouped node IDs come from the filtered `list_nodes` result.

bulk-operations-converge-and-preserve-to.text: All bulk modification operations — deduplication (rewiring both antecedent and outlist references to survivors) and import/sync (dual reconciliation modes with namespace isolation) — both preserve network topology invariants and converge deterministically to stable states through fixpoint iteration and idempotent operations.

justifications.label: Topology preservation ensures bulk operations don't corrupt the dependency graph, while deterministic convergence ensures they reach stable states — together they guarantee bulk modifications are structurally safe and terminating.

bulk-operations-preserve-topology-and-re.text: Both bulk modification operations — deduplication and import/sync — preserve network topology by rewiring justification references (both antecedent and outlist) to survivors or updated targets, while providing distinct reconciliation strategies (dedup via user-editable keep/retract plans, import via dual additive/remote-wins modes)

justifications.label: Two independently-designed bulk operations converge on the same safety property — topology preservation through reference rewriting — suggesting this is an emergent architectural invariant rather than a coincidence

business-planning-documents-live-in-goog.text: Business planning source documents are stored in Google Drive rather than on local disk.

business-planning-lacks-hash-based-chang.text: The business planning network has no hash-based source change detection equivalent to check-stale for local files.

business-premise-verification-can-take-h.text: Verifying a business premise can take hours to weeks per belief.

cache-invalidation-is-mtime-only.text: The network cache uses the SQLite file's modification time (`st_mtime`) as its sole invalidation signal; it does not use inode numbers, file descriptors, or content hashes, so a same-tick content rewrite could produce a false cache hit.

cache-preconditions-require-clear-betwee.text: All tests rely on the pytest `setup_function` hook to empty `_network_cache` before execution; without it, entries would leak because `TemporaryDirectory` only cleans the filesystem, not the dict.

cache-read-returns-identical-object.text: Repeated read-mode calls to `_with_network` on the same DB path with unchanged mtime return the exact same Python `Network` object (identity via `is`), meaning any caller that mutates the returned object in-place corrupts the global cache for all subsequent readers.

cache-write-exception-preserves-prior-st.text: If an exception is raised inside a `with _with_network(db, write=True)` block, the context manager's `__exit__` discards the in-progress network and the pre-exception cached `Network` object remains intact and unmutated.

call-tool-propagates-exceptions-only.text: Only Python exceptions from the awaited `session.call_tool` and from `future.result(timeout=60)` propagate out of `McpBridge.call_tool`; returned `isError=True` results do not raise

call-tool-returns-newline-joined-string.text: `McpBridge.call_tool()` flattens the MCP tool result's `content` list (which may contain multiple content blocks) into a single `\n`-joined string; non-text blocks are stringified via `str()`.

candidate-filter-requires-multi-antecede.text: `review_justifications` only reviews nodes containing an `SL` justification whose antecedent count meets or exceeds `min_antecedents`.

candidate-filtering-precedes-llm-matchin.text: Antecedent-duplicate and derived-belief candidates are removed before `find_matching_premises` runs, causing `no_candidates` without a second LLM round-trip.

canonical-equilibria-are-negation-transp.text: The system converges to canonical evaluation-invariant equilibria where negative semantics are fully transparent — the final stable state is determined solely by the logical content of justifications, independent of both the transformation path taken and whether beliefs were established through positive assertion or negative defeat.

justifications.label: Evaluation invariance + negation transparency together mean equilibria are canonical regardless of how beliefs were established or defeated

canonical-package-imports-legacy-shim.text: `reasons/api.py`, `reasons/repair.py`, and `reasons/review_justifications.py` import `reasons_lib.review`, creating a cross-tree import edge from the new package back to the legacy one.

card-type-is-eem.text: The frontmatter `type` field is always the literal string `"eem"`.

cascade-depth-is-computed-per-target.text: `_cascade_depth` (`reasons/api.py:737`) measures how far a target node sits from the retracted node, used to annotate cascade effects.

cascade-depth-uses-bfs-shortest-path.text: The `_cascade_depth` function performs BFS through dependents edges to find the shortest path from a retracted node to a target.

cascade-does-not-set-retracted-at.text: `retracted_at` is populated only on nodes the user directly retracted; cascade-affected dependents end up `OUT` with an empty `retracted_at`.

cascade-impact-not-computed-by-propose.text: `propose_updates()` never computes cascade impact; proposal Markdown shows “not computed” unless an external caller supplies cascade data.

cascade-is-computed-pre-accept.text: Cascade impact is produced at proposal-generation time via `what_if_retract` and rendered into the proposals markdown; acceptance itself is manual via suggested CLI commands.

cascade-rendering-is-action-dependent.text: RETRACT proposals with cascade data render "will go OUT" language (dependents are destroyed), while UPDATE proposals render "need re-review" language (dependents are invalidated, not retracted) — reflecting the semantic difference between the two actions.

cascades-produce-both-out-and-in-sets.text: `reasons/api.py:517-627` and `reasons/cli.py:114-115` split cascade results into `went_out` and `went_in`.

central-dependency-is-safely-contained.text: Despite `network.py` being imported by virtually every module in the codebase, the three-layer architecture with clean boundaries ensures this central coupling does not create cross-cutting mutation paths — layer separation contains the dependency's blast radius so that the hub topology does not compromise architectural integrity.

justifications.label: clean layer boundaries contain the impact of the central network dependency (depth-2 from depth-0 + depth-1, integrates orphaned base belief)

challenge-adds-to-target-metadata.text: The challenge method appends the new challenge ID to the target's metadata['challenges'] list.

challenge-converts-bare-premise-to-justi.text: Challenging a bare premise with no justifications converts it into a justified node with `SL(antecedents=[], outlist=[challenge_id])`.

challenge-converts-premises-to-justified.text: When a premise (node with no justifications) is challenged, it is converted to a justified node with an SL justification containing empty antecedents and the challenge in the outlist.

challenge-defense-is-crash-safe.text: The dialectical challenge/defend system reaches correct truth states through recursive outlist injection evaluated by deterministic terminating propagation.

justifications.label: Challenge/defend creates new nodes and dependent relationships dynamically; if propagation crashes on a dangling dependent reference, dialectical operations could leave the network inconsistent

challenge-destroys-premise-identity.text: When a premise is challenged, it loses its defining characteristic: premise identity emerges from absence of justifications, but challenge adds a justification (converting the premise to a justified node), meaning the target's truth value becomes conditional on the challenge node being OUT rather than unconditionally held — challenge reclassifies the target in the node type system.

justifications.label: Challenge adds justifications (base) + premise identity is absence of justifications (depth-1) together reveal that challenge is a type-level transformation, not just a truth-value change

challenge-id-auto-generation.text: Auto-generated challenge IDs follow the pattern `challenge-{target}`, then `challenge-{target}-2`, `-3`, etc.; explicit IDs that collide raise `ValueError` rather than auto-deduplicating.

challenge-id-collisions-get-numeric-suff.text: A second call to `challenge(target)` with the same target produces `challenge-<target>-2`, not an error and not an overwrite.

challenge-is-outlist-injection.text: The challenge mechanism creates a new premise node and adds it to the target's outlist; all truth-value changes flow through normal BFS propagation, not direct mutation

challenge-modifies-all-justifications.text: When the target has multiple justifications, the challenge node is added to the outlist of every justification, ensuring no single justification can independently keep the target IN.

challenge-node-is-premise.text: The challenge node itself is always created as a premise (no justifications, IN by default) and can only be driven OUT by explicit retraction or by being challenged/defended.

challenge-premise-starts-in-and-defeats-.text: A challenge creates a new premise node that starts IN, and adding it to the target's outlist makes the target go OUT until defended.

challenge-propagation-is-automatic.text: After creating the challenge, truth value recomputation and BFS propagation through dependents happen within the same call; callers never need to trigger propagation manually.

challenge-registers-dependency.text: After a challenge, the challenge node's dependents set includes the target_id so the target gets recomputed when the challenge changes.

challenge-returns-dict-with-challenge-id.text: `Network.challenge` is contractually required to return `{"challenge_id": ..., "changed": [...]}`, and `"changed"` includes every node whose truth value was affected, including cascaded dependents.

challenge-uses-outlist-mechanism.text: `challenge` works by creating an IN premise node and adding it to the target's outlist in every justification, reusing the same non-monotonic mechanism as `supersede`.

change-event-is-frozen-dataclass.text: `ChangeEvent` is an immutable frozen dataclass with fields `type`, `node_id`, `old_truth_value`, `new_truth_value`, and `db_path`.

change-event-uses-none-for-absent-state.text: `ChangeEvent` encodes absent state as `None`: new nodes have `old_truth_value=None`, and deleted nodes have `new_truth_value=None`.

change-events-are-snapshot-diffs.text: `compute_changes` in `reasons/pubsub.py:96` derives events by diffing truth-value snapshots rather than observing the propagator.

change-events-carry-no-causality.text: `ChangeEvent`s carry old/new truth values and `db_path` but not cause or cascade-root information.

changeevent-uses-none-for-absent-state.text: New nodes have `old_truth_value=None`; deleted nodes have `new_truth_value=None`.

changelog-follows-keep-a-changelog-1-1-0.text: CHANGELOG.md follows the Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 convention with version headers and Added/Fixed/Changed sections.

changelog-records-rms-to-reasons-rename.text: `CHANGELOG.md` records a historical rename from `rms` to `reasons` for the CLI, library, and package name.

check-integrity-findings-have-only-text-.text: `api.check_integrity` partitions Merkle results only into `text_mutations` and `chain_mutations`; there is no structural `cycle` finding category.

check-integrity-maps-findings-to-two-key.text: `api.check_integrity` exposes only `text_mutations` and `chain_mutations`, so a new structural cycle finding would require API/CLI changes (`reasons/api.py:2736-2740`).

check-integrity-returns-result-dict-not-.text: For the corruption and cycle cases covered here, `api.check_integrity()` returns a dict and tests assert on `text_mutations`, `chain_mutations`, and `missing_hashes` rather than expecting exceptions.

check-stale-and-hash-sources-mutate-in-p.text: Both `check_stale` (with `upgrade_hashes=True`) and `hash_sources` modify `node.source_hash` directly on the Network object; neither persists — the caller must save.

check-stale-auto-bumps-pinned-sha-on-con.text: In git-aware mode, `check_stale` auto-bumps `pinned_sha` to the new HEAD when the file content hash is unchanged despite intervening commits, preserving `pinned_lines`.

check-stale-classifies-content-changed-a.text: check_stale categorizes results as content_changed when the hash differs and source_deleted when the resolved path is missing.

check-stale-content-changed-populates-so.text: A `content_changed` result from `check_stale` includes the resolved filesystem path in its `source_path` field.

check-stale-detects-source-staleness-onl.text: `check-stale` detects source staleness (source file changed on disk) via hash comparison but cannot detect world staleness (the belief is outdated even though the source file hasn't changed) — beliefs can silently decay without any artifact triggering re-examination.

check-stale-empty-file-with-matching-has.text: An existing empty source file whose hash matches the node's `source_hash` is treated as fresh and produces no staleness result.

check-stale-existing-empty-file-is-not-d.text: An existing zero-byte source file is not reported as `source_deleted`; it is fresh if its hash matches and `content_changed` if the hash differs.

check-stale-exits-nonzero.text: `cmd_check_stale` calls `sys.exit(1)` when any stale nodes are found, making it usable as a CI or pre-commit gate.

check-stale-exits-nonzero-on-stale.text: `cmd_check_stale` calls `sys.exit(1)` when stale nodes are found (even on success), making the command usable as a CI or pre-commit gate.

check-stale-exits-nonzero-on-stale-nodes.text: Unlike the general error-to-exit-1 convention, `cmd_check_stale` deliberately exits 1 when any source is stale or deleted, enabling CI freshness gates.

check-stale-is-read-only.text: `check_stale` never mutates the network; it returns a list of stale-node dicts and leaves all nodes unchanged — staleness detection is separated from staleness resolution.

check-stale-mutates-in-place-caller-pers.text: `check_stale`, `hash_sources`, and all `pin_*` functions mutate `Node.source_hash` and/or `Node.metadata` in place; callers are responsible for saving the network.

check-stale-mutates-network-in-place.text: `check_stale`, `hash_sources`, and all `pin_*` functions write to `node.source_hash` / `node.metadata` directly; the caller must persist the network.

check-stale-never-raises-on-missing-file.text: `check_stale()` returns a structured `source_deleted` dict for nodes whose source files don't exist on disk; it never raises `FileNotFoundError` or any exception.

check-stale-no-dedup-by-source-path.text: Multiple nodes referencing the same missing source file each produce independent `source_deleted` results — no deduplication by file path.

check-stale-operates-per-node-not-per-fi.text: Multiple nodes pointing to the same source file each receive their own independent result entry in the returned list; the function iterates nodes, not files.

check-stale-output-is-deterministic-and-.text: Staleness checking produces deterministic (sorted by node ID), uniformly structured (consistent 6-key schema across all result types), and exception-free (returns structured dicts for missing files rather than raising) output suitable for programmatic consumption and diffing.

justifications.label: Three output-shape guarantees unify into a programmatic consumption contract

check-stale-processes-only-in-nodes.text: `check_stale` and `pin_sources` skip any node whose `truth_value` is not `"IN"`.

check-stale-propagates-file-read-errors.text: File read errors from hash_file, such as OSError or PermissionError, are not caught by check_stale and propagate to the caller.

metadata.retract_reason: Stale duplicate of check-stale-is-read-only; also contradicted by check-stale-and-hash-sources-mutate-in-place (issue #101)

check-stale-reports-content-changed-and-.text: check_stale returns problem records with one of two reason values: content_changed when the file hash differs, or source_deleted when the resolved file path no longer exists.

check-stale-reports-content-changed-with.text: When a source file changes, `check_stale()` reports a result with `reason='content_changed'` and includes the old and new hashes.

check-stale-repos-none-still-detects-mis.text: `check_stale()` with `repos=None` still returns `source_deleted` results for missing source files instead of raising an exception.

check-stale-repos-none-still-detects-sou.text: When `check_stale` is called with `repos=None`, a missing source file still produces a `source_deleted` result.

check-stale-requires-both-source-fields.text: A node must have both `source` (non-empty) and `source_hash` (non-empty) to be eligible for staleness checking; nodes missing either field are silently skipped.

check-stale-requires-in-source-and-hash.text: `check_stale` only examines nodes that are IN, have a non-empty `source`, and have a non-empty `source_hash`.

check-stale-requires-nonempty-source-and.text: `check_stale` skips nodes that lack `source` metadata, lack `source_hash` metadata, or have an empty-string `source`.

check-stale-requires-source-and-source-h.text: A node must have both source and source_hash metadata to be eligible for stale-checking.

check-stale-requires-source-hash.text: `check_stale()` skips IN nodes that have a `source` but no non-empty `source_hash`.

check-stale-result-schema-is-exact.text: Every result dict must contain exactly `node_id`, `old_hash`, `new_hash`, `source`, `source_path`, and `reason`.

check-stale-result-schema-uniform.text: All `check_stale` result dicts share the same 6-key schema (`node_id`, `old_hash`, `new_hash`, `source`, `source_path`, `reason`) regardless of reason type, so consumers can iterate results without type-checking.

check-stale-results-sorted-by-node-id.text: The list returned by `check_stale` is sorted ascending by `node_id`, providing deterministic output for consumers.

check-stale-returns-3-tuple.text: `check_stale` always returns `(results, upgraded, sha_bumped)`; the third element counts auto-bumped SHAs for pinned beliefs whose content is byte-identical.

check-stale-returns-result-list-and-upgr.text: `check_stale(net, ...)` returns a tuple whose first element is the list of stale-result dicts and whose second element is the upgraded-hash count.

check-stale-returns-results-and-upgrade-.text: `check_stale` returns a tuple whose first element is a stale-result list and whose second element is an upgraded-hash count.
`check_stale()` returns a tuple `(results, upgraded_count)` where `results` is a list of result dicts and `upgraded_count` counts truncated hashes upgraded in place.

check-stale-returns-source-deleted-resul.text: `check_stale` returns an explicit `source_deleted` result with `reason: "source_deleted"`, `new_hash: None`, and `source_path: None` when a tracked source file is missing.

check-stale-scopes-hash-comparison-to-in.text: Staleness detection compares stored source hashes only for IN nodes; `hash-sources` backfills unhashed nodes and `--force` re-hashes all.

check-stale-skip-rules-precede-file-exis.text: Retraction, missing `source`, missing `source_hash`, and empty-string `source` all suppress results even when the referenced file is also missing on disk; the eligibility check precedes the filesystem existence check.

check-stale-skips-ineligible-nodes.text: Nodes that are retracted, lack `source`, lack `source_hash`, or have `source == ""` are omitted from results.

check-stale-skips-nodes-without-source-a.text: check_stale silently skips nodes that do not have both source and source_hash set, emitting no error or report entry.

check-stale-skips-out-nodes.text: Only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` are checked for staleness; retracted (OUT) nodes are ignored even if their source file has changed.

check-stale-source-deleted-returns-none-.text: When a source file is missing, `check_stale` returns a result dict with `reason="source_deleted"`, `new_hash=None`, and `source_path=None` (fix for issue #25 — previously this case was silently skipped).

check-stale-upgrade-hashes-excludes-upgr.text: When upgrade_hashes=True, check_stale silently upgrades matching truncated hashes in place on the node and excludes them from stale results.

ci-gates-main-branch-only.text: The CI workflow triggers exclusively on push to `main` or pull_request targeting `main`; pushes to or PRs targeting any other branch produce no workflow run, meaning feature branches without a PR to main never execute tests.

ci-matrix-jobs-are-independent.text: The four Python version jobs (3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13) run as independent parallel jobs on separate GitHub Actions runners; a failure in one version's job does not cancel or affect the other three.

claims-retracted-is-subset-of-claims-imp.text: In `import_into_network`'s result dict, `claims_retracted` is a subset of `claims_imported`; stale claims counted as retracted still count as imported.

classification-failures-go-to-errors-lis.text: Unclassifiable defeaters are collected in `result["errors"]` instead of being raised or written.

classify-defeat-batch-empty-result-becom.text: In `classify_defeat_reason_types`, an empty classifier result is appended to `result["errors"]` rather than raised or silently discarded.

classify-defeat-batch-result-has-classif.text: `api.classify_defeat_reason_types` returns a dict with `classified`, `skipped`, and `errors`; classified entries contain `id` and `defeat_reason_type`, and skipped entries contain `reason`.

classify-defeat-dry-run-is-write-free.text: When `dry_run=True`, `api.classify_defeat_reason_types` reads the database but performs zero writes; the node's `metadata` dict is provably unchanged (verified by re-reading and asserting the key is absent).

classify-defeat-idempotent-via-metadata-.text: A defeater node that already carries `defeat_reason_type` in its metadata is placed in the `"skipped"` bucket and is never re-sent to the LLM, making repeated batch invocations idempotent.

classify-defeat-parser-prefers-exact-mat.text: `classify_defeat_reason` first returns an exact whole-output match against `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES`, then extracts a member token from prose, otherwise returns `""`.

classify-defeat-reason-maps-to-enum.text: `classify_defeat_reason` resolves LLM output to a `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` value via exact-then-substring matching, otherwise returns `""`.

classify-defeat-reason-returns-empty-on-.text: The pure classifier returns `""` on subprocess exception and on unrecognized LLM output, never raising.

classify-defeat-reason-returns-empty-str.text: `classify_defeat_reason` never raises; every failure path (binary not found, subprocess exception, unparseable LLM output) returns the empty string `""`, allowing callers to distinguish "no classification" from an exception.

classify-defeat-reason-types-dry-run-wri.text: With `dry_run=True`, classifications appear in the result but the defeater's `metadata["defeat_reason_type"]` remains absent (`test_dry_run_classifies_without_writing`)

classify-defeat-reason-types-skips-alrea.text: `api.classify_defeat_reason_types` returns already-classified defeaters under `skipped` with reason `"already classified"` rather than overwriting (`test_skips_already_classified`)

classify-defeat-skips-non-defeater-nodes.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types` ignores non-defeater nodes and does not attempt an LLM call when the database contains only non-defeaters.

claude-child-env-strips-claudecode.text: Before invoking the `claude` CLI, `invoke_model` removes `CLAUDECODE` from the child environment while preserving other environment variables such as `HOME`.

cleanup-order-respects-foreign-keys.text: The teardown `DELETE` loop orders tables leaves-first (`rms_propagation_log`, `rms_justifications`, `rms_nogoods`, `rms_network_meta`, `rms_nodes`) to satisfy foreign-key constraints.

clear-network-cache-supports-specific-or.text: `clear_network_cache(db_path)` removes only that DB path’s cache entry, while `clear_network_cache()` empties the entire cache.

cli-add-justification-warns-multi-premis.text: cmd_add and cmd_add_justification call _warn_multi_premise when an AND justification uses 3 or more antecedents.

cli-add-rejects-duplicate-ids.text: The `add` command rejects duplicate IDs with exit code `1` and stderr containing `"Error"`.

cli-add-supports-derived-nodes-with-sl-f.text: The CLI `add` subcommand supports derived nodes through the `--sl` flag.

cli-any-warning-for-three-plus-sl-premis.text: `_warn_multi_premise` prints a tip when an SL justification has 3 or more premises and `--any` was not passed.

cli-argparse-syntax-errors-exit-2.text: Invalid CLI syntax is handled by argparse, which prints usage to stderr and exits with code 2.

cli-auto-retract-sets-invalid-derived-no.text: `review-beliefs --auto-retract` changes invalid reviewed beliefs to `truth_value="OUT"`, while `--dry-run` prevents the mutation.

cli-backend-kwargs-controls-storage.text: `_backend_kwargs(args)` is the single chokepoint that determines whether a command runs against SQLite or PostgreSQL; every `cmd_*` function must spread its return value into the corresponding `api.*` call

cli-check-stale-exits-1-on-stale.text: `cmd_check_stale` exits with code 1 when stale nodes are found, making it usable as a CI gate that fails the build on belief staleness

cli-command-dispatch-uses-exact-string-d.text: `main()` dispatches subcommands through a `commands` dict mapping command-name strings to `cmd_*` functions, so a subcommand registered in argparse but missing from that dict raises `KeyError`.

cli-db-flag-available-everywhere.text: `--db` is added to the top-level parser and is available to every subcommand, defaulting to `api.DEFAULT_DB`.

cli-db-flag-defaults-to-api-default-db.text: Every CLI subcommand accepts a --db flag defaulting to api.DEFAULT_DB.

cli-db-option-defaults-to-api-default-db.text: Every CLI handler passes args.db through, and the --db option defaults to api.DEFAULT_DB, making the database path user-overridable on every command.

cli-db-option-is-global-before-subcomman.text: The CLI accepts `--db` as a global option before the subcommand, e.g. `reasons --db PATH report-gated`.

cli-deduplicate-has-plan-and-apply-phase.text: cmd_deduplicate supports a two-phase workflow: generating a dedup plan file, or applying one via --accept.

cli-delegates-to-api-except-propagate.text: Every cmd_* handler delegates to reasons_lib.api except cmd_propagate, which directly instantiates Storage, loads the network, calls recompute_all(), and saves.

cli-derive-cluster-and-sample-mutually-e.text: `cmd_derive` enforces that `--cluster` and `--sample` are mutually exclusive before starting derive work.

cli-derive-exhaust-implies-auto.text: cmd_derive's --exhaust mode implies --auto because _derive_one_round checks args.auto or args.exhaust before auto-applying proposals.

cli-derive-exhaust-stops-on-saturation.text: `cmd_derive --exhaust` loops `_derive_one_round` up to `--max-rounds` times and stops when a round adds zero new beliefs (saturation).

cli-dispatch-is-flat-dict-lookup.text: CLI dispatch uses a flat `commands` dict mapping subcommand strings to `cmd_*` handler functions — no plugin system or subclass hierarchy.

cli-dispatch-uses-commands-dict.text: `main()` routes subcommands through a `commands` dict mapping subcommand strings to `cmd_*` functions, rather than using argparse's `set_defaults(func=...)` — keeping all routing visible in one place.

cli-empty-state-queries-exit-zero.text: CLI query commands given an empty database return messages such as `No nodes` or `No matching` with exit code 0, not an error exit code.

cli-entry-point-lives-in-reasons.text: The `reasons` console script targets `reasons.cli:main`, not `reasons_lib.cli:main`, making `reasons/` the canonical CLI package.

cli-errors-go-to-stderr.text: Covered by existing `cli-is-deterministic-and-stream-correct` which addresses stdout/stderr routing.

cli-errors-use-stderr-success-uses-stdou.text: CLI error diagnostics are written to stderr and success output to stdout; tests consistently assert on the correct stream.

cli-exception-types-map-to-failure-modes.text: The CLI maps `KeyError` to node not found, `ValueError` to invalid input, `FileNotFoundError` to missing file, and `PermissionError` to access-tag violation, exiting with code 1.

cli-exit-1-on-error.text: All CLI error paths catch specific exceptions from the API (`KeyError`, `ValueError`, `PermissionError`, `FileNotFoundError`), print to stderr, and call `sys.exit(1)`.

cli-exit-code-contract-is-binary.text: Every CLI subcommand returns exit code 0 for success and 1 for any user-facing error; no other exit codes are used or tested.

cli-exit-code-contract-zero-or-one.text: Every CLI command returns exit code 0 on success and 1 on error; no other exit codes are used across the entire test suite (~90 tests).

cli-exit-code-zero-success-one-error.text: All CLI subcommands use exit code 0 for success and exit code 1 for every error condition (missing nodes, access denied, duplicate IDs, file not found); no other exit codes appear in the test suite.

cli-explain-shows-failed-antecedents-and.text: The CLI `explain` command displays failed antecedents and violated outlists.

cli-flags-override-env-vars.text: `_backend_kwargs` gives precedence to CLI `--pg`/`--project-id` flags over `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`/`REASONS_PROJECT_ID` environment variables when both are present

cli-flags-take-precedence-over-env-vars.text: `_backend_kwargs` resolves the storage backend with CLI flags (`--pg`, `--domain-id`) overriding environment variables (`REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`, `REASONS_PROJECT_ID`); when neither is set, SQLite is the default.

cli-global-db-option-precedes-subcommand.text: The CLI accepts `--db` as a global option before the subcommand, e.g. `reasons --db <path> topics ...`.

cli-global-options-must-precede-subcomma.text: Because global flags are declared on the root parser, they must appear before the subcommand; `reasons --db foo status` works but `reasons status --db foo` generally does not.

cli-handlers-are-api-facade-except-deriv.text: CLI subcommand handlers act as thin facades over `reasons.api`, with `cmd_derive` as the only handler containing real orchestration.

cli-handlers-are-thin-api-wrappers.text: Every `cmd_*` function other than `_derive_one_round` (and its helpers) performs exactly one `reasons.api` call followed by dict-formatted `stdout` output.

cli-has-35-subcommands.text: The CLI entry point (reasons command) exposes 35+ subcommands.

cli-idempotent-operations-report-already.text: The CLI reports `already OUT` when retracting an already-OUT node and `already IN` when asserting an already-IN node.

cli-idempotent-retract-assert-return-zer.text: `retract` on an already-OUT node and `assert` on an already-IN node both return exit code 0 with informational messages rather than an error.

cli-idempotent-transitions-are-success.text: Retracting an already-OUT node or asserting an already-IN node exits `0` and prints `"already OUT"` or `"already IN"` respectively.

cli-init-requires-force-to-overwrite.text: A second `init` without `--force` exits `1` and writes stderr containing `"--force"`.

cli-init-requires-force-to-overwrite-db.text: The CLI `init` command refuses to overwrite an existing database unless `--force` is supplied.

cli-is-deterministic-and-stream-correct.text: The CLI achieves full scriptability through three deterministic properties: flat dict dispatch with no dynamic plugin resolution, binary exit codes (0 success, 1 error) with no ambiguous intermediate codes, and clean stream separation (diagnostics to stderr, results to stdout)

justifications.label: Three independent CLI interface properties — dispatch determinism, exit code simplicity, and stream correctness — combine into full scriptability: shell scripts can dispatch, check status, and parse output without heuristics

cli-is-pure-delegation-layer.text: The CLI is a pure delegation layer: every handler dispatches through a flat dict lookup to API functions with no business logic, producing binary exit codes and correct stream separation — a complete separation of formatting from computation.

justifications.label: Pure delegation holds for all handlers except cmd_propagate, which bypasses the API and goes directly to Storage/Network

cli-is-pure-formatter.text: Every cmd_* function delegates to api.* and only formats the returned dict for terminal output; no business logic lives in the CLI layer.

cli-is-verified-end-to-end.text: The CLI is verified through hermetic end-to-end integration tests (isolated databases per test, full argv-parsing pipeline, deterministic stream-correct output) — unless cmd_propagate bypasses the API layer, leaving one code path's safety guarantees unverifiable through the standard integration testing harness.

justifications.label: Deterministic CLI behavior (depth-1) combined with hermetic test isolation (depth-0) provides end-to-end verification — except for the one handler that skips the API layer entirely

cli-is-verified-pure-delegation.text: The CLI is both structurally pure (every handler delegates to API functions with no business logic) and end-to-end verified (hermetic integration tests confirm delegation produces correct output through the full argv-parsing pipeline).

justifications.label: Structural purity guarantees the CLI adds no behavior; verification confirms this guarantee holds in practice — together they establish the CLI as a trustworthy transparent interface layer.

cli-json-parse-fails-open.text: `_parse_cli_json` returns raw output on any JSON parse failure, ensuring callers always receive a string response.

cli-main-does-not-catch-handler-exceptio.text: `main` does not wrap the `cmd_*` dispatch in try/except, so uncaught handler exceptions propagate as tracebacks and exit code 1.

cli-no-op-cases-exit-zero.text: No-op cases such as already OUT, already IN, no nodes, and no matching nodes print informative messages and return exit code 0 rather than raising errors.

cli-no-subcommand-prints-help-and-exits-.text: When `reasons` is invoked without a subcommand, `main` prints help to stdout and calls `sys.exit(1)`.

cli-output-is-plain-text-not-json.text: CLI command handlers format returned result dicts as plain text for terminal output rather than JSON.

cli-parse-visible-to-returns-none-when-a.text: _parse_visible_to returns None rather than an empty list when --visible-to is absent, and the API layer interprets None as no access control.

cli-parser-and-dispatch-table-are-parall.text: The argparse subcommand registrations and the `commands` dispatch dict are maintained manually in parallel; an out-of-sync command causes `KeyError` at dispatch or dead parser code.

cli-plan-review-apply-pattern.text: Several commands (`derive`, `deduplicate`, `contradictions`) follow a three-phase workflow: (1) generate proposals to a file, (2) human reviews/edits the file, (3) `--accept FILE` parses and applies the reviewed plan — with `--auto` collapsing all three phases

cli-read-commands-enforce-visible-to.text: The `status`, `show`, `explain`, `trace`, and `trace-access-tags` CLI commands enforce `--visible-to`; denied reads exit `1` with `"Access denied"`.

cli-remove-justification-tested-via-subp.text: the CLI test invokes `uv run reasons ... remove-justification <node> <index>` and asserts stdout contains `"Removed justification 0"`.

cli-report-gated-splits-report-and-summa.text: The default CLI writes the Markdown report to stdout and a `blocker(s)` summary to stderr.

cli-report-timestamps-strip-colons.text: Report files written by the CLI use ISO timestamps with colons stripped (for example `T105808`) for filesystem safety.

cli-resolver-rejects-api-vertex-prefixes.text: `resolve_model_cmd` handles only CLI backends and raises `ValueError` for `api:`/`vertex:` model strings, naming both API prefixes in the error.

cli-runner-catches-systemexit.text: `run_cli` catches `SystemExit` from `reasons.cli.main` and returns its exit code with captured stdout/stderr.

cli-search-sources-supports-text-and-jso.text: `cmd_search_sources` emits either text or JSON depending on `args.format`.

cli-search-sources-text-reports-no-match.text: In text mode, zero results print a message containing `"No matching chunks"`.

cli-show-omits-source-type-line-when-abs.text: `cmd_show` omits the `Source type:` line when the node has no `source_type` metadata.

cli-sqlite-only-commands-exist.text: Commands `derive`, `ask`, `review-beliefs`, `deduplicate`, and `contradictions` are guarded by `_require_sqlite()` and exit with an error if `--pg` is set — they do not support PostgreSQL

cli-sqlite-only-commands-guard-before-ap.text: CLI commands marked SQLite-only call `_require_sqlite` and exit with status 1 before any API call when PostgreSQL is configured.

cli-stream-discipline-separates-payload-.text: CLI user payload is written to `stdout`, while diagnostics, warnings, progress, and cost summaries go to `stderr` so commands remain pipeable.

cli-tests-are-black-box-integration.text: All CLI tests invoke `main()` through the full argv-parsing pipeline via the `run_cli` harness rather than calling internal APIs, with one exception (`TestPropagateWithChanges` directly mutates storage to create inconsistent state).

cli-tests-patch-sys-argv-not-subprocess.text: CLI integration tests simulate invocations by patching `sys.argv`, `sys.stdout`, and `sys.stderr` in-process (capturing `SystemExit`), testing only the Python entry point and not the installed script's shebang or shell integration.

cli-tests-set-up-networks-via-chained-cl.text: CLI tests build belief networks by sequentially calling `run_cli("init", ...)`, `run_cli("add", ...)`, and similar commands rather than constructing synthetic database states.

cli-tests-treat-human-readable-output-as.text: CLI tests assert on human-readable output substrings such as `Added a [IN]`, `Went OUT`, and `already IN`, treating CLI output copy as part of the tested API.

cli-tests-use-real-temporary-sqlite-db.text: Every DB-backed test uses a real SQLite file under pytest’s `tmp_path`, created either by `run_cli("init")` or by `TestProposalLifecycle`’s fixture.

cli-threads-db-path-through-api.text: Every CLI command handler threads args.db through to the API, with args.db defaulting to api.DEFAULT_DB.

cli-topics-json-output-is-parseable-json.text: Running `reasons topics --json` must emit stdout that `json.loads` can parse and that contains `topics` and `total_nodes`.

cli-update-errors-without-text-or-source.text: The CLI `update` command returns an error when neither a text nor a source flag is provided.

cli-uses-lazy-imports-for-heavy-modules.text: `asyncio`, `derive`, `ask`, and `Storage` are imported inside function bodies rather than at module level, keeping `reasons --help` fast.

cli-uses-relative-api-import.text: `reasons/cli.py` imports its API via `from . import api`, which is why the same module works unchanged behind the `reasons_lib` shim.

cli-version-requires-installed-ftl-reaso.text: `main` evaluates `importlib.metadata.version("ftl-reasons")` eagerly while building the parser, so a missing package distribution raises `PackageNotFoundError` before help or version handling.

cli-warns-on-three-premise-sl-without-an.text: The CLI warns at add time when an SL justification has 3 or more premises and --any was not used.

cli-what-if-does-not-persist-changes.text: CLI `what-if` tests verify that cascade simulation runs without persisting changes and that output contains `NOT modified`.

cli-what-if-never-modifies-database.text: cmd_what_if is read-only and never modifies the database; its output explicitly states (database NOT modified).

cli-what-if-outputs-not-modified.text: The CLI `what-if` command prints `NOT modified` and does not change network state.

closed-loop-is-origin-agnostic.text: The minimality-sustained closed maintenance loop operates identically across all belief origins — external beliefs achieve full integration parity within the same forward-computation and backward-revision cycle as internally-derived beliefs, making the maintenance loop source-agnostic.

justifications.label: integration parity means external beliefs participate identically in the closed loop

closed-loop-preserves-all-invariants.text: The closed revision-and-lifecycle maintenance loop not only sustains belief consistency but preserves all system invariants through architecturally grounded enforcement — the loop is both self-maintaining and invariant-preserving.

justifications.label: the closed loop inherits invariant preservation from its architectural grounding

cloud-run-mcp-server-exposes-search-show.text: The Cloud Run FastAPI MCP server exposes search, show, explain, list_topics, and get_topic tools.

cloud-run-mcp-server-is-read-side-sharin.text: The Cloud Run MCP server handles the read side and shares network.json with the GCE builder via GCS.

cloud-run-mcp-server-loads-network-json-.text: The Cloud Run MCP server loads network.json from GCS on cold start and caches it in memory.

cloud-run-mcp-server-uses-streamable-htt.text: The Cloud Run MCP server uses Streamable HTTP transport rather than SSE.

cloud-run-scales-to-zero-with-no-idle-co.text: Cloud Run scales to zero and incurs no cost when idle.

cluster-and-sample-are-mutually-exclusiv.text: The `--cluster` and `--sample` flags in `cmd_derive` are mutually exclusive, enforced with an explicit check and `sys.exit(1)` — they represent competing strategies for belief subset selection.

cluster-auto-k-caps-by-budget-thirds.text: `cluster_beliefs` and `cluster_beliefs_intra` use `max_k=min(budget // 3, 20)` for auto-k, while `list_clusters` uses the default `max_k=20`.

cluster-auto-k-floors-at-two.text: `_auto_k` always returns at least 2 clusters (when auto-computed), ensuring cross-domain sampling is meaningful even for small belief sets

cluster-auto-k-heuristic.text: Auto cluster count is computed as `len(beliefs) // 5`, clamped between 2 and `min(budget // 3, 20)`, targeting approximately 5 beliefs per cluster with at least 3 beliefs per cluster given the budget.

cluster-auto-k-is-n-beliefs-div-five-cla.text: `_auto_k` computes the cluster count as `n_beliefs // 5`, clamped to `[2, max_k]`, and `cluster_beliefs` further constrains `max_k` to `budget // 3`.

cluster-beliefs-deterministic-with-seed.text: Given the same beliefs dict, budget, and seed, `cluster_beliefs` produces identical output across calls.

cluster-beliefs-honors-explicit-n-cluste.text: When `n_clusters` is passed to `cluster_beliefs`, the returned `stats['n_clusters']` matches the requested value exactly.

cluster-beliefs-respects-budget.text: `cluster_beliefs` never returns more IDs than the `budget` parameter; each cluster's allocation is individually capped by `min(alloc, len(members))`.

cluster-beliefs-returns-exact-budget.text: `cluster_beliefs` returns exactly `budget` belief IDs when the input set is larger than the budget, and all items when the input set is smaller.

cluster-beliefs-returns-exactly-budget.text: When `0 < budget < len(beliefs)`, `cluster_beliefs` returns exactly `budget` ids, not at most `budget`.

cluster-beliefs-returns-selected-ids-and.text: `cluster_beliefs` returns `(selected_ids, cluster_stats)`, where `cluster_stats` includes cluster count, sizes, and model name.

cluster-budget-cap-can-underselect.text: `cluster_beliefs` caps each cluster’s allocation at cluster size and does not redistribute unused slots, so it can return fewer than `budget` IDs.

cluster-budget-is-hard-ceiling.text: `cluster_beliefs` never returns more than `budget` belief IDs; when the belief set is smaller than budget, it returns all beliefs without clustering

cluster-cache-embed-returns-ids-and-embe.text: `ClusterCache.embed(beliefs)` returns a tuple of belief IDs and their embeddings.

cluster-cache-is-not-thread-safe.text: `ClusterCache._cache` is a plain Python dict with no locking; concurrent `embed()` calls on the same cache instance may double-encode or observe inconsistent intermediate state, relying on the derive pipeline being single-threaded.

cluster-cache-key-includes-text-hash.text: `ClusterCache` keys embeddings by `(node_id, sha256(text)[:16])`, so modified belief text invalidates the cached embedding without requiring explicit cache eviction

cluster-cache-keys-include-content-hash.text: `ClusterCache` keys embeddings by `(node_id, sha256_prefix)`, so editing a belief's text with the same ID forces re-embedding rather than serving stale vectors.

cluster-cache-keys-on-node-id-and-text-h.text: `ClusterCache.embed` invalidates cached embeddings when belief text changes by keying entries on `(node_id, sha256(text)[:16])`.

cluster-cache-no-recompute.text: `ClusterCache.embed()` does not recompute embeddings for previously cached belief texts; cache size stays constant on repeated calls with the same input and grows by exactly the count of new texts on superset calls.

cluster-default-model-is-all-minilm-l6-v.text: The default sentence-transformer model used by `cluster.py` is `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`.
