complete-unified-system-is-production-re.text: The fully unified minimal-dialectical-scalable system with end-to-end integrity is production-ready — all mutations produce correct state, all revision is reliable, all extensions compose safely — but only when every known fragility and bug is resolved.

justifications.label: The positive claim is the system's grand thesis; the negatives are every known defect — any one of them breaks the production-readiness guarantee, creating a punch list for hardening

completeness-and-minimality-are-unified.text: The reasoning-and-revision architecture achieves completeness through minimality rather than despite it — both forward truth computation and backward belief revision derive from the same small set of primitives (outlist, disjunctive truth, vacuous validity), so completeness requires no feature accumulation beyond what minimality already provides.

justifications.label: shared minimal foundations make completeness and minimality co-entailing (depth-5 from two depth-4 IN)

completeness-determinism-and-minimality-.text: The reasoning-and-revision architecture achieves completeness through minimality, and that same minimality produces operational determinism — completeness and determinism are not independently established but co-derived from shared minimal foundations: uniform outlist primitives simultaneously enable complete revision coverage and deterministic evaluation, revealing a single architectural root for both properties.

justifications.label: Both trace to the same minimal primitives (outlist/disjunction); combining reveals completeness and determinism share a single generative origin

compute-changes-emits-deletions-for-miss.text: `compute_changes()` emits a `node_changed` event with `new_truth_value=None` when a node exists in `before` but is absent from `after`.

compute-changes-emits-node-changed-for-a.text: `compute_changes(before, after, db_path)` returns `ChangeEvent(type="node_changed")` for added, deleted, and truth-value-changed nodes, while skipping unchanged nodes.
Modifications, additions, and removals are all emitted as `ChangeEvent(type="node_changed")`; removals use `new_truth_value=None`.

compute-changes-is-pure-diff.text: `compute_changes` compares in-memory `before`/`after` dictionaries and does not read or write SQLite.

compute-changes-is-pure-memory-diff.text: `compute_changes(before, after, db_path)` only compares in-memory `node_id -> truth_value` dictionaries and performs no SQLite or live-network I/O.

compute-changes-produces-node-changed-ev.text: `compute_changes` returns `ChangeEvent` objects with `type="node_changed"` for added, deleted, and modified nodes, skipping unchanged entries.

compute-depth-cycle-guard-is-memo-placeh.text: An in-progress node is temporarily memoized as `0`, preventing infinite recursion but producing traversal-dependent depths for cyclic graphs.

compute-depth-cycle-guard-uses-zero-plac.text: `_compute_depth` temporarily memoizes an in-progress node as `0`, preventing infinite recursion but producing traversal-dependent depths for cyclic graphs.

compute-depth-max-over-all-justification.text: For a node with multiple justifications, `_compute_depth` returns `1 +` the maximum antecedent depth across all justifications.

compute-depth-missing-or-premise-returns.text: `_compute_depth` returns `0` for a missing node and for a node with absent or empty `justifications`.

compute-depth-mutates-shared-memo.text: The optional `memo` mapping is populated with computed values and reused across recursive and top-level calls.

compute-depth-propagates-malformed-struc.text: Malformed node or justification structures can raise `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, or `RecursionError`; the helper itself does not catch them.

compute-depth-returns-zero-for-missing-n.text: A missing `node_id` and a node with absent or empty `"justifications"` both return depth `0`.

compute-depth-uses-max-across-all-justif.text: For a node with multiple justifications, the returned depth is `1 +` the maximum antecedent depth across all justifications.

config-resolution-collects-all-missing-v.text: `_resolve_config` accumulates all missing configuration values (URL, agent_id, api_key) into a single `RuntimeError` message rather than failing on the first absent variable, so a misconfigured deployment reports every gap in one shot.

config-resolution-prefers-explicit-param.text: `_resolve_config` gives explicit function arguments precedence over `MIND_*` environment variables.

conftest-fixtures-are-auto-injected.text: The `pg_api` fixture is exposed to all test modules under `tests/` without any explicit `import`, via pytest's conftest auto-discovery.

console-entry-points-map-to-cli-and-mcp-.text: The `reasons` console entry point maps to `reasons.cli:main`, and the `reasons-mcp` entry point maps to the MCP server module.

content-changed-populates-source-path-st.text: A `content_changed` result sets `source_path` to the resolved file path as a string, unlike `source_deleted` which leaves it `None`.

content-hash-folds-antecedent-text-hashe.text: A justification's `content_hash` incorporates the `text_hash` of every antecedent node, so changing an antecedent's text (even with a consistently-updated `text_hash`) invalidates the dependent's `content_hash` — this is the Merkle-tree property that distinguishes chain mutations from text mutations.

content-iteration-extracts-text-attribut.text: `_call_tool_async` iterates `result.content`, appends `content.text` for blocks that have it, and falls back to `str(content)` otherwise

context-agnosticism-follows-from-minimal.text: Context-agnostic evaluation — producing identical results regardless of evaluation timing, attachment history, or structural origin — is a consequence of semantic minimality with operational determinism: because truth evaluation derives from uniform minimal rules with deterministic pure evaluation, it naturally cannot distinguish between contexts.

justifications.label: Context-agnostic evaluation + semantic minimality → agnosticism as minimality consequence

contradiction-batch-failure-is-isolated-.text: A `RuntimeError` raised during one batch in `detect_contradictions` is caught locally and does not prevent remaining batches from executing; results from the failed batch are simply absent from the aggregated output.

contradiction-batch-failure-is-silent-sk.text: A per-batch LLM failure (timeout, API error, network blip) in contradiction detection is caught by a bare `except Exception`, logged to stderr, and the loop continues to the next batch — there is no retry logic and the function returns partial results.

contradiction-batching-splits-in-beliefs.text: detect_contradictions with 3 IN beliefs and batch_size=2 makes exactly 2 LLM calls.

contradiction-detection-batches-by-const.text: detect_contradictions splits IN-only beliefs into batches of CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE and sends each batch as an independent LLM call.

contradiction-detection-batches-fifty-in.text: `detect_contradictions` sends IN beliefs to the LLM in batches of 50 (`CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE`), requesting NOGOOD sets of ≥2 mutually incompatible beliefs

contradiction-detection-filters-out-node.text: `detect_contradictions` and `detect_contradictions_semantic` both exclude OUT-truth-value nodes before sending any prompt to the LLM, even if those node IDs are explicitly requested in the `belief_ids` parameter.

contradiction-detection-honors-batch-siz.text: `detect_contradictions` uses `batch_size` to determine the number of LLM calls; three IN beliefs with `batch_size=2` trigger two `subprocess.run` calls.

contradiction-detector-checks-in-beliefs.text: The contradiction detector in `reasons/contradictions.py` filters the input to only beliefs with `truth_value == "IN"` before any LLM call; both `detect_contradictions` and `detect_contradictions_semantic` enforce this at entry.

contradiction-dry-run-overrides-auto-app.text: When both `--dry-run` and `--auto-apply` are passed to the `contradictions` CLI subcommand, no nogoods are recorded in the database (applied count is 0).

contradiction-format-skips-missing-node-.text: `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check` silently skips requested node IDs that are missing from the node dict.

contradiction-in-only-filter.text: `detect_contradictions` excludes OUT nodes from LLM prompts even when explicitly listed in `belief_ids`.

contradiction-lazy-imports-break-circula.text: `reasons/contradictions.py` imports `write_contradiction_plan` (from `.api`) and `list_clusters` (from `.cluster`) inside function bodies rather than at module top-level, preventing a `contradictions → api → contradictions` circular import and deferring sentence-transformers loading.

contradiction-management-is-complete-and.text: The system provides complete contradiction management: the revision pipeline reliably resolves contradictions through outlist defeat and dependency-directed backtracking with guaranteed termination, while nogood resolution maintains a consistent referenceable history of all detected contradictions — enabling both automated resolution and post-hoc forensic analysis of belief conflicts.

justifications.label: Reliable automated resolution combined with consistent historical records yields a contradiction management system that is both operationally complete and analytically traceable

contradiction-min-two-claims.text: `parse_contradiction_response` drops any nogood with fewer than 2 valid claim IDs; this is enforced both before and after `valid_ids` filtering.

contradiction-parser-does-not-raise.text: `parse_contradiction_response` never raises for malformed or non-matching LLM output; it simply yields no proposal entries unless well-formed `### NOGOOD` blocks survive parsing.

contradiction-parser-rejects-hallucinate.text: `parse_contradiction_response` threads a `valid_ids` set through the regex parser to discard any claim ID not present in the input nodes, and drops any nogood that has fewer than 2 surviving claims after filtering.

contradiction-parser-returns-empty-on-ma.text: If an LLM contradiction response lacks `### NOGOOD` headers, parse_contradiction_response returns an empty list.

contradiction-plan-append-does-not-dupli.text: Calling `api.write_contradiction_plan` with `append=True` must not repeat the `# Contradiction Plan` header; subsequent appends add `[APPLY]`/`[SKIP]` entries only, preserving plan-file integrity across multiple detection runs.

contradiction-plan-claims-must-not-conta.text: Claims written to a contradiction plan must not contain commas because `parse_contradiction_plan` splits the `- Claims:` line on commas.

contradiction-plan-defaults-entries-to-a.text: `write_contradiction_plan` emits every contradiction block with `[APPLY]`; excluding an entry requires editing it to `[SKIP]` or deleting the block.

contradiction-plan-does-not-create-paren.text: `write_contradiction_plan` opens the output path directly and never creates parent directories, so a missing parent raises `FileNotFoundError`.

contradiction-plan-has-no-input-validati.text: `write_contradiction_plan` performs no validation of required fields or types; missing `id`/`claims` raises `KeyError`, and non-string claims raise `TypeError`.

contradiction-plan-id-must-not-contain-w.text: Contradiction IDs written to a plan must not contain whitespace because `parse_contradiction_plan` matches `NOGOOD` followed by `(\S+)`.

contradiction-plan-round-trips-apply-ent.text: Writing a contradiction plan with `write_contradiction_plan` and parsing it back with `parse_contradiction_plan` preserves all `[APPLY]`-tagged NOGOOD entries with their IDs and claims, while discarding `[SKIP]`-tagged entries — enabling a human review workflow.

contradiction-prompt-truncates-belief-te.text: `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check` caps each belief's rendered text to 200 characters followed by `"..."` to keep LLM prompt size bounded regardless of individual belief length, and silently skips IDs not present in the node map.

contradiction-resolution-achieves-minima.text: Contradiction resolution simultaneously achieves minimal disruption (least-entrenched culprit selection with surgical recovery hints targeting only cascade victims) and complete effect propagation (retraction cascades transitively through all dependent nodes with guaranteed termination) — the system minimizes blast radius while ensuring no node escapes the cascade.

justifications.label: Minimal-disruption culprit selection feeds into transitive terminating cascades

contradiction-resolution-is-lifecycle-sa.text: When contradictions are detected, the entire resolution pipeline respects node lifecycle: backtracking identifies the least-entrenched culprit premise deterministically, retraction cascades through BFS propagation that skips retracted nodes and stops on unchanged truth values, ensuring resolution terminates without disturbing lifecycle-inert nodes.

justifications.label: Deterministic culprit identification feeds into lifecycle-aware propagation — resolution never touches retracted nodes and always terminates

contradiction-resolution-is-minimal-disr.text: The nogood resolution system minimizes network disruption through layered heuristics: the primary path traces justification chains back to premises and selects the least-entrenched for retraction, the fallback uses dependent count when no traceable chain exists, and all contradictions are unconditionally recorded regardless of resolution outcome.

justifications.label: Groups the four nogood-resolution base beliefs into a single characterization: layered heuristics that always prefer minimal disruption with complete audit trails

contradiction-resolution-is-traceable-an.text: Contradiction resolution provides complete operational support along two independent dimensions: it minimizes disruption with guided recovery (least-entrenched culprit selection plus surgical restoration hints for cascade victims), AND creates consistently identifiable artifacts (nogoods with durable collision-free IDs, challenge nodes with deterministic auto-IDs), enabling both forensic root-cause analysis and practical guided recovery.

justifications.label: Identifiable artifacts enable tracing what went wrong; recovery guidance enables fixing it — together they provide full contradiction management support

contradiction-resolution-minimizes-disru.text: Contradiction resolution achieves both minimal impact and guided recovery: dependency-directed backtracking selects the least-entrenched culprit premise to minimize the retraction cascade, while restoration hints identify specific cascade victims that have surviving alternative premises — providing a complete resolve-and-recover pipeline

justifications.label: Minimal disruption limits the blast radius of contradiction resolution, and surgical hints provide targeted recovery paths for the affected nodes — the combination means contradictions are resolved with the smallest possible damage and the clearest possible repair instructions

contradiction-semantic-variant-clusters-.text: detect_contradictions_semantic uses embedding-based clustering to group related beliefs before sending them to the LLM.

contradiction-strategies-share-core-diff.text: `detect_contradictions` and `detect_contradictions_semantic` share the same `CONTRADICTION_PROMPT`, `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check`, `parse_contradiction_response`, and `_flush_results`; they differ only in how beliefs are grouped into batches (random shuffle vs. semantic clusters from sentence-transformers).

contradiction-timeout-parameter-passes-t.text: The timeout parameter to detect_contradictions is passed through to the LLM subprocess call.

contradiction-triggers-deterministic-res.text: When contradictions are detected, resolution and propagation form a deterministic pipeline: backtracking identifies the least-entrenched culprit premise, retraction triggers BFS propagation that terminates via stop-on-unchanged, producing a new consistent state with minimal network disruption and guaranteed convergence.

justifications.label: depth-2 — contradiction resolution selects what to retract (minimal disruption), propagation determines how to settle (deterministic termination); the pipeline composition is the emergent property

contradiction-valid-id-filter-is-global.text: `detect_contradictions` builds `valid_ids` from the full candidate set, not from the current batch, so hallucinated-ID filtering is global across all batches.

contradictions-batch-size-is-50.text: `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` is set to 50, the default number of beliefs sent per LLM contradiction-detection call.

contradictions-batches-50-beliefs-review.text: The contradictions command batches 50 beliefs per LLM call, while review-beliefs batches 20 beliefs with antecedent context.

contradictions-belief-text-truncated-at-.text: `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check` truncates each belief's text at 200 characters in the LLM prompt to avoid blowing context windows on large belief descriptions

contradictions-cli-output-writes-markdow.text: The `reasons contradictions --output` flag writes a markdown report file with proper headers.

contradictions-cross-batch-pairs-undetec.text: Batch boundaries are non-overlapping — each belief appears in exactly one batch per run — so contradictions between beliefs in different batches cannot be detected in a single run.

contradictions-default-batch-size-50.text: `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` defaults to 50 beliefs per LLM call.

contradictions-detects-only-in-beliefs.text: Both `detect_contradictions` and `detect_contradictions_semantic` filter candidate beliefs to nodes whose `truth_value == "IN"` before any LLM call.

contradictions-first-run-checked-526-in-.text: The first live run of reasons contradictions checked all 526 IN beliefs in the ftl-reasons-expert network.

contradictions-first-run-found-8-contrad.text: The first live run of reasons contradictions found 8 contradictions.

contradictions-first-run-retracted-4-bel.text: The first contradictions run retracted 4 beliefs directly.

contradictions-flush-results-incremental.text: Both contradiction detection strategies flush results after each batch via `api.write_contradiction_plan`, using `header_written` to toggle between write-new-file and append modes.

contradictions-format-truncates-text-200.text: `format_beliefs_for_contradiction_check` truncates each belief's text at 200 characters and skips IDs that do not exist in the nodes mapping.

contradictions-medium-severity-findings-.text: The 4 medium-severity contradictions in the first run were filed as issues #100, #101, and #102.

contradictions-min-two-claims-per-nogood.text: The contradiction parser enforces that every returned nogood has at least 2 valid claim IDs; single-claim or empty results are silently dropped.

contradictions-no-storage-dependency.text: `contradictions.py` operates on in-memory node dicts and has no import of `storage.py` or any database layer, making it testable in full isolation.

contradictions-only-checks-in-beliefs.text: `detect_contradictions` filters all input to `truth_value == "IN"` before processing; OUT beliefs are never sent to the LLM for contradiction checking.

contradictions-parser-extracts-nogood-bl.text: `parse_contradiction_response` uses `_NOGOOD_PATTERN` to find `### NOGOOD <id>` blocks and line-parses Claims, Analysis, and Severity fields.

contradictions-prompt-defines-four-contr.text: `CONTRADICTION_PROMPT` defines four contradiction types: direct negation, incompatible properties, scope conflict, and quantitative mismatch.

contradictions-prompt-defines-four-types.text: `CONTRADICTION_PROMPT` defines four contradiction types: direct negation, incompatible properties, scope conflict, and quantitative mismatch.

contradictions-prompt-excludes-tensions.text: The contradiction prompt instructs the LLM not to flag tensions or tradeoffs, only genuine logical incompatibilities.

contradictions-requires-2-claims-per-nog.text: A nogood is only retained when its parsed `claims` list has length ≥ 2, mirroring the prompt's minimum-2 rule.

contradictions-scope-all-in-beliefs-revi.text: The contradictions command checks all IN beliefs, whereas review-beliefs checks only derived beliefs.

contradictions-semantic-has-fixed-batch-.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` does not accept a `batch_size` parameter and always chunks clusters at `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` (50).

contradictions-semantic-skips-singleton-.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` skips any cluster containing fewer than 2 beliefs, since no pairwise contradiction is possible within a singleton

contradictions-semantic-sub-batches-larg.text: `detect_contradictions_semantic` further sub-batches large clusters at `CONTRADICTION_BATCH_SIZE` after clustering.

contradictions-shim-docstring-differs-fr.text: `reasons_lib.contradictions.__doc__` is the shim migration text, not the canonical `reasons.contradictions` docstring.

contradictions-shim-lacks-own-all.text: `reasons_lib.contradictions` does not define `__all__`, so accessing `reasons_lib.contradictions.__all__` raises `AttributeError` even if `reasons.contradictions.__all__` exists.

contradictions-shuffle-prevents-determin.text: Belief IDs are randomly shuffled before batching so that repeated runs cover different pairwise combinations across batch boundaries, increasing cross-batch contradiction coverage.

contradictions-shuffles-before-batching.text: The `contradictions` command randomly shuffles all IN beliefs before partitioning into batches of 50, ensuring that repeated runs probabilistically cover cross-belief comparisons that fixed sequential batching would never surface.

contradictions-swallows-batch-errors.text: Duplicates the existing system-wide belief `batch-fault-isolation-is-universal-across-llm-operations` which already covers per-batch error containment across all LLM-facing modules.

contradictions-swallows-batch-llm-failur.text: `invoke_model` errors are caught per batch, logged as `WARN: …` to stderr, and do not abort the loop — the function always returns a list.

convergence-produces-evaluation-invarian.text: The system converges to equilibrium states where truth evaluation is transformation-invariant: regardless of the mutation path taken — order of additions, retractions, challenges, imports — the converged state evaluates all beliefs identically, because autonomous convergence reaches deterministic stable states and truth evaluation is agnostic to both temporal context and structural origin.

justifications.label: Autonomous convergence (depth-6) reaching deterministic equilibria combined with transformation-invariant evaluation (depth-6) means the final state is path-independent

convergence-trajectories-are-permanently.text: Every convergence trajectory toward an evaluation-invariant equilibrium — deterministic in path and consistently identifiable in its artifacts — is backed by a permanent, comprehensive audit trail covering all self-corrections along that trajectory, ensuring complete retrospective analysis of how the system reached any given stable state

justifications.label: Deterministic referenceable trajectories (depth-8) combined with permanent audit trails (depth-9) provide complete path-level documentation of every convergence sequence

convergent-equilibria-are-documented-and.text: The system's convergent equilibria are simultaneously trajectory-documented (every path to equilibrium generates deterministic identifiable artifacts with negation-transparent final states) and indefinitely auditable (every invariant in the equilibrium state is independently verifiable without temporal degradation), providing complete operational transparency across both the convergence journey and the resulting stable state.

justifications.label: Two depth-13 conclusions from distinct derivation chains combine: documented trajectories explain how equilibria are reached while indefinite auditability verifies what is preserved — covering both the dynamic path and the static result

convergent-equilibria-have-complete-prop.text: System convergence to evaluation-invariant equilibria achieves complete propagation fidelity — every truth change cascades to every transitively dependent node including outlist dependents — and topology preservation covers all reference types, provided the dependency tracking assumption holds.

justifications.label: Convergence + topology preservation achieves full propagation fidelity only when the dependents index is complete

convert-to-premise-preserves-dependents-.text: Converting a derived node to a premise correctly maintains the dependents index by removing the node from former antecedents' dependents sets — the same invariant maintained by every other network mutation.

justifications.label: Premise conversion honors the universal dependents-index maintenance contract

convert-to-premise-removes-dependents.text: When a derived node is converted to a premise via `convert_to_premise`, it is removed from its former antecedents' `dependents` sets because the old justification edges are deleted.

convert-to-premise-removes-reverse-depen.text: After `convert_to_premise("b")`, `"b"` is no longer present in its former antecedents’ `dependents` sets.

convert-to-premise-strips-justifications.text: The convert_to_premise method strips all justifications from a derived node, turning it into an unconditional premise.

core-dependencies-are-empty.text: The base distribution declares `dependencies = []`, so `pip install ftl-reasons` pulls in zero third-party packages and all extras must be lazily imported.

core-propagation-is-synchronous-single-p.text: TMS truth propagation is synchronous within a single process; the core inference engine has no event bus, no microservice boundary, and no async dispatch — all cascade effects resolve in-process before the calling operation returns.

corrections-span-all-origins-with-full-a.text: Every correction mechanism — intentional dialectical challenge/defend and automated contradiction resolution — is both reliable and fully auditable with traceable history, and this complete correction coverage spans all belief origins (human, LLM, agent) — no belief from any provenance can undergo an untraced or unreliable correction.

justifications.label: Correction reliability/auditability combined with origin-spanning dispute resolution ensures universal traceable correction regardless of provenance

cost-recording-requires-successful-cli-j.text: `_parse_cli_json` is the only place `_record_cost` is called; malformed or non-conforming CLI JSON returns the raw string and leaves the cost tracker unchanged.

cost-tracking-is-module-level-accumulato.text: LLM cost accounting uses a module-level mutable dict in `reasons/llm.py` with explicit `reset_cost_tracker()` lifecycle — there is no class instance, and all callers share the same accumulator.

cost-tracking-requires-reset-between-sce.text: `_record_cost` accumulates into process-global state that only `reset_cost_tracker()` clears, so tests must reset between assertions.

count-accumulates-linearly.text: Documents the bug fix for issue #23 — already covered by existing `derive-agent-count-bug` which tracks this defect

cp-and-sl-evaluated-identically.text: CP and SL justifications use the same validity check in `_justification_valid`; the distinction is semantic (support vs. consistency), not computational.

cp-equals-sl.text: CP (conditional-proof) justifications are evaluated with the exact same logic as SL justifications, despite being a distinct type in Doyle's TMS — either an intentional simplification or incomplete implementation

cp-justifications-represent-consistency-.text: CP justifications allow deriving conclusions from hypothetical assumptions that have not been contradicted, based on consistency rather than truth.

cp-justifications-use-sl-evaluation-logi.text: CP justifications use SL evaluation logic.

cp-should-differ-from-sl-beyond-current-.text: This is a normative design recommendation, not a factual codebase claim; current observed behavior is already represented by the existing `cp-equals-sl` belief.

create-repo-is-idempotent-on-409.text: A `HTTPError(..., 409, ...)` from the create endpoint is swallowed and the repo id is returned as if creation succeeded.

create-repo-swallows-409.text: `create_repo` treats HTTP 409 as success so it can be called unconditionally before an upload.

created-at-is-immutable-across-mutations.text: Once `created_at` is set in `network_meta`, adding nodes or saving the network must not change it.

created-at-is-immutable-across-saves.text: After `api.init_db`, subsequent `api.add_node` calls preserve the original `created_at` value in `network_meta`.

created-at-is-immutable-after-init.text: The `created_at` metadata field is written once at `init_db` time and is never overwritten by subsequent `add_node`, `save`, or other mutations — it is a permanent audit timestamp.

critical-operations-converge-to-fixed-po.text: The system's three critical reconciliation operations are all convergent: agent sync produces no changes on re-run with identical input, dependents index rebuilding yields identical results on repeated execution, and truth recomputation iterates to a fixpoint — ensuring the system reaches stable consistent state regardless of operation ordering.

justifications.label: Three independent convergence properties across sync, index maintenance, and truth computation establish system-wide fixed-point behavior

cross-namespace-refs-skip-prefixing.text: `_resolve_namespace` skips node IDs that already contain `:`, treating them as cross-namespace references — so `alice:some-belief` referenced from Bob's namespace stays `alice:some-belief`, not `bob:alice:some-belief`.

culprit-selection-operates-on-premises.text: The iteration variable at `reasons/pg.py:3316` is `premise_id`, indicating culprits are chosen among support nodes rather than among the nogood's own members.

cycle-fallback-out-satisfies-outlist.text: The entry explicitly says the cycle guard/evaluator was not observed, so it cannot claim that cycle-fallback OUT is consumed by outlist checks as OUT.

cycle-guard-returns-empty-string-hash.text: A back-edge encountered during recursive Merkle computation returns `compute_text_hash("")` rather than raising or reporting a cycle.

cyclic-merkle-hash-depends-on-traversal.text: Because the back-edge is replaced with a constant only while a node is in the current `visiting` set, the resulting hash for a cyclic component depends on traversal/cache order (`reasons/merkle.py:17-47`, `reasons/merkle.py:110-127`).

cyclic-merkle-hash-depends-on-traversal-.text: Because the cycle cut is applied only while a node is in the current `visiting` set, the resulting hash for a cyclic component can depend on traversal and cache order.

dangling-dependent-guard-skips-missing-n.text: `_propagate` skips dependent IDs not present in `net.nodes` rather than raising `KeyError`, and emits a structured warning log entry for each (fix for issue #22).

dangling-dependent-produces-warning-log.text: Encountering a dangling dependent emits a `net.log` entry with `action == "warn"` and `target` equal to the missing ID.

dangling-dependent-regression-tests-targ.text: The dangling-dependent regression tests import from `reasons`, not `reasons_lib`, so they directly guard `reasons.network.Network` but do not directly guard parity with `reasons_lib`.

dangling-dependent-tolerance-spans-all-m.text: The dangling-dependent regression suite verifies tolerance through `retract()`, `assert_node()`, `challenge()`, and `add_justification()`-then-retract flows, so guarding only one propagation entry point is insufficient.

dangling-dependent-warning-once-per-enco.text: Every dangling dependent reference encountered during propagation produces exactly one warning entry in `net.log`.

dangling-dependents-are-safely-contained.text: Dangling dependent references are safely contained across all propagation dimensions: BFS skips missing nodes with structured warnings, the changed set never includes ghost IDs, and the visited set excludes dangling IDs so later-created nodes propagate normally.

justifications.label: Three independent containment mechanisms (skip, exclude from changed, exclude from visited) ensure no dangling reference corrupts propagation state

dangling-dependents-do-not-crash-propaga.text: `Network._propagate()` must skip missing dependent node IDs instead of raising `KeyError`.

dangling-dependents-injected-by-direct-s.text: Dangling-dependent tests inject ghost IDs by directly mutating a node's `dependents` set, such as `net.nodes["a"].dependents.add("ghost")`, rather than through the public API.

dangling-dependents-log-not-crash.text: Covered by existing `propagate-assumes-dependents-exist` (documents the assumption) and `tms-core-is-crash-safe` (documents crash safety)

dangling-dependents-produce-warn-log-ent.text: A `dependents` reference to an unknown node produces exactly one `{"action": "warn"}` log entry with `value` containing `"dangling"` and does not raise.

dangling-guard-covers-challenge-and-add-.text: The dangling-dependent propagation guard also fires when propagation is triggered through `challenge()` and `add_justification()`, not only through `retract()` and `assert_node()`.

dangling-guard-is-continue-not-raise.text: When `_propagate` encounters a dependent ID not in `self.nodes`, it logs a structured warning and continues the BFS loop rather than raising `KeyError` or silently skipping.

dangling-ids-excluded-from-changed.text: The `changed` set returned by `retract()` and `assert_node()` never contains IDs that don't correspond to real nodes in the network.

dangling-ids-excluded-from-visited.text: The propagation visited set does not include dangling IDs, so a formerly-dangling ID that becomes a real node will propagate correctly on subsequent operations.

dangling-ids-not-in-changed-or-visited.text: Dangling IDs are excluded from `changed` and must not prevent a later real node with the same ID from participating in propagation.

dangling-refs-excluded-from-changed-set.text: The `changed` set returned by `retract`/`assert_node` never contains node IDs that don't exist in the network.

dangling-refs-excluded-from-visited-set.text: Dangling dependent IDs are not added to the propagation visited set, so later-created nodes with the same ID propagate normally.

dangling-warning-includes-timestamp.text: Dangling-dependent warning entries in `net.log` include a `timestamp` field.

dangling-warning-value-identifies-parent.text: When a dangling dependent is detected, the warning log entry’s `value` must include the parent node ID whose `dependents` set contained the missing ID.

data-integrity-spans-architecture.text: Data integrity is enforced across all three architectural layers: clean layer boundaries prevent cross-cutting mutations, snapshot persistence ensures atomic state transitions, and conservative staleness checking gates CI pipelines.

justifications.label: Each architectural layer contributes a distinct integrity guarantee that together cover the full stack from data model through persistence to CI

data-model-imports-only-stdlib.text: `reasons/__init__.py` imports exclusively from the standard library (`dataclasses`); no third-party packages are required, ensuring the core data model loads in minimal environments without network or database dependencies.

data-model-omits-post-init-validation.text: The `Node`, `Justification`, and `Nogood` dataclasses in `reasons/__init__.py` deliberately omit `__post_init__` validation to keep construction fast in the hot propagation loop; all validation is deferred to boundary layers (API, persistence).

data-model-uses-string-enums.text: Both `Justification.type` ("SL"/"CP") and `Node.truth_value` ("IN"/"OUT") are plain strings, not Python enums; consumers must validate values themselves as invalid states like `"MAYBE"` or `"XYZ"` are representable.

db-fixture-seeds-five-beliefs-through-ap.text: The `db` fixture creates five nodes in a temporary SQLite database via `reasons.api.add_node`, including a support link from `deploy-ci-pipeline` to `testing-unit-coverage`.

db-resolution-priority-chain.text: The MCP server resolves the database path in strict priority order: `REASONS_DB` environment variable → upward filesystem walk from cwd looking for `reasons.db` → `api.DEFAULT_DB` constant fallback; `main()` accepts no parameters.

dedup-auto-keeps-most-dependents.text: In auto mode, `deduplicate` retains the cluster member with the most dependents and retracts all others

dedup-clusters-by-jaccard-on-ids.text: `deduplicate` clusters beliefs by Jaccard similarity on their IDs.

dedup-is-topology-preserving-and-auditab.text: Deduplication preserves network topology (rewrites both antecedent and outlist references to survivors), selects structurally-optimal survivors (most dependents with lexicographic tiebreak), and supports human oversight (KEEP/RETRACT markers in a user-editable plan format).

justifications.label: Dedup's three design choices unify into safe, auditable graph refactoring

dedup-keeps-most-connected-node.text: In auto-dedup mode, the node with the most dependents survives each cluster; ties break by lexicographic ID, and losers are retracted after dependents are rewired.

dedup-plan-is-user-editable.text: The dedup plan format uses KEEP/RETRACT markers that users can swap before applying, making deduplication decisions reviewable and overridable

dedup-plan-roundtrips-through-write-and-.text: api.write_dedup_plan output can be parsed by api.parse_dedup_plan with round-trip fidelity.

dedup-plan-workflow-is-human-in-the-loop.text: `write_dedup_plan`, `parse_dedup_plan`, and `apply_dedup_plan` implement a human-in-the-loop deduplication workflow via an editable plan file.

dedup-reflects-complete-dependency-graph.text: Deduplication survivor selection accurately reflects the complete dependency graph — the node with the most dependents survives each cluster, and that dependent count includes both antecedent-based and outlist-based dependency edges, ensuring the structurally most-connected node is always preserved.

justifications.label: Topology-preserving auditable dedup with topology-reliable survivor selection should reflect the complete dependency graph, but outlist exclusion from dependents means dependent counts undercount true connectivity

dedup-retains-most-connected.text: Covered by existing belief `belief-replacement-is-topology-safe-and-view-consistent` which states "deduplication rewires all justification references to the most-connected survivor."

dedup-rewrites-before-retracting.text: Both `api.deduplicate(auto=True)` and `api.apply_dedup_plan` rewrite justification antecedents and outlist references to the KEEP node before retracting the duplicates, so dependents whose justifications referenced the retracted id stay IN.

dedup-rewrites-both-antecedents-and-outl.text: When a duplicate is retracted via dedup, all justification references (both antecedent and outlist) across the network are rewritten to point at the kept node

dedup-supersession-cascade-flips-all-sup.text: After `mark_duplicate` or `mark_superseded` succeeds, every node linked via support-link (`sl=`) to the retracted node MUST appear in the returned `changed` list and MUST independently be in `OUT` truth state, guaranteeing no dependent is left in a dangling `IN` state.

dedup-supersession-metadata-persists-in-.text: The `duplicate_of` / `superseded_by` and `retract_reason` metadata written by deduplication and supersession persist and are visible through both `show_node` and `export_network`.

dedup-supersession-require-existing-node.text: Both `mark_duplicate` and `mark_superseded` require all referenced node IDs to exist; a missing source/canonical or old/new ID raises `KeyError` whose message matches `"not found"`.

dedup-supersession-retract-reasons-are-d.text: `mark_duplicate` writes a retract reason of the form `"Duplicate of <canonical-id>"`, and `mark_superseded` writes `"Superseded by <new-id>"`.

dedup-supersession-self-reference-valida.text: Self-reference in `mark_duplicate` or `mark_superseded` raises `ValueError` and leaves the node unchanged in `IN`, proving validation occurs before mutation.

dedup-survivor-selection-is-topology-rel.text: Deduplication reliably selects the structurally-optimal survivor in each duplicate cluster by choosing the node with the most dependents, and this selection is correct because the dependents index accurately reflects the justification graph.

justifications.label: Dependent-count-based survivor selection is only reliable when the dependents index is trustworthy

dedup-survivor-selection-is-topology-rel.text: In auto-dedup mode, the survivor in each duplicate cluster is the node with the most dependents (ties broken by lexicographic ID), and upon retraction all justification references—both antecedent and outlist—are rewritten to point at the kept node. The dependents count thus serves as the selection criterion, though the antecedents describe this mechanism without establishing that it yields the structurally-optimal choice.

deduplicate-clusters-by-id-token-jaccard.text: `deduplicate` uses Jaccard similarity on ID tokens to cluster similar beliefs and rewires dependents before retracting duplicates.

deduplicate-clusters-by-jaccard-id-token.text: `deduplicate()` clusters IN beliefs by Jaccard similarity on ID tokens and uses union-find to group similar IDs.

deduplicate-clusters-jaccard-similar-bel.text: api.deduplicate finds clusters of belief IDs that are Jaccard-similar.

deduplication-and-supersession-cascade-t.text: Dependents created with `sl=<source-id>` are listed in `result["changed"]` and become `OUT`.

deep-derivations-accumulate-generalizati.text: Derived beliefs at depth 8-15 accumulate generalization error through successive scope expansion at each derivation step — individually reasonable generalizations compound into conclusions unsupported by original premises, with retracting one invalid belief at depth 8 cascading 52 dependents OUT.

default-defeater-id-follows-pattern.text: When `defeater_id` is omitted, the generated ID is `"{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{justification_index}"`.

default-license-is-mit.text: Calling `export_card()` without `license=` emits `license: mit` in the frontmatter.

default-org-is-eem-hub.text: Bare repo names are namespaced under `EEM-Hub` unless `REASONS_HF_ORG` overrides it.

default-project-name-derives-from-db-ste.text: When `init_db` receives no project name, `project_name` equals the database filename stem, e.g. `my-beliefs.db` → `my-beliefs`.

default-sl-conjunctive-single-justificat.text: Without `any_mode`, `api.add_node` with `sl='a,b,c'` creates a single conjunctive justification with three antecedents.

defeat-cascades-to-dependents.text: Defeating a justification re-propagates and marks every transitive dependent that loses support as `OUT`, all listed in `result["changed"]`.

defeat-is-implemented-via-outlist.text: Defeating a justification works by appending the defeater node ID to that justification's `outlist`, not by deleting the justification.

defeat-justification-adds-defeater-to-ou.text: `defeat_justification` implements defeat by creating an `IN` defeater node and appending its ID to the target justification’s `outlist`.

defeat-justification-encodes-defeat-via-.text: `defeat_justification` implements defeat by appending the defeater ID to the target justification’s `outlist`; the justification record itself remains present.

defeat-justification-error-contract.text: `defeat_justification` raises `KeyError` (message contains "not found") for missing nodes, `ValueError` (message contains "no justifications") for nodes with zero justifications, and `IndexError` (message contains "out of range") for out-of-range justification indices — it never returns an error dict for these conditions.

defeat-justification-requires-a-writable.text: `reasons.api.defeat_justification` raises `ValueError` when the target has no justifications (line 1361) and appends the defeater ID onto `justification.outlist` (line 1392-1393)

defeat-reason-taxonomy-has-four-categori.text: `classify_defeat_reason` in `reasons/review.py` assigns one of four defeater types: `unsupported-conjunct`, `over-generalizes`, `scope-mismatch`, or `migrated-retraction`

defeat-reason-type-absent-when-unset.text: When `defeat_reason_type` is empty or unset in `defeat_with_scope`, the key is deliberately absent from the defeater's metadata dict rather than present with an empty-string value.

defeat-reason-type-metadata-is-condition.text: `defeat_reason_type` is written to metadata only when non-empty (`reasons/api.py:1383-1384`), verified by `test_defeat_reason_type_omitted` vs `test_defeat_reason_type_stored`

defeat-reason-type-omitted-is-empty-and-.text: When `defeat_reason_type` is omitted, `defeat_with_scope` returns `""` and does not store the key in defeater metadata; when supplied, the value is stored in defeater metadata.

defeat-reason-types-are-closed-seven-val.text: `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` in `review.py` is a fixed list of exactly 7 strings that serves as both the LLM's allowed output vocabulary and the validation set in `classify_defeat_reason`; any downstream code matching on `defeat_reason_type` can exhaustively branch over these 7 values plus `""` for unclassified.

defeat-reason-types-are-kebab-case.text: Every entry in `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` contains a hyphen.

defeat-reason-types-is-closed-seven-elem.text: `DEFEAT_REASON_TYPES` contains exactly 7 kebab-case strings; the parser performs a membership check against this set, so any new classification type must be added to this constant before the LLM prompt can reference it.

defeat-reversal-is-automatic-with-guided.text: All outlist-based defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) not only reverse automatically through BFS propagation cascades — recovering all transitively dependent nodes — but also provide surgical recovery guidance through restoration hints that target cascade victims with surviving premises, enabling both automatic and manual recovery paths.

justifications.label: Automatic reversal handles the common case (retract the defeater, everything recovers), while guided recovery handles the complex case (multi-premise justifications where only some premises survive) — together they provide complete recovery coverage.

defeat-reversal-is-topology-complete-wit.text: Automatic defeat reversal with surgical recovery guidance propagates through topology-complete inconsistency-safe cascades — recovery reaches all transitively affected nodes including outlist-connected ones, handles dangling references gracefully, and provides restoration hints targeting only cascade victims with surviving premises.

justifications.label: Defeat reversal (automatic with guided recovery from depth-4) composes with topology completeness (inconsistency-safe from depth-4) into robust complete recovery that strengthens the existing depth-3 belief defeat-reversal-propagates-automatically by adding topology completeness and dangling-reference resilience

defeat-reversal-propagates-automatically.text: All outlist-based defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) not only reverse in principle but propagate recovery automatically through safe terminating BFS — when a defeating node is retracted, the outlist entry becomes satisfied, and propagation cascades truth-value restoration to all affected nodes without manual re-assertion

justifications.label: Defeat reversibility (outlist semantics flip truth without destroying structure) plus safe propagation (BFS with guaranteed termination) should yield automatic recovery — but only if outlist nodes are tracked in the dependents index so that retracting a defeating node triggers propagation to the defeated nodes

defeat-reversal-with-guided-recovery.text: All defeat mechanisms (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) are reversible through outlist semantics, and the system provides surgical restoration hints for cascade victims with viable recovery paths — enabling guided recovery from retraction cascades where multi-premise justifications have surviving premises.

justifications.label: Reversible defeat (depth-1) plus surgical hints (depth-0) provide both mechanism and guidance for recovery — unless missing outlist tracking leaves some cascade effects undetected and therefore unguided

defeat-reversals-are-lifecycle-governed.text: All outlist-based defeat reversals (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) operate within metadata-enabled lifecycle governance — every reversal produces not just a truth-value change but a fully governed lifecycle transition with metadata-tracked state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags), ensuring reversals are first-class lifecycle events rather than bare truth flips.

justifications.label: reversible defeats + metadata governance = reversals are governed lifecycle transitions

defeat-reversals-are-lifecycle-governed-.text: All outlist-based defeat reversals (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) operate within metadata-enabled lifecycle governance and maintain safety across all architectural layers and storage backends — the same lifecycle state transitions and safety guarantees hold regardless of whether backed by SQLite or PostgreSQL

justifications.label: Lifecycle governance of defeat reversals is backend-independent — SQLite and PostgreSQL provide equivalent mechanisms

defeat-uses-outlist.text: The defeat API appends the defeater ID to a justification’s `outlist` rather than deleting or rewriting the justification.

defeat-with-scope-cascades-to-dependents.text: Defeating a node through scope beliefs propagates `OUT` to nodes whose justifications depend on the defeated node.

defeat-with-scope-creates-scope-beliefs-.text: Each scope finding produces one `IN` premise node with no justifications and metadata linking it to the antecedent and defeater.

defeat-with-scope-error-contract.text: `defeat_with_scope` raises `KeyError` for an unknown `node_id`, `ValueError` for no justifications, `IndexError` for an out-of-range `justification_index`, and `ValueError` for empty `scope_findings`.

defeat-with-scope-requires-non-empty-fin.text: `defeat_with_scope` raises `ValueError` (message matches "scope_findings must not be empty") when the `scope_findings` parameter is an empty list, in addition to the standard KeyError/ValueError/IndexError for missing node, no justifications, and out-of-range index.

defeat-with-scope-validates-inputs-with-.text: Missing targets raise `KeyError`, no-justification targets and empty findings raise `ValueError`, and invalid indices raise `IndexError`.

defeater-classification-requires-defeats.text: An outlist node becomes `Defeated by` only when its `defeats_node` metadata matches the current node ID; otherwise it is exported under `Unless`.

defeater-default-id-is-deterministic.text: When `defeater_id` is not provided, the system generates a default ID following the exact pattern `{defeater_type}-{target_node_id}-j{justification_index}` (e.g., `over-generalizes-belief-j0`).

defeater-default-id-pattern.text: When `defeater_id` is omitted, `defeat_justification` generates the defeater ID as `"{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{index}"`.

defeater-export-tests-call-recompute-all.text: All three defeater/outlist tests call `Network.recompute_all()` before invoking `export_markdown`.

defeater-id-default-format.text: A defeater's default ID is `{defeater_type}-{node_id}-j{justification_index}`, overridable via `defeater_id`.

defeater-is-first-class-graph-node.text: A defeater created by `defeat_justification` is a full first-class node in the belief graph with its own `truth_value` ("IN"), metadata, deterministic ID, and is exportable via `export_network` and retractable via `retract_node` like any other node — not a side-table, annotation, or flag.

defeater-metadata-keys-identify-target.text: Every defeater node created by `defeat_justification` carries metadata keys `defeater_type`, `defeats_node`, and `defeats_justification`.

defeater-metadata-records-defeats-node-a.text: A defeater node stores `defeater_type`, `defeats_node`, and `defeats_justification` in its metadata.

defeater-type-filter-matches-existing-me.text: `defeater_type_filter` matches against the defeater node's existing `defeater_type`, not the new `defeat_reason_type`.

defeater-types-are-enumerated.text: Exactly four defeater types are recognized and stored in `metadata["defeater_type"]`: `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`.

defeater-types-are-four.text: The known `defeater_type` values exercised are `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`.

defeater-types-roundtrip-through-metadat.text: The defeat API accepts defeater types `invalid-inference`, `over-generalizes`, `duplicate-of`, and `superseded-by`, and stores the supplied value verbatim in `metadata.defeater_type`.

defeater-vs-regular-outlist-rendering.text: An outlist entry renders as `- Defeated by: <id> (<type>)` if and only if the referenced node carries `defeater_type` metadata; otherwise it renders as `- Unless: <id>`, and the two formats never appear for the same entry.

defend-delegates-to-challenge.text: `Network.defend(target_id, challenge_id, ...)` is implemented by calling `challenge(challenge_id, ...)`, treating a defense as a challenge against the challenge node.

defend-is-challenge-applied-to-challenge.text: The `defend` operation is implemented as `challenge()` applied to the challenge node itself, not as an independent mechanism; this makes dialectical defense a uniform instance of the same outlist-injection primitive.

defend-is-challenge-of-challenge.text: `defend` works by calling `challenge` on the challenge node itself, creating a recursive dialectical structure where truth values resolve automatically through the same outlist mechanism.

defend-is-recursive-challenge.text: Defense is implemented by calling `challenge()` on the challenge node itself, enabling arbitrarily deep dialectical chains using the same outlist mechanism recursively with no special-case code

defend-retracts-challenge-not-target.text: `PgApi.defend(target, challenge_id, ...)` brings `target` back IN by retracting `challenge_id`, so with multiple outstanding challenges the target remains OUT until every challenge is defended (`TestDefend.test_defend_multiple_challenges`).

defense-id-is-derived-from-challenge-id.text: The default defense node ID is `defense-<challenge_id>`, making the defense's identity a deterministic function of the challenge it neutralizes.

defense-in-depth-is-resource-efficient.text: The system's defense-in-depth across LLM and system boundaries — layered defenses including bounded execution, fail-soft error handling, process isolation, and referential integrity validation — achieves comprehensive protection within the same resource-efficient pipeline that spans packaging, startup, and runtime with zero external dependencies and lazy loading.

justifications.label: Defense-in-depth (depth-5) and resource efficiency (depth-4) arise from independent architectural chains; their combination shows comprehensive security does not require unbounded resource consumption

defense-in-depth-spans-llm-and-system-bo.text: Defense-in-depth is enforced at every external interface through two independently-established layers: LLM integration applies layered defenses across application and process isolation boundaries (bounded execution, fail-soft handling, subprocess isolation), while all system boundaries simultaneously enforce strict validation, evolution tolerance, and resource constraints.

justifications.label: LLM-specific defense-in-depth and general boundary enforcement are independently comprehensive — together they show no external interface lacks layered protection.

defense-is-challenge-to-challenge.text: `Network.defend()` is implemented as `challenge(challenge_id, ...)`, making a defense a challenge to the original challenge node.

deferred-imports-for-llm-modules.text: Same architectural pattern already captured by `api-uses-lazy-imports`; the cli.py instance follows the same rationale.

deferred-retraction-ordering.text: During agent import, nodes are added and truth values propagated before explicit retractions are applied, ensuring the dependency graph is fully wired before OUT transitions are forced.

dependency-completeness-enables-accurate.text: Complete dependency tracking for all reference types — both antecedent and outlist entries maintained eagerly by every network mutation — ensures deduplication accurately reflects the complete network topology: survivor selection considers all incoming dependencies including outlist references, and reference rewiring targets both antecedent and outlist positions across all justifications, preventing dedup from creating dangling references or miscounting dependents.

justifications.label: Dedup accuracy is a downstream consequence of dependency tracking completeness — incomplete tracking would cause dedup to misjudge survivors or miss rewiring targets

dependency-tracking-is-complete-for-all-.text: The dependents index fully tracks all relationship types — both antecedent references and outlist references — enabling complete incremental propagation for every truth value change without requiring periodic full recompute as a fallback

justifications.label: Mutations maintain dependents and outlist semantics are fully specified, so if outlist nodes were tracked in the dependents index, incremental propagation would reach all affected nodes — the gap is the sole obstacle to complete incremental consistency

dependents-bidirectional-index.text: Each node maintains a `dependents` set (reverse of antecedent/outlist edges), eagerly maintained by `add_node`, `add_justification`, `supersede`, `challenge`, and `convert_to_premise`.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-index-covers-outlist.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `dependency-tracking-is-complete-for-all-reference-types`, `every-network-mutation-maintains-dependents-invariant`, and `rewrite-dependents-updates-both-antecedents-and-outlists` which already establish that both antecedent and outlist edges populate the dependents index.

dependents-index-derived-on-load.text: The `node.dependents` set is never persisted to SQLite; it is rebuilt by walking all justification antecedents and outlists during `load()`.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-index-is-derived-from-justifi.text: The `dependents` reverse index is reconstructible via `_rebuild_dependents()` and validated by `verify_dependents()`; no independent source of truth exists.

dependents-index-is-fragile-denormalizat.text: The dependents set is a manually-maintained denormalized reverse index that is never persisted and must be rebuilt on every load, creating a consistency obligation on all mutation paths

justifications.label: Three beliefs triangulate the same fragility: any mutation path that forgets to update dependents silently corrupts propagation

dependents-index-is-reference-counted.text: a node remains in an antecedent's `dependents` set as long as *any* surviving justification references it.

dependents-integrity-errors-distinguish-.text: `verify_dependents()` error strings distinguish bogus reverse entries containing `"extra"` from absent reverse entries containing `"missing"`.

dependents-is-a-denormalized-reverse-ind.text: `Node.dependents` is a `set[str]` that must mirror the inverse of all `antecedents` and `outlist` edges; this module never populates or checks it.

dependents-is-manual-reverse-index.text: `Node.dependents` is a denormalized reverse pointer set that must be kept in sync by external code (primarily `network.py`); nothing in the data model enforces consistency.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31

dependents-not-self-enforced.text: The `Node.dependents` reverse index is not maintained by the data model itself; `network.py` is responsible for keeping it consistent with justification references (antecedents and outlists).

dependents-set-deduplicates-multiple-jus.text: Because `dependents` is a set, multiple justifications referencing the same antecedent produce a single reverse-index entry rather than duplicate entries.

dependents-survive-storage-roundtrip.text: After `Storage.save()` followed by `Storage.load()`, the loaded network's dependents index passes `verify_dependents()` with no errors.

dependents-tracks-outlist-entries.text: `outlist` entries are added to and removed from `dependents` the same way as `antecedents`.

derive-achieves-flexibility-with-reprodu.text: The derive pipeline resolves the tension between strategic flexibility and deterministic reproducibility: three budget strategies (alphabetical truncation, random sampling, semantic clustering) provide diverse exploration approaches, while fixed-seed deterministic sampling and accurate proportional allocation ensure each strategy produces identical results across runs.

justifications.label: multiple strategies with deterministic seeds = flexibility without sacrificing reproducibility

derive-agent-budget-proportional.text: When agents are present, `_build_beliefs_section` allocates prompt token budget proportionally to each agent's belief count, with a floor of 5 beliefs per agent

derive-agent-budget-proportional-formula.text: The agent belief budget in `_build_beliefs_section` is computed as `max(5, int(max_beliefs * len(agent_beliefs) / total_all))`.

derive-agent-count-bug.text: `_build_beliefs_section` has a bug: `count += len(belief_ids)` is inside the per-belief loop instead of outside it, inflating the count and shrinking the non-agent budget below intended size

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #33

derive-agent-count-increment-moved-outsi.text: `_build_beliefs_section` was fixed by moving the belief-count increment outside the per-belief loop, preventing count inflation and non-agent budget shrinkage.

derive-apply-auto-stamps-source-type-der.text: `apply_proposals` unconditionally sets `metadata["source_type"] = "derived"` on every newly created derived node, regardless of what the proposing LLM or caller specifies in the proposal dict.

derive-apply-fail-soft.text: Duplicates the existing belief `derive-apply-isolates-per-proposal-errors` which already captures that `apply_proposals` catches exceptions per-proposal.

derive-apply-is-isolated-and-caller-vali.text: The derive apply stage achieves defense-in-depth: callers must run validation before apply (trust boundary), and even if invalid proposals reach apply, each proposal is wrapped in independent error handling so one failure cannot corrupt the batch.

justifications.label: Validation-before-apply establishes the trust contract; per-proposal isolation provides the safety net when the contract is violated

derive-apply-isolates-per-proposal-error.text: `apply_proposals` wraps each `api.add_node()` call in try/except and accumulates `(proposal, error_string)` tuples, so one malformed proposal does not abort the batch.

derive-apply-tags-source-type-as-derived.text: `apply_proposals` in `reasons/derive.py` calls `api.add_node()` with `source_type="derived"` for every accepted proposal, marking the provenance of the belief so downstream tooling can distinguish LLM-derived beliefs from observations or imports.

derive-auto-assigns-derived-source-type.text: `apply_proposals` stamps generated derivation nodes with `source_type="derived"` without caller input.

derive-auto-writes-json-round-report.text: derive --auto writes a JSON report with round-by-round stats, and --no-report suppresses the report.

derive-budget-agent-match-uses-startswit.text: `_build_beliefs_section` identifies agent beliefs by checking whether node IDs start with the agent name followed by a colon.

derive-budget-allocation-is-accurate.text: The derive pipeline's proportional belief-budget allocation produces correct per-agent token counts

justifications.label: Budget allocation is correct only when the belief count is correct; the per-belief loop count bug inflates counts and distorts proportional allocation

derive-budget-allocation-is-proportional.text: When agent namespaces are detected, _build_beliefs_section allocates the belief budget proportionally by agent size.

derive-budget-ceiling-enforced.text: In `_build_beliefs_section`, the sum of agent-shown and local-shown beliefs never exceeds `max_beliefs`.

derive-budget-ceiling-invariant.text: `_build_beliefs_section` enforces that the combined count of agent-shown and local-shown beliefs never exceeds the configured `max_beliefs` budget.

derive-budget-count-accumulates-across-a.text: Agent belief count in `_build_beliefs_section` accumulates across all agents rather than resetting per agent.

derive-budget-count-is-linear.text: Agent belief counting in `_build_beliefs_section` accumulates as N (number of beliefs shown per agent), not N² — the corrected behavior after the issue #23 fix where `count += len(belief_ids)` was moved outside the per-belief loop

derive-budget-floor-five.text: Each agent group and the non-agent group are guaranteed at least 5 belief slots in the prompt regardless of proportional budget allocation.

derive-budget-is-efficient-and-floor-bou.text: The derive pipeline's per-agent budget allocation is both computationally efficient (O(N) linear accumulation, not quadratic) and representation-safe (each agent and local group guaranteed at least 5 belief slots), ensuring proportional allocation never starves minority agents.

justifications.label: Linear counting ensures scalability while floor guarantees ensure minimum representation — together they make budget allocation both performant and fair

derive-budget-is-flexible-and-efficient.text: The derive pipeline's budget allocation is both strategically flexible (three selection strategies: alphabetical truncation, random sampling, semantic clustering) and computationally efficient (linear accumulation with guaranteed floor of 5 per agent group), enabling callers to trade off reproducibility, diversity, and semantic coherence without performance penalty.

justifications.label: Strategy flexibility (what to select) and computational efficiency (how fast selection runs) are independently established — combining them shows the system avoids the usual flexibility-performance tradeoff

derive-budget-local-floor-is-five.text: `_build_beliefs_section` guarantees at least 5 local beliefs are shown regardless of agent budget pressure, via `max(5, max_beliefs - count)`

derive-budget-local-remainder-formula.text: When enough local beliefs exist, `_build_beliefs_section` sets `local_shown` to `max(5, max_beliefs - agent_total)`.

derive-budget-proportional-allocation-mi.text: When multiple agents contribute beliefs, `build_prompt` divides prompt budget proportionally to each agent's belief count with a minimum floor of 5.

derive-budget-sampling-is-seed-determini.text: In sample mode, `_build_beliefs_section` produces identical output across calls when given the same random seed.

derive-budget-section-handles-empty-inpu.text: `_build_beliefs_section` returns a valid formatted string for empty nodes, empty agents, or agents pointing to missing nodes.

derive-budget-tests-parse-header-format.text: Test infrastructure coupling detail (regex parsing of `_build_beliefs_section` headers), not a production code invariant.

derive-budget-tests-parse-output-headers.text: Test implementation detail (regex parsing of `"showing N"` headers), not a production code invariant

derive-budget-three-strategies.text: `_build_beliefs_section` supports three budget strategies — alphabetical truncation (default), random sampling (`sample=True`), and semantic clustering (`cluster=True`) — all controlled by a single `max_beliefs` parameter.

derive-build-beliefs-groups-by-id-prefix.text: Without agents, `_build_beliefs_section` groups beliefs by the first ID segment before `-`.

derive-build-prompt-default-budget-is-30.text: build_prompt has a default budget of 300 beliefs.

derive-build-prompt-returns-prompt-and-s.text: `build_prompt` returns a tuple of prompt text and a stats dict.

derive-build-prompt-wraps-template-forma.text: `build_prompt` catches `KeyError` and `ValueError` from `str.format()` and suppresses the original traceback with `from None`.

derive-cluster-and-sample-are-mutually-e.text: `cmd_derive` exits with code 1 if both `--cluster`/`--intra-cluster` and `--sample` are supplied, before making any API call.

derive-cluster-import-is-lazy.text: `cluster` is imported lazily inside `_build_beliefs_section` only when `cluster=True`.

derive-cross-agent-task-injected-when-mu.text: `CROSS_AGENT_TASK` is injected into the derive prompt only when multi-agent beliefs are detected.

derive-default-budget-groups-by-kebab-pr.text: In default budget mode, `_build_beliefs_section` groups beliefs by kebab-case ID prefix and outputs groups largest first, truncating at budget.

derive-delegates-llm-invocation-to-calle.text: `reasons/derive.py` owns prompt construction, response parsing, validation, and persistence but does NOT perform the LLM call itself — the `invoke_model` call is made by `api.py` or `cli.py`, which import and orchestrate the derive pipeline stages.

derive-depth-cycle-guard.text: `_get_depth` sets `memo[node_id] = 0` before recursing to prevent infinite recursion on cyclic justification chains; cycles resolve to depth 0

derive-depth-cycle-guard-returns-zero.text: _get_depth sets memo[node_id] = 0 before recursing into antecedents, so circular justification chains terminate with depth 0 rather than infinite recursion.

derive-depth-cycle-guard-sets-memo-befor.text: `_get_depth` in `reasons/derive.py` sets `memo[node_id] = 0` *before* recursing into antecedents, so a cyclic justification graph resolves the back-edge to depth 0 rather than causing infinite recursion.

derive-depth-is-max-antecedent-depth-plu.text: Premises have depth 0 and derived nodes have depth equal to the maximum antecedent depth plus 1.

derive-depth-memoizes-and-guards-cycles.text: _get_depth memoizes computed depths and sets memo[node_id] to 0 before recursion as a cycle guard.

derive-depth-premises-zero-derived-one-p.text: `_get_depth` assigns premises depth 0 and derived nodes depth 1 plus the maximum antecedent depth, using memoization.

derive-derived-section-sorts-deepest-fir.text: `_build_derived_section` renders existing derived conclusions sorted by depth deepest first, showing status, antecedents, and outlist.

derive-detect-agents-skips-active.text: `_detect_agents` identifies multi-agent networks by colon-namespaced IDs and skips `:active` premise nodes when scanning.

derive-detect-agents-skips-active-sentin.text: `_detect_agents` identifies agent namespaces from colon-separated node IDs and skips `:active` sentinel nodes.

derive-exhaust-iterates-until-no-new-pro.text: The derive --exhaust option iterates until the LLM produces no new proposals.

derive-exhaust-run-added-119-derived-bel.text: A derive --exhaust run of 10 rounds added 119 new derived beliefs to the network.

derive-fail-soft-validation.text: `validate_proposals` filters invalid proposals into a skipped list rather than raising; `apply_proposals` catches per-item exceptions so one bad proposal never blocks others

derive-imports-unused-subprocess-sys-pat.text: `derive.py` imports `subprocess`, `sys`, and `Path` but does not use them.

derive-local-budget-has-floor-of-five.text: The derive prompt builder gives the local-belief section at least 5 slots even when agent sections consume the nominal budget.

derive-min-antecedents-is-prompt-only.text: The minimum-2-antecedents rule for derived beliefs is enforced only by the LLM prompt instructions, not validated in code by `validate_proposals`.

derive-min-antecedents-is-soft-constrain.text: The requirement that derived beliefs use ≥ 2 antecedents is enforced only through the prompt instruction to the LLM; `validate_proposals` does not check antecedent count, so a single-antecedent proposal will pass code-level validation.

derive-no-llm-call.text: `derive.py` builds prompts and parses responses but never calls an LLM itself; the caller (CLI or API) is responsible for the model invocation.
