derive-parse-distinguishes-derive-and-ga.text: `parse_proposals` distinguishes DERIVE proposals from GATE proposals, where GATE proposals supply outlist entries.

derive-parse-proposals-backward-compat.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new `### DERIVE id` format first and falls back to the legacy `### DERIVE: \`id\`` format with bold markdown labels, so it can consume outputs from any version.

derive-parse-returns-empty-list-on-no-ma.text: parse_proposals silently returns an empty list when the LLM response matches neither the new nor old proposal format.

derive-parse-strips-backticks.text: `parse_proposals` strips backticks from proposal IDs and antecedent IDs.

derive-parse-supports-two-format-version.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new `### DERIVE id` format first, falling back to the older `### DERIVE: \`id\`` format only when the new parser returns zero matches.

derive-parse-supports-two-formats.text: `parse_proposals` tries the new format first (v0.10+: `### DERIVE id`), falls back to old format (v0.9: `### DERIVE: \`id\``) only when no new-format matches are found

derive-parser-falls-back-to-legacy-forma.text: parse_proposals tries the current ### DERIVE format first and only falls back to the legacy bold-field format if zero matches are found.

derive-parser-supports-legacy-and-backti.text: `parse_proposals` accepts both current `### DERIVE`/`### GATE` markdown blocks and legacy `### DERIVE:`/`**Antecedents**:` format, stripping backticks from IDs and lists.

derive-parser-supports-legacy-format-fal.text: `parse_proposals` in `reasons/derive.py` tries the v0.10+ regex pattern (`### DERIVE <id>`) first, then falls back to the v0.9 regex (`### DERIVE: \`belief-id\``), ensuring backward compatibility with previously-generated or user-edited files.

derive-parser-supports-two-formats.text: `parse_proposals` supports a new v0.10+ format and an old v0.9 format, falling back to the old format only when the new format yields no matches.

derive-pipeline-achieves-end-to-end-faul.text: The derive pipeline achieves end-to-end fault tolerance through three independent layers: proactive defense (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), reactive resilience (partial results persisted via JSON reports after each round, error states signaled through return codes), and prompt reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds enables consistent re-runs after failures).

justifications.label: proactive defense + reactive resilience + reproducible re-runs = end-to-end fault tolerance

derive-pipeline-constraints-are-structur.text: The derive pipeline enforces its structural constraints at the code level — fail-soft validation filters invalid proposals, and application explicitly tags source-type as "derived" — BUT the min-antecedents constraint is only enforced at the prompt level, leaving a gap where structurally-valid but semantically-weak proposals can pass.

justifications.label: The code-level enforcement (validation filtering + explicit tagging) establishes structural constraints; the gate acknowledges that the min-antecedents semantic constraint is not code-enforced, limiting the claim's scope.

derive-pipeline-has-complete-coverage.text: The derive pipeline achieves complete coverage along three axes: safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination), and production-readiness (accurate proportional budgets, roundtrippable prompt format).

justifications.label: Two independently-established depth-2 properties (safety+completeness and production-readiness) unify into full pipeline coverage — connecting the previously-orphaned derive-pipeline-is-safe-and-complete

derive-pipeline-has-end-to-end-quality-e.text: The derive pipeline achieves end-to-end quality enforcement: defensive validation prevents invalid proposals, Jaccard retraction guards prevent re-derivation of known-bad conclusions, budget allocation is accurate, AND the minimum-antecedents rule for derived beliefs is enforced in code — not just as an LLM prompt instruction that can be ignored.

justifications.label: Defensive validation (depth-1) and production readiness (depth-2) establish pipeline quality, but true end-to-end enforcement requires the min-antecedents rule to be validated in code rather than relying solely on LLM prompt compliance

derive-pipeline-is-defensive.text: The derive pipeline applies multiple defensive measures: fail-soft validation, Jaccard-based retraction guard, and environment variable stripping to prevent recursive spawning

justifications.label: Each defense addresses a distinct failure mode (bad proposals, re-derivation of retracted beliefs, infinite recursion)

derive-pipeline-is-error-accumulating.text: Covered by existing `derive-fail-soft-validation` (validation returns skipped entries with reasons) and `derive-pipeline-is-defensive` (broader defensive characterization)

derive-pipeline-is-exhaustive-and-termin.text: The derive pipeline supports exhaustive exploration mode while guaranteeing termination: `--exhaust` enables automatic application of all discovered proposals, and depth-based cycle detection with pre-recursion memoization prevents infinite loops even when justification chains are cyclic.

justifications.label: Depth-1 — completeness mode (exhaust) and termination guarantee (cycle guard) together yield the strongest usable exploration strategy: explore everything, stop safely

derive-pipeline-is-production-ready.text: The derive pipeline correctly allocates budgets, validates proposals defensively, and produces well-formed beliefs through a round-trippable prompt contract.

justifications.label: The pipeline's defensive validation and prompt contract provide production-grade reliability, but the count-accumulation bug in `_build_beliefs_section` undermines budget accuracy

derive-pipeline-is-reproducible-and-defe.text: The derive pipeline achieves both reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation) and defense-in-depth at the application stage (validation-before-apply trust boundary with per-proposal error isolation), ensuring pipeline runs are repeatable and any surviving bad proposal cannot corrupt sibling proposals.

justifications.label: Reproducibility guarantees identical inputs across runs; application isolation guarantees safe outputs regardless of individual proposal quality — two orthogonal quality axes covering the full pipeline.

derive-pipeline-is-reproducible-and-full.text: The derive pipeline achieves quadruple assurance: reproducibility (deterministic sampling with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation), safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination), and efficiency (O(N) budget accumulation with guaranteed floor) — four independently established properties reinforcing pipeline trustworthiness.

justifications.label: Reproducibility and defense-in-depth combine with safety, completeness, and efficiency for full pipeline assurance

derive-pipeline-is-safe-and-complete.text: The derive pipeline simultaneously provides safety (fail-soft validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation) and completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed cycle-free termination), ensuring LLM-driven belief generation discovers all derivable conclusions without corruption risk.

justifications.label: Defensive validation prevents harmful output while exhaustive mode with cycle guard ensures the derivation space is fully explored (depth-2)

derive-pipeline-is-safe-complete-and-eff.text: The derive pipeline simultaneously achieves safety (fail-soft validation with Jaccard retraction guards and environment isolation), completeness (exhaustive exploration with guaranteed termination via cycle guards), and efficiency (linear O(N) budget accumulation with a floor of 5 beliefs per agent preventing representation starvation).

justifications.label: Safety+completeness and efficiency are independently established — together they show the derive pipeline is production-ready across all quality dimensions.

derive-pipeline-provides-three-level-ope.text: The derive pipeline exposes its operational state at three independent granularities: per-item error accumulation in the skipped list (fine-grained), partial JSON reports written after each round (medium-grained, crash-surviving), and a return code of -1/0/positive-N (coarse-grained completion signal).

justifications.label: Convergent observability — each mechanism independently provides a distinct level of operational visibility; even if one is unavailable (e.g., reports disk full), the other two still communicate pipeline state to callers and operators.

derive-prompt-detects-multi-agent-networ.text: build_prompt detects multi-agent networks and adjusts the prompt accordingly.

derive-prompt-is-deterministic-and-repro.text: The derive pipeline's prompt construction is fully reproducible: deterministic sampling with fixed seeds selects consistent belief subsets, and accurate proportional budget allocation ensures each agent receives the same token share across runs.

justifications.label: Deterministic sampling plus accurate budgets yield reproducible derive prompts

derive-prompt-round-trippable.text: `write_proposals_file` output can be parsed back by `parse_proposals` with no data loss, enabling a write-review-accept cycle where humans edit proposals in the same format the parser reads

derive-prompt-roundtrips-through-parser.text: The `### DERIVE` / `### GATE` format is a shared contract between `DERIVE_PROMPT` LLM output, `parse_proposals()` input, and `write_proposals_file()` output, forming a closed serialization loop

derive-proposals-file-roundtrips-through.text: write_proposals_file output parses identically through parse_proposals.
`write_proposals_file` serializes valid proposals to the same `### DERIVE` and `### GATE` markdown format that `parse_proposals` can re-read for human review.

derive-quality-is-comprehensively-code-e.text: All derive pipeline quality constraints — structural validation, retraction guards, environment isolation, format contracts, AND minimum-antecedent requirements — are enforced through code-level validation, ensuring no invalid proposals can reach the database regardless of LLM prompt compliance.

justifications.label: Defensive code validation and the prompt/parser round-trip contract provide comprehensive code-level enforcement — but only once the minimum-antecedents rule is moved from prompt instructions to code validation

derive-report-json-has-rounds.text: The `derive` CLI with `--report-dir` writes a JSON file named `derive-<ts>.json` containing keys `status`, `model`, `exhaust`, `rounds`, and `total_added`; `--exhaust` appends a saturation round whose `added == 0`.

derive-report-json-has-rounds-array.text: The `reasons derive --auto --report-dir` command writes a JSON report containing a `rounds` array where each entry has `proposals_found` and `added` counts.

derive-reports-survive-partial-runs.text: `cmd_derive` and `cmd_review_beliefs` write partial JSON reports after each round/batch via `_write_derive_report`, so crash recovery is possible from the last completed step.

derive-resilience-preserves-progress-on-.text: The derive pipeline is resilient to partial failures: partial results are persisted via JSON reports after each round, and error states are signaled through return codes (-1 for error, 0 for saturation, positive for progress) rather than exceptions, enabling callers to recover and resume.

justifications.label: Two independently-established resilience properties (durable partial output + structured error signaling) combine to ensure no derivation work is lost on failure

derive-retraction-guard.text: Proposals whose ID has at least 50% Jaccard token overlap with any OUT node ID are rejected.

derive-retraction-guard-uses-jaccard.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposed belief ID with Jaccard similarity >= 0.5 to an existing OUT node, preventing re-derivation of retracted beliefs

derive-returns-negative-one-on-error.text: `_derive_one_round` returns -1 on error, 0 on saturation, and a positive int for the number of beliefs added, which `cmd_derive` uses to control the exhaust loop.

derive-review-contradict-is-convergent-c.text: The full belief maintenance cycle is `derive --exhaust → review-beliefs → retract invalid → contradictions → retract/fix/file → derive --exhaust`, where each tool catches a different error class (derive generates, review validates individual steps, contradictions finds cross-belief inconsistencies) and the cycle converges toward a stable belief set.

derive-round-return-codes-are-zero-satur.text: _derive_one_round returns 0 when derivation is saturated and -1 on error.

derive-round-returns-negative-on-error.text: `_derive_one_round` returns -1 on error, 0 on saturation, and a positive count on success — using return values instead of exceptions for flow control in the exhaust loop.

derive-sample-uses-reservoir-sampling.text: `_sample_beliefs` uses reservoir-style random sampling to stay within the token budget.

derive-sampling-uses-reservoir.text: `_sample_beliefs` uses reservoir-style random sampling to stay within token budgets and returns identity when the list is already under budget.

derive-shim-has-no-all.text: Already covered by existing `reasons-lib-is-uniform-star-reexport-shim` and related star-import beliefs.

derive-shim-import-executes-target-side-.text: Importing `reasons_lib.derive` causes `reasons.derive` module-level initialization/side effects to run once, not duplicated per import path.

derive-shim-name-rebinding-does-not-affe.text: Reassigning a name on `reasons_lib.derive` only changes the shim namespace; functions inside `reasons.derive` that reference their own module global continue to see the original binding.

derive-strips-claudecode-env.text: `_derive_one_round` explicitly removes the `CLAUDECODE` environment variable before spawning the model subprocess, preventing recursive Claude Code invocation.

derive-topic-filter-ors-keywords.text: `_filter_by_topic` treats space-separated keywords as OR conditions so any keyword match passes.

derive-topic-filter-uses-or-keyword-matc.text: `_filter_by_topic` keeps nodes whose ID or text matches any whitespace-separated topic keyword, using OR semantics.

derive-topic-filter-uses-or-semantics.text: `_filter_by_topic` matches space-separated terms case-insensitively against node ID and text, including a node if any keyword matches.

derive-unused-imports.text: Dead code observation (`subprocess`, `sys`, `Path` imported but unused) — unstable detail that will change when cleaned up.

derive-uses-subprocess-not-sdk.text: The derive command invokes LLMs by shelling out to `claude` or `gemini` CLI binaries via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, not through any Python SDK.

derive-validate-before-apply.text: `apply_proposals` trusts its input unconditionally; callers must run `validate_proposals` first or risk database errors from missing antecedents or duplicate IDs.

derive-validate-blocks-retracted-redisco.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose ID has >= 50% Jaccard token overlap (tokenized on hyphens/colons) with an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of previously retracted conclusions

derive-validate-rejects-duplicate-ids.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose belief ID already exists in the network, preventing overwrites of existing beliefs through the derive pipeline.

derive-validate-rejects-jaccard-similar-.text: validate_proposals skips any proposal whose ID has at least 50% Jaccard token similarity to an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of retracted conclusions.

derive-validate-rejects-missing-antecede.text: validate_proposals rejects proposals whose antecedent or outlist references do not exist in the current network.

derive-validate-rejects-similar-retracte.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposed belief whose tokenized ID has ≥50% Jaccard overlap with an existing OUT belief, preventing re-derivation of retracted conclusions.

derive-validate-rejects-similar-to-out.text: Covered by existing `derive-retraction-guard-uses-jaccard` which captures the same invariant

derive-validate-requires-existing-antece.text: `validate_proposals` rejects a proposal if any antecedent or unless node does not exist in the network.

derive-validation-is-layered-with-semant.text: The derive pipeline's validation is stratified: structural validity (parse success, fail-soft filtering) and semantic similarity (Jaccard rejection of OUT-near-duplicates) are code-enforced, but the cardinality constraint (≥2 antecedents) is delegated to LLM prompt instructions, making the most semantically meaningful constraint the least code-enforced.

justifications.label: Three validation layers form a coherent stratification only when all three are present together; removing any one collapses the "layered" characterization into a flat claim.

derive-validation-requires-antecedent-ex.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal whose antecedents or unless-list reference nodes that are not present in the network.

derive-validation-requires-at-least-two-.text: `validate_proposals` rejects any proposal with fewer than two antecedents as skipped.

derive-write-proposals-file-roundtrips-t.text: write_proposals_file serializes proposals to a markdown file in the same format parse_proposals() can read back, enabling human review before reasons accept.

derived-access-tags-union-antecedent-tag.text: Derived nodes' `metadata["access_tags"]` is the union of their explicit tags and all tags reachable through antecedent justifications, including transitive chains and diamond graphs.

derived-belief-pipeline-achieves-code-en.text: The derived belief pipeline — creation via defensive derivation with structural validation, Jaccard retraction guards, and environment isolation, followed by independent review with scope restricted to derived beliefs and mutation gated behind dry-run — achieves completely code-enforced quality assurance including logical soundness validation, only when inference soundness checking is implemented in code rather than relying solely on LLM prompt instructions.

justifications.label: Creation-phase structural safety + evaluation-phase scoped review achieve full code enforcement only when logical soundness moves from prompt-only to programmatic validation

derived-belief-soundness-is-llm-only.text: Structural validation ensures justification references exist and are IN, but the logical soundness of the inference from antecedents to derived conclusion is validated only by the proposing LLM — no code-level check verifies that the reasoning step is logically valid.

derived-claims-get-sl-justifications.text: Every `DERIVED` claim is imported with exactly one justification of `type == "SL"` whose `antecedents` equal the `Depends on:` list.

derived-node-evaluates-on-creation.text: Adding a derived node evaluates its justification immediately, and the new node starts OUT if its antecedents are OUT.

derived-node-merges-explicit-and-inherit.text: A derived node's effective `access_tags` merge any explicit tags declared on the node with the inherited tags from its antecedents.

derived-nodes-union-access-tags.text: A derived node’s `access_tags` is the union of its explicit tags and all antecedent tags across its justifications, and adding a justification can propagate new tags to dependents.

detect-agents-excludes-active-sentinel.text: _detect_agents identifies colon-namespaced agent prefixes and excludes :active sentinel nodes from belief counts.

detect-contradictions-only-considers-in-.text: Both `detect_contradictions` and its semantic variant skip any node whose `truth_value` is not `"IN"`.

detect-contradictions-swallows-batch-err.text: A `subprocess.run` exception during batching is caught and yields `[]` rather than propagating to the caller.

determinism-enables-safe-dialectical-ext.text: Dialectical transformation is operationally safe precisely because it composes with the minimal deterministic engine — the irreversible premise-to-justified conversion inherits deterministic propagation and uniform evaluation, so dialectics need no dedicated safety machinery beyond what the core already provides.

justifications.label: Cross-cuts the minimality/determinism narrative with the dialectical safety narrative; reveals that dialectical safety is not independently engineered but inherited from core determinism

determinism-spans-revision-semantics-thr.text: Determinism is maintained end-to-end from belief revision semantics through source integrity verification: revision operations produce deterministic traceable state transitions (structured before/after diffs with controlled irreversibility), AND the source verification that triggers revision actions is itself deterministic and architecturally grounded (fail-safe path resolution, exact SHA-256 comparison, clean layer boundaries) — no step in the revision-triggered-by-source-change pathway introduces non-determinism.

justifications.label: End-to-end determinism from the source change that triggers revision through the revision that responds to it

deterministic-history-extends-to-all-ori.text: Every state change for every belief — including externally-originated beliefs at full integration parity — follows a deterministic path with complete traceable history, meaning origin can never be used as an excuse for opacity.

justifications.label: Depth-8 — integration parity means external beliefs get the same deterministic traceable history as internal ones, eliminating provenance as a source of audit gaps

deterministic-reasoning-is-boundary-safe.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine operates within evolution-tolerant boundaries AND produces reproducible LLM-driven derivations through deterministic prompt construction with fixed seeds and accurate budget allocation — determinism extends from core truth evaluation through system boundaries to external model interaction.

justifications.label: Core determinism (uniform evaluation, guaranteed termination) extends through validated boundaries to reproducible derive prompts with defense-in-depth

deterministic-reasoning-operates-on-soun.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine operates on architecture with no hidden fragility — architectural stability ensures that determinism holds in deployed operation, not just in theoretical isolation.

justifications.label: Engine determinism is practically guaranteed because the substrate has no hidden fragility that could violate it

deterministic-reasoning-with-gapless-lif.text: The system's belief-state trajectory is both fully determined and fully monitored: deterministic reversible reasoning ensures any given set of premises produces exactly one truth-value assignment, while gapless lifecycle management ensures no belief escapes monitoring across any lifecycle phase — the state at any point is predictable from its inputs and verifiable through its monitoring infrastructure.

justifications.label: Deterministic reasoning (from TMS core branch) plus gapless lifecycle monitoring (from staleness/propagation branch) bridges predictability with verifiability

deterministic-reasoning-within-evolution.text: The deterministic reversible reasoning engine — producing predictable terminating results through uniform evaluation — operates within system boundaries that gracefully handle format and schema evolution, ensuring deterministic correctness remains stable as external data formats change over time.

justifications.label: Deterministic reasoning provides correctness within a format version; evolution-tolerant boundaries extend that correctness across format versions without breaking deterministic properties

deterministic-self-correction-spans-all-.text: Self-correction operates deterministically across both temporal dimensions — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection — on architecturally sound foundations, meaning the system's corrective behavior is predictable at every timescale.

justifications.label: Depth-5 — determinism on sound architecture combined with full temporal coverage yields predictable self-correction: no timescale produces surprising corrective behavior

dialectical-api-wraps-load-operate-save.text: The `reasons.api` dialectical functions (`challenge`, `defend`) wrap each call in a load → operate → save cycle against the SQLite file at `db_path`, ensuring the public API is a faithful pass-through to `Network` methods.

dialectical-assurance-achieves-governanc.text: Dialectical operations achieve complete bidirectional assurance (forward reliability and backward recovery with dual semantic grounding) within a governance framework that is complete across topology, source, and traceability — every dialectical challenge, defend, and reversal produces outcomes that meet the full governance quality bar across all three output dimensions.

justifications.label: bidirectional dialectical assurance + three-dimensional governance = dialectics produce governance-complete outcomes

dialectical-default-ids-use-prefix-and-c.text: Challenge nodes default to `challenge-<target>` with `-2`, `-3`, … on collision, and defense nodes default to `defense-<challenge_id>`.

dialectical-defeat-is-reversible-but-ide.text: The dialectical system exhibits a fundamental asymmetry between defeat and identity: the truth-value defeat caused by a challenge is fully reversible (defending or retracting the challenge node restores IN status via outlist semantics), but the premise-to-justified identity transformation is permanent — a challenged premise can never return to unjustified status because the added justification cannot be removed, only defeated.

justifications.label: Outlist reversibility at the truth level coexists with irreversibility at the structural level, a designed asymmetry

dialectical-edges-are-metadata-encoded.text: Challenge/defense relationships are encoded in node metadata via keys such as `challenge_target`, `challenges`, `defense_target`, and `defends`, not a dedicated edge table.

dialectical-errors-use-keyerror-not-cust.text: `Network.challenge()` and `Network.defend()` raise the built-in `KeyError` (not a domain-specific exception) when the target or challenge node ID does not exist in the network.

dialectical-metadata-links-are-bidirecti.text: A challenge node always records `metadata["challenge_target"]` pointing to the target, and the target always records the challenge ID in its `metadata["challenges"]` list; defenses follow the same pattern with `defense_target` and `defends`.

dialectical-naming-convention-is-determi.text: Challenge nodes are named `challenge-{node_id}` (with sequential `-2`, `-3`… suffixes for duplicates on the same target); defense nodes are named `defense-{challenge_id}`; the first challenge always gets the bare suffix.

dialectical-nodes-are-metadata-linked-no.text: Challenges and defenses attach to the graph via `metadata["challenge_target"]` / `metadata["challenges"]` / `metadata["defense_target"]` / `metadata["defends"]`, not via a separate edge collection.

dialectical-operations-raise-keyerror-fo.text: `Network.challenge` and `Network.defend` raise `KeyError` when the target or challenge node does not exist, rather than silently creating stubs.

dialectical-pipeline-is-three-stage.text: The challenge-and-defense pipeline flows in order: `contradictions.py` discovers NOGOODs → `network.py` executes formal retraction via outlist propagation → `repair.py` attempts defense (link/soften/abandon) before final commitment

dialectical-revision-governs-rich-tracea.text: Dialectical revision — deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete with controlled irreversibility — governs metadata-enriched state beyond binary truth values, producing traceable deterministic changes to retraction flags, stale reasons, and access tags through every challenge/defend operation, not just binary IN/OUT transitions.

justifications.label: Dialectical revision's three trustworthiness properties (determinism, reliability, completeness) apply to the full richly-governed state space, not merely binary truth

dialectical-revision-is-deterministic-re.text: The dialectical revision system achieves three independent trustworthiness properties simultaneously: determinism (through semantic transparency inheriting uniform evaluation rules), reliability (through safe crash-free premise-to-justified transformation), and semantic completeness with controlled irreversibility (comprehensive negative semantics where all defeats reverse but identity transformation is permanent) — making dialectical operations fully production-trustworthy.

justifications.label: Deterministic reliable dialectics composed with complete controlled-irreversibility semantics yields production-trustworthy revision

dialectical-revision-is-exception-safe-w.text: Dialectical revision — deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete — simultaneously governs metadata-enriched traceable state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, supersession) AND operates within an exception-safe richly-governed framework, ensuring that all dialectical operations produce rich auditable state transitions with safe failure recovery across all revision mechanisms.

justifications.label: dialectical revision unifies rich traceable state with exception-safe governance

dialectical-state-survives-storage-round.text: A challenge+defend sequence and its metadata survive `Storage.save` → `Storage.load`, and retraction behavior remains the same after reload.

dialectical-structure-is-recursive-outli.text: The entire challenge/defend dialectical system is implemented as recursive outlist injection with no dedicated dialectical machinery

justifications.label: Dialectics emerge from composing a single primitive (outlist injection) recursively

dialectical-transformation-is-fully-reli.text: The irreversible premise-to-justified transformation during challenge is both semantics-preserving (the resulting node inherits complete outlist evaluation with conjunction, absence, and persistence semantics) and crash-safe (recursive dialectical chains terminate deterministically), making dialectical operations reliable despite their irreversibility.

justifications.label: Irreversibility is safe because both semantic inheritance and operational termination are guaranteed

dialectical-transformation-is-operationa.text: The irreversible premise-to-justified transformation during challenge is both semantically safe (inherits uniform outlist evaluation and truth maintenance properties from the dialectical structure) and operationally safe (executes within atomic load/save transactions with deterministic BFS propagation).

justifications.label: depth-4 — challenge is the most destructive semantic operation (it permanently changes node identity) so proving it is operationally atomic AND semantically preserving is a meaningful safety property

dialectical-transformation-preserves-sem.text: Challenging a premise irreversibly transforms its identity from unjustified to justified node, but the resulting dialectical structure inherits complete outlist semantics — conjunction over multiple outlists, absence-as-OUT permissiveness, and persistence survival — ensuring the transformation preserves well-defined evaluable behavior.

justifications.label: depth-3 — the identity transformation (premise → justified) is destructive, but the semantic framework (outlist rules) remains intact across the transformation

dialectics-achieve-forward-reliability-a.text: Dialectical operations achieve complete bidirectional assurance: forward activation is deterministic, reliable, and semantically complete (challenge/defend evaluated uniformly with controlled irreversibility), while backward reversal is topology-complete with surgical guided recovery (recovery reaches all transitively dependent nodes, hints target only cascade victims with surviving premises) — the full dialectical cycle from engagement through resolution is assured in both directions.

justifications.label: dialectical operations assured both in forward engagement and backward recovery

dialectics-are-atomic-and-transparent.text: Challenge/defend dialectics are both semantically transparent (indistinguishable from ordinary beliefs, evaluated by uniform outlist rules) and atomically safe (mutations follow the same context-managed load/save pipeline as all other operations), requiring no special transaction handling.

justifications.label: depth-4 — dialectics inherit both semantic uniformity and mutation safety from the shared infrastructure

dialectics-are-deterministic-and-reliabl.text: Dialectical challenge/defend operations are simultaneously deterministic (through semantic transparency inheriting uniform evaluation rules from the core TMS) and fully reliable (semantics-preserving with crash safety through terminating propagation) — achieving safe predictable behavior without dedicated dialectical machinery.

justifications.label: Deterministic dialectics (via transparency) + reliable dialectics (via crash-safe propagation) → dialectics are both predictable and dependable

dialectics-are-deterministic-by-transpar.text: Dialectical challenge/defend structures receive deterministic reversible evaluation without special-casing — semantic transparency ensures the deterministic engine treats dialectical nodes identically to ordinary beliefs, so dialectical correctness requires no independent proof.

justifications.label: transparent nodes evaluated by deterministic engine without distinction (depth-4 from two depth-3 IN)

dialectics-are-dually-grounded-by-purity.text: Dialectical operations achieve dual semantic grounding from independent sources: evaluation purity (uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free validity checking) enables richly-governed exception-safe dialectics, while uniform edge-case semantics transitively ground deterministic reliable dialectics through complete negative semantics — together ensuring dialectics are both governable and semantically well-founded from first principles.

justifications.label: dialectics grounded independently by evaluation purity and semantic uniformity

dialectics-are-semantically-transparent.text: Challenge/defend dialectics are semantically indistinguishable from ordinary beliefs: they inherit fully-specified outlist semantics (conjunction, absence-as-OUT, persistence) and are evaluated by the same uniform pure rules that govern all truth maintenance — no dialectical special cases exist anywhere in the engine.

justifications.label: Complete outlist semantics (depth-2) + uniform truth evaluation (depth-2) together prove dialectical nodes have no privileged or special-case behavior

dialectics-complete-the-revision-system.text: The system handles both automated belief revision (outlist defeat for proactive retraction, dependency-directed backtracking for reactive contradiction resolution) and interactive dialectics (challenge/defend for human-driven contestation) — both operating atomically through the same outlist primitive with transparent, uniform evaluation semantics.

justifications.label: Automated revision handles machine-detected contradictions; dialectics handle human-initiated contestation — together they span the full space of belief challenges

dialectics-inherit-complete-outlist-sema.text: The recursive challenge/defend dialectical system inherits fully-specified semantics from the outlist primitive: conjunction over multiple outlists, absent-means-OUT permissiveness, and persistence guarantees all apply to dialectical structures without additional rules.

justifications.label: Dialectical structure is pure outlist, so all outlist semantic guarantees transfer directly

diary-update-pipeline-has-propose-and-ac.text: The `diary-update` pipeline records two ordered steps: `propose-beliefs` followed by `accept-beliefs`.

diary-update-pipeline-records-two-ordere.text: The `diary-update` pipeline records exactly two ordered steps: `propose-beliefs` followed by `accept-beliefs`.

diary-update-report-is-generated-run-art.text: `.forge/report.json` is a generated run-report artifact for the `diary-update` pipeline; this commit only refreshes run metadata and counts rather than editing domain logic.

diff-hunks-use-old-side-and-drop-pure-in.text: `parse_diff_hunks` returns OLD-side line ranges from `git diff` hunks and drops pure-insertion hunks with old count zero, so insertions above a pinned range do not flag it.

direct-access-raises-list-access-filters.text: API functions for single-node access (`show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`) raise `PermissionError` on forbidden nodes, while list/export functions (`list_nodes`, `search`, `export_network`) silently exclude them from results.

dispute-resolution-is-complete-and-relia.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms — intentional (dialectical challenge/defend with irreversible premise transformation) and automated (contradiction detection with dependency-directed backtracking) — are individually fully reliable, crash-safe, and traceable, leaving no dispute pathway that could silently fail or lose history.

justifications.label: Dialectical reliability (depth-4) and contradiction traceability (depth-4) are independently established; together they show the system resolves disputes at every level without silent failure

dispute-resolution-is-topology-accurate.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms — intentional dialectical challenge/defend and automated contradiction resolution — propagate their effects through an accurate convergent topology with complete dependency tracking, ensuring every transitively affected node reaches its correct truth state after any dispute.

justifications.label: Complete dispute resolution (depth-5) operating on accurate topology (depth-7) guarantees disputes resolve across the true dependency graph — no affected node is silently left in an inconsistent state

dispute-resolution-spans-all-origins.text: Both dispute resolution mechanisms (intentional dialectical and automated contradiction) are complete and reliable, and all belief origins participate in the same deterministic revision pipeline — every belief from any source can be disputed and resolved through identical mechanisms.

justifications.label: complete dispute resolution plus origin-agnostic deterministic revision ensures all beliefs are uniformly disputable

distribution-name-differs-from-executabl.text: The installable distribution is `ftl-reasons` (`pip install ftl-reasons`, `uv tool install ftl-reasons`) while the console executable is `reasons`.

distribution-name-differs-from-import-pa.text: The PyPI distribution name is `ftl-reasons`, distinct from the importable packages `reasons` and `reasons_lib`.

distribution-name-is-ftl-reasons.text: The distribution is named `ftl-reasons` while the shipped import packages are `reasons` and `reasons_lib`.

domain-data-must-be-reconstructed-via-im.text: The belief graph (`network.json`), exported beliefs (`beliefs.md`), and individual entry files (`entries/`) are excluded from version control and must be reconstructed through import pipelines (`import_beliefs`, `import_agent`) rather than read from the repository.

domain-id-enables-multi-tenancy.text: every SQL statement filters by `self.domain_id`, and `(id, domain_id)` is the nodes/nogoods primary key, so tenant data is isolated at the schema level.

domain-id-is-the-multi-tenancy-key.text: All persistence is partitioned by `domain_id`; two `PgApi` instances with distinct `domain_id`s can hold the same node id with independent content and no cross-contamination.

double-export-is-stable-modulo-updated-a.text: Two successive export/import cycles yield identical markdown except for lines beginning with `updated_at`.

double-roundtrip-is-idempotent.text: `export_markdown(import_into_network(export_markdown(net)))` must produce markdown identical to `export_markdown(net)`, with the sole permitted difference being `updated_at` timestamp lines that change per import.

download-network-maps-401-and-404-to-run.text: `HTTPError` with code 401 becomes a `RuntimeError` matching `"Authentication required"`; code 404 becomes a `RuntimeError` matching `"not found"`.

download-network-rethrows-non-401-404.text: `download_network` only wraps 401 and 404 into `RuntimeError`; other `HTTPError` codes propagate raw, unlike `create_repo` and `upload_file` which wrap all codes.

download-network-returns-raw-json-text.text: `download_network` returns the response body as a `str`; parsing is the caller's responsibility.

download-network-uses-fixed-network-json.text: `download_network` always requests `<repo>/resolve/main/network.json` and appends it to the normalized repo id.

dry-run-does-not-write-metadata.text: `classify_defeat_reason_types(..., dry_run=True)` never adds `defeat_reason_type` to node metadata.

dry-run-prevents-all-writes.text: `dry_run=True` causes `migrate_retract_to_defeaters` to compute candidates without creating defeater nodes, omitting `defeater_id` from results and leaving `retract_reason` intact.

dry-run-prevents-both-retraction-and-met.text: The `dry_run` flag in review-beliefs prevents both truth-value changes (retraction of invalid beliefs) and metadata side-effects (`last_reviewed` timestamp, `review_result` classification), making it fully read-only — extending beyond what `auto-retract-respects-dry-run` covers.

dry-run-prevents-database-mutations.text: When `dry_run=True`, the tested repair path avoids `retract_node`, `add_justification`, and `set_metadata` calls while still reporting planned statuses such as `softened` or `abandoned`.

dry-run-prevents-db-mutation.text: `api.repair_premises(dry_run=True, …)` leaves node `text` and `metadata["repair_action"]` unchanged and only populates counters/results.

dry-run-reports-success-status-while-sup.text: Every repair pattern sets its success status regardless of `dry_run`, while all `api.*` write calls are gated behind `if not dry_run`.

dry-run-still-reports-success-status.text: Every pattern sets its success status (`linked`/`softened`/`abandoned`/`needs_research`) regardless of `dry_run`; only the `api.*` write calls are gated by `if not dry_run`.

dry-run-suppresses-api-mutations.text: `dry_run=True` still performs LLM and search calls but skips `add_justification`, `supersede_with_text`, `retract_node`, and `set_metadata`.

dual-backend-atomicity-is-feature-comple.text: Both storage backends provide atomic isolated operations with complete API coverage — the SQLite backend's context-managed mutations and PgApi's per-method transactions cover the same full set of operations

justifications.label: Backend-independent atomicity achieves full feature parity only when PgApi implements the complete API surface

dual-mode-detects-emptiness-via-prompt-s.text: Dual mode classifies an empty TMS answer via the exact `NO_BELIEFS_MSG` string or the substring `"don't have enough beliefs"`, coupling it to prompt wording.

dual-mode-makes-exactly-three-llm-calls.text: Dual mode performs exactly three `invoke_model` calls in sequence: TMS-leg answer → FTS-leg answer → merged synthesis answer.

dual-mode-requires-sources-db.text: `ask()` with `dual=True` raises `ValueError` immediately if `sources_db` is `None`, since the dual retrieval path (TMS + FTS-RAG merge) is meaningless without a source-chunk database.

dual-package-distribution-split.text: `reasons/` and `reasons_lib/` form a full-versus-library distribution split: `reasons` adds merkle proofs and metadata on top of the shared TMS core modules, while `reasons_lib` ships the lighter variant without those additions.

dual-package-layout-reasons-and-reasons-.text: The repo maintains two import trees (`reasons/` and `reasons_lib/`) with identical module names; tests import from `reasons`, and `pyproject.toml` may alias one to the other, so a developer must verify which tree is canonical before editing.

dual-quality-enforcement-spans-automated.text: Belief quality is enforced by two independent mechanisms that cannot interfere: automated self-correction autonomously maintains consistency through contradiction resolution and staleness detection, while explicit quality review independently evaluates derived beliefs with read-only fault tolerance — dual enforcement ensures quality even when one mechanism is insufficient.

justifications.label: Automated self-correction and read-only review provide independent non-interfering quality enforcement

dual-quality-gates-are-complementary-and.text: The system enforces belief quality through dual non-mutating gates targeting complementary validity dimensions: review validates logical soundness of derived beliefs (scoped to justified nodes, dry-run gated auto-retraction), while staleness checking validates source currency of all IN beliefs (conservative CI gate with nonzero exit on drift) — neither gate can corrupt network state.

justifications.label: Review validates logical soundness while staleness validates source currency

dual-storage-backends-are-interchangeabl.text: Both SQLite and PostgreSQL backends can be used interchangeably for any operation, with identical safety guarantees through backend-appropriate mechanisms and complete API surface coverage, so applications can switch backends without behavioral changes.

justifications.label: Backend safety equivalence (depth-4) and backend-independent atomicity (depth-2) establish interchangeability, but only when PgApi achieves full API coverage — partial coverage means some operations work on SQLite but not PostgreSQL

duplicate-and-nogoods-do-not-change-node.text: `duplicate_of` is a metadata bullet and nogoods are a separate `## Nogoods` network section; neither changes a node’s exported status label.

duplicate-content-based-ids-get-numeric-.text: Adding the same generated nogood twice yields `nogood-a-b` followed by `nogood-a-b-2`.

duplicate-import-is-a-noop.text: Re-importing an identical file returns `claims_imported == 0`, `claims_skipped == N`, and `created_premise == False`; no exceptions are raised for the collision.

duplicate-node-id-raises-valueerror.text: `api.add_node()` raises `ValueError` when given a node ID that already exists in the network — node IDs are unique.

duplicate-of-is-metadata-only-in-markdow.text: `export_markdown` renders `metadata['duplicate_of']` as a `Duplicate of:` bullet without changing the node’s status label or truth value.

each-cli-test-creates-isolated-db.text: Every CLI test method initializes a fresh SQLite database via `run_cli("init")` in a pytest `tmp_path`, ensuring zero shared state between tests.

edge-case-safety-spans-creation-and-main.text: The system handles edge cases safely across both temporal dimensions: at creation time, uniform revision covers all semantic edge cases (vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents) through minimal primitives; at maintenance time, contradiction resolution and staleness detection actively catch drift — no edge case is safe only at one point in time.

justifications.label: Edge-case uniformity at creation (depth-5) combined with bidirectional self-correction at maintenance (depth-4) closes the temporal gap where edge cases could escape handling

edge-case-uniformity-follows-from-minima.text: Uniform handling of all semantic edge cases — vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents — is a consequence of semantic minimality: because every edge case derives from the same primitives that drive deterministic core semantics, no special-case logic exists.

justifications.label: depth-5 — edge-case uniformity and semantic minimality have a causal relationship: minimality is what makes uniformity possible rather than coincidental

edge-case-uniformity-reinforces-complete.text: Uniform handling of all semantic edge cases — vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, empty antecedents — reinforces the completeness and recoverability of negative semantics: every edge case within the negation lifecycle (missing outlist nodes treated as OUT, challenge of already-justified nodes, recovery from outlist defeat) is handled by the same minimal evaluation rules that ensure reversibility.

justifications.label: Minimality-driven uniformity means negative semantics don't need special-case handling for edge conditions — the same rules that make negation complete also make edge cases uniform

eem-builder-runs-on-gce-vms.text: The EEM builder currently runs on GCE VMs.

eem-card-has-yaml-frontmatter-with-schem.text: An EEM card has YAML frontmatter with schema_version "1.0" and type "eem".

eem-card-is-readme-md-modeled-on-hugging.text: The EEM_CARD.md format is modeled on HuggingFace model cards and is the README.md in the EEM repo.

eem-expert-published-to-huggingface-at-b.text: The eem-expert knowledge base was published to HuggingFace at benthomasson/eem-expert on 2026-05-23.

eem-wiki-generates-static-html-from-netw.text: The eem-wiki generates static HTML from network.json belief exports.

eem-wiki-publicly-deployed-to-cloudflare.text: The eem-wiki is currently deployed publicly to Cloudflare Pages at wiki.llmeem.ai.

egress-is-resilient-governed-and-self-co.text: All information leaving the system is simultaneously resilient (queries degrade gracefully across all access paths with deterministic output), governed (authorized, budget-constrained, and CI-ready), and serves a self-correcting knowledge base — the system's complete information egress is both trustworthy and operationally sustainable.

justifications.label: Query resilience and output governance jointly ensure trustworthy information egress

empty-antecedents-vacuously-valid.text: An SL justification with an empty antecedent list is valid (vacuous truth via `all([])`), allowing outlist-only justifications to function as "IN unless Y" — used by `challenge` and `supersede` for converted premises

empty-file-is-content-changed-not-delete.text: A zero-byte file that exists on disk is never classified as `source_deleted`; if its hash differs from the stored hash it produces `content_changed`, if it matches it produces no result.

empty-file-not-source-deleted.text: An empty file on disk is not treated as a deleted source; if its hash does not match, `check_stale` reports `content_changed`, not `source_deleted`.

empty-file-with-wrong-hash-is-content-ch.text: An existing empty source file with a mismatched stored hash produces a `content_changed` result whose `new_hash` is the SHA-256 of empty content.

empty-mcp-instructions-produce-no-prompt.text: `_build_mcp_instructions` returns `""` for empty instructions, and `build_ask_prompt` then omits the `"Data Source Instructions"` header entirely.

empty-network-is-safe.text: `export_card` handles an empty network because retraction percentage guards `total == 0` and `max_depth` uses `default=0`.

empty-network-produces-valid-card.text: `export_card(Network())` succeeds and emits a card with all counts `0` and a title derived from `project_name`.

empty-optional-fields-omitted-from-expor.text: When `source_url` or `accepted_pr` is unset, `export_markdown` omits the corresponding markdown line entirely.

empty-outlist-vacuously-valid.text: An SL or CP justification with an empty outlist is valid whenever all its antecedents are IN, providing pure monotonic support.

empty-premise-ids-returns-empty-list.text: `repair_premises` returns `[]` immediately when `premise_ids` is empty, with no LLM calls.

empty-result-message-is-api-specific.text: `api.search` returns text containing `"No results found"` while `api.lookup` returns `"No beliefs found"` when no IN matches exist.

empty-source-hash-skips-stale-check.text: `check_stale` skips nodes with an empty `source_hash`, even if their source file is missing.

empty-stale-list-cannot-distinguish-fres.text: An empty result from check_stale cannot distinguish all source files being fresh from no nodes having source tracking.

empty-string-status-sentinel-means-all.text: In MCP listing tools, `status=""` and `proposal_status=""` are sentinel values meaning “no filter / all statuses”, not an error or empty-result request.

entrenchment-beliefs-type-lookup-is-case.text: `_entrenchment()` uppercases `node.metadata["beliefs_type"]` before table lookup, so `"axiom"` and `"AXIOM"` both receive the AXIOM score.

entrenchment-favors-premises-sources-and.text: The _entrenchment scoring heuristic ranks premises above derived nodes, sourced nodes above unsourced, and nodes with many dependents above those with few.

entrenchment-has-backend-specific-implem.text: `_entrenchment` is implemented separately in `reasons/network.py` and `reasons/pg.py`, so backend parity must be maintained independently.

entrenchment-hierarchy-sourced-observati.text: The backtracking entrenchment score encodes a strict priority: sourced premises > unsourced, OBSERVATION type > DERIVED type, and fewer dependents = lower entrenchment (retracted first).

entrenchment-increases-with-source-obser.text: `_entrenchment` scores sourced premises, `OBSERVATION` metadata, and nodes with more dependents above their unsourced/derived/less-depended counterparts.

entrenchment-is-implemented-per-backend.text: `_entrenchment` has two independent definitions, `reasons/network.py:291` and `reasons/pg.py:3328`, with different signatures.

entrenchment-is-uncached.text: `_entrenchment` recomputes from live node state on every call; there is no memoization, so score reflects `dependents`/`source` changes immediately.

entrenchment-ranks-popular-above-lonely.text: Tests assert `_entrenchment("popular") > _entrenchment("lonely")`, making widely depended-on beliefs harder to retract than isolated ones.

entrenchment-ranks-premises-above-derive.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `add-nogood-retraction-prefers-least-entrenched` and `backtracking-retracts-least-entrenched` which already establish that premises (evidence) are preferred over derived nodes (speculation) during retraction selection.

entrenchment-score-is-uncached-and-live.text: `_entrenchment()` recomputes its score from live node state on every call and performs no memoization.

entrenchment-scoring-uses-weighted-heuri.text: `find_culprits` scores premise candidates for retraction using additive weights: premise +100, has `source` +50, has `source_hash` +25, per-dependent +10, and `beliefs_type` ranges from 10 (NOTE) to 90 (AXIOM/WARNING), preferring retraction of speculative assumptions over evidence.

entrenchment-tie-order-is-nondeterminist.text: Equal entrenchment scores in `find_culprits` are sorted from set iteration order, so tie-breaking is not reproducible across runs.

entrenchment-ties-are-nondeterministic.text: Equal scores sort by insertion order from a `set` in `find_culprits`, so tie-breaking is not reproducible across runs.

entrenchment-uses-three-tier-ordering.text: Entrenchment scoring enforces a strict three-tier preference: premises (highest) > source-backed derived nodes (middle) > pure derived nodes (lowest), with dependent count as a tiebreaker within tiers, ensuring `find_culprits` always retracts speculation before evidence.

entry-point-mapping.text: The `reasons` CLI command maps to `reasons_lib.cli:main` via `[project.scripts]` in `pyproject.toml` and is the only registered script entry point.

env-org-override-does-not-apply-to-expli.text: Setting `REASONS_HF_ORG` changes the default org for bare names only; explicit `owner/repo` inputs are returned unchanged.

env-vars-read-at-resolve-time.text: `_resolve_config` reads `MIND_SERVICE_URL`, `MIND_AGENT_ID`, and `MIND_API_KEY` from `os.environ` when called, not at import time.

equilibria-are-negation-transparent-with.text: The system's convergent equilibria simultaneously satisfy two independent completeness criteria: negation transparency (the final stable state is uniquely determined by declarative semantics with no hidden procedural effects from negation) and complete propagation fidelity (every truth change cascades to every transitively dependent node with topology preservation and guided recovery).

justifications.label: Semantic completeness (negation fully resolved) and structural completeness (every dependent reached) together establish that equilibria leave no unresolved state in any dimension

equilibria-are-transparent-and-trajector.text: The system's convergent equilibria are simultaneously negation-transparent (the final stable state is uniquely determined by evaluation rules with complete propagation fidelity) and trajectory-documented (every convergence path generates deterministic traceable events backed by permanent durable audit trails) — convergence is not just mathematically guaranteed but operationally verifiable.

justifications.label: Transparent equilibria plus permanent trajectory documentation yield verifiable convergence

equilibrium-trajectory-is-deterministic-.text: Every convergence trajectory toward an evaluation-invariant equilibrium generates consistently identifiable artifacts with deterministic traceable events, enabling complete post-hoc reconstruction of how each stable state was reached.

justifications.label: Convergence to stable states combined with consistent artifact identification means each equilibrium's history is fully reconstructible

estimate-tokens-char-floor-four-min-one.text: `estimate_tokens(text)` returns `max(1, len(text) // 4)`, using character count rather than word count.

estimate-tokens-chars-div-4.text: `estimate_tokens` uses `len(text) // 4` with a minimum return value of 1; it never returns 0, even for empty strings.

estimate-tokens-uses-char-count.text: The tests require `estimate_tokens(text)` to equal `len(text) // 4` with a minimum return value of `1`.

evaluation-is-traceable-and-context-agno.text: Every truth evaluation is simultaneously context-agnostic (producing identical results regardless of evaluation timing, attachment history, or belief origin) and fully traceable (every state change follows a deterministic path recorded in the system's operational history), enabling both reproducibility and post-hoc explanation of any evaluation outcome.

justifications.label: Context-agnostic evaluation (depth-4) and deterministic traceable history (depth-6) from distinct chains combine: you know both WHAT the system computes and WHY each computation occurred

evaluation-is-uniformly-context-and-orig.text: Truth evaluation produces identical results regardless of both attachment history (when/how a justification was added) and structural origin (ordinary belief vs. dialectical construct) — no belief receives special treatment based on provenance, timing, or role in the network.

justifications.label: Context-independence (depth-2) guarantees timing irrelevance while semantic transparency (depth-3) guarantees origin irrelevance; together they close all evaluation-bias vectors.

evaluation-purity-enables-complete-minim.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — is the concrete computational property that makes the completeness-minimality unification possible: purity simultaneously grounds context-agnosticism (enabling the minimal primitive set to handle all cases uniformly) and ensures that architectural completeness follows from rather than despite minimality (because pure evaluation needs no case-specific logic).

justifications.label: Purity is the bridge between the minimal primitive set and complete architectural coverage

evaluation-purity-grounds-agnosticism-an.text: Evaluation purity (uniform, deterministic, no metadata inspection) independently grounds both context-agnosticism (identical results regardless of timing/origin) and semantic minimality (no special-case logic), making them co-occurring consequences of the same architectural choice rather than causally related.

justifications.label: Pure uniform evaluation is the single architectural choice that produces both properties independently

evaluation-purity-grounds-dialectics-thr.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — enables the complete minimal architecture whose negative semantics ground deterministic dialectics, establishing a causal chain from the most fundamental computational property through architectural completeness to dialectical reliability.

justifications.label: Evaluation purity enables architecture and negative semantics ground dialectics; combining reveals the causal chain from the computational foundation (purity) through architecture (completeness via minimality) to the highest-level feature (deterministic dialectics)

evaluation-purity-grounds-governance-tha.text: Evaluation purity provides the semantic foundation for richly governed dialectics while exception safety preserves that rich traceable governance through all failure modes — purity creates the governance properties and exception safety ensures they are never lost, establishing complementary roles in governance assurance.

justifications.label: Purity creates the governance properties, exception safety preserves them through all failure modes

evaluation-traceability-persists-through.text: Every truth evaluation is traceable and context-agnostic from individual computation through system-wide convergence: all structural transformations converge to documented equilibria with deterministic identifiable artifacts, and every evaluation along those convergence trajectories is deterministically reproducible regardless of timing or origin.

justifications.label: Context-agnostic traceable evaluation (depth-7) composes with documented convergent equilibria (depth-9) — traceability persists from individual computations through to final stable states

every-cli-subcommand-has-db-argument.text: Every CLI subcommand inherits a --db argument defaulting to api.DEFAULT_DB.

every-imported-belief-has-inactive-in-ou.text: Namespaced beliefs all carry `{agent}:inactive` in their outlist, which is what makes retracting `{agent}:active` cascade through every belief.

every-mutation-reports-its-effects.text: All mutating operations report their effects as structured data: retract returns the full changed set, add_justification returns a change dict with old/new truth values, and API mutating operations use before/after truth-value diffing to capture deltas.

justifications.label: Three independent mutation-reporting mechanisms unify into a single observability property — every state change is reported to callers

every-network-mutation-maintains-depende.text: After any public mutation method on `Network` (`add_node`, `retract`, `assert_node`, `add_justification`, `supersede`, `challenge`, `defend`, `convert_to_premise`, `add_nogood`, `summarize`), `verify_dependents()` returns an empty list.

After any public Network mutation (add_node, retract, assert_node, add_justification, supersede, challenge, defend, convert_to_premise, add_nogood, summarize), the dependents index passes `verify_dependents()` — completeness and minimality are maintained incrementally

evolution-tolerance-audit-finds-not-all-.text: Issue #121 evolution tolerance audit found that not all system boundaries have documented forward-compatibility mechanisms.

example-and-access-tags-coexist-in-metad.text: An example and access tags can be stored together in node metadata without either field interfering with the other.

example-flag-persists-to-metadata.text: CLI `add --example` stores the value under `metadata["example"]` and returns exit code 0.

example-key-absent-when-unspecified.text: Omitting the `example` parameter in `api.add_node` results in the key being entirely absent from `node["metadata"]`, not present as `None` or an empty string.

example-stored-verbatim-in-metadata.text: The `example` field is stored as the exact string provided (no trimming, escaping, or wrapping) and retrieved via `node["metadata"]["example"]` as a flat string value within the metadata JSON blob.

exception-safety-spans-tms-and-source-li.text: The system handles failures safely across both domains: the TMS core resolves exceptional conditions (contradictions via backtracking, challenges via deterministic propagation) while the source integrity pipeline handles its failure modes (missing files, changed content, deleted sources) — no exception in either domain can produce inconsistent or undefined state.

justifications.label: TMS exception safety + fail-safe source lifecycle → unified failure safety across both domains

execution-fallback-chain-three-strategie.text: CLI execution follows a prescribed three-step fallback chain: try the installed `reasons` binary → `cd <repo> && uv run reasons …` → `uvx --from ftl-reasons reasons …`, with the agent trying each in order until one succeeds.

exhaust-implies-auto.text: In `_derive_one_round`, proposals are auto-applied when either `args.auto` or `args.exhaust` is true; the `--exhaust` flag does not require the user to also pass `--auto`.

exhaustive-knowledge-expansion-within-co.text: The system achieves exhaustive knowledge expansion — deterministic reversible reasoning combined with complete LLM-driven derivation with guaranteed termination — within multi-level information boundaries that gate authorization, constrain output size, and defensively validate all ingested beliefs, ensuring unbounded knowledge growth never escapes system controls.

justifications.label: Exhaustive reasoning and derivation combined with multi-level information control ensures knowledge grows without escaping authorization, budget, or validation boundaries

expert-pipeline-extracts-per-document.text: The expert-agent-builder pipeline extracts beliefs per-document (summarize entire document → propose beliefs → record file path), not per-section — the connection between a belief and its source material is a file-level pointer, not a section-level one.

explain-distinguishes-valid-and-violated.text: `Network.explain` reports `outlist` for valid outlist justifications and `violated_outlist` for invalidated outlist justifications.

explain-node-delegates-to-network-explai.text: `explain_node()` delegates to `Network.explain()` for a step-by-step proof trace.

explain-node-distinguishes-cycles-from-d.text: `api.explain_node` returns ordered `steps` with reasons such as `"premise"` and uses `"circular …"` only for genuine cycles, never labeling diamond-shaped dependencies as circular.

explain-node-supports-premise-and-chain.text: `api.explain_node` provides explanations for both premise nodes and derived chain nodes.

explain-out-node-includes-failed-anteced.text: `Network.explain()` on an OUT node includes `failed_antecedents` identifying what broke the justification.

explain-trace-includes-violated-outlist.text: `Network.explain()` returns step dicts that include a `violated_outlist` key (list of IN node IDs) specifically when a justification is defeated by its outlist, in addition to the always-present `outlist` key showing the declared list.

explicit-config-overrides-env.text: Explicit `url`, `agent_id`, and `api_key` arguments take precedence over their environment-variable counterparts.

explicit-params-override-env.text: Explicit parameters to `_resolve_config` take precedence over the corresponding `MIND_*` environment variables.

export-access-filtering-constructs-in-me.text: `export_network` and `export_markdown` support access-tag filtering by constructing a filtered `Network` in memory.

export-api-counts-errors-instead-of-rais.text: `api.export_api` swallows per-node failures, returning aggregate `nodes_exported` and `errors` counters rather than propagating exceptions.

export-api-fault-tolerant-per-node.text: `api.export_api` catches per-node HTTP errors internally, increments an `errors` counter, and continues pushing remaining nodes rather than aborting on the first failure; callers inspect `result["errors"]` rather than catching exceptions.

export-card-always-emits-yaml-frontmatte.text: `export_card()` always emits a frontmatter block delimited by `---` lines that `yaml.safe_load` can parse.

export-card-belief-counts-are-exhaustive.text: In the EEM card frontmatter, `beliefs_in + beliefs_out == beliefs_total` and `premises + derived == beliefs_total`, where a node is a premise if and only if it has zero justifications.

export-card-body-sections-and-usage-comm.text: The exported card body must contain the stats table, `## How to Use` with `reasons import-json network.json`, `## Quality`, and `## License` sections.

export-card-counts-stale-nodes-as-out.text: `export_card` counts nodes strictly by `truth_value`, so a markdown-`STALE` node is counted as `OUT` in the card frontmatter and stats.

export-card-cycle-sentinel-prevents-infi.text: `_node_depth` assigns `memo[nid] = 0` before recursing, preventing infinite recursion on cyclic networks without validating acyclicity.

export-card-defaults-are-explicit.text: `export_card` defaults to `license="mit"`, `domain=[]`, and `base_network=None` when callers omit these parameters; `type` is always the literal string `"eem"` and `schema_version` equals `reasons.metadata.SCHEMA_VERSION`.

export-card-depth-uses-supporting-justif.text: When `supporting_justification` is a valid index, `_node_depth` in `export_card.py` traverses only that single justification's antecedents (the "live" proof path), ignoring sibling justifications; an out-of-range or `None` index falls back to considering all justifications.

export-card-empty-network-produces-zero-.text: `export_card` handles an empty network by producing a valid titled card with zero belief, premise, derived, and nogood counts.

export-card-empty-network-safe.text: `export_card` handles empty networks safely by guarding percentage division with `total == 0` and using `default=0` for `max_depth`.

export-card-has-yaml-frontmatter.text: `export_card()` output is a single string with a YAML frontmatter block delimited by `---` lines.

export-card-invalid-supporting-justifica.text: When `supporting_justification` is not a valid index into `node.justifications`, depth traversal falls back to considering all justifications.

export-card-max-depth-is-longest-justifi.text: The "Max derivation depth" reported in the card body equals the length (number of edges) of the longest justification chain in the network; a network with only premises has depth 0.

export-card-out-count-is-exact-in-only.text: A node is counted as IN only when `truth_value == "IN"` exactly; every other truth value contributes to OUT.

export-card-partition-is-exhaustive.text: In `export_card`, the node partition is exhaustive: `in_count + out_count == total` (every node is either `"IN"` or not) and `premises + derived == total` (a node is a premise iff it has zero justifications), with no third state.

export-card-premise-depth-is-zero.text: `_node_depth` returns `0` for missing nodes and for nodes without justifications.

export-card-requires-node-depth.text: `export_card` depends on `_node_depth` to populate the `Max derivation depth` metric in the generated card.

export-card-returns-string-with-no-io.text: `export_card` returns a single string and performs no file writes; callers persist the `README.md` themselves.

export-card-shim-consumers-include-api-a.text: Known first-party importers of `reasons_lib.export_card` include `reasons/api.py` and `tests/test_export_card.py`, so both must migrate before the shim can be removed.

export-card-title-derived-from-project-n.text: The Markdown H1 title in the card body is produced by applying Python's `.title()` method to the `project_name` value (e.g., `k8s-ops-expert` → `K8S Ops Expert`).

export-card-type-is-eem.text: The exported card frontmatter always uses the constant type value `"eem"`.

export-card-yaml-fields-mostly-unescaped.text: Only `project_name`, `schema_version`, and `base_network` are quoted in frontmatter; `license`, `domain`, `source_repos`, and `generator` values are inserted unescaped.

export-dash-emits-json-on-stdout.text: `export --output=-` is expected to print pure JSON to stdout, as verified by `json.loads(out)` in `test_export_json`.

export-import-json-roundtrip-preserves-b.text: The `export_network` → `import_json` pipeline preserves not only structural fidelity (node count, justification structure, outlist entries, metadata) but also behavioral equivalence: defeasible propagation (retract, re-assert, cascade) on the imported database produces identical truth-value outcomes to the source database.

export-import-preserves-hashes.text: `api.export_network()` includes existing hashes, and `api.import_json()` restores them so the imported database verifies with no text or chain mutations.

export-import-preserves-merkle-hashes.text: `api.export_network`/`api.import_json` round-trips preserve node and justification hash fields so the imported database verifies cleanly.

export-import-round-trip-preserves-metad.text: A node's `source_type` and `accepted_pr` stored in `node.metadata` survive `export_markdown → import_into_network` unchanged.

export-markdown-aggregates-justification.text: `Depends on` is the de-duplicated union of antecedents across all of a node’s justifications, preserving first-seen order.

export-markdown-classifies-defeaters-via.text: An outlist ID is rendered as `Defeated by` only when the referenced node’s metadata has `defeats_node` equal to the current node ID; otherwise it is rendered under `Unless`.

export-markdown-deps-emit-dangling-refs-.text: The `all_deps` collection in `export_markdown` does not guard against antecedent IDs that reference non-existent nodes; a dangling antecedent is emitted as a plain string in the "Depends on" line without crashing, unlike the defeater lookup which uses a `nodes.get()` guard.

export-markdown-emits-source-type.text: `export_markdown` writes the line `- Source type: <value>` only for nodes whose metadata contains `source_type`.

export-markdown-emits-source-type-line-o.text: `export_markdown` writes `- Source type: <value>` only for nodes whose metadata contains `source_type`.

export-markdown-empty-network-handled.text: export_markdown accepts PG connection kwargs for an empty belief network and produces markdown without error.

export-markdown-flattens-justifications-.text: Multiple justifications are flattened into node-level `Depends on`, `Unless`, and `Defeated by` bullets, losing per-justification grouping in the Markdown output.

export-markdown-heading-encodes-status-a.text: Claim headings are asserted as `### <id> [<STATUS>] <TYPE>` with statuses `IN`, `OUT`, or `STALE` and types such as `OBSERVATION`, `DERIVED`, or `WARNING`.

export-markdown-includes-optional-node-m.text: The exporter is expected to emit metadata lines such as `- Source:`, `- Source hash:`, `- Date:`, `- Stale reason:`, and `- Superseded by:` when present.

export-markdown-is-pure-string-export.text: `export_markdown` returns a markdown string and performs no file I/O or network mutation.

export-markdown-maps-out-with-stale-or-r.text: A node with truth value `OUT` and metadata `stale_reason` or `retract_reason` is rendered with status `STALE`.

export-markdown-metadata-serialization-i.text: Only curated metadata fields are serialized, keeping the Markdown schema stable rather than dumping arbitrary node metadata.

export-markdown-nogood-id-uses-nogood-id.text: For `add_nogood(["a", "b"])`, Markdown export contains a `nogood-a-b` identifier under a `## Nogoods` section.

export-markdown-nogoods-preserve-network.text: Nogoods are emitted in `network.nogoods` order and are not sorted by ID.

export-markdown-orders-in-before-out.text: Within the `## Claims` section of `export_markdown` output, all `[IN]` node entries appear at a lower character offset than any `[OUT]` or `[STALE]` entry.

export-markdown-pg-reconstructs-network.text: The `export_markdown` PostgreSQL path reconstructs a full `Network` object from `export_network()` output — creating Node/Justification objects and wiring the dependents index — because the markdown exporter requires a wired dependency graph, not a flat dict.

export-markdown-repos-kwarg-emits-repos-.text: Passing `repos={...}` to `export_markdown` emits a `## Repos` section in the Markdown.

export-markdown-returns-string-with-no-i.text: `export_markdown` returns a Markdown string, performs no file I/O, and does not mutate the passed `Network`.

export-markdown-roundtrips-with-import-b.text: `reasons export-markdown` emits beliefs.md-compatible markdown that `reasons import-beliefs` consumes, with `nogoods.md` auto-detected as a sibling of `beliefs.md`.

export-markdown-section-ordering-is-fixe.text: The document structure follows the fixed order: `# Belief Registry` → `## Claims` (all node entries) → `## Nogoods` (if any nogoods exist); an empty network still emits the section headers.

export-markdown-shim-emits-no-deprecatio.text: Neither the import nor any access emits a warning; migration is enforced only by the docstring.

export-markdown-shim-is-covered-by-expor.text: Several exporter-related test modules load through `reasons_lib.export_markdown`, making the shim part of the regression surface for export, metadata, roundtrip, and source-type behavior.

export-markdown-shim-requires-reasons-ex.text: Importing `reasons_lib.export_markdown` raises immediately if `reasons.export_markdown` cannot be imported; failures are reported at line 2 of the shim.

export-markdown-sort-in-before-out.text: `export_markdown` sorts nodes by the composite key `(truth_value != "IN", id)`, guaranteeing all `IN` nodes appear before all `OUT`/`STALE` nodes with alphabetical tiebreaking — producing deterministic, diff-friendly output.

export-markdown-sorts-in-nodes-before-no.text: Claims are sorted with `truth_value == "IN"` first, then all non-IN nodes, alphabetically by node ID within each group.

export-markdown-splits-outlist-defeaters.text: Outlist nodes with defeater metadata render via `- Defeated by:`, while outlist nodes without defeater metadata render via `- Unless:`.

export-markdown-stale-status-precedes-ou.text: A node with `stale_reason` metadata renders as `[STALE]` rather than `[OUT]` in the tested stale/retracted scenario.

export-markdown-status-maps-truth-value.text: `export_markdown` uses `node.truth_value` as the status and only maps `OUT` to `STALE` when `stale_reason` or `retract_reason` metadata exists.

export-markdown-tests-bind-to-reasons-pa.text: The export-Markdown tests import `Justification`, `Network`, and `export_markdown` from the `reasons` package rather than `reasons_lib`, so they cover the `reasons` modules directly.

export-markdown-tests-target-reasons-pac.text: The test module imports `Justification`, `Network`, and `export_markdown` from the `reasons` package, not from `reasons_lib`.

export-markdown-type-inference-fallback.text: When `node.metadata["beliefs_type"]` is absent or empty, `export_markdown` infers the type as `DERIVED` if the node has at least one justification, or `OBSERVATION` otherwise — ensuring the output always conforms to the beliefs.md schema type token requirement.

export-markdown-unquoted-values-are-not-.text: Node text, IDs, reason strings, repo paths, and many metadata strings are not escaped before insertion into Markdown.

export-network-drops-restricted-nogoods.text: `export_network` removes a nogood when any referenced node is invisible to the caller.
