llm-subprocess-isolation-prevents-recurs.text: All LLM subprocess invocations strip the CLAUDECODE environment variable to prevent recursive Claude Code entry, enforced centrally in invoke_model() and inherited by all LLM-facing modules (ask, derive, review).

justifications.label: Centralized enforcement in invoke_model covers all LLM-facing modules

llm-subprocess-mock-requires-two-patches.text: Testing infrastructure detail (which objects to patch), not a production code invariant. The underlying fact about `shutil.which` + `subprocess.run` is already captured by `all-external-execution-is-subprocess-isolated` and `invoke-claude-raises-when-binary-missing`.

llm-thinking-strip-ollama-only.text: Thinking-marker stripping (`Thinking...` / `...done thinking.`) is applied only to Ollama model output; Claude and Gemini output passes through unmodified even if it contains the same markers.

llm-thinking-strip-requires-both-markers.text: invoke_model strips Ollama thinking output only when both 'Thinking...' and '...done thinking.' markers are present; partial markers leave output unchanged.

llm-three-error-types.text: Too granular — the three error types (ValueError, FileNotFoundError, RuntimeError) are implementation details of the error taxonomy already captured by existing beliefs about fail-fast and fail-soft behavior.

load-bypasses-add-node.text: `load()` constructs `Node` objects directly and calls `network._rebuild_dependents()` instead of using `Network.add_node`.

loaded-network-supports-further-inferenc.text: A `Network` returned by `Storage.load()` is a fully operational inference engine (retract, restore, and propagation all work), not a frozen read-only snapshot — the storage layer must reconstruct all internal graph links including SL/justification connections.

loaded-networks-remain-operational.text: A `Network` loaded from SQLite supports `retract` and `assert_node` with propagation to dependent nodes.

local-budget-floor-is-five.text: `TestBudgetFloor` asserts the local belief budget never drops below 5 when agents exceed the budget.

lookup-searches-all-terms-substring.text: `lookup()` performs an all-terms substring search across the full belief block, including ID, text, source, and dependencies.

main-blocks-on-run.text: `mcp.run()` is a blocking stdio transport loop, so `main` normally never returns during server operation.

main-dispatches-by-command-string-dict.text: `main()` routes subcommand execution through a `commands: dict[str, Callable]` table rather than `argparse.set_defaults(func=...)`.

main-exits-1-on-missing-subcommand.text: When `args.command` is `None`, `main` prints the help to stdout and calls `sys.exit(1)` rather than relying on argparse's `required=True`.

main-finds-db-without-validating-existen.text: `_find_db()` may return `api.DEFAULT_DB` for a path that does not exist; `main` does not verify the file is present or readable.

main-requires-global-flags-before-subcom.text: Global options (`--db`, `--pg`, `--version`, etc.) must precede the subcommand token because they are declared on the root parser, not passed through to subparsers.

main-requires-mcp-package.text: Importing `reasons.mcp_server` fails with `ImportError` if the `mcp` package is unavailable, before `main` can run.

main-resolves-db-before-run.text: `main` assigns `_db = _find_db()` before calling `mcp.run()`, so all tool calls use the same resolved path without re-running discovery.

main-resolves-db-eagerly.text: `main` assigns `_db` via `_find_db()` before calling `mcp.run()`, so all tool calls use the same path without re-discovery.

main-shares-db-with-get-db.text: `main` and `_get_db` intentionally share the module global `_db`, and `_get_db`'s `None`-check makes the eager assignment in `main` idempotent.

maintenance-loop-is-fully-observable.text: The minimality-sustained closed maintenance loop has complete observability: every self-correction leaves traceable history (nogoods, retraction records, staleness reports), enabling full audit of how the system maintains itself over time.

justifications.label: closed-loop maintenance combined with traceable correction history yields full observability of all maintenance activity

make-nodes-excludes-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a claim about production code behavior

make-nodes-omits-active-premises.text: Test helper implementation detail, not a production code invariant

malformed-pinned-lines-falls-back-to-has.text: A `pinned_lines` value that fails `int-int` parsing triggers the full-file hash path rather than silently succeeding (check_stale.py:110-113).

mark-duplicate-and-superseded-reject-sel.text: Both `mark_duplicate(x, x)` and `mark_superseded(x, x)` raise `ValueError` with a message indicating self-reference is forbidden, leaving the node in its original `IN` truth state unchanged.

mark-duplicate-overwrites-prior-retract-.text: Calling `mark_duplicate` or `mark_superseded` on a node that is already `OUT` (from a prior retraction) succeeds and overwrites the existing `retract_reason` metadata with the dedup/supersession-specific message (e.g., `"Duplicate of <canonical>"`) rather than failing or appending.

mark-duplicate-requires-existing-source-.text: `api.mark_duplicate` raises `KeyError("not found")` when either ID is missing.

mark-operations-overwrite-existing-retra.text: Marking an already-retracted node replaces its prior `retract_reason` with the duplicate/supersession reason.

mark-superseded-requires-existing-old-an.text: `api.mark_superseded` raises `KeyError("not found")` when either ID is missing.

markdown-export-maps-stale-metadata-to-s.text: When `export_markdown` sees an `OUT` node with `stale_reason` or `retract_reason` metadata, it emits `[STALE]` while the stored `truth_value` remains `OUT`.

markdown-export-nogood-section-is-networ.text: `export_markdown` appends a `## Nogoods` section only when `network.nogoods` is non-empty, and each nogood lists its affected node IDs under `Affects:`.

markdown-export-omits-empty-source-url-a.text: `export_markdown` omits the `- Source URL:` and `- Accepted PR:` lines when those fields are unset.

markdown-export-quotes-schema-version.text: Markdown frontmatter emits `schema_version: "1.0"` with the version value quoted.

markdown-frontmatter-is-first-block.text: Markdown exports begin at byte 0 with a `---`-delimited frontmatter block containing schema metadata.

markdown-frontmatter-is-yaml-at-byte-zer.text: `export_markdown(net)` output starts with `---\n` and YAML frontmatter; `strip_frontmatter` returns `(text, {})` when no such header exists.

markdown-frontmatter-roundtrip-preserves.text: `net.meta` keys survive the Markdown frontmatter export/import round-trip, with string values emitted quoted.

markdown-import-maps-unless-to-outlist.text: An exported `- Unless: <id>` line re-imports as `justifications[0].outlist == [<id>]`.

markdown-nogood-format-gap.text: Duplicate of existing belief `nogood-export-format-mismatch`; no new belief needed.

markdown-roundtrip-preserves-accepted-pr.text: The Markdown export→import pipeline preserves an `accepted_pr` value stored in `node.metadata`.

max-derivation-depth-counts-justificatio.text: `Max derivation depth` equals the longest chain of antecedent edges in the network (0 for premises-only, 1 for `d ← a`, 2 for `c ← b ← a`).

mcp-bridge-caches-tools-at-connect.text: `list_tools()` returns tool metadata cached during `connect()` and does not re-query the server afterward.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-joins-content-parts.text: `call_tool()` returns the MCP result as a single joined string of all content parts.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout.text: `call_tool()` blocks on the background future with a 60-second timeout and does not explicitly cancel the coroutine on timeout.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout-60s.text: `call_tool()` blocks for up to 60 seconds per invocation via `future.result(timeout=60)`; if the MCP server hangs, the calling thread unblocks with `TimeoutError`.

mcp-bridge-call-tool-timeout-is-60-secon.text: `McpBridge.call_tool` uses `future.result(timeout=60)`, raising `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` if the tool call exceeds 60 seconds.

mcp-bridge-close-joins-thread-with-5s-ti.text: `close()` signals `_shutdown`, joins the background thread with a 5-second timeout, then closes the event loop.

mcp-bridge-command-is-shell-string.text: `McpBridge.__init__` expects a single shell command string (e.g. `"npx @mcp/server-fs /path"`) which is parsed via `shlex.split`; passing a list of arguments directly is not supported.

mcp-bridge-command-parsed-with-shlex.text: `McpBridge` parses its command string with `shlex.split()` into argv for `StdioServerParameters`.

mcp-bridge-command-uses-shlex-no-shell.text: `McpBridge` parses its command with `shlex.split`; the first token is the executable and no shell is used.

mcp-bridge-connect-blocks-up-to-30s.text: `connect()` blocks the calling thread for up to 30 seconds waiting for MCP session initialization via `_ready.wait(timeout=30)`, then raises `TimeoutError` if the server doesn't respond.

mcp-bridge-connect-startup-timeout.text: `connect()` waits up to 30 seconds for server readiness and raises `TimeoutError` if `_ready` is not set.

mcp-bridge-duck-type-interface.text: The ask module's MCP dispatch expects any bridge object to implement `list_tools() → list[dict]`, `get_instructions() → str`, and `call_tool(name, arguments) → str`; no concrete class import is required.

mcp-bridge-get-instructions-returns-serv.text: `get_instructions()` returns the server-provided instructions string captured from `session.initialize()`.

mcp-bridge-implements-context-manager.text: `McpBridge` implements `__enter__` and `__exit__`, enabling `with McpBridge(command) as bridge:` for automatic connect/close.

mcp-bridge-is-deliberately-stateless-and.text: The MCP bridge is architecturally committed to simplicity over resilience: it is a one-shot session with no retry or reconnection, its tool catalog is a frozen snapshot taken at connect time, and its interface is duck-typed (no formal protocol) — trading operational robustness for predictability and minimal coupling.

justifications.label: Convergent design philosophy — each property independently supports the "deliberately ephemeral" characterization; the conclusion holds as long as any one of these constraints is in force, since each individually precludes long-lived stateful integration.

mcp-bridge-is-one-shot-session.text: `McpBridge` has no retry logic, no reconnection, and no health-check; if the MCP server dies mid-session, the caller must create a new `McpBridge` instance and call `connect()` again.

mcp-bridge-is-timeout-bounded-at-all-pha.text: MCP bridge operations are timeout-bounded at both connection establishment (30s) and per-tool execution (60s), preventing indefinite blocking on unresponsive MCP servers at any lifecycle phase.

justifications.label: Connection and execution timeouts independently bound both MCP lifecycle phases

mcp-bridge-pre-try-startup-errors-masked.text: Startup errors before the lifecycle `try` block are not stored in `_error`, so `connect()` may surface a 30-second timeout instead of the original exception.

mcp-bridge-propagates-background-init-er.text: If MCP session initialization fails on the background thread, `_session_lifecycle` stores the exception in `self._error` and sets `_ready`; `connect()` then re-raises it in the calling thread.

mcp-bridge-raises-exceptions-but-not-ise.text: Only Python exceptions from `session.call_tool` and `future.result(timeout=60)` propagate out of `McpBridge.call_tool`; an `isError=True` result does not raise.

mcp-bridge-requires-mcp-package.text: Constructing `McpBridge` raises `ImportError` when the optional `mcp` package is unavailable.

mcp-bridge-runs-dedicated-event-loop-thr.text: Each `McpBridge` instance runs its own asyncio event loop on a daemon thread; the MCP session stays alive until `close()` signals the shutdown event, bridging the sync/async boundary via `run_coroutine_threadsafe`.

mcp-bridge-stringifies-nontext-content-b.text: `_call_tool_async` appends `content.text` for blocks that have it and falls back to `str(content)` for non-text MCP content blocks.

mcp-bridge-tools-snapshot-at-connect.text: The tool catalog and server instructions are populated once during `connect()` and never refreshed — there is no mechanism to pick up tools added after the initial handshake.

mcp-client-does-not-reference-calltoolre.text: The codebase contains no explicit references to the `CallToolResult` type; it duck-types on `.content` and `.text` only

mcp-client-ignores-calltoolresult-iserro.text: `_call_tool_async` never reads `CallToolResult.isError`; tool-reported errors are returned to callers as ordinary text strings

mcp-client-shim-is-pure-star-reexport.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that every `reasons_lib` shim is a pure `from reasons.X import *` re-export with no local logic.

mcp-client-shim-propagates-import-errors.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that shims have no error handling and propagate canonical import failures unchanged.

mcp-db-discovery-precedence-env-then-cwd.text: `_find_db()` resolves the SQLite path with strict precedence: `REASONS_DB` environment variable, then walking up from `os.getcwd()`, then `api.DEFAULT_DB` — and `_get_db()` caches the result in the module-level `_db` attribute.

mcp-db-resolution-precedence.text: Database path resolution follows a strict order: `REASONS_DB` env var → walk up from `cwd` looking for `reasons.db` → `api.DEFAULT_DB`, with the result cached in a module-level `_db` singleton resolved at most once per process.

mcp-error-as-data-not-control-flow.text: Exceptions in MCP tool handlers are caught and serialized to `{"error": "..."}` JSON strings so the LLM receives a parseable recovery message; the MCP connection never dies from a tool exception.

mcp-falsy-to-none-idempotency.text: The MCP layer converts falsy sentinels (`0` for limit, `""` for optional string params like status/namespace) to `None` via `x or None` before calling `reasons.api` functions, which treat `None` as "no filter / no limit."

mcp-instructions-concatenated-across-bri.text: `_build_mcp_instructions` concatenates `get_instructions()` from all MCP bridges and returns an empty string when every bridge has empty instructions.

mcp-is-optional-dependency.text: The `mcp` package is guarded by try/except at import time; `_require_mcp()` defers the `ImportError` to `McpBridge` construction so the module can be imported unconditionally without the SDK installed.

mcp-names-only-handled-locally-for-lists.text: `list_beliefs`, `status`, and `list_gated` implement `output_format="names-only"` by post-processing API results, whereas `search` and `compact` forward `output_format` into the API.

mcp-read-only-tools-lack-error-wrapping.text: The read-only tools (`compact`, `search`, `list_beliefs`, `status`, `list_gated`, `export_markdown`, `topics`) have no try/except wrapper, so any `api` exception propagates as a raw MCP protocol-level error rather than a structured `{"error": "..."}` JSON response.

mcp-read-tools-propagate-exceptions.text: `search`, `list_beliefs`, `compact`, `list_proposals`, `status`, `list_gated`, `export_markdown`, and `topics` have no try/except and let exceptions surface to FastMCP, unlike mutating tools which return `{"error": ...}`.

mcp-server-delegates-all-mutations-to-ap.text: Every tool body calls a `reasons.api.*` function; no tool accesses the database directly.

mcp-server-docstrings-are-tool-schemas.text: FastMCP derives MCP tool names from function names and tool schemas/descriptions from signatures and docstring `Args:` blocks, making docstrings part of the public MCP contract.

mcp-server-errors-are-value-objects.text: Every failure path (missing id, bad state, invalid argument) is reported as `{"error": ...}` in the JSON payload, never by raising an exception.

mcp-server-import-requires-mcp-extra.text: Importing `reasons.mcp_server` raises `ImportError` if the `mcp` package is missing, directing users to install `ftl-reasons[mcp]`.

mcp-server-is-zero-logic-facade.text: `reasons/mcp_server.py` contains zero domain logic; every tool body is a one-or-two-line delegation into `reasons/api.*` with a try/except wrapper, and the module owns only wire-protocol serialization and DB path discovery.

mcp-server-names-only-formatting-is-loca.text: For `list_beliefs`, `status`, and `list_gated`, the MCP server handles `"names-only"` formatting locally; `search` and `compact` forward `output_format` into the API.

mcp-server-propose-update-stores-conditi.text: The `propose_update` tool calls `api.propose_update`, then optionally chains `api.store_llm_proposals` when `store` is true and proposals exist.

mcp-server-registers-tools-through-singl.text: All tool registration in `reasons/mcp_server.py` goes through the single module-level `mcp = FastMCP("reasons")` instance and its `@mcp.tool()` decorators.

mcp-server-stdio-purity-contract.text: The MCP server process must not emit anything to stdout other than JSON-RPC frames; any `print()` or stray output would corrupt the stdio transport and break the client, so `main()` and all tool handlers must avoid writing to stdout.

mcp-server-tests-enter-through-shim.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that deleting `reasons_lib` shims breaks test imports and that the test suite validates the shim import chain.

mcp-server-tools-are-tiered-facade.text: `reasons/mcp_server.py` organizes tools into four tiers: core, reasoning, proposals, and data management.

mcp-server-tools-return-json-strings.text: Every MCP tool in `mcp_server` returns a JSON-parseable `str`; `compact`, `export_markdown`, and any `output_format="names-only"` call are the only string-returning exceptions (non-JSON payloads).

mcp-server-uses-module-global-db-cache.text: `mcp_server._db` is a module-level cache consulted by `_get_db()`; setting it in a fixture bypasses filesystem discovery.

mcp-server-what-if-supersede-requires-te.text: The `what_if` MCP tool requires non-empty `text` when `action=="supersede"` and otherwise returns a structured error.

mcp-servers-bump-max-iterations-to-five.text: When `mcp_servers` is non-empty, `ask()` allows up to 5 tool rounds, so `invoke_model` is called at most 6 times.

mcp-supports-sse-and-streamable-http-tra.text: MCP supports two HTTP transports: SSE and Streamable HTTP.

mcp-tool-errors-are-swallowed.text: Exceptions raised by `bridge.call_tool` are caught inside `ask()` (recorded in tool history) and never propagate to the caller.

mcp-tool-json-renders-no-trailing-comma.text: When a MCP tool has zero parameters, `_build_tools_section` renders the JSON example as `'{"tool": "name"}'` (no trailing comma), preventing LLM JSON-parser failures.

mcp-tool-registration-requires-mcp-extra.text: Importing `reasons/mcp_server.py` requires the optional `mcp>=1.0` extra declared in `pyproject.toml`; otherwise the module raises a targeted `ImportError` before any tool is registered.

mcp-tools-never-raise-return-error-json.text: Every MCP tool function in `reasons/mcp_server.py` catches internal exceptions and returns a JSON string containing `{"error": "<message>"}` rather than raising — the protocol contract is "JSON-or-text, never an exception."

mcp-tools-return-strings-only.text: All MCP tool handlers in `reasons/mcp_server.py` return `str` (JSON-dumped or markdown); no structured type crosses the MCP boundary, a requirement of the `FastMCP` tool contract.

mcpbridge-caches-tools-at-connect.text: Tool metadata is fetched once during `connect()` and returned from `list_tools()` without re-querying the server.

mcpbridge-call-tool-flattens-content.text: `call_tool()` returns newline-joined text or stringified content from the MCP `CallToolResult`.

mcpbridge-close-uses-thread-safe-signali.text: `close()` sets the asyncio shutdown event through `loop.call_soon_threadsafe`.

mcpbridge-keeps-session-open-until-shutd.text: `_session_lifecycle` awaits `_shutdown.wait()` inside the `stdio_client` and `ClientSession` context managers to keep the MCP session alive.

mcpbridge-requires-mcp-package.text: Constructing `McpBridge` raises `ImportError` when the optional `mcp` package is unavailable.

memo-pre-set-prevents-infinite-recursion.text: `memo[nid]` is set to `0` before recursing, which terminates cycles but can undercount depth in cyclic graphs.

merkle-antecedents-sorted-for-determinis.text: In `_fresh_content_hash`, antecedent Merkle hashes are collected and `sorted(...)` before concatenation, guaranteeing the content hash is identical regardless of the order antecedents appear in the justification's list.

merkle-backfill-can-assign-hashes-to-cyc.text: `backfill_hashes` calls `compute_content_hash` for missing justification hashes, so cyclic justifications can receive normal-looking hashes instead of being reported as invalid.

merkle-backfill-is-lossless.text: After `backfill_hashes()` fills empty `text_hash`/`content_hash` fields, a subsequent `check_integrity()` reports zero missing hashes and zero mutations — the backfill operation is idempotent and produces a clean graph.

merkle-backfill-only-fills-missing-hashe.text: `backfill_hashes` fills only missing `text_hash` and `content_hash` values; it never overwrites existing or stale hashes.

merkle-content-hash-is-order-independent.text: Justification content hashes sort antecedent Merkle hashes before joining them, so antecedent order does not affect the hash.

merkle-cycle-produces-empty-string-hash.text: A cyclic justification chain does not raise or loop infinitely; `_fresh_merkle_hash` detects the cycle via the `visiting` set and returns `sha256("")` (hash of empty string), silently weakening the integrity guarantee without crashing.

merkle-cycle-safety-test-asserts-clean-r.text: The actual assertions in `test_cycle_safety` are outside the observed excerpt; only the visible docstring saying it checks for infinite loops was observed.

merkle-duplicate-antecedents-not-dedupli.text: Duplicate antecedent IDs are not deduplicated when computing a justification content hash; each occurrence contributes its hash.

merkle-fresh-computation-is-non-circular.text: The `_fresh_merkle_hash` and `_fresh_content_hash` functions compute hashes exclusively from `node.text` and network topology; they never read `node.text_hash` or `justification.content_hash` from the network, ensuring verification compares a freshly-derived value against the stored one.

merkle-hash-follows-single-justification.text: The Merkle hash for a node incorporates only its `supporting_justification` and that justification's antecedents recursively; other justifications on the same node do not affect the computed hash, making the integrity guarantee per-path rather than per-node.

merkle-hash-follows-supporting-justifica.text: A node’s Merkle hash only incorporates its `supporting_justification`; alternate justifications do not affect that node hash.

merkle-missing-antecedents-are-omitted.text: `_fresh_content_hash` filters antecedents to those present in `net.nodes`, silently omitting missing antecedent IDs.

merkle-missing-hashes-are-not-findings.text: `verify_all` counts missing hashes in `missing_hashes` and does not emit findings for them; missing hashes are treated as unverified, not mismatched.

merkle-module-is-stdlib-only.text: `reasons/merkle.py` imports only `hashlib` from the standard library with zero third-party or intra-package dependencies, enabling isolated unit testing and reuse without pulling in the full network stack.

merkle-mutation-detection-is-transitive-.text: A single leaf-node text mutation cascades up the DAG: `check_integrity` flags all transitive ancestors (not just direct dependents) as chain mutations, because each ancestor's `content_hash` incorporates its child's hash.

merkle-py-is-present-only-in-reasons.text: `merkle.py` exists in `reasons/` but not in `reasons_lib/`, making it the module-level asymmetry between the two packages.

merkle-supporting-justification-assumed-.text: `_fresh_merkle_hash` assumes `supporting_justification` is either `None` or a valid index; invalid values can raise `IndexError` or use Python negative indexing unexpectedly.

merkle-verification-never-raises.text: `verify_node`, `verify_justification`, and `verify_all` never raise exceptions; they return `None` (clean) or a structured finding dict with a `"type"` discriminator (`"text_mutation"` or `"chain_mutation"`), making all integrity issues data rather than control flow.

metadata-actively-governs-truth-propagat.text: Lifecycle state carried in node metadata (retraction flags, stale reasons) is not passive storage but actively governs truth propagation behavior — retracted nodes are skipped during BFS traversal and trigger nodes are never recomputed — ensuring that the universal extension mechanism directly controls truth maintenance rather than merely recording state

justifications.label: Metadata extensibility means any lifecycle concern can be expressed as a metadata key, and propagation's lifecycle awareness means that metadata directly influences truth computation — the combination closes the loop between state representation and state enforcement

metadata-created-at-preservation-contrac.text: If the caller passes a non-empty `created_at` string, it is preserved verbatim as the original creation timestamp; if empty or `None`, current UTC time is used. `updated_at` is always current UTC regardless of caller input, so the two diverge on re-export.

metadata-enables-lifecycle-governance-be.text: Node metadata enables lifecycle governance capabilities that transcend the binary IN/OUT truth model: extensible metadata provides structured lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags, supersession markers) that actively governs both read and write paths, while staleness information is preserved and surfaced in compact output despite having no dedicated truth state in the TMS data model.

justifications.label: Metadata governance (depth-4) and staleness surfacing (depth-3) together show metadata compensates for the binary truth model's expressiveness limitations

metadata-generator-degrades-to-unknown.text: `_get_generator()` wraps `importlib.metadata.version("ftl-reasons")` in a `try/except Exception`; any failure (including `PackageNotFoundError`) results in `"ftl-reasons/unknown"` rather than raising, ensuring metadata stamping never blocks an export.

metadata-generator-version-lookup-is-laz.text: `_get_generator()` imports `importlib.metadata.version` inside the function, so importing `metadata` does not require installed distribution metadata.

metadata-governance-flows-through-safe-t.text: Metadata-carried lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags) actively governs truth propagation that is itself topology-complete and inconsistency-safe — lifecycle decisions propagate through all transitive dependencies including outlist-connected paths, even in the presence of dangling references, without runtime errors.

justifications.label: Active metadata governance combined with inconsistency-safe topology-complete propagation

metadata-governance-has-topology-complet.text: The rich lifecycle state carried in metadata — retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags — participates in topology-complete robust propagation that reaches all transitively dependent nodes under all graph conditions, ensuring lifecycle governance decisions cascade completely through the network rather than stopping at direct dependents.

justifications.label: Metadata governance and topology-complete propagation are independently established; combining shows lifecycle decisions (retraction pins, access tag inheritance, staleness) cascade completely and robustly through the full dependency graph

metadata-governed-modifications-are-bidi.text: Bidirectional belief modifications — contradiction resolution and defeat reversal — propagate metadata-governed lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, access tags) topology-completely within a deterministic lifecycle, ensuring every modification in either direction carries complete metadata through the entire dependency graph with no governance gap between forward and backward changes.

justifications.label: Both beliefs share topology-complete propagation within deterministic lifecycle; combining reveals bidirectional modifications are fully metadata-governed

metadata-governs-lifecycle-across-read-a.text: Node lifecycle state carried in metadata actively governs both mutation behavior (retracted nodes skipped during truth propagation, sticky retraction surviving recompute) and inspection behavior (staleness checking skips OUT nodes, compact surfaces stale reasons) — a single metadata mechanism controls the system's complete operational surface.

justifications.label: Write-path governance (depth-2) and read-path governance (depth-2) share the same metadata fields, making lifecycle a unified cross-cutting concern rather than two independent implementations.

metadata-is-single-source-of-truth-for-e.text: Six production modules (`api.py`, `cli.py`, `export_card.py`, `export_markdown.py`, `pg.py`, `storage.py`) all call `build_meta()` rather than constructing the metadata dict inline, centralizing the schema to prevent field-name drift across export formats.

metadata-is-universal-extension-mechanis.text: Node metadata is the universal extension mechanism carrying all structured lifecycle state (retraction flags, stale reasons, challenges, access tags, supersession markers), and retraction flags pinned in metadata survive recomputation to enforce sticky retraction.

justifications.label: Metadata carries structured state AND survives recomputation — it is both the carrier and the enforcer of lifecycle semantics

metadata-module-is-formatter-not-validat.text: `build_meta()` contains no `raise` statements and performs no input validation; passing `node_count=-1`, `project_name=None`, or a non-ISO `created_at` string will not trigger an error — input correctness is the caller's responsibility.

metadata-new-record-timestamps-are-ident.text: `build_meta` computes `now` once; for falsey `created_at`, both `created_at` and `updated_at` receive the same value.

metadata-provides-extensible-lifecycle-g.text: Node metadata is simultaneously the universal extension mechanism for network state (carrying all structured lifecycle properties with consistent audit tracking) and the active governor of truth propagation behavior across both read and write paths — retracted and stale nodes are skipped in propagation and staleness checking respectively, driven by the same metadata fields.

justifications.label: Metadata is not merely storage — it both defines extensible state and actively constrains system behavior, making it the unifying mechanism for state management and lifecycle governance.

metadata-schema-version-is-1-0.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION` is asserted equal to `"1.0"` and is stored in SQLite `network_meta` and exported metadata.

metadata-schema-version-is-hardcoded.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION` is a hardcoded `"1.0"` module constant and is independent of the installed package version.

metadata-shim-emits-no-deprecation-signa.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that importing any `reasons_lib` shim emits no `DeprecationWarning` or runtime migration signal.

metadata-shim-is-backward-compatibility-.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that `reasons_lib/<module>.py` is a pure compatibility alias re-exporting `reasons/<module>.py`.

metadata-timestamps-are-utc-second-preci.text: Generated metadata timestamps use `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")`, producing UTC ISO-8601 strings with seconds precision.

metadata-updated-at-is-always-regenerate.text: `build_meta` always regenerates `updated_at` from the current UTC time; callers cannot supply or preserve it.

migrate-defeaters-distinguishes-noncandi.text: A node with no `retract_reason` is not a candidate and is omitted from `skipped`, while a node with `retract_reason` but an unsatisfied antecedent is reported in `skipped`.

migrate-defeaters-node-id-filter-limits-.text: When `node_ids` is supplied to `migrate_retract_to_defeaters`, only the listed candidates are migrated and non-listed candidates keep their `retract_reason`.

migrate-defeaters-preserves-target-out-a.text: After a successful non-dry-run migration, the original target node remains `OUT`; only the retraction representation changes.

migrate-defeaters-unknown-node-ids-are-n.text: `migrate_retract_to_defeaters` reports unknown `node_ids` under `errors` instead of raising an exception.

migrate-returns-structured-result.text: `migrate_retract_to_defeaters` always returns a dict with `migrated`, `skipped`, and `errors` keys and never raises on unknown `node_ids`.

migrated-defeater-id-format-is-determini.text: Defeater IDs follow `migrated-retraction-{node_id}-j{index}`; `-j0` for the first justification.

migrated-retraction-agent-beliefs-underg.text: Invalid: missing bridge between agent subsystem and general revision system (defeats agent-beliefs-undergo-full-revision justification 0)

migrated-retraction-all-identification-i.text: review-beliefs: "Collision-free" is strictly stronger than the "consistent, referenceable identification" established by the antecedents — addressability does not imply collision prevention across identifier spaces. (defeats all-identification-is-deterministic-and-collision-free justification 0)

migrated-retraction-all-llm-interactions.text: review-beliefs: The claim attributes environment isolation to both paths, but only the derive antecedent mentions it; additionally "All LLM-facing operations" is overclaimed when review and list-negative modules are unaddressed. (defeats all-llm-interactions-are-bounded-and-fail-soft justification 0)

migrated-retraction-all-network-modifica.text: Invalid: doesn't cover import operations (defeats all-network-modifications-are-auditable-and-topology-preserving justification 0)

migrated-retraction-api-enforces-typed-p.text: review-beliefs: Three specific boundary validations demonstrate a pattern but cannot establish the claim of "consistent error contract at every entry point" without enumerating all entry points. (defeats api-enforces-typed-preconditions justification 0)

migrated-retraction-architecture-has-no-.text: review-beliefs: Two positive safety properties and one gated known fragility cannot prove the universal negative "no hidden consistency hazards" — absence of evidence for other fragilities is not evidence of their absence. (defeats architecture-has-no-hidden-fragility justification 0)

migrated-retraction-ask-degrades-across-.text: review-beliefs: The claim describes FTS5 degradation via "self-healing derived index with substring fallback" but neither antecedent establishes this mechanism — the first antecedent only describes falling back TO FTS5, not handling FTS5's own failure. (defeats ask-degrades-across-all-external-dependencies justification 0)

migrated-retraction-batch-fault-isolatio.text: review-beliefs: The review antecedent describes per-batch skipping (entire batch dropped on LLM failure), which contradicts the claim of fault isolation at the "individual item level." (defeats batch-fault-isolation-is-universal-across-llm-operations justification 0)

migrated-retraction-both-revision-paths-.text: Invalid: over-generalizes from 2 specific properties to all system invariants (defeats both-revision-paths-preserve-system-invariants justification 0)

migrated-retraction-budget-enforcement-i.text: Invalid: universalizes floor bounds to all budget operations when only derive has floor-5 (defeats budget-enforcement-is-efficient-across-pipeline justification 0)

migrated-retraction-bulk-operations-pres.text: review-beliefs: The import antecedent establishes dual reconciliation modes and truth state handling but does not mention rewiring justification references (antecedent or outlist), which the claim attributes to both operations. (defeats bulk-operations-preserve-topology-and-reconcile justification 0)

migrated-retraction-cli-is-pure-delegati.text: review-beliefs: The claim includes "producing binary exit codes and correct stream separation" which neither antecedent establishes — delegation and flat dispatch do not entail specific exit code semantics or stream routing. (defeats cli-is-pure-delegation-layer justification 0)

migrated-retraction-compact-budget-contr.text: review-beliefs: The first antecedent presupposes budget truncation works ("survive budget truncation") rather than establishing it, making the derivation circular; the summary-hiding antecedent describes a scenario where output grows, not how the budget constrains it. (defeats compact-budget-controls-output-size justification 0)

migrated-retraction-compact-is-efficient.text: Invalid: claims no trade-offs but chars/4 is explicitly an accuracy trade-off (defeats compact-is-efficient-deterministic-and-bounded justification 0)

migrated-retraction-context-agnosticism-.text: False causal claim: context-agnosticism comes from evaluation purity, not from minimality. They co-occur but are not causally linked. (defeats context-agnosticism-follows-from-minimality justification 0)

migrated-retraction-critical-operations-.text: review-beliefs: Individual convergence of three operations does not establish the system-level claim of reaching stable state "regardless of operation ordering" — without commutativity or serialization guarantees, interleaved operations could produce different fixed points. (defeats critical-operations-converge-to-fixed-points justification 0)

migrated-retraction-derive-pipeline-is-e.text: Invalid: cycle guard in _get_depth != termination of exhaust loop (defeats derive-pipeline-is-exhaustive-and-terminating justification 0)

migrated-retraction-derive-pipeline-is-p.text: review-beliefs: The claim asserts the pipeline "correctly allocates budgets" but neither antecedent establishes budget allocation correctness — the defensive antecedent covers validation and the prompt antecedent covers serialization format. (defeats derive-pipeline-is-production-ready justification 0)

migrated-retraction-dispute-resolution-i.text: Invalid: traceability not established for dialectical path (defeats dispute-resolution-is-complete-and-reliable justification 0)

migrated-retraction-every-mutation-repor.text: review-beliefs: Three mutation-reporting mechanisms are demonstrated but the universal claim "All mutating operations" is not established — add_node, propagate, dedup, and import mutations are not shown to report their effects. (defeats every-mutation-reports-its-effects justification 0)

migrated-retraction-external-belief-inge.text: review-beliefs: The claim that both paths "converge on the same underlying mutation infrastructure" is not stated in or derivable from either antecedent — each antecedent describes its own defense mechanisms without addressing shared infrastructure. (defeats external-belief-ingestion-is-defensively-layered justification 0)

migrated-retraction-minimality-produces-.text: review-beliefs: Antecedent 1 establishes minimality→uniformity, but antecedent 2 presents minimality and determinism as co-existing properties that are *unified* in the system, not as one generating the other — the BFS fixpoint and conservative failure semantics are independent operational design choices, not consequences of semantic minimality, so the claim that minimality is the 'shared generative root' of determinism is an unsupported causal upgrade from co-occurrence to generation. (defeats minimality-produces-uniformity-and-determinism justification 0)

migrated-retraction-negative-semantics-a.text: Internal contradiction: claims 'permanent identity effects from challenge' but antecedent (negative-semantics-are-complete-reversible-and-recoverable) characterizes negative semantics as fully reversible and recoverable (defeats negative-semantics-are-uniform-through-minimality justification 0)

migrated-retraction-premise-identity-is-.text: review-beliefs: The claim references 'dialectical challenge' and 'defend' as transformation mechanisms while the antecedents only establish add_justification, and the 'irreversibly' qualifier is not established — convert-to-premise could reverse the transformation (defeats premise-identity-is-inherently-transient justification 0)

migrated-retraction-propagation-automati.text: review-beliefs: The inference relies on the unstated assumption that propagation traverses the dependents index to reach all affected nodes — TMS background knowledge not captured in either antecedent (defeats propagation-automatically-cascades-on-all-truth-changes justification 0)

migrated-retraction-revision-is-lifecycl.text: Invalid: cross-applies properties between mechanisms without support (defeats revision-is-lifecycle-safe-and-semantics-preserving justification 0)

migrated-retraction-rich-governance-emer.text: Invalid: metadata/governance is additional machinery beyond minimal TMS primitives, not emergent from them (defeats rich-governance-emerges-from-minimal-foundations justification 0)

migration-clears-both-retraction-metadat.text: `migrate_retract_to_defeaters` atomically removes both `retract_reason` and `_retracted` from the target node's metadata; clearing only one constitutes a half-migrated state and is a bug.

migration-clears-legacy-metadata.text: Both `retract_reason` and `_retracted` are removed from the target on successful migration.

migration-defeater-id-encodes-justificat.text: The migrated defeater node ID is always `f"migrated-retraction-{source_node_id}-j0"` where `-j0` denotes justification index 0, making the ID deterministic and referenceable for reversal.

migration-dry-run-is-pure-read.text: `migrate_retract_to_defeaters(dry_run=True)` must not create any defeater node nor mutate any existing node's metadata; it is a pure read that only reports candidate counts.

migration-is-reversible.text: Retracting a migrated defeater (`retract_node("migrated-retraction-...")`) flips the original target back to `IN`.

migration-preserves-truth-value.text: After migration, the target node's `truth_value` remains `"OUT"`; only its metadata and a new defeater node change.

migration-requires-satisfied-justificati.text: An OUT node whose antecedents are themselves OUT (unsatisfied justification) is placed in `result["skipped"]` and not migrated, because its OUT state is explained by the collapsed support chain rather than a retraction reason.

migration-reversibility-through-defeater.text: After successful migration, the defeater node is the exclusive causal reason for the target's OUT state; retracting the defeater must restore the target to IN, guaranteeing lossless reversibility.

mind-api-key-authorization-bearer.text: `fetch_export` and `push_belief` send `MIND_API_KEY` as an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header.

mind-api-key-is-bearer-token.text: `fetch_export` and `push_belief` send `MIND_API_KEY` as an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header.

mind-env-config-has-no-nonempty-default.text: The Mind service environment fallback is an empty string with no non-empty built-in default, so missing values must be supplied by arguments or environment or `_resolve_config` fails.

mind-env-vars-read-at-resolve-time.text: `reasons.mind_service._resolve_config()` reads `MIND_SERVICE_URL`, `MIND_AGENT_ID`, and `MIND_API_KEY` from `os.environ` when called, not at module import time.

mind-env-vars-unset-in-ci-and-docs.text: The checked-in docs and `.github/workflows/tests.yml` do not set or reference `MIND_SERVICE_URL`, `MIND_AGENT_ID`, or `MIND_API_KEY`; tests set/clear them only with `monkeypatch`.

mind-service-404-handling-is-asymmetric.text: `fetch_export` special-cases HTTP 404 as a `RuntimeError` with a friendly message, but `push_belief` does not catch 404 — a 404 on the push endpoint propagates as a raw `HTTPError` to the caller.

mind-service-client-is-pure-stdlib.text: The module imports only from `json`, `os`, and `urllib.*`; no third-party HTTP library is required.

mind-service-client-is-stdlib-only.text: `reasons/mind_service.py` imports only stdlib modules (`json`, `os`, `urllib.*`) and requires no third-party HTTP library.

mind-service-config-explicit-overrides-e.text: `_resolve_config` gives explicit `url`, `agent_id`, and `api_key` arguments precedence over `MIND_SERVICE_URL`, `MIND_AGENT_ID`, and `MIND_API_KEY`.

mind-service-config-precedence-explicit-.text: `_resolve_config` resolves parameters in strict precedence order (explicit keyword args > `MIND_SERVICE_URL`/`MIND_AGENT_ID`/`MIND_API_KEY` env vars), and raises `RuntimeError` if `url` or `agent_id` is unresolvable after both lookups.

mind-service-config-resolution-prefers-e.text: `_resolve_config` gives explicit function arguments precedence over the corresponding `MIND_*` environment variables.

mind-service-config-strips-trailing-slas.text: `_resolve_config` strips a trailing slash from the configured mind-service URL before endpoint construction.

mind-service-http-endpoints-are-agent-ex.text: The mind-service client fetches exports via `GET {base}/api/agents/{agent_id}/export` and pushes beliefs via `POST {base}/api/agents/{agent_id}/beliefs`.

mind-service-missing-config-is-aggregate.text: `_resolve_config` collects all missing fields and raises a single `RuntimeError` rather than failing on the first.

mind-service-requests-use-bearer-auth.text: Every outbound mind-service HTTP request carries an `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` header.

mind-service-resolved-url-strips-trailin.text: `_resolve_config` always strips trailing `/` from the resolved URL before returning it.

mind-service-shim-is-load-bearing-for-re.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that `reasons/api.py` imports through `reasons_lib` and that removing the shims would break internal production code.

mind-service-symbols-are-identical-acros.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that shim re-exports preserve object identity across `reasons` and `reasons_lib` import paths.

mind-service-symbols-are-identity-equal-.text: Names imported from `reasons_lib.mind_service` and `reasons.mind_service` resolve to the identical objects, so `isinstance` and equality checks work across both paths.

mind-service-url-strips-trailing-slash.text: `_resolve_config` always strips a trailing slash from the base URL before it is used for path concatenation, preventing double-slash URLs like `//api/agents/...`.

mind-service-url-trailing-slashes-stripp.text: `_resolve_config()` strips trailing slashes from the resolved Mind service URL.

mind-service-uses-stdlib-http-only.text: `reasons/mind_service.py` uses `urllib.request` for all HTTP operations; it has zero third-party HTTP dependencies (no `requests`, `httpx`, etc.), keeping it deployable in minimal environments.

minimality-generates-universal-revision-.text: Universal revision safety is a consequence of minimality: the system has no revision blind spots because both uniform edge-case handling and comprehensive lifecycle coverage emerge from the same minimal primitives that power truth maintenance — minimality does not merely simplify the design but actively prevents the coverage gaps that would arise from feature-specific revision paths.

justifications.label: both universal coverage and uniform handling trace to same minimal source (depth-6 from two depth-5 IN)

metadata.retract_reason: Invalid: causal overclaim from edge-case uniformity to universal revision safety

minimality-is-both-generative-and-unifyi.text: Minimality is simultaneously the generative source of each individual system property (extensibility, robustness, revision completeness) and the unifying principle that makes them cohere — the system achieves unity not by coordinating independently-designed features but because every feature is a different manifestation of the same minimal primitive set.

justifications.label: depth-7 nodes establish minimality as generative and design as unifying independently; combining reveals they are the same fact from different vantage points

minimality-is-self-sustaining.text: Minimality is a fixed point: it generates the closed forward/backward maintenance loop and the self-correction mechanisms that actively maintain that loop, so the generative principle sustains itself through its own consequences.

justifications.label: self-correction preserves the loop that minimality generates, closing the generative circle

minimality-is-the-universal-generative-p.text: Minimality is the single generative architectural principle underlying all emergent system properties — extensibility and robustness arise from transparent extension composition on the minimal core, while revision completeness arises from uniform edge-case handling within the same core — revealing that these typically independent qualities share a common origin rather than requiring separate design effort.

justifications.label: Both depth-6 conclusions independently derive different system properties from the same minimal core; combining them reveals minimality as a universal generative principle rather than multiple independent design decisions

minimality-produces-uniformity-and-deter.text: Minimality is the shared generative root of two independently-established system properties: edge-case uniformity (all cases handled by the same rules without special-casing) and operational determinism (predictable terminating evaluation with conservative failure), demonstrating that a single design principle produces both semantic and operational guarantees simultaneously.

justifications.label: Two independent consequences of minimality — one semantic, one operational — confirm it as the single generative principle

minimality-spans-computation-and-revisio.text: Minimality is the shared generative root of both forward and backward system properties: forward computation achieves uniformity and determinism, backward revision achieves universal safety covering all edge cases and lifecycle states — the same minimal primitives produce correctness in both directions without requiring separate design efforts or independent correctness arguments.

justifications.label: forward computation correctness and backward revision safety both trace to minimality (depth-7 from depth-6 IN + depth-5 IN)

minimality-sustains-closed-loop-maintena.text: Minimality generates both forward computation properties (uniformity, determinism) and backward revision properties (universal safety), while lifecycle management ensures every generated belief remains under active maintenance with no escape path — together forming a self-sustaining architecture where the generative principle and the maintenance loop are co-dependent.

justifications.label: The two depth-7 IN beliefs represent complementary halves — one establishing minimality as the shared root of computation and revision, the other closing the loop so no belief escapes maintenance; their conjunction is a self-sustaining system

minimality-yields-extensibility-and-robu.text: The minimal core simultaneously enables two independent emergent properties — transparent extension composition (dialectics, multi-agent federation) and uniform edge-case handling (vacuous premises, asymmetric absence) — demonstrating that minimality is operationally productive, not merely aesthetically elegant.

justifications.label: Both depth-5 claims trace back to the same minimal outlist/disjunction primitives but manifest in independent dimensions (extensibility vs. robustness); combining reveals that minimality has a multiplicative rather than singular payoff

missing-antecedent-yields-zero.text: An antecedent id absent from `nodes` is silently scored as depth `0` rather than raising.

missing-belief-raises-keyerror.text: `api.report_belief` raises `KeyError` for a nonexistent belief ID.

missing-frontmatter-preserves-existing-m.text: Importing Markdown without frontmatter leaves existing `project_name` metadata unchanged.

missing-fts-schema-raises-operational-er.text: Passing a SQLite path without the expected `chunks_fts` table raises `sqlite3.OperationalError`.

missing-graph-references-raise-keyerror.text: `challenge` and `defend` both raise `KeyError` (not a custom exception, not a silent no-op) when the target or challenge node is absent.

missing-mind-config-raises-runtimeerror.text: `_resolve_config` raises `RuntimeError` naming each missing url/agent-id/api-key before network calls proceed.

missing-node-entrenchment-is-zero.text: `_entrenchment()` returns `0` for a missing node ID, which is strictly lower than any existing node's minimum score of `20`.

missing-node-scores-zero.text: A nonexistent `node_id` returns `0`, strictly lower than any existing node's minimum score of `20`.

missing-nodes-have-asymmetric-fail-seman.text: Missing nodes are treated asymmetrically: absent antecedents fail validation (conservative), absent outlist nodes pass (permissive), creating a "believe unless proven otherwise" default

justifications.label: The asymmetry is consistent across all three beliefs and encodes a deliberate epistemic stance

missing-outlist-node-counts-as-out.text: A nonexistent outlist node is treated as `OUT`, so it does not block the default justification.

missing-outlist-nodes-are-out.text: A nonexistent outlist node is treated as `OUT` and does not block the justification.

missing-outlist-nodes-pass-validation.text: In `_justification_valid`, missing antecedent nodes cause the check to fail (node goes OUT), but missing outlist nodes pass (don't block) — an open-world default.

missing-premise-nodes-silently-omitted.text: A `premise_id` absent from `nodes` produces an empty formatted chunk and no corresponding result entry, with no warning emitted.

missing-source-file-is-silent.text: If a node's source file no longer exists on disk, `check_stale` silently skips it; callers cannot distinguish "file deleted" from "file never tracked."

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #32

missing-source-produces-source-deleted.text: A tracked node whose source file is absent produces a `check_stale` result with reason `source_deleted`.

missing-source-produces-source-deleted-r.text: `check_stale` reports a node whose resolved source file is missing with `reason == "source_deleted"`, `new_hash is None`, and `source_path is None`.

model-string-grammar-is-closed-set.text: Valid model strings for `invoke_model` are exactly: `claude`, `gemini`, `claude:<sub>`, `gemini:<sub>`, `ollama:<model>`, `api:<model>`, `vertex:<model>`, `openai:<model>`; any other form raises `ValueError` from `resolve_model_cmd`.

module-is-a-validation-free-schema-layer.text: The file defines no `__post_init__`, no methods, and no validation, so invalid states such as an out-of-range `supporting_justification` or an unknown `truth_value` are constructible without error.

multi-agent-reasoning-is-sound-and-scala.text: The system provides both individually sound reasoning (deterministic, reversible, terminating truth maintenance) and safe multi-agent operation (isolated namespaces, reversible lifecycle control, clean architectural boundaries), enabling arbitrarily many agents without sacrificing correctness guarantees.

justifications.label: Per-agent soundness (depth-3) + cross-agent isolation (depth-3) together establish that correctness is preserved as agent count scales

multi-agent-revision-is-semantically-uni.text: Multi-agent operation does not carve out exceptions to the universal revision semantics — agent beliefs undergo the same uniform revision (outlist defeat, contradiction backtracking, edge-case handling) as local beliefs because agent namespacing and relay pairs operate above the evaluation layer, not within it.

justifications.label: Connects the multi-agent soundness story with the revision universality story; agent isolation mechanisms are orthogonal to revision evaluation, so universality extends across agent boundaries without special cases

multi-agent-safety-spans-all-layers.text: Multi-agent operation is safe across the full system: agent isolation prevents cross-contamination between namespaces with reversible lifecycle control, while data integrity is enforced across all three architectural layers through clean boundaries and snapshot persistence.

justifications.label: Agent self-containment provides logical isolation; architectural data integrity provides physical isolation — together they prevent both semantic and structural cross-agent corruption

multiline-example-lines-are-indented.text: Multiline examples are displayed with each example line prefixed by two spaces.

multiple-eems-merge-into-single-reasons-.text: Multiple EEM repositories can be imported into a single reasons.db, where shared node IDs connect across networks and contradictions are detected as nogoods.

multiple-justifications-are-alternative-.text: A node with two valid justifications remains `IN` after one supporting antecedent is retracted.

multiple-justifications-or-semantics.text: A node with N justifications stays `IN` while at least one justification remains valid, and flips `OUT` only after the last valid justification is defeated.

multiple-outlist-is-conjunction.text: When a justification has multiple outlist entries, ALL must be OUT for the justification to be valid; any single outlist node going IN defeats the entire justification

mutation-methods-preserve-dependents-int.text: `add_node`, `retract`/`assert_node`, `add_justification`, `supersede`, `challenge`/`defend`, `convert_to_premise`, `add_nogood`, and `summarize` are covered and leave the index clean.

mutation-pipeline-is-atomic-snapshot.text: Every network mutation follows an atomic snapshot pipeline: API context management ensures load/save atomicity with write-flag gating, while storage performs full-replace persistence — no partial state is ever visible between operations.

justifications.label: API atomicity and snapshot storage together guarantee no partial-write visibility

mutation-pipeline-produces-consistent-st.text: Every mutation produces a fully consistent persisted network: atomic load/save ensures no partial writes, deterministic propagation ensures all truth values are correctly derived, and lifecycle-aware traversal prevents stale recomputations.

justifications.label: End-to-end mutation safety is contingent on the denormalized dependents index staying consistent and all dependent references being valid

mutation-safety-spans-all-dimensions.text: Every mutation is safe along three orthogonal dimensions simultaneously: source dimension (human, LLM, or agent), semantic dimension (uniform revision via outlist defeat and backtracking), and lifecycle dimension (respects retraction state and propagation bounds) — no mutation path is exempt from any dimension.

justifications.label: one covers source+semantic uniformity, the other covers lifecycle+source safety; combining closes the three-dimensional coverage

mutations-achieve-full-traceability.text: Every mutation is fully traceable from initiation to persisted outcome: atomicity ensures operations complete or roll back entirely, the audit log and structured before/after diffs provide historical context, and consistent artifact identification (deterministic challenge auto-IDs, monotonic nogood IDs) enables referencing specific mutation outcomes indefinitely.

justifications.label: atomicity + audit + consistent identification = full operational traceability

mutations-are-atomic-and-safely-propagat.text: Every network mutation follows an end-to-end safety pipeline: API context management ensures atomic load/save with write-flag gating, truth propagation terminates deterministically with lifecycle-aware BFS traversal, and snapshot persistence captures the final consistent state — no mutation can produce an inconsistent or divergent network.

justifications.label: Atomic persistence (depth-2) + safe propagation (depth-2) together guarantee the full mutation cycle from API entry through propagation to storage is end-to-end safe

mutations-are-atomic-audited-and-index-c.text: Every network mutation achieves three simultaneous guarantees: transactional atomicity (context-managed load/save with write-flag gating), historical auditability (timestamped audit log entries), and structural consistency (dependents index updated synchronously) — forming a complete mutation-safety contract.

justifications.label: API-layer atomicity and network-layer audit/index invariants unify into a complete mutation contract

mutations-are-observable-audited-and-ind.text: Every network mutation achieves triple-layered traceability: callers receive structured before/after diffs at the API level, the internal audit log records timestamped events for historical analysis, and the dependents index is simultaneously maintained — providing both external and internal observability.

justifications.label: Internal traceability (audit log + index maintenance at depth-2) combined with external observability (API-level diffing) means mutations are traceable end-to-end across abstraction layers

mutations-are-traceable-through-transiti.text: Every network mutation and its resulting retraction cascades are simultaneously traceable (atomic operations with audit logging, structured before/after diffs, consistent artifact identification) and transitively complete (propagation reaching all dependent nodes with guaranteed termination), ensuring every cascaded effect is as auditable as the triggering mutation

justifications.label: Traceability extends through transitive cascades — audit coverage does not degrade with cascade depth

names-only-format-outputs-bare-ids.text: When `--format names-only` is used, the output contains only bare node IDs with no brackets, status words, or labels — a strict contract for machine-parseable scripted consumption across multiple commands.

names-only-output-format-is-plain-newlin.text: Tools supporting `output_format="names-only"` return newline-separated identifiers without JSON brackets.

namespace-active-premise-gates-beliefs-v.text: `ensure_namespace` creates a normal `{ns}:active` premise and `add_node` inserts that premise as the first antecedent, so retracting it cascades namespace beliefs OUT through ordinary SL propagation.

namespace-active-premise-gates-namespace.text: `ensure_namespace` creates a `<ns>:active` premise node that all namespaced beliefs depend on, so retracting that single premise cascades the entire namespace OUT.

namespace-active-premise-invariant.text: When `namespace` is set, `add_node` auto-creates a `{namespace}:active` premise node and wires it as an antecedent into every namespaced justification; retracting that single premise cascades OUT every belief from that namespace.

namespace-add-node-implicitly-depends-on.text: `PgApi.add_node(..., namespace=ns)` auto-creates `<ns>:active` and adds it to the SL antecedents, so retracting `<ns>:active` cascades the whole namespace to OUT.

namespace-add-prefixes-and-wires-active-.text: Adding a node with `namespace=` prefixes the id, auto-creates `<ns>:active`, and adds that active premise as an implicit antecedent so retracting it cascades the whole namespace.

namespace-colon-convention-enables-cross.text: `_resolve_namespace` only prefixes belief IDs that don't already contain `:` — the colon serves as both the namespace delimiter and the signal that no prefixing is needed, allowing cross-namespace references to pass through unchanged.

namespace-empty-string-means-local-only.text: In the review pipeline, `namespace=""` filters to local-only nodes (those whose IDs do not contain a colon separator), as opposed to a specific namespace prefix match.

namespace-is-colon-convention-with-auto-.text: The namespace system is a colon-based convention with automatic infrastructure wiring: colon presence prevents double-prefixing, the `agent:id` format provides scoping, and node creation auto-wires a `{ns}:active` premise as an antecedent.

justifications.label: Three namespace beliefs define a complete convention: format, idempotency guard, and automatic kill-switch wiring

namespace-kill-switch-uses-active-premis.text: Retracting the `{ns}:active` premise node cascades all beliefs in that namespace to OUT; `ensure_namespace()` creates this node with `role: agent_premise` metadata as the namespace's kill switch.

namespace-prefix-is-colon-separated.text: Agent namespacing uses the format `agent_name:belief_id`; `_resolve_namespace()` skips prefixing any ID that already contains a colon, preventing double-prefixing of cross-namespace references

namespace-resolution-preserves-existing-.text: The `_resolve_namespace` function prefixes bare IDs with `namespace:` but leaves IDs already containing `:` untouched.

namespace-resolve-preserves-cross-refs.text: `_resolve_namespace` only prefixes a node ID with `namespace:` when the ID contains no colon — cross-namespace references like `other-agent:some-belief` are left intact.

namespaced-writes-prepend-active-premise.text: `add_node(namespace=...)` prefixes the id via `_resolve_namespace` and inserts `{ns}:active` at position 0 of the first justification's `antecedents` (creating the premise node if missing), making retraction of `{ns}:active` a cascade kill switch.

namespaces-discovered-by-active-premise-.text: Namespaces are discovered at runtime by scanning for nodes matching `*:active` with `role: agent_premise` metadata.

natural-mode-strips-belief-metadata.text: When `natural=True`, prompts omit `**Status:**`, `###` headers, and citation instructions, and include `plain natural language`.

negation-is-transparent-to-evaluation.text: The system's complete negative semantics — structural absence creating premise behavior, explicit outlist defeat with automatic reversal, and guided recovery — operate within transformation-invariant truth evaluation: negation mechanisms alter belief topology but never create special-case evaluation paths, because the same uniform rules evaluate all resulting structures identically regardless of how they were produced.

justifications.label: Complete reversible negative semantics (depth-5) combined with transformation-invariant evaluation (depth-6) shows negation doesn't carve out special evaluation paths

negative-belief-classifier-reduced-196-c.text: The negative belief classifier reduced 196 keyword candidates to 9 genuinely negative beliefs, a 95.4% false-positive rate among candidates.

negative-semantics-are-complete-reversib.text: The system's negative semantics form a complete belief modification lifecycle: complete semantics cover all negation forms (structural absence and explicit outlist defeat), all defeat mechanisms reverse automatically through BFS propagation cascades, and surgical restoration hints target only cascade victims with surviving premises — every belief retraction can be undone with guided recovery.

justifications.label: Negative semantic completeness (depth-3) and automatic reversal with guided recovery (depth-4) combine into the emergent property that negation is a full lifecycle with entry, exit, and recovery

negative-semantics-are-uniform-through-m.text: The system's complete negative semantics — structural absence creating premise behavior, explicit outlist defeat with automatic reversal, permanent identity effects from challenge — handle all edge cases uniformly because they derive from the same minimal primitives as all other truth evaluation, with no special-case handling for negation.

justifications.label: Complete negative semantics + minimality-derived uniformity → negation is uniform through minimality

negative-semantics-ground-deterministic-.text: Complete reversible negative semantics — structural absence producing emergent premise behavior plus explicit outlist defeat with automatic reversal and guided recovery — are the foundation that enables deterministic reliable dialectics: challenge/defend operations inherit their determinism from evaluation purity applied to outlist primitives, and their reliability from the inherent reversibility of outlist-based defeat.

justifications.label: Dialectical determinism and reliability are inherited properties of the complete negative semantics layer

negative-semantics-have-reversible-defea.text: The system's complete negative semantics — structural absence creating premise behavior and explicit outlist defeat — exhibit a fundamental asymmetry: all outlist-based defeat operations (challenge, kill-switch, supersession) are fully reversible in truth value, but dialectical challenge permanently destroys premise identity by injecting a justification into a formerly unjustified node, an irreversible structural transformation.

justifications.label: Complete negative semantics combined with the defeat/identity asymmetry reveals negation is reversible in truth value but permanent in node structure

network-add-duplicate-node-raises-valuee.text: `Network.add_node` called with an ID that already exists in `net.nodes` raises `ValueError` (with "already exists" in the message) rather than overwriting or silently ignoring the duplicate.

network-add-node-duplicate-id-raises-val.text: `Network.add_node` raises `ValueError("already exists")` when called with an existing node ID.

network-add-node-no-justification-is-pre.text: `Network.add_node` sets `truth_value` to `"IN"` when no justifications are supplied; otherwise it computes truth from the justifications.

network-add-node-raises-valueerror-on-du.text: `add_node()` raises `ValueError` when given an already-existing node ID.

network-add-node-rejects-duplicate-ids.text: `Network.add_node` raises `ValueError` if the supplied node ID already exists.

network-add-node-rejects-duplicates.text: `Network.add_node()` raises `ValueError` if a node with the given ID already exists in the network.

network-alternate-justification-keeps-no.text: A derived node with multiple `Justification` entries remains IN as long as at least one justification has all its antecedents IN; retracting antecedents of one justification does not flip the node to OUT if another justification is still satisfied.

network-belief-set-contains-only-in-node.text: `Network.get_belief_set()` returns only the IDs of nodes whose truth value is `IN`.

network-bfs-propagation-uses-deque-and-v.text: `_propagate()` uses a `deque`-based BFS through the dependents reverse index and a `visited` set to prevent cycles.

network-cache-keyed-by-db-path.text: `_network_cache` is a dict keyed by DB path strings whose values are `(mtime, network)` tuples.

network-cache-keyed-by-exact-db-path.text: `_network_cache` is keyed by the exact `db_path` string and stores `(mtime, Network)` tuples.

network-cache-keyed-by-mtime.text: `_network_cache` stores `(mtime, Network)` per `db_path`, and read-only calls (`write=False`) reuse the cached `Network` iff the current file mtime equals the cached one; otherwise a fresh `Storage(db_path).load()` is performed.

network-cache-successful-write-repopulat.text: After a successful `_with_network(..., write=True)` block, the cache entry is updated with the new network and mtime.

network-cache-write-mode-bypasses-cache.text: `_with_network(db_path, write=True)` always yields a freshly loaded `Network` distinct from any cached instance.

network-centrality-enables-single-point-.text: Because the network is the single architectural import point for all modules AND self-records every mutation in an append-only log, the entire system's operational history is observable through one auditable hub

justifications.label: Centrality without self-logging would be a single point of failure with no visibility; self-logging without centrality would produce fragmented per-module audit trails. The composition yields a single, complete, ordered system-level audit that no individual module needs to maintain independently.

network-challenge-converts-premise-to-ju.text: If `challenge()` targets a premise, it converts that premise to a justified node with the challenge node in its outlist.
When Network.challenge targets a premise, it converts that target into a justified node with an SL justification containing the challenge in its outlist.

network-class-has-nodes-nogoods-repos-lo.text: The Network class holds four attributes: nodes (dict[str, Node]), nogoods (list[Nogood]), repos (dict[str, str]), and log (list[dict]).

network-convert-to-premise-unlinks-depen.text: `convert_to_premise()` strips all justifications, unlinks the node from its antecedents' dependents sets, and makes it a premise that defaults to IN.

network-defend-delegates-to-challenge.text: `defend(target_id, challenge_id, reason)` is implemented by delegating to `challenge()`.

network-defend-implemented-via-challenge.text: Network.defend is implemented by calling self.challenge on the challenge node, creating a premise in the challenge's outlist.

network-disjunctive-justification.text: A node is IN if ANY of its justifications is valid (disjunction); each individual justification requires ALL antecedents IN and ALL outlist members OUT (conjunction) — the SL justification semantics from Doyle's 1979 paper.

network-duplicate-node-add-raises-valuee.text: `Network.add_node` raises `ValueError` with message 'already exists' when called with a duplicate node ID.

network-enforces-complementary-structura.text: The network maintains structural integrity through three complementary, non-overlapping invariants: ID uniqueness at creation, minimum-justification preservation at modification, and disjunctive truth survival at evaluation

justifications.label: Each invariant guards a different lifecycle phase (creation, modification, evaluation) and a different failure mode (identity collision, orphaned justification, unjustified truth). Together they form a complete structural integrity envelope with no overlapping or gap-covered region.

network-entrenchment-prefers-premises.text: Covered by existing `add-nogood-retraction-prefers-least-entrenched` which captures the entrenchment scoring and premise preference.

network-entrenchment-ranks-premises-abov.text: `_entrenchment()` scores premises higher than derived nodes, sourced nodes higher than unsourced nodes, and nodes with more dependents higher than nodes with fewer dependents.

network-explain-recurses-through-valid-j.text: Network.explain recursively traces why a node is IN by finding its valid justification and recursing into antecedents, and why a node is OUT by reporting failed antecedents and violated outlist nodes.

network-explain-recurses-valid-justifica.text: For an IN node, `explain()` finds the valid justification and recursively explains its antecedents; for an OUT node, it lists failed antecedents and violated outlist items.

network-explain-returns-structured-trace.text: `Network.explain(id)` returns a list of dictionaries containing keys such as `node`, `truth_value`, `reason`, `label`, and `failed_antecedents`.

network-has-zero-external-dependencies.text: The Network class imports only stdlib (`collections.deque`, `datetime`) plus package data types (`Node`, `Justification`, `Nogood`); it has zero external dependencies.

network-idempotent-retract-assert-return.text: Retracting an already-OUT node or asserting an already-IN node returns an empty change list.

network-implements-doyles-1979-tms.text: `Network` implements Doyle's 1979 Truth Maintenance System algorithm with nodes, justifications, and automatic truth-value propagation.

network-internal-modules-use-reasons-lib.text: This duplicates the existing belief that at least nine canonical `reasons/` modules (including `api.py`, `storage.py`, `check_stale.py`, `compact.py`, `export_card.py`, `export_markdown.py`, `import_agent.py`, and `import_beliefs.py`) import from `reasons_lib.*`.

network-is-central-dependency.text: `network.py` is imported by essentially every other module — api, storage, import, export, compact, check_stale, and all test files — making it the central data structure of the project.

network-is-pure-in-memory-semantic-engin.text: `Network` owns only the in-memory belief graph and truth maintenance; persistence and API concerns live in `storage.py` and `api.py`.

network-is-sole-truth-propagation-engine.text: All truth value computation and propagation in the system flows through `Network._propagate()` and `Network._compute_truth()`; no other module modifies truth values directly.

metadata.retract_reason: Contradicted by pg-reimplements-network-in-sql: PgApi has its own SQL-based propagation

network-justification-methods-not-observ.text: The tests call `Network.add_justification` and `Network.remove_justification`, but their definitions are absent from the supplied observations.

network-log-is-append-only-audit-trail.text: `net.log` is an append-only list of action entries (add, retract, propagate, warn); no operation removes or reorders entries, and production code must not truncate it, ensuring a complete chronological audit trail.

network-metadata-carries-structured-stat.text: Node state such as `_retracted`, `retract_reason`, `superseded_by`, `challenges`, `access_tags`, and `summarized_by` lives in the generic `metadata` dict rather than typed Node fields, keeping the dataclass stable while features layer on behavior.

network-missing-node-id-raises-keyerror.text: Missing-node operations such as `retract`, `assert_node`, `add_nogood`, and `explain` raise `KeyError("not found")` rather than silently succeeding.

network-missing-node-operations-raise-ke.text: `Network.retract`, `assert_node`, `explain`, and `add_nogood` raise `KeyError("not found")` when referencing a nonexistent node.

network-multiple-justifications-survive-.text: A node with multiple justifications remains IN when only one justification's antecedent is retracted.

network-mutations-append-to-audit-log.text: Every network mutation records a timestamped event in `self.log`, an append-only list that serves as the propagation audit trail.

network-mutations-are-audited-and-index-.text: Every network mutation simultaneously maintains dual invariants: the audit log receives a timestamped event providing historical traceability, and the dependents reverse index is kept consistent ensuring correct future propagation.

justifications.label: Every mutation maintains both observability (audit log) and structural consistency (dependents index) as co-invariants

network-no-external-deps.text: `network.py` depends only on stdlib (`deque`, `datetime`) and project dataclasses; it has zero external package dependencies.

network-nogoods-preserve-insertion-order.text: `Network.nogoods` preserves insertion order, so tests can address the first- and second-added nogoods by index.

network-persistence-is-atomic.text: `Storage.save()` in `reasons/storage.py` wraps the full network rewrite in a single SQLite `with self.conn:` transaction.

network-propagate-mutates-supporting-jus.text: `Network._propagate()` calls `_compute_truth(dep)`, which can mutate `dep.supporting_justification` even when the node's truth value does not change.

network-propagate-returns-only-changed-d.text: `Network._propagate()` returns only dependent node IDs whose truth value actually changed, and it never includes the seed `changed_id`.

network-propagate-skips-retracted.text: Covered by existing `metadata-actively-governs-truth-propagation` which states retracted nodes are skipped during BFS traversal.

network-propagate-traversal-order-is-non.text: `Network._propagate()` traverses `dependents` sets, so BFS order and the returned changed-list order are nondeterministic across runs.
