network-propagate-warns-on-dangling-depe.text: `_propagate()` logs a warning for a dangling dependent ID that is absent from `self.nodes` but does not raise an exception.

network-recompute-all-bound-by-node-coun.text: `recompute_all()` iterates to a fixpoint over all derived nodes and is bounded by `len(self.nodes) + 1` iterations.

network-remove-justification-cleans-depe.text: `remove_justification()` cleans up dependents entries for references no longer used by the remaining justifications.

network-remove-justification-refuses-emp.text: `Network.remove_justification` raises `ValueError` when removing the last justification from a derived node and directs callers to `convert_to_premise` or `retract`.

network-requires-justification-type-sl.text: `Network.add_node` accepts justifications of type `"SL"`; the test suite only exercises this type, so other types are untested contracts.

network-retracted-nodes-persist.text: Retracted nodes remain in `self.nodes` with `_retracted` metadata set; they are never deleted from the graph, enabling later restoration via `assert_node()` without rederivation.

network-shim-exports-only-public-names.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that `import *` skips underscore-prefixed names unless the canonical module explicitly includes them in `__all__`.

network-shim-preserves-object-identity.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that `reasons_lib.<module>.X is reasons.<module>.X` for re-exported names.

network-single-justification-removal-blo.text: `remove_justification()` raises `ValueError` when a node has exactly one justification, forcing callers to use `convert_to_premise` or `retract` instead — preventing accidental creation of unjustified non-premise nodes.

network-sl-justification-requires-all-an.text: An `SL` justification is conjunctive: every antecedent must be `IN` for the justified node to be `IN`.

network-state-is-extensible-and-consiste.text: Network state management is both extensible (metadata carries all lifecycle state — retraction flags, stale reasons, challenges, access tags, supersession — as a universal key-value mechanism) and consistently tracked (every mutation maintains the audit log and dependents index simultaneously), ensuring new state dimensions can be added without compromising existing consistency guarantees

justifications.label: Metadata extensibility means new lifecycle concerns can be added without schema changes, while audit+index consistency means those new concerns are automatically covered by the existing mutation tracking — extensibility composes safely with consistency

network-tests-are-database-free.text: Test infrastructure detail, not a production code claim

network-trace-access-tags-unions-backwar.text: `trace_access_tags(node_id)` returns the union of `access_tags` metadata across the entire backward dependency subgraph.

network-trace-assumptions-returns-leaf-p.text: Network.trace_assumptions walks backward through justification chains to return all leaf premise nodes with no justifications.

network-validator-receives-full-justific.text: `_justification_valid(self, j: Justification)` at `reasons/network.py:976` is called with a `Justification` at lines 856, 860, and 970, so it has access to `j.type`.

network-verify-dependents-audits-index-d.text: `verify_dependents()` compares the live dependents index against what justifications imply and returns error strings.

network-verify-dependents-detects-index-.text: `verify_dependents()` recomputes the dependents index from justifications and diffs it against the live index to detect drift.

next-nogood-id-skipped-on-load.text: `load()` explicitly skips the `next_nogood_id` key in `network_meta`, leaving the counter to be recomputed from loaded nogoods.

no-accept-function-in-propose-update.text: There is no `accept` symbol in `reasons/propose_update.py`; grep for "accept" returns zero matches, confirming acceptance is out-of-band.

no-copy-tooling-connects-the-two-trees.text: A search for `copytree|shutil.copy|rsync|ln -s|symlink` found no mechanism that mirrors `reasons/` into `reasons_lib/`.

no-deprecation-warning-emitted-on-shim-i.text: Importing any `reasons_lib.*` module does not raise `DeprecationWarning` or `PendingDeprecationWarning`; the sole deprecation signal is the docstring text directing users to the `reasons.*` path.

no-file-sync-tooling-connects-reasons-an.text: No `rsync`, `copytree`, `shutil.copy`, mirror script, or CI generation step connects `reasons/` and `reasons_lib/`; apparent `sync`/`duplicate` matches refer to belief operations or git metadata.

no-internal-python-references-to-reasons.text: The provided Python-reference search found zero matches for `reasons_lib`.

no-logic-in-shim.text: The shim defines no functions, classes, or constants of its own; all behavior lives in `reasons.review_premises`.

no-schema-version-migration-exists.text: The `migrat` matches refer to retract-to-defeater migration and table migration comments, not schema-version data migration.

no-schema-version-migration-or-rejection.text: No observed code performs `schema_version` compatibility checks, rejection of unsupported versions, or version-driven data migration; the existing `migrat*` paths are retract-to-defeater and storage-table related.

no-synth-mode-skips-llm.text: When `no_synth=True`, `ask()` returns formatted FTS5 search results without invoking `_invoke_claude()` — the LLM is never contacted.

node-count-includes-retracted-nodes.text: The `node_count` metadata field reflects the total number of nodes in the network at export time, including retracted (OUT) nodes — it is a structural count, not an active-belief count.

node-count-tracks-exported-nodes.text: `export_network` metadata `node_count` equals `len(data["nodes"])`, including retracted nodes still present in the export.

node-defaults-to-in-for-premises.text: `Node.truth_value` defaults to `"IN"` and a premise is defined as a `Node` with an empty `justifications` list, so freshly constructed premises are `IN` without any propagation pass.

node-depth-base-case.text: A node that is missing from `nodes` or has an empty `justifications` list returns depth `0`.

node-depth-base-case-is-zero.text: `_node_depth` returns 0 when the node ID is absent from `nodes` or the node has no justifications.

node-depth-derivation-formula.text: For a node with justifications, the returned depth is `1 + max(depth(antecedent))` over the selected justifications.

node-depth-formula-is-one-plus-max-antec.text: For a derived node, `_node_depth` returns `1 + max(_node_depth(antecedent))` over the selected justifications.

node-depth-memo-preset-terminates-cycles.text: `_node_depth` sets `memo[nid] = 0` before recursing, which prevents infinite recursion on cycles but can undercount depth for cyclic graphs.

node-depth-missing-antecedent-is-zero.text: An antecedent ID absent from `nodes` is silently treated as depth 0 rather than raising.

node-depth-mutates-caller-supplied-memo.text: `_node_depth` mutates the caller-supplied `memo` dict, so sharing a memo across calls can reuse cached depths.

node-depth-propagates-structural-errors.text: `_node_depth` has no try/except; missing `.justifications`/`.antecedents` attributes or non-integer `supporting_justification` propagate as `AttributeError` or `TypeError`.

node-in-if-any-justification-valid.text: A Node is IN when at least one of its Justifications is valid; a Justification is valid when all antecedents are IN and all outlist nodes are OUT (disjunctive over justifications, conjunctive within each).

node-in-is-any-justification.text: A node is `IN` if at least one of its justifications holds; it is `OUT` only when none holds.

node-in-requires-any-valid-justification.text: A node with multiple justifications is `IN` if at least one justification is valid.

node-is-in-if-any-justification-valid.text: `_compute_truth` returns IN at the first valid justification scanned in reverse order and sets `supporting_justification` to that index.

node-is-in-iff-premise-or-valid-justific.text: A node is IN if and only if it is an unretracted premise or at least one of its justifications is valid under SL (`all inlist IN`), CP (assumptions consistent), or outlist (`inlist IN and outlist OUT`) semantics.

node-premise-is-implicit.text: A node is a premise (believed without justification) iff its `justifications` list is empty; there is no explicit `is_premise` flag or type discriminator.

node-supporting-justification-is-list-in.text: `Node.supporting_justification` is an index into the node's `justifications` list, not a justification or node ID, so any reordering/insertion/removal must recompute or invalidate it.

node-text-hash-is-sha256-of-text.text: Nodes created through `api.add_node` have `text_hash` equal to `hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()`.

node-timestamps-are-unvalidated-strings.text: `Node` lifecycle timestamps (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `reviewed_at`, `verified_at`, `retracted_at`) are plain strings with no format enforcement, and a non-empty `retracted_at` is the retraction signal.

node-to-page-maps-node-ids-to-filenames.text: `node_to_page` is a `{node_id: "<slug>.md"}` dict built before rendering and reused by `_format_node` and `_linkify` for cross-reference resolution.

node-truth-default-valid-only-for-premis.text: `Node.truth_value` defaults to `"IN"`, which is only correct for premises with no justifications; derived nodes must have their truth value recomputed by propagation.

node-truth-derives-from-justifications.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `node-in-if-any-justification-valid`, `truth-is-disjunctive-over-conjunctive-rules`, and `truth-semantics-are-emergent-and-uniform` which already capture that truth values are computed from justifications and premises default to IN.

node-truth-disjunctive.text: A node is IN if ANY of its justifications is valid (disjunctive semantics); adding a justification to a node can never cause it to go OUT.

node-truth-is-disjunction-of-justificati.text: A node is `IN` when at least one of its justifications is valid.

node-without-justifications-is-premise-i.text: A node with no justifications is treated as a premise with `truth_value = "IN"` by default; it is not computed through `_compute_truth` and retains its initial value unless explicitly retracted or asserted.

nodes-can-hold-multiple-sl-justification.text: A node can carry multiple SL justifications, allowing mixed representations such as an original multi-antecedent row plus additional any-mode single-antecedent rows.

nogood-conflict-resolution-is-complete-a.text: Nogood-based conflict resolution is complete (transitive cascade reaches all transitively affected nodes) and identifiable (deterministic, collision-free, monotonically-increasing IDs) — BUT this completeness is gated by the assumption that the nogood ID counter is append-only, which import operations could violate.

justifications.label: Deterministic identification (monotonic + content-derived) and transitive cascade completeness are logically interdependent; the append-only assumption is the fragility that could break the ID uniqueness guarantee on which both properties depend.

nogood-conflict-resolution-is-complete-a.text: Nogood-based conflict resolution supports transitive cascade propagation (retracting a node propagates to all transitively dependent SL-derived nodes) and provides deterministic, content-derived identifiers (nogood IDs constructed by concatenating member node IDs) backed by a monotonic counter that, per current implementation, is never decreased by deletion, clearing, save/load, or import. The stability and uniqueness of these identifiers depend on the monotonicity property being preserved; any future operation that resets or decreases the counter would undermine the no-reuse guarantee that the deterministic concatenation scheme relies on.

nogood-content-id-sorts-and-hyphen-joins.text: Content-based nogood IDs are formed by lexicographically sorting node IDs and joining them with hyphens after the `nogood-` prefix.

nogood-defines-set-of-incompatible-nodes.text: A Nogood represents a recorded contradiction: a set of node IDs that cannot all be IN simultaneously.

nogood-duplicate-receives-incremental-su.text: A second `add_nogood` call with the same node set appends `-2` (then `-3`, etc.) to the base ID rather than overwriting or rejecting the entry, ensuring unique IDs while preserving both nogoods.

nogood-export-format-mismatch.text: The nogood exporter writes IDs in `nogood-NNN` format (no colon, no label) but `parse_nogoods` expects `nogood-N: label` format, meaning nogood round-trip is currently broken and only the export side is tested.

nogood-id-backwards-compat.text: Databases created before the monotonic counter fix (lacking `network_meta` table) load without error; the counter is derived from max existing nogood ID + 1, or defaults to 1 if none exist

nogood-id-collision-prevention.text: After importing nogoods, `_next_nogood_id` is set to one past the highest imported ID, preventing `network.record_nogood` from generating a conflicting ID later.

nogood-id-counter-is-monotonic.text: `Network._next_nogood_id` only ever increases — deletion, clearing, save/load, and import never decrease it, preventing ID reuse after the issue #26 fix

nogood-id-follows-nogood-a-b-pattern.text: `Nogood.id` is constructed as `"nogood-" + "-".join(node_ids)` preserving input order.

nogood-id-format-is-zero-padded.text: Nogood IDs follow the format `nogood-NNN` with 3-digit zero-padded integers (e.g., `nogood-001`), and `_next_nogood_id` holds the next integer to assign, not the last used

nogood-id-import-sync.text: Both `import_json` and `import_into_network` must advance `_next_nogood_id` past the highest imported nogood ID to prevent collisions with pre-existing IDs

nogood-id-monotonic.text: `Network._next_nogood_id` only ever increases; deletions and clears do not decrement it, preventing ID reuse (fix for issue #26)

nogood-id-node-order-is-normalized.text: Supplying nodes as `["b", "a"]` produces the same ID as `["a", "b"]`.

nogood-id-persisted-in-meta.text: The nogood counter is stored in the `network_meta` SQLite table and survives save/load cycles as a high-water mark, not a count of current nogoods

nogood-id-persists-opaque-through-storag.text: `Nogood.id` is stored as an opaque string in SQLite and is byte-identical after a `Storage.save` → `Storage.load` round-trip; no re-derivation or normalization occurs at the storage layer.

nogood-id-survives-storage-round-trip.text: `Storage.save` followed by `Storage.load` preserves a nogood’s content-derived ID.

nogood-identification-is-deterministic-a.text: Nogood conflict IDs are deterministically content-derived with a monotonically increasing collision-free counter, while the propagation engine ensures conflicts cascade transitively through all dependents while respecting retraction pins — every conflict is both uniquely identifiable and completely resolved.

justifications.label: The identification guarantee (deterministic + monotonic + collision-free) and the resolution guarantee (transitive cascade + pin-respecting) are logically dependent: without monotonic IDs, cascade targets become ambiguous; without pin-respecting, cascade completeness is illusory.

nogood-ids-are-durable-and-collision-fre.text: Nogood IDs form a durable collision-free sequence: the counter only increases (surviving deletions and clears), persists across save/load cycles via the network_meta table, and advances past imported IDs to prevent collisions — no operation can produce a reused or ambiguous contradiction identifier

justifications.label: Three independent ID management properties — monotonicity, persistence, and import-aware advancement — combine into a single durability guarantee that ID-based contradiction references never become ambiguous

nogood-ids-assume-append-only.text: Nogood IDs are derived from `len(self.nogoods) + 1`, so deleting a nogood from the list would cause ID collisions on subsequent calls

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #35

nogood-ids-follow-deterministic-concaten.text: Nogood IDs are deterministically constructed as `"nogood-" + "-".join(member_node_ids)`, providing a stable, content-derived identifier that survives serialization round-trips without requiring a separate counter.

nogood-ids-format-sequential-nnn.text: Nogood IDs are formatted as `nogood-NNN` with a zero-padded sequential number starting at `nogood-001`.

nogood-is-a-set-of-incompatible-inodes.text: Duplicates existing beliefs `contradictions-only-checks-in-beliefs`, `contradiction-management-is-complete-and-traceable`, and `contradiction-resolution-is-minimal-disruption` which already define nogoods as sets of mutually exclusive IN nodes.

nogood-legacy-ids-coexist-with-content-b.text: Nogood IDs imported from legacy JSON (`"nogood-005"`) or beliefs text (`"nogood-010"`) are stored verbatim and do not collide with newly generated content-based IDs (`"nogood-a-b"`); the ID namespace is a free-form string space where the content-based scheme is a convention for new entries only.

nogood-markdown-round-trip-is-not-implem.text: `export_markdown` emits `nogood-NNN` without a colon while `parse_nogoods` expects `nogood-N: label`, so nogoods are export-only via markdown today.

nogood-old-db-without-meta-defaults-coun.text: When loading a pre-fix database with no `network_meta` table and no existing nogoods, `_next_nogood_id` defaults to 1.

nogood-pre-fix-ids-used-len-plus-one.text: Before the issue #26 fix, nogood IDs were derived from `len(self.nogoods) + 1`, which allowed ID reuse after deletion.

nogood-records-mutually-exclusive-node-s.text: A Nogood records a set of node IDs that cannot all be IN simultaneously.

nogood-requires-at-least-two-valid-claim.text: `parse_contradiction_response` discards any `### NOGOOD` block with fewer than 2 claims after applying the optional `valid_ids` allow-list.

nogood-requires-list-while-propose-updat.text: `nogood(node_ids: list[str])` (line 175) lacks a default, so `node_ids` is required; `propose_update(belief_ids: list[str] | None = None)` (line 203) is the only tool in the file that makes the list parameter optional.

nogood-resolution-maintains-consistent-i.text: Nogood recording and resolution produces a consistent, referenceable history of contradictions

justifications.label: The append-only ID scheme means any nogood deletion would cause ID collisions, corrupting the contradiction history

nogood-resolution-retracts-a-premise-not.text: Recording a nogood triggers dependency-directed backtracking that walks the justification graph backward and retracts a responsible premise chosen for minimal disruption.

nogood-short-circuits-when-not-all-nodes.text: `add_nogood` records the `Nogood` object but returns `[]` and performs no backtracking unless every listed node is currently `IN`.

nogood-tests-simulate-schema-migration-b.text: The backwards-compatibility tests drop the `network_meta` table with raw SQL to simulate databases created before the monotonic counter fix.

nogood-tests-use-tmp-sqlite-db-fixture.text: The nogood ID tests use a `db` fixture that creates a fresh SQLite database in `tmp_path` for each test.

nogood-tests-use-two-phase-storage-reope.text: Persistence tests save a `Storage` instance, close it, and open a new `Storage` on the same path to prove the counter is written to disk.

nogood-visibility-is-atomic-any-restrict.text: A nogood is hidden from a caller if ANY of its constituent nodes carries an `access_tags` restriction; the nogood is treated as an atomic unit for visibility filtering rather than being partially revealed.

nogoods-require-all-affected-nodes-to-ex.text: A nogood is skipped (not partially imported) if any ID in its `Affects:` list is absent from `net.nodes`, and it contributes nothing to `nogoods_imported`.

nogoods-require-at-least-two-live-nodes.text: A nogood is only appended if `len([a for a in affects if a in network.nodes]) >= 2`; otherwise it is dropped silently.

nogoods-require-valid-nodes.text: Nogoods whose `Affects` list references node IDs not present in the network are silently skipped rather than raising an error during import

non-monotonic-system-is-single-reversibl.text: The entire non-monotonic reasoning system — challenges, kill-switches, supersession, and dialectics — is built on a single primitive (outlist) that is inherently reversible, with no dedicated machinery for any defeat pattern.

justifications.label: Three depth-1 conclusions all converge on the same architectural insight — outlist is both the universal mechanism and the source of reversibility and recursive dialectics

none-default-parameters-are-optional-in-.text: Any MCP tool parameter with a `None` default is omitted from the schema's `required` list and can be omitted or sent as JSON `null`.

noqa-suppresses-f401-and-f403.text: The trailing `# noqa: F401,F403` suppresses "unused import" and "wildcard import" lint diagnostics, both of which are intentional for this shim pattern.

normalization-drops-unknown-refs.text: Both `_normalize_markdown` and `_normalize_json` silently drop antecedent/outlist references to IDs not present in the import set, preventing dangling edges in the dependency graph.

normalize-markdown-maps-stale-or-out-to-.text: _normalize_markdown maps STALE and OUT statuses to is_out=True.

ollama-calls-skip-cost-recording.text: Ollama invocations bypass the JSON-parsing envelope and cost recording: the response is returned as raw text (after thinking-marker stripping) and `_record_cost` is never called, so `get_cost_summary()` will not include Ollama calls.

ollama-models-skip-cost-tracking.text: `ollama:*` responses return before `_parse_cli_json`, so they never call `_record_cost` and never appear in `by_model`.

ollama-thinking-strip-is-fragile.text: The ollama output post-processing strips exact string markers (`Thinking...\n` / `...done thinking.\n`) that are coupled to ollama's current output format and may break across versions.

ollama-thinking-strip-requires-both-mark.text: Ollama output is thinking-stripped only when it both starts with `Thinking...` and contains `...done thinking.`; a truncated marker leaves raw output untouched.

ollama-thinking-stripping-requires-both-.text: output lacking either `Thinking...` or `...done thinking.` is returned unchanged, and Claude output is never stripped.

omission-and-hidden-lines-bypass-budget-.text: The `... (N more … omitted)` and `(N nodes hidden by summaries)` lines are appended without `_over_budget` checks, so a run can exceed `budget` slightly.

omitted-example-omits-metadata-key.text: Adding a node without `example` leaves the metadata without an `"example"` key.

on-batch-callback-receives-cumulative-re.text: `on_batch` is invoked after each batch with the full accumulated `all_results`, not just the newest batch's results.

on-batch-receives-mutable-cumulative-lis.text: `on_batch` is invoked with the same `all_results` list object, mutated in place, after each batch.

on-result-receives-accumulating-list.text: The `on_result` callback is invoked with the full growing `all_results` list after each item, not with a single new result.

only-in-truth-value-gets-plus-marker.text: The structured renderer maps only `truth_value == "IN"` to `[+]`; every other value, including `UNKNOWN`, maps to `[-]`.

only-reasons-lib-is-distributed.text: Only the `reasons_lib` package is included in built distributions — `tests/`, `entries/`, and `reviews/` are excluded by the explicit `packages = ["reasons_lib"]` declaration in pyproject.toml.

only-reasons-lib-packaged.text: Setuptools is configured to include only the `reasons_lib` package in distributions; tests, entries, reviews, and knowledge-base artifacts are excluded from wheels

openai-integration-uses-responses-api.text: The `openai:` provider path in `llm.py` uses the OpenAI Responses API (`client.responses.create`) rather than Chat Completions, and records cost as `0.0` because the Responses API does not return USD cost in the expected shape.

openai-prefix-bypasses-resolve-model-cmd.text: `resolve_model_cmd` deliberately raises for `openai:` models, which are dispatched earlier in `invoke_model` via `_invoke_openai` and the Responses API.

operational-assurance-is-resource-effici.text: The system's comprehensive operational assurance — spanning temporal self-correction, end-to-end reliability, and external control — is achieved within a resource-efficient pipeline that minimizes footprint at every lifecycle phase, ensuring operational guarantees do not degrade under resource constraints.

justifications.label: Comprehensive operational assurance operates within resource-efficient bounds

operational-guarantees-span-safety-and-t.text: The system's operational guarantees span two independent enforcement dimensions: safety that is universal and condition-independent (holding across all layers, backends, and adverse conditions) and trust boundaries that are comprehensively enforced (architectural self-containment and information flow control at every boundary) — together ensuring no operational path can compromise system integrity regardless of layer, backend, or external interaction.

justifications.label: Universal condition-independent safety + comprehensive trust boundaries means integrity enforcement has no gaps along either dimension

operational-integrity-is-end-to-end.text: Every network operation achieves both transactional atomicity (load/save gating, snapshot persistence) and semantic determinism (uniform pure evaluation, terminating propagation, reversible defeat), ensuring every mutation produces a predictable, recoverable network state.

justifications.label: Atomic mutation pipeline guarantees no partial writes while deterministic reversible reasoning guarantees no ambiguous truth states — together they close both operational and semantic failure modes

operational-integrity-survives-all-graph.text: End-to-end operational integrity holds across all semantic edge cases — including vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, and empty antecedents — only when the dependents graph is consistent and propagation handles all node references safely.

justifications.label: depth-5 gate — operational integrity claims assume a well-formed graph, but the fragile denormalized index and unchecked dependent lookups can violate that assumption under edge-case graph topologies

operational-profile-is-safe-assured-and-.text: The system's complete operational profile achieves both safety (defense-in-depth reinforced across LLM and system boundaries with resource-efficient layered defenses) and assurance (spanning temporal self-correction, end-to-end reliability, and external control within efficient pipeline bounds) — neither safety nor assurance requires resource trade-offs against the other.

justifications.label: Safety's defense-in-depth is resource-efficient (depth-9) independently of assurance's resource-efficiency (depth-8) — combining them proves the complete operational profile fits within bounded resources

operational-profile-is-traceable-through.text: The system's safe, assured, resource-bounded operational profile produces evaluations that are traceable from individual computation through system-wide convergence to documented equilibria — operational guarantees hold not just at a point in time but longitudinally across the system's entire trajectory toward stable states.

justifications.label: Operational assurance extends from point-in-time to longitudinal — every equilibrium path is traceable within the bounded operational profile

operational-profile-spans-all-backends.text: The safe, assured, resource-bounded operational profile holds identically across all storage backends — the same safety, assurance, and resource-efficiency guarantees apply uniformly to both SQLite and PostgreSQL deployments.

justifications.label: Operational profile universality gated on PostgreSQL API completeness — currently OUT because PgApi has partial coverage, flips IN when parity is achieved

operational-safety-is-defense-in-depth-r.text: The system's operational safety guarantees — universal across all architectural layers and condition-independent — are concretely reinforced by defense-in-depth at every external boundary: LLM integration applies layered defenses (bounded execution, fail-soft handling, subprocess isolation) and system boundaries enforce validation, resilience, and resource constraints simultaneously

justifications.label: Universal operational safety (depth-7) and boundary defense-in-depth (depth-5) are complementary — one establishes the scope of safety guarantees while the other establishes the concrete enforcement mechanism at every external interface

operational-safety-is-resource-efficient.text: The system's operational safety guarantees — universal across all architectural layers and condition-independent — are concretely reinforced by defense-in-depth spanning LLM and system boundaries, and this defense-in-depth is achieved within a resource-efficient pipeline from packaging through runtime, meaning comprehensive safety does not trade off against operational cost.

justifications.label: Safety reinforced by defense-in-depth could imply expensive layered enforcement; demonstrating resource efficiency across the full pipeline proves that safety depth and operational efficiency are not in tension.

operational-safety-is-universal-and-cond.text: Operational safety holds universally across two independent dimensions: across all architectural layers and storage backends (SQLite and PostgreSQL enforce equivalent safety through backend-appropriate mechanisms), AND under all graph conditions including adverse states (dangling references trigger graceful degradation, cyclic justifications are bounded, concurrent access uses WAL mode)

justifications.label: Safety across layers (depth-4) and safety under adverse conditions (depth-5) are independently established — their combination means there is no combination of backend choice and graph state that can produce unsafe behavior

operational-safety-spans-all-mutation-so.text: Operational safety extends across both internal mutation pipelines (atomic load/save transactions, deterministic propagation, write-flag gating) and external belief ingestion pathways (defensive validation, Jaccard retraction guards, environment isolation, agent namespace containment), ensuring every mutation source — whether programmatic, LLM-driven, or agent-imported — passes through integrity enforcement.

justifications.label: Unifies the internal integrity pipeline (atomic snapshot + deterministic propagation) with the external bounding pipeline (defensive validation + agent containment); together they cover the complete mutation surface area

operational-traceability-enables-efficie.text: The system's operational profile — traceable from individual truth evaluation through system-wide equilibria — combines with quality-complete self-correction operating within an efficient pipeline, so that every correction and its full cascade is simultaneously traceable and resource-bounded from individual computation through stable-state convergence.

justifications.label: Connects operational traceability through equilibria with efficient complete self-correction — observable correction within bounded resources

origin-agnostic-guarantees-are-verifiabl.text: The origin-agnostic closed loop delivers both trustworthiness and invariant grounding from a single architectural source, and these guarantees are independently verifiable through the same self-sustaining maintenance loop's observability — verification and origin-agnosticism are inherently coupled rather than independently achieved.

justifications.label: Depth-12 — the maintenance loop simultaneously provides origin-agnosticism, self-sustainability, and observability for verification, making these three properties inseparable consequences of a single mechanism

origin-agnostic-loop-grounds-external-in.text: External beliefs achieve complete invariant grounding along all three dimensions (origin, time, structure) precisely because the closed maintenance loop operates origin-agnostically — the loop's indifference to belief provenance is the mechanism that delivers invariant parity to external beliefs.

justifications.label: Causal connection: origin-agnostic loop is the mechanism producing external invariant grounding; the loop's indifference explains the parity

origin-agnostic-trustworthiness-is-fully.text: The system's complete revision trustworthiness holds identically across all belief origins and is independently verifiable through full maintenance loop observability — trustworthiness is not merely claimed but provable through origin-agnostic audit trails — provided propagation's dependents invariant holds.

justifications.label: Triple convergence of three independent depth-9 achievements; gated because broken propagation dependents would make observability misleading and trustworthiness incomplete

origin-agnosticism-unifies-trustworthine.text: The system's origin-agnostic closed loop simultaneously delivers two independent guarantees from a single architectural source: verifiable trustworthiness across all belief origins and complete invariant grounding for external beliefs — origin indifference is not merely a property but the shared mechanism producing both guarantees.

justifications.label: Two leaf depth-10 conclusions sharing the origin-agnostic loop as common source produce distinct guarantees (trustworthiness verification and invariant grounding) that unify into a single comprehensive origin-agnostic property

other-static-hosts-lack-built-in-google-.text: GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, S3+CloudFront, and nginx do not have built-in Google OAuth gating.

out-beliefs-imported-as-bare-premises.text: Covered by existing `out-beliefs-imported-without-justifications` which captures the same invariant

out-beliefs-imported-without-justificati.text: Beliefs that are OUT or STALE in the source are imported with an empty justification list, preventing `recompute_all` from resurrecting them to IN

out-count-is-not-in.text: A node is counted as OUT whenever its `truth_value` is anything other than the exact string `"IN"`.

out-filter-precedes-neighbor-expansion.text: Retracted beliefs are excluded even when they are dependents of a live node returned by `api.search` (`### derived-out` is absent from output).

out-source-status-survives-recompute.text: A belief imported with source status `[OUT]` remains `OUT` even after `Storage(db).load().recompute_all()`, while `[STALE]` beliefs can be propagated back to `IN` on recompute.

outlist-absent-means-out.text: An outlist node that doesn't exist in the network is treated as OUT (justification satisfied); absent antecedent nodes fail validation — this asymmetry makes missing counter-evidence permissive while missing supporting evidence is strict

outlist-behavior-requires-live-justifica.text: The outlist test only passes if import wires justifications back into the inference engine, not merely into storage; `assert_node("y")` must propagate to `x`.

outlist-enables-non-monotonic-reasoning.text: The `outlist` field on `Justification` allows beliefs to be retracted when a defeating node becomes IN — this is the core non-monotonic mechanism powering `supersede`, `challenge`, and default-logic patterns.

outlist-enables-non-monotonic-retraction.text: `Justification.outlist` encodes defeaters: a justification is invalidated whenever any node in `outlist` becomes `IN`, which is what allows beliefs to be retracted without deletion.

outlist-invalidates-when-node-in.text: An `SL` justification with an outlist is invalid if any outlist node is `IN`.

outlist-is-universal-defeat-mechanism.text: The outlist primitive is the sole defeat mechanism underlying all non-monotonic features: challenges, agent kill-switches, supersession, and direct defeasible reasoning

justifications.label: Four independent features all route through outlist injection rather than implementing custom defeat logic

outlist-nodes-are-dependents.text: Unlike pure antecedent-only TMSes, this implementation registers outlist nodes in `dependents`, which is what lets retracting a superseder restore the superseded node.

outlist-nodes-not-in-dependents-index.text: Outlist nodes are not tracked in the `dependents` index, so when an outlist node is retracted (goes OUT), dependent GATE beliefs are not enqueued for re-evaluation by `_propagate` — requiring manual `reasons assert` as a workaround.

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #31 (commit 5316c1a, 2026-04-23) — _rebuild_dependents, add_node, and add_justification now track outlist nodes

outlist-only-justification-holds-as-defa.text: A justification with an empty inlist but non-empty outlist represents a default premise that holds while all blocker nodes remain `OUT`.

outlist-only-justification-is-default-be.text: An `unless`-only justification represents a premise that holds by default while its blockers are `OUT`, as supported by `reasons/api.py:333`.

outlist-propagates-to-unless.text: The original `SL` justification's `outlist` is forwarded as the `unless` argument to `add_justification` (asserted as `"blocker-x"` in `test_preserves_outlist`).

outlist-relationships-survive-persistenc.text: Outlists are stored as `outlist_json` in the SQLite `justifications` table; on load, the dependent index is rebuilt for both antecedents and outlist nodes, preserving propagation behavior across save/load cycles

outlist-rendered-in-report.text: Outlist identifiers from explanation steps are rendered into the generated belief report.

outlist-semantics-are-fully-specified.text: The outlist primitive has complete, well-defined semantics: multiple entries form a conjunction (all must be OUT), absent nodes are treated as OUT (permissive default), and outlist relationships survive persistence through JSON serialization with rebuilt dependent indexes.

justifications.label: These three beliefs specify the complete behavioral contract of the outlist primitive — conjunction, absence handling, and persistence — independent of how it is used

outlist-semantics-enable-nonmonotonic-re.text: Covered by existing `challenge-is-outlist-injection`, `kill-switch-uses-outlist-not-antecedent`, and `dialectics-inherit-complete-outlist-semantics`, which together establish that all non-monotonic operations reduce to outlist manipulation.

output-governance-is-complete-authorized.text: All system output is simultaneously structurally complete (priority-ordered compact summaries with predictable bounds), authorized (access-tag subset gating with transitive inheritance), resource-constrained (accurate bidirectional token budgets), and machine-parseable (deterministic CI-ready staleness reports with nonzero exit codes).

justifications.label: Production output readiness (bounded, CI-gated) and information governance (authorized, resource-constrained) combine into a single comprehensive output contract.

output-governance-is-comprehensive-and-s.text: All system output is simultaneously comprehensively governed (normalized schemas with deterministic structure, authorized via access-tag subset gating, resource-constrained via token budgets) AND self-sustaining in quality (knowledge freshness actively maintained through staleness detection feeding back into the pipeline, query resilience ensuring graceful degradation across all access paths) — output governance is not a static structural property but an actively maintained dynamic one.

justifications.label: Connects two orphaned output-governance chains (depth-5 normalization/authorization and depth-6 resilience/self-correction) into a comprehensive+self-sustaining claim

output-header-format-is-contract-for-reg.text: `_count_local_shown` and `_count_agent_shown` parse exact header patterns such as `Local beliefs (N beliefs, showing M)` and `Agent: name (N beliefs, showing M)`.

package-list-explicit-reasons-lib.text: `[tool.setuptools]` explicitly lists `reasons_lib` as the only package to include, preventing auto-discovery of tests or scripts.

package-name-split.text: The pip-installable name is `ftl-reasons` but the importable Python package is `reasons_lib`; these are deliberately decoupled.

packages-list-requires-manual-update.text: `[tool.setuptools].packages` explicitly lists `reasons` and `reasons_lib`; any new top-level package is silently excluded from wheels until added to this list.

page-name-normalizes-to-lowercase-hyphen.text: `_page_name` normalizes spaces and special characters to hyphens and falls back to `"other"` when the normalized result is empty.

pageindex-can-automate-staleness-verific.text: PageIndex could automate retrieving the current source section for staleness verification before an LLM checks whether it still supports a belief.

pageindex-can-ground-derived-beliefs-in-.text: PageIndex could search indexed documents for supporting or contradicting evidence and attach source sections to derived beliefs.

pageindex-hierarchical-rag.text: PageIndex is a separate tool, not part of the ftl-reasons codebase — claims about its architecture belong in a PageIndex knowledge base, not here.

pageindex-tms-integration-requires-pagei.text: The proposed PageIndex integration requires PageIndex workspace sharing or API access from other tools.

pageindex-tms-integration-would-add-sect.text: Integrating PageIndex with ftl-reasons would let beliefs carry section-level provenance such as document UUID, section path, and page range.

pageindex-tree-diff-can-flag-changed-sec.text: A section-level diff between old and new PageIndex trees could flag beliefs sourced from changed sections as potentially stale.

parallel-batching-preserves-results.text: With `batch_size=1` and `parallel=2`, `review_justifications` invokes `invoke_model` per candidate batch and combines both parsed responses.

parallel-mode-loses-batch-order.text: When `parallel > 0`, results are appended in `as_completed` order, so the returned list is not necessarily in the original `belief_ids` order.

parallel-mode-preserves-completion-order.text: Parallel results are appended in `as_completed` order, so `all_results` may not match the order of `premise_ids`.

parse-beliefs-defaults-dependency-lists-.text: `parse_beliefs` defaults `depends_on` and `unless` to empty lists when the corresponding markdown bullets are absent.

parse-beliefs-defaults-missing-source-ty.text: `parse_beliefs` returns `source_type == ""` for claim blocks without a Source type line.

parse-beliefs-does-not-validate-dependen.text: `parse_beliefs` returns a flat list of claim dicts and does not validate that referenced `depends_on` or `unless` IDs exist.

parse-beliefs-returns-dicts.text: Too granular — the dict-return pattern is partially covered by `api-functions-return-dicts`, and the specific field list is an implementation detail likely to evolve

parse-beliefs-splits-unless-into-comma-l.text: `parse_beliefs` comma-splits the `Unless:` value into a list and preserves the `Depends on:` entries as an ordered list.

parse-beliefs-triggers-on-h3-headers.text: `parse_beliefs` parses claim blocks structurally from `###` headers and does not require the surrounding `# Belief Registry` or `## Claims` sections.

parse-beliefs-truncates-text-to-first-no.text: `parse_beliefs` sets each claim's `text` to the first non-metadata, non-empty line after the header, truncating multi-line descriptions.

parse-cli-json-is-the-only-cost-sink.text: `_record_cost` is invoked from `_parse_cli_json`; invalid JSON therefore leaves `get_cost_summary()["calls"] == 0`.

parse-contradiction-extracts-nogood-id-s.text: parse_contradiction_response extracts ### NOGOOD <id> sections from LLM responses, pulling out claims, analysis, and severity.

parse-contradiction-filters-hallucinated.text: `parse_contradiction_response` drops any claim not present in `valid_ids` and discards a nogood if fewer than 2 claims survive.

parse-contradiction-response-uses-nogood.text: parse_contradiction_response expects nogoods in markdown format with `### NOGOOD <id>` headers and `Claims:`, `Analysis:`, and `Severity:` fields.

parse-defaults-classification-to-all.text: `parse_justification_review` normalizes missing, null, or omitted classification to `"ALL"`.

parse-defaults-to-accurate.text: `parse_premise_review_response` defaults `accurate` and `well_scoped` to `True` when the LLM omits them.

parse-diff-hunks-ends-inclusive.text: `parse_diff_hunks("@@ -89,5 +89,7 @@")` returns `[(89, 93)]` (start + count − 1) and excludes zero-count hunks like `@@ -89,0 @@`.

parse-diff-hunks-uses-old-line-ranges.text: `parse_diff_hunks` parses unified-diff hunk headers into inclusive `(start, end)` ranges using the old-file line numbers and excludes zero-width hunks.

parse-failures-downgrade-to-retract.text: An unparseable LLM response yields `{"action": "retract", "rationale": "Could not parse repair response"}`.

parse-justification-review-returns-first.text: `parse_justification_review` scans for the first bracket with a successfully decoded JSON list containing an item with `id`, and ignores subsequent arrays.

parse-match-response-filters-unknown-ids.text: `parse_match_response` drops any `matched_ids` value that is not in the supplied candidate set, returning only the intersection.

parse-nogoods-affects-is-comma-split-lis.text: `parse_nogoods` returns each nogood with `id`, `label`, `resolution`, and a comma-split `affects` list.

parse-premise-review-response-scans-ever.text: `parse_premise_review_response` iterates every `[` in the response and uses `JSONDecoder.raw_decode`, returning the first parseable list with id-bearing dicts.

parse-proposals-parses-gate-blocks-with-.text: parse_proposals extracts GATE blocks that include `unless` outlists.

parse-proposals-supports-legacy-v09-form.text: parse_proposals supports the old v0.9 format with backtick-delimited IDs and bold field names, as well as ### DERIVE and ### GATE blocks.

parse-proposals-supports-v09-bold-field-.text: parse_proposals can parse the older v0.9 proposal format that uses bold field names.

parse-repair-defaults-to-retract.text: When the LLM omits the `"action"` field in its JSON response, `parse_repair_response` defaults to `"retract"` with `corrected_text=None`, making the safe (non-fabricating) action the default.

parse-repair-response-allows-rewrite-wit.text: `parse_repair_response` does not require `corrected_text` when `action` is `"rewrite"`; missing or null `corrected_text` becomes `None`.

parse-repair-response-catches-only-jsond.text: `parse_repair_response` catches only `json.JSONDecodeError` during candidate-array decoding; other malformed response types may raise.

parse-repair-response-defaults-to-retrac.text: When an LLM result dict omits `action`, `parse_repair_response` fills in `action="retract"`, `corrected_text=None`, and `rationale=""`.

parse-repair-response-does-not-validate-.text: Missing `action` defaults to `"retract"`, but any present action value is accepted unchanged.
A present `action` value is copied unchanged even if invalid or `None`; only a missing `action` defaults to `"retract"`.

parse-repair-response-drops-malformed-it.text: `parse_repair_response` scans for the first valid JSON array, keeps only dict items containing `id`, normalizes surviving items with defaults, and returns `[]` if none parse.

parse-repair-response-normalizes-to-four.text: `parse_repair_response` returns new dicts with exactly `id`, `action`, `corrected_text`, and `rationale`; extra fields from decoded items are dropped.

parse-repair-response-returns-normalized.text: Every returned item contains exactly the keys `id`, `action`, `corrected_text`, and `rationale`.

parse-repair-response-scans-for-first-va.text: Parsing iterates over each `[` position and returns the first list containing at least one dict with an `id` key, dropping malformed entries.

parse-repair-response-searches-all-brack.text: The parser scans every `[` and returns the first decoded array that yields at least one valid item.

parse-repair-response-skips-items-withou.text: Items that are not dictionaries or lack an `"id"` key are filtered out before returning results.

parse-repo-id-rejects-non-hf-hosts.text: `_parse_repo_id` raises `ValueError("Not a HuggingFace URL ...")` for any URL whose host is not `huggingface.co`.

parse-review-defaults-to-passing.text: `parse_review_response` defaults missing fields to valid=True, sufficient=True, necessary=True, unnecessary_antecedents=[] — the LLM only needs to report failures explicitly; omission means the belief passed.

parse-review-response-catches-jsondecode.text: `parse_review_response` catches `json.JSONDecodeError` per candidate position but does not catch `TypeError` from non-string input.

parse-review-response-defaults-missing-b.text: `parse_review_response` defaults missing `valid`, `sufficient`, and `necessary` boolean fields to `True`.

parse-review-response-defaults-to-permis.text: Missing `valid`/`sufficient`/`necessary` fields in LLM JSON default to `True`.

parse-review-response-filters-dicts-with.text: Non-dict items and dicts missing `"id"` are silently dropped from the returned list.

parse-review-response-first-qualifying-a.text: `parse_review_response` returns the first non-empty qualifying JSON array found and ignores any later arrays or trailing prose.

parse-review-response-is-pure.text: The function performs no I/O, mutates no arguments, and cannot raise on malformed JSON.

parse-review-response-never-raises.text: `parse_review_response` returns an empty list on any malformed input — bad JSON, non-list JSON, items missing `id` fields — rather than raising exceptions, with missing boolean fields defaulting to `True`.

parse-review-response-normalizes-schema.text: Every emitted dict contains all nine canonical keys, with `True`/`[]`/`""` defaults when the model omitted them.

parse-review-response-parse-failure-indi.text: Callers cannot distinguish total parse failure from a legitimate zero-result review because `parse_review_response` returns `[]` in both cases.

parse-review-response-returns-empty-list.text: Returns `[]` when no `[` position decodes to a list containing at least one dict with an `"id"` key.
`parse_review_response` returns an empty list on malformed input — bad JSON, non-list JSON, or items missing `id` fields — rather than raising an exception.

parse-review-response-returns-empty-on-m.text: Malformed JSON, non-list JSON, and items missing `id` do not produce review entries.

parse-review-response-skips-empty-filter.text: A successfully decoded but empty-or-fully-filtered list does not end the scan; later `[` positions continue to be tried.

parse-update-proposals-coerces-enum-fiel.text: Out-of-taxonomy `action`/`failure_mode`/`basis` values are downgraded to `"update"`/`""`/`"prior-knowledge"` respectively rather than rejected.

parse-update-proposals-does-not-type-che.text: Any decoded item that is a dict with an `"id"` key is accepted even if the `id` value is not a string.

parse-update-proposals-is-total-function.text: `parse_update_proposals` never raises: malformed JSON, non-list input, or missing keys all produce `[]` or a filtered list of validated dicts; items lacking an `id` key are silently dropped rather than defaulted.

parse-update-proposals-may-raise-on-non-.text: Passing `None` or a non-string `response` raises `TypeError` from `enumerate`/`raw_decode` rather than returning `[]`.

parse-update-proposals-normalizes-taxono.text: Invalid `action`, `failure_mode`, and `basis` values are coerced to `"update"`, `""`, and `"prior-knowledge"` respectively.

parse-update-proposals-passes-through-no.text: When present, `evidence` and `comment` are copied verbatim even if non-string; the empty-string default applies only when the keys are absent.

parse-update-proposals-preserves-canonic.text: `parse_update_proposals` returns fresh dicts containing exactly `id`, `action`, `proposed_text`, `failure_mode`, `basis`, `evidence`, and `comment`; extra LLM fields are dropped.

parse-update-proposals-requires-id.text: Items that are not dicts or that lack an `"id"` key are silently dropped.

parse-update-proposals-returns-empty-lis.text: `parse_update_proposals("not json at all")` returns `[]` rather than raising.

parse-update-proposals-returns-first-non.text: `parse_update_proposals` returns immediately on the first `[` position that `raw_decode`s into a list with at least one valid `{id: ...}` dict, ignoring any later arrays.
The function returns at the first `[` whose decoded list yields at least one valid item; later arrays in the same response are ignored.

parse-update-proposals-strips-extra-fiel.text: The parser rebuilds each proposal with exactly `id, action, proposed_text, failure_mode, basis, evidence, comment`, dropping any `cascade` field the model might output.

parse-update-proposals-swallows-json-err.text: `JSONDecodeError` is caught and the scan continues; the function never propagates JSON parse errors.

parse-update-proposals-takes-first-valid.text: `parse_update_proposals` returns the first parsed JSON array that yields at least one valid dict item and ignores later candidate arrays in the same response.

parse-update-proposals-uses-raw-decode.text: `parse_update_proposals` uses `json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode` at every `[` character to extract a JSON array from prose around it.

parse-verify-response-drops-missing-verd.text: Entries in the LLM JSON without a `verdict` key are excluded from the parsed result.

parse-verify-response-never-raises.text: `reasons.verify.parse_verify_response` returns an empty dict `{}` for any malformed JSON, empty string, or missing `"verdict"` key — it never raises an exception

parse-verify-response-normalizes-verdict.text: `parse_verify_response` uppercases the `verdict` string but does not validate it against the four allowed values.

per-customer-wiki-uses-own-dist-build-be.text: Each enterprise customer's private wiki uses its own dist/ build deployed behind IAP and gated to their Google Workspace domain.

per-model-elapsed-requires-prior-cost-re.text: The `if model in _cost_tracker["by_model"]` guard means per-model elapsed time only accumulates after a successful `_record_cost` created the entry.

persistence-is-snapshot-not-incremental.text: The storage layer operates as a full snapshot: save replaces all rows, load trusts stored values without re-propagation, and the dependents index is rebuilt from scratch

justifications.label: Four independent storage behaviors all point to a snapshot-and-rebuild strategy rather than incremental sync

persistence-round-trip-is-lossless.text: The save/load round trip preserves all network state faithfully: snapshot persistence captures the full graph, stored truth values are trusted without re-propagation, justification insertion order is preserved via rowid, and outlist relationships survive serialization.

justifications.label: Round-trip is lossless for persisted state, but the dependents index must be rebuilt on load — a fragile denormalization that could diverge if rebuild logic doesn't perfectly mirror the original construction

persistence-verification-form-safe-write.text: The storage layer's atomic full-replace writes and trust-based loads pair with the verification layer's pure, read-only, non-raising reads to create a safe duality: state can be persisted without partial-write risk and audited without mutation risk.

justifications.label: Write path (atomic, trust-based) and read/verify path (pure, non-raising) are independently sufficient to guarantee "save without corruption, verify without side effects"; together they form a complete safe duality.
