pg-access-control-raises-permission-erro.text: `PgApi.show_node()` raises `PermissionError` when called with a `visible_to` list that doesn't intersect the node's `access_tags`, enforcing per-node access control at the API boundary

pg-activation-is-atomic-all-or-nothing.text: PostgreSQL backend activation is all-or-nothing per function: each API method independently checks for both conninfo and project_id, and the absence of either triggers an immediate early-return to the SQLite path—no partial PG mode or half-routed queries exist.

justifications.label: The early-return mechanism (how) combined with the mandatory project_id constraint (what) together establish the atomicity; either alone is insufficient to prove all-or-nothing behavior.

pg-activation-is-atomic-all-or-nothing-v.text: The observed PostgreSQL dispatch mechanism operates at the function level: each API function checks `pg_conninfo` and, when present, short-circuits to `_pg_dispatch`, which instantiates PgApi and routes the call via `getattr`, rather than relying on inheritance or factory patterns. Separately, when `pg_conninfo` is supplied without a corresponding `project_id`, the system terminates via `sys.exit()` rather than proceeding with an incomplete configuration. Taken together, the mechanism appears to engage the PG backend on a per-function basis such that a given call is either routed through PgApi or through the default (non-PG) path, with no observed support for partial PG routing or half-routed queries within a single function call.

pg-add-justification-requires-sl-or-cp.text: `PgApi.add_justification` raises `ValueError` when both the `sl` and `cp` justification inputs are empty.

pg-antecedent-refs-have-no-fk-constraint.text: Antecedent and outlist references in `rms_justifications` are JSONB arrays without foreign key constraints; nonexistent referenced nodes default to truth value OUT via `truth_cache.get(a, "OUT")`.

pg-api-accepts-connection-string-or-exis.text: `PgApi` constructor accepts either a PostgreSQL connection string or an existing `psycopg` connection, plus a `project_id`.

pg-api-defend-id-collision-raises-valuee.text: `PgApi.defend` raises `ValueError` when the provided `defense_id` collides with an existing node.

pg-api-duplicate-add-node-raises-generic.text: `PgApi.add_node` with an existing node ID raises a generic `Exception` rather than a specific subclass.

pg-api-fixture-initializes-db.text: The `pg_api` fixture calls `init_db()` on the UUID-scoped `PgApi` instance before yielding it to the test.

pg-api-fixture-requires-database-url.text: `pg_api` skips (does not fail) when `DATABASE_URL` is unset, via `pytest.skip` inside the fixture body.

pg-api-fixture-skips-when-database-url-m.text: This duplicates the existing belief that PG tests are gated by `DATABASE_URL` availability.

pg-api-idempotent-retract-assert-return-.text: `PgApi.retract_node` on an already-OUT node and `assert_node` on an already-IN node return an empty changed list rather than raising.

pg-api-import-is-deferred.text: `from reasons.pg import PgApi` is executed inside the fixture body (not at module top) to avoid importing DB drivers at collection time when `DATABASE_URL` is absent.

pg-api-missing-node-operations-raise-key.text: `PgApi.retract_node`, `show_node`, `what_if_retract`, `what_if_assert`, `challenge`, `defend`, `add_justification`, and `add_nogood` raise `KeyError` for nonexistent node IDs.

pg-api-what-if-never-mutates.text: `PgApi.what_if_retract()` and `what_if_assert()` are read-only operations — they return cascade analysis (changed/went_in/went_out) without modifying database state, verified by checking `get_status()` before and after

pg-assert-restores-dependents-except-ind.text: Asserting a PgApi node restores transitive dependents whose justifications are satisfied but does not restore nodes that were independently retracted.

pg-available-is-import-time-immutable.text: `pg_available` is a module-level boolean evaluated once at `conftest.py` import time as a snapshot of `DATABASE_URL`; setting or unsetting the environment variable after pytest starts has no effect on which tests are skipped.

pg-backend-requires-domain-id.text: `_backend_kwargs` refuses to return PostgreSQL kwargs unless a domain id is supplied via flag or the `REASONS_DOMAIN_ID`/`REASONS_PROJECT_ID` env var, exiting with code 1 otherwise.

pg-cached-validator-lacks-justification-.text: `_justification_valid_cached` in `reasons/pg.py:3524` takes only `cur`, `antecedents`, and `outlist`, so it cannot directly distinguish SL from CP.

pg-challenge-creates-outlist-entry-forci.text: A PgApi challenge creates an outlist entry that forces the target node OUT.

pg-challenge-defense-uses-outlist.text: PgApi challenge and defend operate through the outlist non-monotonic mechanism rather than directly toggling truth values, and defending all challenges restores the target to IN.

pg-cleanup-covers-five-tables.text: Fixture teardown deletes from exactly `rms_propagation_log`, `rms_justifications`, `rms_nogoods`, `rms_network_meta`, and `rms_nodes` — adding a new `project_id`-scoped table without updating the fixture will leak test data.

pg-cleanup-deletes-in-dependency-order.text: The `pg_api` teardown deletes rows across the five tracked tables in dependency order, with `rms_propagation_log` first and `rms_nodes` last.

pg-compact-generates-budget-constrained-.text: `PgApi.compact()` produces a markdown summary of the belief network constrained by a token budget, filtered by `visible_to` access tags, sorted by dependent count, with summary-node elision and nogood inclusion

pg-compatible-command-count-is-25.text: 25 CLI commands dispatch to PostgreSQL through `PgApi`.

pg-conninfo-accepts-flag-envvar-or-both.text: PostgreSQL connection is configured via `--pg`/`--project-id` CLI flags or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO`/`REASONS_PROJECT_ID` environment variables, with CLI flags taking precedence over env vars — `_backend_kwargs(args)` handles the dispatch.

pg-convert-to-premise-deletes-justificat.text: `PgApi.convert_to_premise` deletes all justifications for a node and sets its truth value to IN.

pg-data-integrity-achieves-defense-in-de.text: PgApi's data integrity achieves defense-in-depth through both application-level enforcement (write-time referential validation and outlist-aware dependent queries spanning antecedent and outlist references) and comprehensive input validation at all system boundaries, but full defense-in-depth requires database-level foreign key constraints to provide a second independent enforcement layer

justifications.label: Application-level integrity enforcement combined with comprehensive boundary validation provides one defense layer; adding FK constraints would complete the defense-in-depth pattern with a second database-level layer

pg-defend-creates-outlist-entry-restorin.text: A PgApi defense creates an outlist entry on the challenge node, neutralizing the challenge and restoring the target.

pg-derived-access-tags-union-antecedent-.text: In PgApi, a derived node inherits the union of its antecedents' access tags.

pg-derived-node-inherits-union-access-ta.text: When PgApi creates a derived node, `_inherit_access_tags` sets its access tags to the union of its antecedents' access tags.

pg-derived-node-inherits-union-of-antece.text: Derived nodes in PgApi inherit the union of their antecedents' access tags.

pg-dispatch-context-manages-pgapi-and-fo.text: `_pg_dispatch` opens `PgApi` as a context manager, calls the requested method via `getattr`, forwards kwargs verbatim, returns the method result unchanged, and does not swallow exceptions.

pg-dispatch-is-context-managed.text: `_pg_dispatch` instantiates `PgApi` as a context manager and delegates the named method with forwarded kwargs, returning its result unchanged.

pg-dispatch-is-function-level-early-retu.text: PostgreSQL routing uses a function-level early-return pattern — each API function checks `pg_conninfo` and short-circuits to `_pg_dispatch`, which instantiates PgApi and calls the matching method via `getattr` — rather than using abstract base classes, subclassing, or factory patterns.

pg-dispatch-requires-project-id.text: When `pg_conninfo` is provided (via CLI `--pg` flag or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` env var) without a corresponding `project_id`, the system calls `sys.exit()` rather than proceeding with an incomplete configuration

pg-export-network-filters-private-metada.text: `PgApi.export_network` filters out private metadata keys that start with `_`.

pg-export-network-respects-visible-to.text: `PgApi.export_network(visible_to=...)` filters exported nodes by access tags using the `visible_to` argument.

pg-extra-required-for-postgres.text: PostgreSQL support requires installing the `pg` or `test-pg` optional extra (`psycopg[binary]>=3.1`); it is not available in a bare install.

pg-extra-requires-psycopg-binary-3-1.text: The pg optional dependency extra requires psycopg[binary] >=3.1.

pg-fixture-cleans-five-tables-in-fk-safe.text: This duplicates the existing beliefs about the five-table cleanup set and FK-safe deletion order.

pg-fixture-lazily-imports-pgapi.text: This duplicates the existing belief that `PgApi` is imported lazily inside the fixture to avoid collection-time database imports.

pg-fixture-provides-per-test-isolation.text: Each pg test receives an isolated `PgApi` instance via the `pg_api` fixture, which creates a fresh project namespace (UUID) and tears down after each test, ensuring zero shared state between tests.

pg-fixture-rolls-back-before-delete-clea.text: The `pg_api` fixture calls `api.conn.rollback()` before its DELETE cleanup to clear aborted transaction state left by failed test SQL.

pg-fixture-teardown-close-not-guaranteed.text: The `pg_api` teardown has no try/finally, so a failure in one of its DELETE statements can prevent `api.close()` from running.

pg-fixture-uses-uuid-isolation.text: Each `pg_api` test fixture partitions its data by a unique UUID v4 `project_id` rather than using transactions or ephemeral databases, enabling safe concurrent test execution against a shared database.

pg-get-status-reports-justification-coun.text: `PgApi.get_status` lists all nodes with truth values and justification counts.

pg-import-is-deferred.text: `PgApi` is imported inside the `pg_api` fixture body, not at module top-level, so the test suite loads without Postgres dependencies when running SQLite-only tests.

pg-internal-helpers-do-not-commit.text: Internal PgApi helpers such as `_add_node_raw`, `_propagate`, and `_compute_truth` operate on a passed cursor without committing; the public caller owns the transaction boundary.

pg-keyerror-includes-missing-node-id.text: When `add_node` references a nonexistent node in `sl=` or `unless=`, PgApi raises `KeyError` with the missing node ID in the exception message — tested via `pytest.raises(KeyError, match="ghost")` — enabling callers to identify which reference is dangling.

pg-list-gated-excludes-satisfied-gates.text: PgApi list_gated excludes satisfied gates, where a gate is satisfied when its blocker is OUT.

pg-list-gated-finds-out-nodes-blocked-by.text: `PgApi.list_gated` finds OUT nodes blocked by IN outlist nodes (GATE beliefs).

pg-list-gated-finds-out-nodes-by-outlist.text: `list_gated` finds OUT nodes that would flip IN if their outlist blocker nodes were retracted (GATE pattern).

pg-lookup-substring-searches-id-text-sou.text: `PgApi.lookup` performs an all-terms substring search over the full belief block: ID, text, source, and references.

pg-marker-registration-does-not-skip-tes.text: `pytest_configure` registers the `pg` marker for selection and warning suppression, but the marker itself does not skip tests; skipping requires `skip_no_pg` or `pytest.skip` in the fixture.

pg-marker-requires-pytest-configure.text: The `pg` marker is registered by `pytest_configure`; without that hook, `@pytest.mark.pg` would trigger unknown-marker warnings.

pg-missing-psycopg-raises-importerror-wi.text: `PgApi.__init__` calls `_require_psycopg()`, which raises `ImportError` with install instructions when the `psycopg` driver is unavailable.

pg-mode-requires-domain-id-or-exits.text: When PG is configured (via CLI flag or `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` env) but `domain_id` cannot be resolved from either source, `_backend_kwargs` raises `SystemExit` rather than proceeding.

pg-multi-tenancy-allows-node-id-reuse-ac.text: Two PgApi instances with different project_id values sharing one database can reuse the same node ID independently.

pg-multi-tenancy-is-referentially-comple.text: PgApi's multi-tenant isolation with composite primary keys and application-level BFS propagation prevents all cross-project data leakage and ensures consistent truth maintenance — unless antecedent references stored as JSONB arrays lack foreign key constraints, allowing phantom node references within a project.

justifications.label: Multi-tenant isolation (depth-1) and consistent propagation semantics (depth-0) are undermined if JSONB reference arrays can point to nonexistent nodes without database-level enforcement

pg-multi-tenancy-via-project-id.text: `PgApi` isolates beliefs by `project_id` so identical node IDs in different projects store independent data with no cross-contamination — each test gets a unique UUID project

pg-namespace-auto-creates-active-premise.text: Calling PgApi.add_node with a namespace parameter auto-creates an <ns>:active premise node and adds it to the derived node's antecedent list.

pg-namespace-prefixing-is-idempotent.text: PgApi.add_node with namespace=agent1 produces agent1:x for input x and does not double-prefix an already-prefixed agent1:x ID.

pg-network-meta-stores-per-project-confi.text: `rms_network_meta` is a key-value store for per-project configuration such as repo paths and the nogood counter.

pg-propagate-ignores-justification-type.text: `PgApi._propagate()` fetches justification type but evaluates both `SL` and `CP` justifications using the same antecedent/outlist rules.

pg-propagate-missing-seed-yields-empty-l.text: `PgApi._propagate()` does not raise a dedicated error for a missing `changed_id`; if no dependents are found it can return empty lists.

pg-propagate-only-writes-truth-value-and.text: `PgApi._propagate()` updates only `rms_nodes.truth_value` and writes `rms_propagation_log`; it does not modify `updated_at`, `retracted_at`, metadata, or justifications.

pg-propagate-returns-went-out-and-went-i.text: `PgApi._propagate()` returns a `(went_out, went_in)` pair of node-ID lists and excludes `changed_id` from both lists.

pg-propagate-visits-nodes-only-after-tru.text: `PgApi._propagate()` adds a node to `visited` only when its truth value changes, so each changed node is evaluated at most once per propagation call.

pg-propagation-achieves-atomic-efficient.text: The PostgreSQL backend achieves topology-complete, terminating propagation through application-level BFS with JSONB containment queries for efficient dependent lookup, wrapped in single-transaction-per-method atomicity — correctness lives in Python logic while performance lives in the GIN-indexed data layer.

justifications.label: Multi-step architectural argument — BFS provides the traversal algorithm, JSONB+GIN provides the O(1) per-operation dependent lookup that makes BFS feasible at scale, and per-method transactions guarantee that a partially-completed propagation never leaves inconsistent state. Removing any one breaks the architecture (no algorithm, no efficiency, or no atomicity).

pg-propagation-matches-sqlite-semantics.text: The PostgreSQL backend's propagation achieves the same topology-complete, terminating, inconsistency-safe semantics as the SQLite backend — identical BFS traversal with equivalent correctness guarantees — enabling true backend-agnostic operation for all truth-maintenance operations.

justifications.label: Positive claim (PG matches SQLite propagation semantics) gated by the known gap that PgApi's public surface doesn't cover the full API — until partial coverage is resolved, we cannot assert full semantic equivalence across all operations.

pg-psycopg-is-optional-dependency.text: `psycopg` (v3) is soft-imported with fallback to `None`; `_require_psycopg()` raises `ImportError` with install instructions at `PgApi` construction time, mirroring the `mcp_client.py` lazy-guard pattern.

pg-reference-integrity-is-application-co.text: PG achieves referential integrity through application-level compensation (pre-insert validation + GIN-indexed containment queries) rather than database-level FK constraints on JSONB reference arrays

justifications.label: The three facts together establish a compensating-control pattern: write-time validation ensures referential integrity at insertion, GIN-indexed containment ensures complete dependent discovery at query time, and the absence of FK constraints is precisely what makes the first two necessary rather than redundant. Retracting any one (e.g., FKs added, GIN index removed, or validation removed) breaks the "compensating" characterization.

pg-reference-integrity-is-write-verified.text: PG achieves full reference integrity at both write time (pre-insert validation of all antecedent/outlist refs) and read time (GIN-indexed containment queries discovering all dependents including outlist-connected nodes)

justifications.label: Write-time validation prevents dangling references at insertion; read-time GIN containment ensures no dependent is missed during cascade queries (including outlist-connected nodes). The claim is gated because partial API coverage means some PG-routed operations may bypass either validation or the complete dependent query path, breaking the "full integrity" guarantee until the API surface is complete.

pg-reimplements-network-in-sql.text: `PgApi` reimplements the in-memory `Network`'s algorithms (BFS propagation, entrenchment scoring, nogood resolution, dialectical operations) directly in SQL rather than delegating to the `Network` class.

metadata.retract_reason: Over-generalizes: claims dialectical operations are reimplemented in SQL, contradicted by pgapi-partial-api-coverage which says dialectics are deferred

pg-remove-justification-deletes-nth-by-s.text: `PgApi.remove_justification(node_id, index)` deletes the Nth justification by serial ID order.

pg-remove-justification-prevents-zero-ju.text: `PgApi.remove_justification` refuses a removal that would leave a derived node with zero justifications.

pg-requires-domain-id.text: `_backend_kwargs` raises `SystemExit` when PostgreSQL is selected without a resolvable domain/project id, whereas `_require_sqlite` raises `SystemExit` whenever PostgreSQL is configured at all.

pg-requires-optional-psycopg.text: `psycopg` is imported in a `try/except`; `_require_psycopg` raises `ImportError` with install instructions when it's missing.

pg-retract-already-out-returns-empty-cha.text: Retracting an already-OUT node in PgApi returns an empty changed list.

pg-retracted-pin-survives-antecedent-rea.text: In PgApi, a node explicitly retracted remains OUT when its antecedent is re-asserted, even though the justification chain is satisfied.

pg-schema-constrains-truth-values-and-ju.text: The PostgreSQL schema constrains `truth_value` to `'IN'` or `'OUT'` and justification `type` to `'SL'` or `'CP'` via CHECK constraints.

pg-search-combines-full-text-and-ilike-f.text: `PgApi.search` uses PostgreSQL `to_tsvector`/`plainto_tsquery` full-text search plus an ILIKE fallback on node IDs and includes 1-hop neighbor expansion.

pg-search-includes-one-hop-neighbors.text: PostgreSQL full-text search via `plainto_tsquery` includes 1-hop neighbor expansion — direct antecedents and dependents of matching nodes are included in results, providing richer context than exact-match-only search.

pg-teardown-deletes-in-fk-safe-order.text: The `pg_api` fixture teardown deletes rows in foreign-key-safe order (children before parents): `rms_propagation_log` → `rms_justifications` → `rms_nogoods` → `rms_network_meta` → `rms_nodes`; reversing this order would violate FK constraints.

pg-teardown-rollback-before-delete.text: The `pg_api` fixture calls `conn.rollback()` before cleanup deletes to recover from any failed-transaction state left by the test, preventing cleanup failures from cascading.

pg-test-suite-is-backend-parity.text: `test_pg.py` is a parity test suite: every behavior tested has a corresponding expected behavior from the SQLite backend, validating that PgApi returns the same dict shapes and enforces the same invariants to ensure backend interchangeability.

pg-tests-gated-by-database-availability.text: The entire `test_pg.py` suite (18 test classes) is conditionally skipped via `skip_no_pg` marker from conftest when PostgreSQL is unavailable, and selectively collectible via `pytest.mark.pg` — enabling CI without a Postgres dependency.

pg-tests-require-database-url.text: The PgApi tests in `tests/test_pg.py` are marked `@pytest.mark.pg` and skipped when `DATABASE_URL` is not set.

pg-tests-skip-without-postgres-connectio.text: All tests in `test_pg.py` carry the `pytest.mark.pg` marker and `skip_no_pg` conditional skip — they are silently skipped when no PostgreSQL connection is available

pg-unsupported-features-raise-before-dis.text: API features unsupported by the PostgreSQL backend (e.g. `any_mode`, tag-filtered `search`, `min_depth`) raise `NotImplementedError` before `_pg_dispatch`, rather than silently using SQLite behavior.

pg-unsupported-params-raise-not-implemen.text: When PgApi-routed commands receive unsupported parameters (e.g., search with `depth != 1`, list with `challenged`/`min_depth`, add with `namespace`), the dispatch raises `NotImplementedError` with a clear message rather than silently ignoring the parameter.

pg-update-node-updates-only-provided-fie.text: `PgApi.update_node` performs a dynamic UPDATE that only sets provided `text`, `source`, and `source_url` fields.

pg-uses-jsonb-with-gin-for-dependent-que.text: PgApi stores antecedents and outlist as JSONB arrays with GIN indexes, enabling per-operation dependent lookups via `@>` containment queries — unlike the SQLite backend which loads the full network, PgApi queries relationships incrementally.

pg-uses-project-id-for-multi-tenancy.text: Every `PgApi` query includes `project_id` in its WHERE clause, providing multi-tenant isolation with no cross-project queries and composite primary keys `(id, project_id)`.

pg-what-if-is-safely-simulated.text: PgApi's what-if operations achieve safe simulation: mutations are performed against real PostgreSQL data for accurate cascade analysis, then rolled back within a transaction to guarantee zero persistent side effects — combining fidelity with safety.

justifications.label: Transaction rollback bridges the gap between accurate simulation and mutation safety

pg-what-if-isolation-is-ownership-agnost.text: PG what-if operations achieve transactional isolation (mutations rolled back) regardless of whether PgApi owns or borrows the underlying connection

justifications.label: In "borrowed" connection mode, the caller might close the connection mid-analysis; in "owned" mode, the lifecycle is managed internally. Transaction rollback in both cases guarantees that hypothetical cascade analysis never leaks into committed state, making the what-if contract independent of connection ownership mode.

pg-what-if-operations-are-read-only.text: PgApi what_if_retract() and what_if_assert() report cascades without mutating database state.

pg-what-if-rolls-back-unconditionally.text: `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` mutate rows inside a transaction, collect cascade results, and then unconditionally call `self.conn.rollback()` in a `finally` block so simulations are side-effect-free.

pg-what-if-uses-transaction-rollback.text: `what_if_retract`/`what_if_assert` perform real mutations inside a transaction, collect cascade effects, then rollback — reusing the propagation engine without duplicating logic.

pgapi-achieves-implementation-parity.text: PgApi achieves full behavioral parity with the in-memory Network implementation: it reimplements the core algorithms (entrenchment scoring, nogood resolution, BFS propagation, dialectics) in SQL with BFS propagation executed in application-level Python.

justifications.label: PgApi reimplements core Network algorithms but has not yet achieved full API coverage — when pgapi-partial-api-coverage is retracted (all operations implemented), this GATE flips IN to confirm parity

pgapi-add-node-classifies-premise-vs-der.text: `PgApi.add_node` returns `{node_id, truth_value, type}` and classifies nodes as `premise` when `sl` is omitted and `derived` when `sl` is supplied.

pgapi-add-node-inherits-access-tags-from.text: PgApi.add_node inherits access tags from a node's antecedents.

pgapi-add-node-returns-contract-and-reje.text: `PgApi.add_node` raises `ValueError` if the node ID already exists and returns a dict containing `node_id`, `truth_value`, `type`, and `premise_count`.

pgapi-add-node-returns-node-type-and-pre.text: PgApi.add_node returns the node type (premise vs. derived) and the current premise count.

pgapi-bfs-propagation-in-python.text: PgApi implements BFS propagation in application-level Python (not stored procedures), using JSONB containment queries (`@>`) against GIN indexes to find dependents

pgapi-connection-ownership-dual-mode.text: `PgApi` constructor either owns a connection (opens from a connection string) or borrows an existing `psycopg.Connection`; `close()` semantics differ accordingly (closes owned, leaves borrowed intact)

pgapi-connection-ownership-is-constructo.text: `PgApi` closes its connection on `close()` only when constructed from a conninfo string; an injected `psycopg.Connection` is not closed by `PgApi`.

pgapi-constructor-accepts-connection-str.text: The PgApi constructor accepts either a PostgreSQL connection string or an existing psycopg connection, plus a project_id.

pgapi-coverage-gaps-decomposed-into-eigh.text: 23 missing PgApi functions were catalogued and filed as 8 focused sub-issues numbered #63 through #70 by category.

pgapi-defers-api-imports-to-avoid-circul.text: `PgApi` defers imports from `reasons.api`, `llm`, `check_stale`, `import_beliefs`, `metadata`, and `import_agent` into function bodies to avoid a circular import with `reasons.api`.

pgapi-enforces-referential-integrity-bid.text: PgApi enforces referential integrity in both directions: write-time validation checks all antecedent and outlist IDs exist before inserting justifications, while read-time dependent discovery queries both antecedent and outlist JSONB containment to find all affected nodes.

justifications.label: Write-time validation and read-time discovery are complementary halves of PgApi's referential integrity enforcement

pgapi-find-dependents-queries-outlist.text: PgApi's `_find_dependents` queries both `antecedents @>` and `outlist @>` JSONB containment, correctly enqueuing outlist-dependent nodes for re-evaluation — a capability the in-memory Network historically lacked until PR #31.

pgapi-has-no-retry-logic.text: `PgApi` uses one connection per instance with no retry on transient database errors; callers are expected to handle `psycopg` exceptions from connection failures or serialization conflicts.

pgapi-import-uses-kahn-with-cycle-fallba.text: Both `import_json` and `import_beliefs` topologically sort nodes via a multi-pass ready-set loop (Kahn's algorithm) with a fallback insertion pass for cycles, ensuring all nodes are inserted in dependency order

pgapi-init-db-uses-idempotent-column-pro.text: `PgApi.init_db` checks `information_schema.columns` and applies `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` for missing columns, making migrations idempotent.

pgapi-is-complete-sql-reimplementation.text: PgApi is a complete SQL-native reimplementation of the in-memory Network: it re-implements core algorithms (BFS propagation, entrenchment scoring, nogood resolution) directly in SQL with multi-tenant composite keys and per-method transaction semantics, achieving full behavioral parity.

justifications.label: SQL-native multi-tenancy composed with algorithm reimplementation yields full parity — but only when API coverage is complete

pgapi-is-sql-native-multi-tenant.text: PgApi operates as a SQL-native multi-tenant implementation: all operations execute directly against PostgreSQL with no in-memory Network object constructed, composite primary keys on all tables provide project-level isolation, and each public method is a single committed transaction.

justifications.label: Three architectural properties (no in-memory object, composite keys, per-method transactions) characterize PgApi as a distinct SQL-native implementation pattern

pgapi-jsonb-defensive-parsing.text: JSONB column values returned by psycopg may be Python strings depending on the active `row_factory`; all read paths must guard with `isinstance(x, str): json.loads(x)` before using the value

pgapi-jsonb-fields-checked-for-string-be.text: PgApi defensively checks every metadata, antecedents, and outlist field with isinstance(x, str) before calling json.loads, because psycopg may or may not auto-deserialize JSONB.

pgapi-justifications-cascade-delete-with.text: The `rms_justifications` table has `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `rms_nodes`, so deleting a node deletes its justifications.

pgapi-list-gated-finds-out-nodes-flippab.text: PgApi.list_gated finds OUT nodes that would flip IN if their outlist blockers went OUT, implementing the GATE pattern.

pgapi-list-nodes-missing-challenged-dept.text: PgApi `list_nodes()` does not support the `challenged`, `min_depth`, or `max_depth` filter parameters.

pgapi-missing-namespace-and-import-expor.text: PgApi is missing namespace support, import/export, and some maintenance operations; PRs #52-56 added challenge, defend, compact, list-gated, and what-if but did not close those gaps.

pgapi-multi-tenant-composite-keys.text: All PgApi tables use composite primary keys `(id, project_id)` for multi-tenancy, with JSONB columns (not TEXT) for antecedents, outlist, and metadata

pgapi-no-cli-backend-flag.text: The CLI has no `--backend pg` flag or `DATABASE_URL` handling for selecting PgApi.

pgapi-no-in-memory-network.text: `PgApi` executes all operations as direct SQL against PostgreSQL — no in-memory `Network` object is ever constructed, enabling concurrent writers

pgapi-one-transaction-per-method.text: Each PgApi public method is a single PostgreSQL transaction that commits or rolls back at the end; __exit__ rolls back on exception

pgapi-optional-psycopg-guard.text: The `psycopg` import is wrapped in `try/except ImportError` with `_require_psycopg()` raising a descriptive `ImportError`, making the PostgreSQL backend an optional dependency rather than a hard requirement

pgapi-partial-api-coverage.text: PgApi implements core operations (add/retract/assert/search/nogood/explain) but defers simulation, dialectics, namespace support, import/export, and maintenance operations to future work

metadata.retract_reason: All PgApi feature issues closed: #51 (challenge/defend/compact), #55 (what-if), #60 (coverage gaps), #63 (queries), #64 (export), #65 (namespace), #66 (import), #67 (maintenance), #68 (derive), #69 (dedup), #70 (repos/list-negative). Only #133 (N+1 perf) remains as optimization.

pgapi-patched-via-module-namespace.text: Every test patches `reasons.pg.PgApi` (not `reasons.api.PgApi`), implying `reasons.api` resolves `PgApi` through the `reasons.pg` module at call time rather than as a module-level import binding.

pgapi-propagate-recomputes-from-scratch.text: `PgApi.propagate()` recomputes truth values from scratch, allowing recovery after out-of-band raw SQL writes to `rms_nodes.truth_value`.

pgapi-propagation-batch-fetches-avoiding.text: `_propagate` drains the BFS queue in batches, issuing a single `SELECT … WHERE id = ANY(…)` per batch and a single `UPDATE` per changed node, avoiding N+1 queries on large cascades

pgapi-public-mutations-commit-per-operat.text: `PgApi` public mutation methods commit at the end of each operation; there are no long-lived transactions spanning multiple public calls.

pgapi-raw-add-node-bypasses-validation-a.text: `PgApi._add_node_raw` is an unsafe insert used by import paths: it does not validate references, inherit access tags, or commit.

pgapi-reference-integrity-raises-keyerro.text: `PgApi.add_node` and `PgApi.add_justification` reject `sl` or `unless` references to missing nodes with `KeyError`, while premise-only additions skip reference validation.

pgapi-referential-integrity-is-database-.text: PgApi achieves complete referential integrity: application-level bidirectional enforcement (write-time validation and outlist-aware dependent querying) is complemented by database-level foreign key constraints, preventing orphaned justification references even under direct SQL manipulation outside the application layer.

justifications.label: Application-level bidirectional ref enforcement (depth-1) on a SQL-native multi-tenant backend (depth-1) would achieve complete referential integrity IF the FK constraint gap were closed

pgapi-schema-contains-five-tables.text: PgApi defines five project-partitioned tables: rms_nodes, rms_justifications, rms_nogoods, rms_propagation_log, and rms_network_meta.

pgapi-search-uses-plainto-tsquery.text: PgApi search uses `plainto_tsquery` instead of manually quoted `to_tsquery` to handle user input containing single quotes.

pgapi-used-as-context-manager-in-dispatc.text: The `_pg_dispatch` helper instantiates `PgApi(conninfo, domain_id)` inside a `with` block, so `PgApi` must implement `__enter__`/`__exit__`; exceptions inside the block propagate (not suppressed).

pgapi-uses-psycopg-v3.text: `PgApi` uses psycopg v3 as its PostgreSQL driver, and psycopg is an optional dependency not required by CLI users.

pgapi-validates-refs-before-justificatio.text: PgApi's `_validate_refs` checks all antecedent and outlist node IDs exist in `rms_nodes` before inserting a justification, providing application-level referential integrity that compensates for JSONB arrays' inability to enforce foreign key constraints.

pgapi-what-if-tracks-cascade-depth.text: PgApi what_if_retract and what_if_assert annotate cascade effects with BFS depth by following both antecedents and outlist via _find_dependents.

pgapi-what-if-uses-transaction-rollback.text: PgApi's `what_if_retract` and `what_if_assert` wrap BFS cascade analysis inside a database transaction with `try/finally` guaranteed ROLLBACK, achieving read-only simulation by never committing the exploratory mutations.

pin-lines-auto-pins-sha.text: `pin_lines` sets `pinned_sha` and `source_hash` automatically when the node was not previously pinned.

pin-lines-raises-on-bad-range.text: `pin_lines` raises `ValueError` when `start < 1` or `start > end`, and `KeyError` when the target node id is absent from the network.

pin-lines-uses-1-indexed-inclusive-range.text: Line ranges in `pin_lines` are 1-indexed and inclusive (e.g., `"89-93"` covers lines 89 through 93); the function raises `ValueError` for `start < 1` or `start > end`, and `KeyError` for nonexistent node IDs.

pin-source-url-github-only.text: `pin_source_url` rewrites only `github.com` URLs; non-GitHub URLs are returned unchanged regardless of the SHA argument.

pin-source-url-rewrites-github-blob-to-s.text: `pin_source_url` rewrites GitHub `/blob/<branch>/<path>` URLs to `/blob/<sha>/<path>` using the provided commit SHA, passes through non-GitHub URLs unchanged, and uses a `source_path` hint to handle slashed branch names.

pin-source-url-rewrites-only-github.text: `pin_source_url` rewrites GitHub `blob/<branch>/<path>` URLs to `blob/<sha>/<path>` and leaves non-GitHub URLs unchanged.

pin-sources-is-idempotent-without-force.text: `pin_sources` skips nodes that already have `metadata["pinned_sha"]` set, returning zero results unless `force=True` is explicitly passed to re-pin.

pin-sources-skips-pinned-out-missing-and.text: `pin_sources` skips already-pinned nodes unless `force=True`, skips `OUT` nodes, skips nodes without a source, and skips missing source files while returning per-node pin reports.

pin-sources-skips-pinned-unless-forced.text: `pin_sources(net, ...)` returns zero results when every eligible node already has `metadata["pinned_sha"]`, unless `force=True` is passed.

pin-update-never-raises.text: `pin_update` reports failures via the `"error"` key in each result dict (`"not found"`, `"no source"`, `"source not found"`) and does not raise for these cases.

pin-update-reports-per-node-errors.text: `pin_update` returns per-node error dicts such as `{"error": "not found" | "no source" | "source not found" | "not in git repo"}` instead of silently skipping failures as `pin_sources` does.

pin-update-returns-error-dicts-not-excep.text: `pin_update` never raises for not-found nodes, missing sources, or missing source files; it returns an `{error: ...}` dict for those cases and refreshes `source_hash` on success.

pinned-lines-fast-path-skips-hashing-on-.text: When `pinned_lines` is present and no diff hunk overlaps the pinned range, `check_stale` continues without calling `hash_file`.

pinned-lines-malformed-falls-back-to-has.text: During `check_stale`, malformed `metadata["pinned_lines"]` silently falls through to whole-file hash checking, while `pin_lines` itself validates line ranges on write.

pinned-lines-requires-pinned-sha.text: The line-range staleness fast path in `check_stale` only activates when `pinned_sha` exists in node metadata; `pin_lines` auto-creates `pinned_sha` (and `verified_at`) if missing, establishing a strict dependency where `pinned_lines` implies `pinned_sha`.

pinned-lines-sha-bump-refreshes-source-h.text: When the pinned-lines fast path confirms the pinned range unchanged but HEAD has advanced, it bumps `pinned_sha` and recomputes `source_hash` once.

pinned-lines-shortcircuit-hashing.text: When `file_lines_changed_since` finds no overlapping hunk, `check_stale` `continue`s without calling `hash_file` (check_stale.py:115-122).

pinned-sha-coarse-check-requires-clean-h.text: With only `pinned_sha`, the fast path skips `hash_file` only when both `git log <sha>..HEAD -- <file>` and `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <file>` are clean.

pinned-sha-has-coarse-file-fallback.text: If `pinned_lines` is absent, `file_changed_since` is used instead and still avoids `hash_file` when no commit or working-tree change touches the file (check_stale.py:123).

prefix-hash-upgrade-requires-flag.text: A stored hash that is a prefix of the actual SHA-256 digest is only upgraded when `upgrade_hashes=True`; otherwise it is reported as `truncated_hash`.

premise-behavior-emerges-from-absence.text: Premise behavior is not explicitly implemented — it emerges from three defaults: nodes with no justifications default to IN, empty antecedent lists are vacuously valid, and the system preserves a premise's current truth value rather than deriving it.

justifications.label: The "premise" concept requires no special case in the engine — it falls out of the general evaluation rules applied to empty structures

premise-bonus-applies-to-all-scored-node.text: Because `find_culprits` only scores nodes from `trace_assumptions` (premises), the `+100` premise bonus fires for every node scored in the primary path.

premise-can-receive-justification.text: A premise node (initially no justifications) can receive a justification via `add_justification`, giving it a derived backup path that keeps it IN even if its premise status is retracted.

premise-count-is-per-justification-max.text: `premise_count` in the return value reports the maximum antecedent count across the node's justifications, not the total across all justifications (any_mode with 3 premises returns 1, not 3).

premise-count-reflects-per-justification.text: `premise_count` in API return dicts reflects per-justification antecedent width (1 for any_mode, SL size for normal, 0 for bare premise), not the total number of premises in the SL string.

premise-count-reflects-single-justificat.text: The `premise_count` field in add results is N for a conjunctive SL with N antecedents, 1 for `any_mode` expansions regardless of original N, and 0 for premise nodes.

premise-default-in.text: Covered by existing `premise-behavior-emerges-from-absence` which captures this as an emergent property

premise-defaults-to-in.text: A node with no justifications (a premise) defaults to IN; `_compute_truth` preserves its current truth value rather than recomputing it.

premise-derived-verifiability-asymmetry.text: Premises record source file and line range at assertion time, enabling check-stale to verify them against current code; derived beliefs have no equivalent source-level grounding and can only be structurally validated (references exist and are IN).

premise-identity-is-bidirectionally-tran.text: Premise identity can be both destroyed (via dialectical challenge adding justifications) and created (via convert-to-premise removing them), with both directions preserving the dependents invariant — making premise/derived status a fully reversible structural property of the network.

justifications.label: Both transformations maintain the dependents index and propagate truth correctly, so the structural boundary between premise and derived node is crossable in either direction without corrupting network state.

premise-identity-is-inherently-transient.text: Premise identity is inherently transient because it emerges from the absence of justifications, and any justification addition — whether from dialectical challenge, defend, or direct add_justification — irreversibly transforms a premise into a derived node without explicit opt-in.

justifications.label: Emergent identity (from absence) combined with unrestricted justification attachment means premise status has no structural protection against transformation

premise-identity-transformation-is-archi.text: Premise identity transformation exhibits a fundamental architectural asymmetry rooted in the same emergent property: premise identity is inherently transient because it arises from the absence of justifications, and dialectical challenge exploits this transience to permanently transform premises into justified nodes — while the truth-value defeat itself remains fully reversible through outlist semantics, creating an irreversible identity change layered atop reversible truth dynamics

justifications.label: Both beliefs trace back to premise-behavior-emerges-from-absence but capture different consequences — transient identity explains WHY challenge can destroy premise status, while the defeat/identity asymmetry shows that this destruction is permanent even as truth values freely oscillate

premise-review-batch-failures-non-fatal.text: A subprocess exception in one batch of `review_premises` does not abort the remaining batches; the function returns whatever results were successfully collected (possibly `[]`) rather than propagating the error.

premise-review-filters-to-source-backed-.text: The premise review pipeline filters to nodes that have no `sl` field (true premises) AND have a `source` field; derived nodes (with `sl`) are never entered into the review loop regardless of other attributes.

premise-review-format-missing-node-retur.text: `format_premise_for_review` returns `""` for a missing premise ID rather than raising an exception.

premise-review-format-source-line-is-con.text: `format_premise_for_review` emits a `Source reference:` line only when the node has a `source`, while still including the premise text and provided source content.

premise-review-metadata-has-two-keys.text: Non-dry runs persist both `premise_review_result` (error_type or `"pass"`) and `last_premise_reviewed` on each reviewed node.

premise-review-on-batch-callback-is-per-.text: `review_premises` calls `on_batch` once per completed batch with that batch’s results.

premise-review-parser-defaults-to-passin.text: `parse_premise_review_response` defaults missing LLM fields to safe passing values: `accurate=True`, `well_scoped=True`, `error_type=None`, `comment=""` — a vague or partial LLM response cannot trigger a false-positive repair action.

premise-review-persists-error-type-or-pa.text: A non-dry-run premise review writes `metadata.premise_review_result` as either the result’s `error_type` or `"pass"`, and sets `last_premise_reviewed`.

premise-review-skips-sourceless-nodes.text: Premise nodes without a `source` field are excluded from LLM review entirely, counted in the `skipped_no_source` summary field, and never sent to the model — the LLM requires source text to verify against.

premise-review-total-premises-counts-bef.text: `api.review_premises` reports `total_premises` as the premise count before `sample` or `belief_ids` narrowing is applied.

premises-accept-added-justifications.text: Premise nodes are not immutable: `Network.add_justification` can add an SL justification to an existing premise node.

premises-cannot-be-defeated.text: Calling `defeat_justification` on a node with no justifications raises `ValueError("... no justifications ...")`.

premises-default-in-and-skip-compute.text: `add_node` sets `truth_value = "IN"` for zero-justification nodes, and `_compute_truth` returns the current value for premises rather than recomputing.

premises-defined-by-empty-justifications.text: A node is counted as a premise when its `justifications` list is empty; any node with at least one justification is counted as derived.

premises-have-depth-zero.text: `_node_depth` returns `0` for missing nodes, nodes without justifications, and premise nodes.

premises-have-no-justifications.text: A premise node is represented by an empty `justifications` list and defaults to `truth_value="IN"`; the system treats the empty-justifications case as a special unconditional belief.

premises-un-defeatable-at-justification-.text: A node with no justifications (a premise/axiom) cannot be targeted by `defeat_justification`; the API raises `ValueError` because justification-level defeat requires at least one justification to exist.

private-wiki-build-uses-eem-wiki-build-a.text: The private wiki build pipeline uses eem-wiki build-all to produce the dist/ directory.

private-wiki-deployment-uses-iap-in-fron.text: A private wiki deployment option uses Google Cloud IAP in front of a Cloud Run service to handle Google OAuth.

process-batch-returns-list-not-tuple.text: Despite its docstring saying `(batch_results, error_or_None)`, `_process_batch` returns a single `list[dict]` from `parse_premise_review_response`.

production-packages-do-not-import-tests.text: Neither the `reasons/` nor `reasons_lib/` package imports the `tests` package.

project-has-zero-external-coupling.text: The project enforces zero external coupling at both the packaging level (empty `dependencies` list in pyproject.toml) and the implementation level (core Network class uses only stdlib imports), eliminating supply-chain risk and simplifying deployment.

justifications.label: Zero-dependency property holds at both packaging and source-code levels

project-id-is-deprecated-alias-for-domai.text: The `--project-id` CLI flag is a deprecated alias silently accepted by `_backend_kwargs`, which checks `domain_id` first and falls back to `project_id`; new code should use `--domain-id`.

project-name-defaults-to-db-filename-ste.text: When `project_name` is not explicitly provided to `init_db`, it defaults to the database filename minus its extension (e.g., `my-beliefs.db` → `"my-beliefs"`).

project-version-is-0-22-0.text: The project version recorded in the session summary is 0.22.0.

prompt-builders-gate-tool-definitions-an.text: Prompt builders gate tool definitions: only `build_ask_prompt` includes `search_beliefs`; simple mode defaults to citation instructions and switches to plain natural language when `natural=True`.

prompt-template-validation-raises-valuee.text: `build_prompt` raises `ValueError` with message "unknown placeholder" for unrecognized `{placeholder}` tokens in custom templates, and `ValueError` with message "malformed braces" for unclosed braces — these are programmer errors, not runtime data errors.

propagate-assumes-changed-id-exists.text: `_propagate` accesses `self.nodes[changed_id]` without a membership check, so a missing changed ID raises `KeyError`.

propagate-assumes-dependents-exist.text: Every ID in `node.dependents` is accessed via `self.nodes[dep_id]` without a membership check; a dangling dependent reference will raise `KeyError` — this is intentional (broken invariant = bug)

metadata.retract_reason: Fixed in PR #27

propagate-bfs-order-guarantee.text: The BFS ordering of changed nodes is an implementation detail that no caller currently depends on for correctness — tracking it as a belief adds noise without preventing breakage

propagate-cascade-stops-on-unchanged.text: If a dependent's recomputed truth value equals its current value, it is not enqueued — the cascade terminates along that path, making propagation selective rather than exhaustive

propagate-does-not-change-trigger.text: The seed node (`changed_id`) is added to `visited` immediately and never has its own truth value recomputed; callers must update it before calling `_propagate`

propagate-excludes-seed-node.text: The seed `changed_id` is never included in `_propagate`'s returned list; callers must prepend it themselves.

propagate-guards-cycles-with-visited-set.text: The `visited` set (seeded with `changed_id`) is the only safeguard against cycles in the justification graph; termination relies on its monotonic growth.

propagate-has-nondeterministic-order.text: Because `dependents` is a set, both the BFS traversal order and the returned `changed` list order are non-deterministic across runs/processes.

propagate-logs-each-changed-node.text: `_propagate` appends a `propagate` log entry via `_log` for each node whose truth value changes.

propagate-requires-reverse-index.text: Correct propagation depends on `node.dependents` being up-to-date with justifications; `_rebuild_dependents`/`verify_dependents` exist because this can drift.

propagate-returns-changed-excluding-trig.text: `_propagate` never includes the seed `changed_id` in its returned changed list; callers prepend it separately.

propagate-returns-empty-when-no-dependen.text: If the seed node has no dependents, `_propagate` returns an empty list.

propagate-skips-retracted-nodes.text: `_propagate` never recomputes truth values for nodes with `_retracted` in metadata, even if their justifications would support IN; only `assert_node` can restore them

propagate-traverses-dependents-forward.text: `_propagate` walks forward along `dependents` edges from the changed node and does not traverse antecedents.

propagate-uses-visited-set.text: `_propagate` uses a `visited` set seeded with `changed_id` to prevent cycles and redundant recomputation.

propagation-automatically-cascades-on-al.text: Truth propagation automatically cascades to all dependent nodes whenever any node's truth value changes, including nodes that appear only in outlists — making GATE belief re-evaluation fully automatic with no manual intervention required after outlist node retraction.

justifications.label: Safe terminating propagation combined with fully-specified outlist semantics should ensure automatic cascade on all truth changes, but outlist exclusion from the dependents index prevents automatic GATE re-evaluation

propagation-continues-past-dangling-refe.text: Valid dependents still update truth values and are included in `changed` even when ghost dependents are present.

propagation-guards-dangling-dependent-re.text: `_propagate` was fixed to skip dangling dependent references with `if dep_id not in self.nodes: continue`, preventing a `KeyError`.

propagation-is-bfs.text: Truth value propagation in `_propagate` uses `deque`-based BFS through the `dependents` graph, not DFS, ensuring breadth-first wavefront expansion.

propagation-is-crash-free.text: Truth propagation completes without runtime errors across all reachable nodes

justifications.label: Propagation is safe when all dependent IDs resolve and termination is guaranteed; a dangling dependent reference causes an uncaught KeyError that crashes the BFS walk

propagation-is-safe-and-terminating.text: Truth propagation is both lifecycle-safe and guaranteed to terminate: retracted nodes are skipped, trigger nodes are never recomputed, BFS prevents stack overflow, and stop-on-unchanged prevents oscillation — propagation respects every node state it encounters.

justifications.label: Termination guarantees and lifecycle-awareness are independent properties that together ensure safe traversal

propagation-is-safe-under-graph-inconsis.text: Truth propagation achieves correctness even when the dependency graph contains dangling references: missing nodes are skipped with structured warnings rather than crashing, dangling IDs are excluded from both the changed and visited sets, and this graceful degradation composes with the underlying termination and lifecycle-awareness guarantees for all reachable nodes.

justifications.label: Dangling-reference containment composes with propagation safety to handle graph inconsistency gracefully

propagation-is-topology-complete-and-inc.text: Truth propagation is both topologically complete — reaching all transitively dependent nodes including those connected through outlist entries, not just antecedent references — and safe under graph inconsistency, skipping dangling dependent references with structured warnings rather than crashing, ensuring correct cascading even in networks with imperfect structural integrity such as nodes deleted without full reference cleanup.

justifications.label: Completeness and inconsistency-safety are independent properties that together make propagation production-ready for real-world networks

propagation-log-records-add-retract-prop.text: The propagation audit trail records `add`, `retract`, and `propagate` events with their targets.

propagation-respects-node-lifecycle.text: Truth propagation respects node lifecycle states: retracted nodes are skipped during BFS traversal, and the trigger node itself is never recomputed — callers must set its truth value before invoking propagation.

justifications.label: Propagation treats retracted and trigger nodes as boundaries, not participants, preventing unintended reactivation and circular recomputation

propagation-terminates-deterministically.text: Truth propagation is guaranteed to terminate: BFS prevents stack overflow, stop-on-unchanged prevents oscillation, and fixpoint iteration bounds the outer loop

justifications.label: Three complementary mechanisms each address a different termination failure mode

proposal-accept-drift-detection-marks-st.text: Accepting a proposal whose target state changed between propose and accept (node already OUT, node deleted, ID collision) results in `applied=False` and `status="stale"` rather than an exception.

proposal-acceptance-is-single-commit-poi.text: `propose_*` tools create pending proposals and do not mutate target nodes; `accept_proposal` is the single mutating commit point that applies the proposed change.

proposal-ids-follow-target-action-prefix.text: Proposal IDs for retract/supersede/add proposals begin with `prop-<target>-<action>-`.

proposal-lifecycle-fixture-preloads-thre.text: `TestProposalLifecycle.db_path` initializes a DB with `a`, `b`, and `derived-ab` before each test in that class.

proposal-lifecycle-is-idempotent-state-m.text: Once a proposal reaches a terminal state (`accepted`, `rejected`, or `withdrawn`), any further `accept_proposal`, `reject_proposal`, or `withdraw_proposal` call returns an error rather than re-applying or mutating.

proposal-markdown-emits-suggested-cli-co.text: `format_proposal_markdown()` emits suggested `reasons update` / `reasons retract` commands but does not execute them.

proposal-markdown-escapes-only-double-qu.text: `format_proposal_markdown` escapes only double quotes in `proposed_text` when building copy-paste commands; backticks, dollar signs, backslashes, and single quotes pass through unchanged.

proposal-parse-failures-return-empty-lis.text: `parse_update_proposals()` returns `[]` for malformed LLM output, indistinguishable from an empty proposal set.

proposal-parser-does-not-validate-node-i.text: `parse_update_proposals()` accepts any item with an `id` key and does not check membership in the graph.

proposal-safety-covers-race-and-duplicat.text: The proposal lifecycle is protected against two distinct failure classes: drift detection catches state changes between propose and accept (preventing stale accepts of already-mutated nodes), and the idempotent state machine prevents double-application (terminal states are immutable). Together they close the race-condition and replay holes.

justifications.label: Two-layer safety argument — drift detection addresses the temporal race (state changed between read and write) while idempotency addresses the replay risk (same proposal applied twice). Each alone leaves the other vulnerability open; both together provide complete proposal safety.

proposal-statuses-enumerated.text: Valid terminal proposal statuses are `accepted`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`, and `stale`; any further resolution of an already-resolved proposal returns `{"error": ...}`.

proposal-taxonomies-are-closed-enums.text: Already covered by the existing `update-proposals-validate-enums-with-safe-defaults` belief.

proposals-defer-mutation-until-acceptanc.text: `propose_retract`, `propose_supersede`, and `propose_add` create `pending` records but leave the belief DB unchanged until `accept_proposal` is invoked.

proposals-schema-not-owned-by-storage.text: `PROPOSALS_SCHEMA` DDL is defined as a module-level constant in `reasons/storage.py` but is NOT created by `Storage._init_schema()`; it is applied elsewhere (e.g., `propose_update.py` or the API layer), so the `proposals` table may not exist in a database opened via `Storage` alone.

proposals-schema-unused-here.text: `PROPOSALS_SCHEMA` is declared in this file but never executed by `Storage._init_schema`.

propose-batch-errors-are-swallowed.text: `propose_updates()` catches per-batch exceptions, logs a warning, and returns partial results rather than raising.

propose-beliefs-consumes-entries-and-pro.text: The `propose-beliefs` step reports its input as `entries` and its output as `proposed` beliefs.

propose-stage-requires-external-accept.text: `format_proposal_markdown()` emits suggested `reasons update`/`reasons retract` commands but does not execute them.

propose-update-batch-failure-preserves-p.text: An exception in `invoke_model` for one batch is caught per-batch, logged to `stderr`, and remaining batches still execute; the function returns all successfully-parsed results from non-failed batches

propose-update-belief-ids-is-nullable-ar.text: The `belief_ids: list[str] | None = None` parameter on `propose_update` (`reasons/mcp_server.py:203`) serializes to a nullable array whose schema is not in `required`.

propose-update-defaults-to-in-beliefs-on.text: `propose_updates` defaults `belief_ids` to all nodes with `truth_value == "IN"`; OUT beliefs are excluded from LLM auditing as already-retracted beliefs

propose-update-failure-modes-and-bases-a.text: `parse_update_proposals` coerces `failure_mode` to one of six `FAILURE_MODES` values or `""`, and `basis` to one of three `BASES` values or `"prior-knowledge"`.

propose-update-module-is-read-only-propo.text: `reasons/propose_update.py` only produces proposal dicts and markdown; it does not apply accepted changes to storage.

propose-update-normalizes-empty-list-to-.text: `propose_update` passes `belief_ids=belief_ids or None`, collapsing both an omitted/`null` value and an empty list into `None` before calling `api.propose_update`.

propose-update-parser-coerces-closed-tax.text: `parse_update_proposals` never raises on unknown `failure_mode`, `basis`, or `action` values; it silently substitutes `""`, `"prior-knowledge"`, and `"update"` respectively, ensuring structured output always conforms to the closed vocabularies

propose-update-produces-review-artifact-.text: The module's output contract is a markdown document containing ready-to-paste CLI commands (`reasons update`/`reasons retract`); it never applies changes to the network itself

propose-update-prompt-annotates-basis-wi.text: `PROPOSE_UPDATE_PROMPT` annotates `source-divergence` as cheap to accept and `prior-knowledge` as needing scrutiny, making `basis` the intended review-tier axis.

propose-update-prompt-does-not-annotate-.text: The proposal prompt gives `detected-contradiction` no explicit cheap-to-accept or needs-scrutiny annotation.

propose-update-public-surface-maps-to-up.text: The shim's public API is exactly the public surface of `reasons.propose_update` (its `__all__` if defined, otherwise all non-underscore names).

propose-update-shim-requires-canonical-m.text: Importing the shim requires `reasons.propose_update` to be importable, and any failure there propagates with no interception.

propose-update-store-flag-controls-persi.text: `propose_update` with `store=True` persists proposals and includes `stored_count`, while `store=False` returns `proposals`/`llm_proposals` without persisting and without `stored_count`.

propose-update-tests-patch-invoke-model.text: Model-calling tests replace `reasons.propose_update.invoke_model` with a mock to avoid real LLM invocation.

propose-updates-batch-size-not-validated.text: `batch_size` is not validated: `0` raises `ValueError` from `range`, while a negative value silently produces no batches and returns `[]`.

propose-updates-batches-and-calls-on-bat.text: `propose_updates` chunks selected belief ids according to `batch_size`, calls the model once per batch, and invokes `on_batch` with per-batch results.

propose-updates-batches-belief-ids.text: `propose_updates` calls `invoke_model` once per batch; three belief IDs with `batch_size=2` produce two calls.

propose-updates-batches-beliefs.text: `propose_updates` splits the resolved belief ID list into chunks of `batch_size` and issues exactly one `invoke_model` call per chunk.

propose-updates-catches-on-batch-callbac.text: Exceptions raised by the `on_batch` callback are caught by the per-batch `try/except` and reported as batch failures rather than propagated.

propose-updates-default-candidacy-is-in-.text: `propose_updates` selects only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` when `belief_ids` is `None`, and filters explicit `belief_ids` to IDs present in `nodes`.

propose-updates-defaults-to-in-beliefs.text: When `belief_ids` is `None`, `propose_updates` selects only nodes with `truth_value == "IN"`, iterating them in sorted order for determinism.

propose-updates-defaults-to-in-nodes.text: When `belief_ids` is `None`, `propose_updates` selects all nodes with `truth_value == "IN"` for the LLM prompt; empty or all-nonexistent ID lists short-circuit to `[]` without invoking the model.

propose-updates-does-not-emit-cascade.text: `propose_updates` returns only the LLM fields whitelisted by `parse_update_proposals`; it never calls a what-if simulator and never emits a cascade key.

propose-updates-emits-markdown-not-decis.text: `propose_updates` + `format_proposals_file` produce a markdown document of proposals with suggested commands; they do not return or apply an auto-accepted subset.

propose-updates-empty-input-skips-llm.text: `propose_updates` returns `[]` without calling the LLM or printing progress when the selected belief list is empty.

propose-updates-empty-result-is-ambiguou.text: An empty return from `propose_updates` cannot distinguish “no proposals,” “no beliefs after filtering,” and “every batch failed.”

propose-updates-explicit-belief-ids-filt.text: When `belief_ids` is explicitly provided, `propose_updates` filters it to IDs present in `nodes` but does not filter by `truth_value`.

propose-updates-filters-unknown-belief-i.text: Explicitly supplied `belief_ids` not present in `nodes` are silently dropped, and no `truth_value` filtering is applied to the survivors.

propose-updates-filters-unknown-ids.text: When an explicit `belief_ids` list is passed, IDs not present in `nodes` are dropped before any LLM call.

propose-updates-is-read-only.text: `propose_updates()` returns proposal dicts and never mutates the belief graph.

propose-updates-on-batch-receives-cumula.text: The `propose_updates` `on_batch` callback receives the cumulative results list, not the current batch slice.
`on_batch` is invoked once per successful batch with the running `all_results` list, even when that batch returned zero proposals.

propose-updates-short-circuits-empty-or-.text: `propose_updates` returns `[]` without calling the model when `belief_ids` is empty or contains only nonexistent ids.

propose-updates-swallows-batch-errors.text: Any exception inside the per-batch `try` block (including exceptions raised by the `on_batch` callback) is logged to stderr as `WARN: batch N failed` and never propagated.

provider-dispatch-is-string-prefix-not-p.text: Provider selection in `invoke_model` is a flat `startswith` cascade (`api:`, `vertex:`, `openai:`, then CLI) with no class hierarchy, plugin registry, or factory pattern — adding a provider requires one new `if` branch and one `_invoke_*` function.

publish-hf-produces-three-files.text: `publish_hf` uploads exactly `{"network.json", "beliefs.md", "README.md"}` and issues 4 `urlopen` calls (1 create + 3 uploads).

publish-hf-requires-token.text: `publish_hf` raises `RuntimeError("token required")` when neither `HF_TOKEN` nor `~/.huggingface/token` supplies a token.

publish-isolates-subscriber-errors.text: `publish` catches/logs exceptions from one subscriber and continues dispatching to later subscribers.

publish-isolates-subscriber-exceptions.text: A subscriber exception is caught and logged by `publish()`, and other subscribers still receive the event batch.

publish-noops-on-empty-event-list.text: `publish()` returns immediately when `events` is empty and does not notify subscribers.

publish-routes-to-global-and-db-scoped-s.text: `publish` dispatches each event batch to global subscribers plus subscribers registered for the event’s `db_path`.

publish-routes-to-global-and-db-specific.text: `publish` sends each event batch to global subscribers plus subscribers registered for the event’s `db_path`.

pubsub-and-mind-service-are-optional-not.text: `pubsub.py` and `mind_service.py` provide optional external notification hooks outside the core inference path; they are not required for TMS correctness and do not participate in propagation or evaluation.

pubsub-callbacks-receive-whole-event-lis.text: `publish(events, db_path)` passes the entire event list as one argument to each subscriber callback, not one event at a time.

pubsub-clear-resets-all-subscribers.text: `clear()` removes both global and db-scoped subscribers, and `has_subscribers()` returns `False` afterward.

pubsub-empty-publish-is-no-op.text: `publish([], db_path)` must not invoke any subscribers.

pubsub-events-computed-by-snapshot-diff.text: `compute_changes(before, after, db_path)` derives pub/sub events by diffing truth-value snapshots rather than observing intermediate propagation.

pubsub-events-fire-post-persistence.text: Pubsub events are delivered to subscribers only after the database write has committed, so any side-effect in a subscriber callback (e.g., reading the DB) observes the already-persisted new state.

pubsub-events-lack-cause-and-cascade-roo.text: The `ChangeEvent` dataclass omits `cause` and `cascade_root` because events are computed from pre/post snapshots.

pubsub-exposes-only-post-save-state.text: Subscribers observe only the final stable post-save snapshot; intermediate cascade states during fixpoint computation are structurally invisible because `publish()` is called only after the full transaction commits

pubsub-failed-mutation-emits-no-events.text: If an API mutation raises an exception (e.g., `KeyError` on a nonexistent node), the snapshot-diff-publish pipeline is never reached and zero events are delivered to subscribers.

pubsub-insertion-indistinguishable-from-.text: A new node (present in `after`, absent from `before`) produces a `ChangeEvent` with `old_truth_value=None` and `type="node_changed"`, making it indistinguishable from a value change by the `type` field alone

pubsub-is-synchronous-in-process.text: `publish()` blocks until all subscribers return; there is no queue, thread, or IPC mechanism — safe in single-threaded use but unsafe under concurrent calls without external synchronization

pubsub-publish-noop-on-empty-list.text: If the `events` list passed to `publish` is empty, no subscriber callback is invoked at all — the dispatch loop short-circuits before iterating subscribers.

pubsub-publishes-only-final-stable-state.text: `reasons/pubsub.py` documents that subscribers receive events only after `_with_network` commits, never for intermediate cascade states.

pubsub-scoped-subscriber-receives-matchi.text: Subscriber scoping is inclusive (OR semantics): a subscriber registered without a `db_path` (global) AND a subscriber registered with a specific `db_path` both fire when an event for that database is published.

pubsub-subscribe-allows-duplicates.text: Calling `subscribe(callback, db_path)` twice with the same callback registers it twice; `publish` will invoke it twice per event batch — there is no deduplication check

pubsub-subscriber-exception-isolation.text: A subscriber callback that raises an exception is caught and logged without preventing delivery of the same event to subsequent subscribers in the registry.

pubsub-subscriber-exceptions-are-isolate.text: A raising subscriber does not prevent other subscribers from receiving the same event batch, nor does it propagate to the caller of `publish()`; each subscriber is wrapped in an independent `try/except`

pure-evaluation-enables-richly-governed-.text: Evaluation purity — grounding dialectics through the minimal architecture — simultaneously enables richly-governed exception-safe revision, so dialectical structures are both minimality-grounded in their computation and richly-governed in the state they produce: challenge/defend operations inherit pure deterministic evaluation while producing metadata-enriched recoverable state changes.

justifications.label: Pure evaluation is the shared computational foundation enabling both minimal dialectics and rich governance; combining reveals dialectics benefit from both

pure-evaluation-enables-richly-governed-.text: Evaluation purity — uniform, deterministic, side-effect-free justification validity checking — grounds dialectical reliability through a minimal architecture, and the system's revision component supports richly-governed, metadata-enabled state management (retraction reasons, staleness markers, access tags) while maintaining exception-safety and recoverability under failure conditions.

push-belief-404-propagates-as-httperror.text: `push_belief` special-cases only HTTP 401; HTTP 404 from the push endpoint propagates as an `HTTPError` rather than becoming a `RuntimeError`.

push-belief-omits-empty-optional-fields.text: `push_belief` conditionally excludes `sl` and `source` from the JSON request body when they are empty strings; the remote server must treat field absence as "not provided" rather than interpreting it as an empty value.

push-belief-omits-empty-sl.text: `push_belief` omits the `sl` key from the JSON body when no justification string is provided.

push-belief-omits-empty-sl-key.text: When `sl` is `None`, `push_belief` omits the `sl` key entirely from the JSON POST body rather than sending `"sl": null`, allowing the remote API to distinguish "no antecedents" from "unspecified."

push-belief-uses-bearer-auth-and-post.text: `push_belief` sends an HTTP POST to `/api/agents/{agent_id}/beliefs` with an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header.

pyproject-declares-both-packages-for-whe.text: The only non-docstring reference to `reasons_lib` is `packages = ["reasons", "reasons_lib"]` in `pyproject.toml`, ensuring both import paths ship in the wheel.

quality-lifecycle-is-complete-and-resour.text: The complete LLM-driven quality lifecycle — creation via derive with defensive validation, classification via list-negative with batch scalability, and validation via review with read-only fault tolerance — operates within resource-efficient bounds spanning zero-dependency packaging through lazy-loading startup through bounded runtime execution, ensuring quality assurance scales sustainably with belief network size.

justifications.label: Quality lifecycle completeness and resource efficiency are independently established properties that together ensure sustainable quality management

quality-lifecycle-is-fault-tolerant-and-.text: The complete LLM-driven quality lifecycle — creation via derive, classification via list-negative, review, and self-correction — is simultaneously resource-efficient (accurate budgets, linear allocation, minimal footprint) and fault-tolerant at every phase (graceful degradation on LLM failures, batch fault isolation, deterministic fallbacks).

justifications.label: Resource efficiency and fault tolerance are independent quality axes — the lifecycle achieves both simultaneously across all phases

quality-lifecycle-operates-within-self-m.text: The complete belief quality lifecycle — fault-tolerant creation, classification, review, and correction with resource-efficient operation — executes within trust boundaries that are both structurally enforced (zero external dependencies, defensive ingestion) and dynamically maintained (convergent self-correction preserving trust invariants), requiring no external trust infrastructure.

justifications.label: Quality lifecycle operates within self-maintaining trust perimeters — trust enforcement is not external to quality but embedded within it

query-degradation-is-deterministic-acros.text: All information access paths degrade gracefully while maintaining deterministic output: interactive queries cascade through tiered modes (LLM synthesis → bounded tool loop → raw FTS5 search), structured reads self-heal missing indexes via derived FTS5 reconstruction, and all fallback paths produce deterministic sorted output.

justifications.label: Tiered query degradation and deterministic read resilience are independently established — together they show every information access path is both fault-tolerant and predictable.

query-resilience-serves-self-correcting-.text: All query access paths — interactive LLM synthesis, batch search, and compact summarization — degrade gracefully with deterministic output while operating against a knowledge base that actively self-corrects through contradiction resolution and staleness detection, ensuring degraded queries still return data from a consistency-maintained belief network

justifications.label: Deterministic query degradation (depth-4) ensures reliable access while self-correction (depth-4) ensures the accessed data is actively maintained — users get reliable reads against a self-healing store

read-and-write-paths-are-both-reliable.text: Both the read path (staleness checking detects all forms of source drift without false negatives) and the write path (truth propagation completes without runtime errors across all reachable nodes) are operationally reliable, ensuring the system functions correctly in both observational and mutational modes.

justifications.label: Independent operational reliability of the read-only inspection path and the write-path propagation engine combine to cover both system operation modes

read-source-never-raises-returns-none.text: `read_source` catches `OSError` and `UnicodeDecodeError`, returning `None` instead of raising when the source cannot be resolved or read.

read-source-requires-resolve-source-path.text: `read_source` depends on `check_stale.resolve_source_path` for path resolution and has no independent path-resolution logic.

readme-import-export-markdown-roundtrip.text: README specifies that `export-markdown` emits `beliefs.md`-compatible markdown and `import-beliefs` consumes exactly that shape, forming a documented round-trip contract.

reasoning-and-knowledge-expansion-are-bo.text: The system achieves exhaustive coverage in both formal reasoning (deterministic reversible truth evaluation with guaranteed-terminating exploration of all derivable conclusions) and LLM-driven knowledge expansion (complete coverage with fault tolerance across all interactive and batch LLM operations)

justifications.label: Formal TMS reasoning and LLM-driven derivation independently achieve exhaustive coverage through complementary mechanisms

reasoning-and-revision-form-complete-arc.text: The system provides a complete reasoning-and-revision architecture: the deterministic reversible engine reliably computes truth states in the forward direction, while the comprehensive minimal revision system handles all forms of belief change (outlist defeat, contradiction resolution, dialectical challenge) in the corrective direction — together covering the full lifecycle of belief management.

justifications.label: Forward inference engine plus corrective revision system yields complete belief lifecycle coverage

reasoning-engine-is-deterministic-and-re.text: The TMS engine achieves deterministic reversible non-monotonic reasoning: truth maintenance produces predictable terminating results through uniform evaluation and conservative asym­metry, while every non-monotonic operation (challenge, kill-switch, supersession, dialectics) is inherently undoable through the single outlist primitive.

justifications.label: Determinism (from uniform evaluation + BFS termination) and reversibility (from outlist universality) are independent properties that together make the engine both predictable and undoable

reasoning-is-exhaustively-deterministic.text: The reasoning system produces deterministic, reversible truth evaluations AND can exhaustively explore all derivable conclusions with guaranteed termination, ensuring the system finds every reachable belief state with predictable outcomes.

justifications.label: Deterministic reversible TMS evaluation combined with exhaustive terminating derive exploration guarantees complete predictable inference (depth-4)
