rich-governance-inherits-minimality-comp.text: Rich lifecycle governance — deterministic and lifecycle-complete — achieves its determinism not as an independently-engineered property but as a consequence of the same minimality that generates completeness: the unified minimality-completeness-determinism triad ensures that rich governance's predictable state trajectories and gapless monitoring arise from the same minimal primitives that produce comprehensive truth maintenance coverage.

justifications.label: rich governance determinism arises from the same minimality that generates completeness

rich-governance-is-deterministic-and-lif.text: The deterministic lifecycle-complete architecture governs state richer than binary truth values — deterministic reasoning ensures predictable state trajectories and gapless lifecycle monitoring ensures no belief escapes management, while metadata-enabled governance extends these guarantees to retraction reasons, staleness tracking, and access control beyond IN/OUT.

justifications.label: Deterministic lifecycle-complete architecture + rich state governance → deterministic lifecycle-complete rich governance

rich-governance-is-deterministic-excepti.text: Rich lifecycle governance simultaneously achieves end-to-end determinism from revision semantics through source integrity and exception safety across TMS and source lifecycle — governance is both predictable in its state trajectories and resilient to all exceptional conditions.

justifications.label: Two independent depth-8 properties of rich governance (determinism-through-source and exception-safety) compose into fully characterized governance that is both predictable and fault-tolerant

rich-governance-is-exception-safe.text: The system's rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, extending beyond binary truth to metadata-enabled state with full monitoring — operates within an exception-safe framework spanning both TMS core and source lifecycle: contradictions are resolved through deterministic backtracking, challenges reach correct truth states through crash-safe propagation, and source failures degrade gracefully through fail-safe path resolution — ensuring that rich state transitions never produce corrupted or inconsistent lifecycle metadata.

justifications.label: Deterministic lifecycle-complete governance plus exception safety across both TMS and source domains eliminates unsafe rich-state transitions

rich-governance-spans-all-backends.text: The system's exception-safe rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, and spanning revision through source integrity — operates identically across all storage backends, achieving full behavioral parity between SQLite and PostgreSQL for metadata-enabled lifecycle management.

justifications.label: Rich governance properties are established on the SQLite path; PgApi's partial API coverage is the sole barrier to backend universality — this GATE flips IN when PgApi achieves full API parity

rich-governance-spans-all-backends-v2.text: The system's rich lifecycle governance — deterministic, lifecycle-complete, and spanning TMS core through source lifecycle — operates within an exception-safe framework for metadata-enabled state management, supporting predictable state trajectories, crash-safe propagation of challenges, and graceful degradation on source failures, with the architectural design intended to prevent corrupted or inconsistent lifecycle metadata from rich state transitions.

richer-revision-preserves-evaluation-inv.text: Although the revision system governs state richer than binary truth values — including metadata-enabled lifecycle governance with retraction reasons, staleness indicators, and access controls — truth evaluation remains transformation-invariant, producing identical results regardless of attachment history or structural origin; the richer governance layer operates orthogonally to evaluation, enriching management capabilities without compromising core determinism.

justifications.label: Richer-than-binary revision + transformation-invariant evaluation means governance richness and evaluation simplicity are orthogonal

rollback-prevents-aborted-transaction-er.text: `api.conn.rollback()` at the start of teardown resets failed-transaction state left by the test so the subsequent `DELETE`s succeed.

roundtrip-double-export-stability.text: Duplicate of existing belief `double-roundtrip-is-idempotent`; no new belief needed.

roundtrip-omits-empty-fields.text: Markdown export must omit any `- Field: value` line when the field is None or empty string, preventing ambiguity between "not set" and "set to empty" in the serialized format.

roundtrip-preserves-retraction-and-stale.text: A retracted node (truth_value "OUT") with a `stale_reason` must survive export→import unchanged, and the import result must report `claims_retracted == 1` so callers can detect retracted content in the imported markdown.

run-cli-builds-argv-and-captures-streams.text: The `run_cli` test helper builds a synthetic `sys.argv` starting with "reasons" (plus optional `--db`), patches stdout/stderr with `StringIO`, calls `main()`, and returns `(stdout, stderr, exit_code)`.

run-cli-catches-system-exit-only.text: Test harness implementation detail, not a production code invariant; the relevant production behavior is captured by `cli-exit-code-contract-zero-or-one`.

run-cli-catches-systemexit.text: `run_cli()` catches `SystemExit` and returns its `.code`, so tests assert numeric exit codes instead of expecting process termination.

run-cli-catches-systemexit-only.text: The `run_cli` helper catches `SystemExit` and maps `None` to exit code `0`, while any non-`SystemExit` exception propagates to pytest.

run-cli-converts-system-exit-to-code.text: The `run_cli` helper catches `SystemExit` and returns its code, defaulting `None` to `0`.

run-cli-harness-catches-systemexit.text: The `run_cli` test helper catches `SystemExit` raised by the CLI `main()` function and extracts its exit code.

run-cli-harness-invokes-cli-in-process.text: The run_cli test harness invokes reasons_lib.cli:main in-process by patching sys.argv, sys.stdout, and sys.stderr, returning stdout, stderr, and exit code.

run-cli-helper-catches-systemexit.text: The `run_cli` test harness intercepts `SystemExit` to extract exit codes, preventing argparse errors or explicit `sys.exit()` calls from terminating the test process.

safe-universal-revisability.text: Any mutation source — human dialectical challenge, LLM-derived proposal, or multi-agent import — can safely revise any belief in the network through complete minimal mechanisms; the system imposes no restrictions on who can revise what, while guaranteeing that every revision path preserves consistency.

justifications.label: one establishes that all sources are safe and uniform, the other that revision is complete from minimality; combining yields unrestricted-yet-safe revisability

safety-and-uniformity-are-co-derived.text: Dialectical safety (deterministic evaluation of irreversible premise transformations) and edge-case uniformity (consistent handling of vacuous premises, asymmetric absence, and empty antecedents) are independently derived from the same shared root — semantic minimality with operational determinism — revealing them as two faces of a single architectural property rather than independent design achievements.

justifications.label: Both conclusions share semantic-minimality-with-operational-determinism as their root, exposing dialectical safety and edge-case uniformity as co-derived rather than independently designed

safety-integrity-and-uniformity-converge.text: Three independently-established properties — boundary-agnostic integrity (internal/external indifference), dialectical safety (deterministic evaluation of irreversible transformations), and edge-case uniformity (consistent handling of vacuous and asymmetric cases) — converge to a single architectural invariant because all three derive from the same minimal evaluation rules applied uniformly.

justifications.label: one establishes integrity agnosticism across boundaries and sources, the other co-derives safety with uniformity from minimality; combining shows three-way convergence

safety-is-enforced-across-all-layers-and.text: Safety is enforced uniformly across both the architectural dimension (clean layer boundaries with atomic isolated mutations) and the storage dimension (equivalent guarantees through backend-appropriate mechanisms in SQLite and PostgreSQL) — no safety property depends on a specific backend or architectural layer.

justifications.label: Connects backend-agnostic storage safety with layer-enforced architectural safety into a cross-cutting safety invariant; storage-layer-is-backend-agnostic-and-safe is currently unused

sample-beliefs-deterministic-budget-boun.text: _sample_beliefs returns all beliefs when under budget, caps at the budget when over, and is reproducible with a seeded RNG.

sample-mode-is-deterministic.text: `_build_beliefs_section` with `sample=True` and a fixed `seed` produces identical output across calls, enabling reproducible derive prompts

sample-mode-is-deterministic-with-same-s.text: `test_sample_mode_deterministic` asserts identical output for the same input and `seed=99`.

save-preserves-external-tags-and-sources.text: `save()` snapshots `node_tags`/`node_sources` before clearing and restores them for nodes still present.

save-replaces-whole-network.text: `save()` deletes every row in every core table and re-inserts from the in-memory `Network` inside a single transaction.

scan-repo-core-tms-module-list-is-specul.text: The entry presents the core module list as likely rather than as an established invariant, so it is not a reliable codebase claim.

scan-repo-reasons-lib-is-legacy-mirror.text: This duplicates existing beliefs that `reasons_lib/` is a near-duplicate legacy/compat mirror.

scan-repo-sqlite-default-postgres-option.text: This duplicates existing beliefs about interchangeable SQLite/Postgres backends.

scan-repo-two-entry-points.text: This duplicates the existing belief about the two console entry points.

schema-version-constant-is-1-0.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION` is defined as `"1.0"` in `reasons/metadata.py`, and `build_meta()` always emits that value.

schema-version-is-constant.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION` is defined as `"1.0"` in `reasons/metadata.py` and `build_meta()` always emits that value.

schema-version-is-hardcoded.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION` is a module constant `"1.0"` and is not derived from the installed package version.

schema-version-is-pinned-to-1-0.text: `SCHEMA_VERSION == "1.0"` and both JSON and Markdown exports assert this literal, so changing it requires updating this suite.

scope-belief-ids-are-unique-across-defea.text: Scope-belief IDs are uniquely generated per defeat; multiple defeats on the same node with different justification indices produce disjoint sets of `scope_belief_ids`.

scope-belief-ids-are-unique-per-defeat-c.text: Two defeats on the same target create disjoint scope-belief ID sets; scope beliefs are anchored to a specific defeater rather than deduplicated globally.

scope-belief-metadata-links-antecedent-a.text: Scope-belief metadata records `scope_of` as the antecedent and `for_defeater` as the generated defeater ID.

scope-beliefs-are-atomic-in-premises.text: Scope beliefs created by `defeat_with_scope` are always `IN` with zero justifications (atomic leaf premises), and carry `metadata.scope_of` (which antecedent they scope) and `metadata.for_defeater` (which defeater consumes them).

scope-beliefs-are-premises.text: Scope beliefs created by `defeat_with_scope` have `truth_value == "IN"`, an empty `justifications` list, and metadata keys `scope_of` and `for_defeater`, per `test_scope_beliefs_are_premises`

scope-beliefs-carry-scope-of-and-for-def.text: Each scope belief stores `scope_of` pointing to the original antecedent and `for_defeater` pointing to the defeater that consumes it.

scope-defeater-justification-links-to-sc.text: The defeater node produced by `defeat_with_scope` has exactly one SL justification whose antecedents are the scope-belief IDs, making the defeater structurally derived from the scope beliefs rather than independently inserted.

scope-finding-creates-in-premise-scope-b.text: `defeat_with_scope` creates one scope-belief node per scope finding, and each scope belief is an `IN` premise with an empty `justifications` list.

scope-over-generalization-is-primary-der.text: The most common invalid derivation pattern is scope over-generalization — claiming "all X" or "every X" when antecedents establish only specific instances — followed by conjunction distribution fallacy, strength escalation, causal overclaim, and missing bridge assumptions.

scoped-subscribers-require-matching-db-p.text: A subscriber registered with `db_path` only receives publishes made with that exact `db_path`; global subscribers receive all.

search-and-link-preserves-outlist.text: `_do_search_and_link` passes the original `outlist` through as the `unless` argument to `api.add_justification` so the blocking set is unchanged.

search-and-link-restricts-candidates-to-.text: Search-and-link candidate selection excludes the belief itself, existing antecedents, non-`IN` nodes, and nodes with justifications.

search-default-excludes-out.text: `api.search` omits retracted nodes from its results when `include_out` is not specified.

search-depth-expansion-adds-antecedents.text: `api.search()` depth expansion returns only direct hits at depth 0, adds direct antecedents at depth 1, and adds transitive antecedents at depth 2.

search-empty-query-falls-back-to-match-a.text: An empty non-OR query causes `_fts_search` to return `[]`, then `_substring_search("")` matches every node because `"" in text` is always true.

search-expands-neighbors-via-justificati.text: `search` performs neighbor expansion by BFS along justification edges after the FTS5 query.

search-falls-back-to-substring.text: `api.search()` tries FTS5 full-text search first, then falls back to substring matching if FTS5 tables don't exist or error; it always produces results if substring matches exist.

search-has-four-output-formats.text: The `search` function supports four output formats: markdown, json, minimal, and compact — selected by the caller to match the consumption context (human, API, LLM prompt, compact view).

search-is-resilient-across-index-states.text: Search operates correctly regardless of FTS5 index availability: the index is derived (rebuilt from scratch on every save) so stale indexes are self-healing, and search falls back to substring matching when FTS tables don't exist or error

justifications.label: A derived (rebuildable) index plus a substring fallback provides index-state-independent search

search-lookup-compact-hide-out-by-defaul.text: All three model-facing retrieval functions (`api.search`, `api.lookup`, `api.compact`) exclude OUT-status beliefs from their output by default; callers must explicitly pass `include_out=True` to include retracted beliefs.

search-names-only-skips-neighbor-expansi.text: The `names-only` format in `search` returns IDs only and skips neighbor expansion entirely.

search-namespace-and-tag-filter-matches-.text: `search` applies `namespace` and `tag` filters only to matched nodes, not to neighbor nodes added during expansion.

search-namespace-and-tag-filters-do-not-.text: The `namespace` and `tag` parameters filter only matched IDs, not expanded neighbor IDs.

search-relaxation-capped-at-50-queries.text: FTS progressive relaxation drops terms via `combinations()` (largest subsets first) until results appear, capped at 50 total relaxation queries to prevent combinatorial explosion on long search strings.

search-resilience-degrades-gracefully-at.text: The search pipeline guarantees non-empty results through three independent degradation mechanisms: stop-word filtering prevents degenerate queries, progressive term relaxation handles multi-term FTS5 misses, and substring fallback handles complete FTS5 infrastructure failure.

justifications.label: Convergent resilience — each mechanism independently prevents a distinct failure mode (all-stop-words, partial FTS5 match, missing FTS5 tables), and the conclusion "search always returns results" holds as long as at least one tier functions.

self-correction-completeness-has-efficie.text: The system's quality-complete self-correction — concretely grounded in source integrity, fully documented with referenceable artifacts, deterministically convergent, and evolution-tolerant — operates through a fault-tolerant, resource-efficient quality lifecycle pipeline where individual LLM failures are isolated at both module and batch levels without compromising correction completeness or exhausting bounded resource budgets.

justifications.label: Connects two terminal high-depth conclusions (depth-10 quality completeness and depth-8 fault-tolerant efficiency) to show the HOW (efficient fault-tolerant pipeline) meets the WHAT (complete quality dimensions) of self-correction

self-correction-has-complete-traceable-h.text: The system's self-correction is both temporally complete (spanning creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection) and historically traceable (nogoods recorded consistently with stable IDs), ensuring corrections can be audited and understood after the fact.

self-correction-history-is-durably-docum.text: Every self-correction produces documentation that is both complete (traceable history with consistent artifact identification) and durable (identifiers survive persistence boundaries and format evolution) — the correction history remains addressable and interpretable across sessions and system versions.

justifications.label: Self-documenting corrections (depth-7) and durable references (depth-5) combine into the guarantee that correction history is permanently addressable, not just temporarily traceable

self-correction-is-complete-across-all-q.text: Self-correction simultaneously achieves all quality dimensions: concretely grounded in source integrity verification, fully documented with referenceable artifacts, convergent to accurate topology, tolerant of system evolution at all boundaries, and structurally and resource sustainable — no quality dimension is achieved at the expense of another.

justifications.label: Grounded-documented-convergent (source integrity + artifacts + topology accuracy) and evolution-tolerant-sustainable (unfragile architecture + resource bounds + boundary tolerance) are independently established, proving all dimensions hold simultaneously

self-correction-is-evolution-tolerant-an.text: The system's structurally and resource sustainable self-correction — operating on unfragile architecture with accurate bounded budgets — is additionally evolution-tolerant: parser fallbacks, forward-compatible import parsing, and schema migration tolerance at every boundary ensure self-correction mechanisms remain effective as external data formats change.

justifications.label: Structural and resource sustainability ensures self-correction works within a format version; evolution tolerance at boundaries ensures it continues working across format versions

self-correction-is-exhaustive-across-lif.text: Self-correction is exhaustive across the complete belief lifecycle: at creation time, the derive pipeline exhaustively discovers all derivable conclusions with guaranteed termination; at maintenance time, contradiction resolution and staleness detection ensure existing beliefs remain consistent and current.

justifications.label: Exhaustive derive exploration covers creation-time completeness while lifecycle-spanning contradiction and staleness correction covers maintenance-time consistency (depth-5)

self-correction-is-exhaustive-and-artifa.text: Every self-correction — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection alike — is exhaustive in coverage, sustainable in resource consumption, and produces consistently-identifiable artifacts (deterministic challenge auto-IDs, unconditionally-recorded nogoods with monotonic IDs), making the system's self-maintenance history fully referenceable

justifications.label: Exhaustive sustainable self-correction combined with consistent artifact identification yields fully-referenceable self-maintenance history

self-correction-is-exhaustive-and-self-c.text: The system's self-correction is both exhaustive in scope (creation-time contradiction resolution through dependency-directed backtracking and maintenance-time staleness detection through source hash comparison) and self-contained (requiring zero external runtime dependencies) — complete autonomous consistency maintenance with no external coupling.

justifications.label: Exhaustiveness (depth-5) guarantees no correction gaps; self-containment (depth-5) guarantees no external failure modes can disable correction — the system is its own complete maintenance authority.

self-correction-is-exhaustive-and-sustai.text: Self-correction is both exhaustive in coverage (creation-time contradiction resolution via exhaustive derivation and maintenance-time staleness detection) and doubly sustainable (resource-bounded through accurate token budgets and structurally sound through unfragile architecture) — it can operate indefinitely without coverage gaps or resource exhaustion.

justifications.label: Connecting two orphan branches — lifecycle-exhaustive self-correction (depth-5) and structurally/resource-sustainable self-correction (depth-6) — into a unified property: exhaustive coverage that won't degrade

self-correction-is-fully-self-documentin.text: The system's self-correction is simultaneously exhaustive in scope (spanning creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection), self-contained in execution (requiring zero external dependencies), and artifact-producing in operation (every correction generates consistently-identifiable records) — making every self-correction event fully traceable without external logging infrastructure.

justifications.label: Exhaustive + self-contained coverage ensures nothing escapes correction, while artifact production ensures nothing escapes documentation — together they make the system a complete self-documenting correctness engine.

self-correction-is-grounded-documented-a.text: The system's self-correction simultaneously achieves three independent properties: concretely grounded in source-level integrity verification (fail-safe path resolution, SHA-256 hashing), self-documenting through traceable artifacts (consistent identification across persistence boundaries), and convergent through accurate topology (complete dependency tracking to deterministic stable states).

self-correction-is-minimality-enforced.text: The system's active self-correction (contradiction resolution, staleness detection, exception handling) preserves the same universal revision safety that minimality generates — self-correction enforces minimality's guarantees rather than adding independent safety layers, making the two properties mutually reinforcing.

justifications.label: Minimality generates the revision rules (depth-6) while self-correction enforces them (depth-6); together they show the system's maintenance is both principled and active

self-correction-is-resilient-to-llm-unav.text: The system's core self-correction mechanisms — contradiction resolution through dependency-directed backtracking and staleness detection through source hash comparison — require no external dependencies and execute on stdlib alone, while all LLM-facing operations apply consistent fail-soft error handling — LLM unavailability degrades knowledge expansion but never compromises correction integrity.

justifications.label: Zero-dependency self-correction plus fail-soft LLM integration means LLM unavailability cannot compromise system integrity

self-correction-is-resource-sustainable.text: The system's self-correction capability — contradiction resolution at derivation time and staleness detection at maintenance time — is resource-sustainable: accurate bidirectional token budgets support continuous belief derivation and maintenance, ensuring the correction loop can operate indefinitely without resource exhaustion.

justifications.label: Self-correction requires sustainable resources; resource management requires correction targets that consume budgets; the gate inherits all deficiency conditions from both antecedents' dependency chains.

self-correction-is-source-grounded-and-s.text: The system's self-correction is simultaneously grounded in concrete source-level integrity (fail-safe path resolution, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing, comprehensive staleness detection) and fully self-documenting (every correction produces consistently-identifiable referenceable artifacts), connecting abstract correctness guarantees to verifiable filesystem-level truth and auditable history

justifications.label: Depth-6 — two independent sustainability guarantees (resource and structural) close off both failure modes that could degrade self-correction over time

self-correction-is-temporally-complete-a.text: Self-correction operates deterministically across all temporal dimensions — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection alike — AND is resource-sustainable with gapless lifecycle coverage, enabling the system to maintain consistency indefinitely without resource exhaustion or temporal blind spots.

justifications.label: Temporally-complete deterministic self-correction plus resource-sustainable gapless lifecycle ensures indefinite consistency maintenance

self-correction-is-topology-accurate-and.text: The system's exhaustive self-correction operates on an accurate convergent topology: every correction propagates through complete dependency tracking (including outlist entries) to a deterministic stable state, ensuring no transitively affected node is missed and no oscillation occurs during correction.

justifications.label: Self-correction exhaustiveness (depth-7) combined with topology accuracy (depth-7) from independent chains guarantees corrections traverse the true dependency graph rather than an approximate or incomplete one

self-correction-operates-within-efficien.text: The system's structurally and resource sustainable self-correction operates within a pipeline that is itself resource-efficient at every phase — from zero-dependency packaging through lazy-loading startup to budget-constrained derivation — ensuring self-correction never outgrows its resource envelope.

justifications.label: Pipeline-wide resource efficiency reinforces self-correction sustainability

self-correction-produces-referenceable-a.text: Every self-correction — creation-time contradiction resolution and maintenance-time staleness detection alike — produces consistently identifiable artifacts (deterministic challenge IDs, monotonic collision-free nogood IDs), enabling a complete referenceable correction history that survives across save/load cycles.

self-correction-requires-no-external-dep.text: The system's self-correction capabilities — contradiction resolution through dependency-directed backtracking and staleness detection through source hash comparison — operate entirely within a self-contained, safely-layered architecture with zero external dependencies, ensuring maintenance is never blocked by unavailable services, network failures, or broken supply chains

justifications.label: Self-correction (depth-4) depends only on capabilities within the self-contained architecture (depth-2) — no external service can prevent the system from detecting and resolving its own inconsistencies

self-correction-spans-creation-and-maint.text: The system self-corrects along both temporal axes: it detects and resolves active contradictions through lifecycle-safe backtracking at derivation time, and it detects and flags source material drift through conservative staleness checking over a belief's lifetime — ensuring beliefs are correct both when first derived and as their evidential basis evolves.

self-correction-sustains-lifecycle-indef.text: Resource-sustainable self-correction operating within a deterministic, architecturally-grounded, structurally-sound lifecycle means the system can maintain belief quality indefinitely — resource efficiency prevents degradation while structural soundness prevents architectural drift.

self-sustainability-is-reinforced-by-res.text: The system's self-sustaining minimality loop — where minimality generates the closed maintenance loop and self-correction mechanisms that actively maintain minimality itself — is reinforced by pervasive resource efficiency: zero external dependencies eliminate supply-chain risk to the loop's operation, lazy loading reduces maintenance overhead, and O(1) budget tracking ensures the loop operates within bounded computational cost.

self-sustaining-invariants-are-independe.text: The system's self-sustaining invariant preservation does not require blind trust: the same maintenance loop observability that enables trustworthiness verification independently confirms that minimality's fixed-point continues to sustain invariant preservation — self-sustainability is verifiable, not merely claimed.

self-sustaining-preservation-encompasses.text: Self-sustaining invariant preservation fully encompasses external beliefs: the correction and equivalence guarantees for external beliefs are dynamically sustained by minimality's fixed-point property, not merely statically established — external integration quality is actively maintained as part of the system's self-maintenance loop.

justifications.label: Static external-belief equivalence (from integration chain) combined with dynamic self-sustaining preservation (from minimality chain) yields the stronger claim that external integration is actively maintained; cross-chain combination.

semantic-contradiction-reuses-cluster-in.text: Semantic contradiction detection delegates embedding and clustering to the existing `list_clusters()` from `reasons_lib/cluster.py` — the same infrastructure that serves deduplication also serves contradiction detection, with no duplicate embedding/clustering implementation.

semantic-contradictions-cluster-before-l.text: The `--semantic` flag on `detect-contradictions` embeds beliefs via sentence-transformers, clusters with KMeans via `list_clusters()`, and sends each cluster to the LLM as a batch — ensuring topically related beliefs are analyzed together instead of being scattered across random batches of 50.

semantic-minimality-with-operational-det.text: The system unifies semantic minimality (all non-monotonic features and truth semantics derive from uniform outlist/disjunction primitives) with operational determinism (all operations terminate predictably via BFS fixpoint with conservative failure semantics), yielding a small trusted kernel that powers all reasoning.

semantics-and-revision-share-minimal-fou.text: Both truth maintenance semantics and belief revision achieve comprehensive coverage through the same minimal primitives — the outlist primitive simultaneously enables emergent truth evaluation (disjunction over conjunction with absence semantics) and all non-monotonic revision mechanisms (defeat, backtracking, dialectics), confirming minimality as a cross-cutting architectural principle rather than a property of any single subsystem.

setuptools-68-is-build-backend.text: `pyproject.toml` declares `setuptools >= 68.0` as the PEP 517 build backend.
