setuptools-explicit-packages.text: Only `reasons_lib/` is included in the distribution via explicit `[tool.setuptools] packages` configuration; `tests/`, `entries/`, `reviews/`, and other directories are excluded from packaging.

setuptools-packages-list-is-explicit.text: The `[tool.setuptools]` packages list is an explicit `["reasons", "reasons_lib"]` rather than auto-discovery; any new top-level package directory must be manually appended or it will be omitted from the wheel.

sha-bump-refreshes-source-hash.text: In the pinned-lines fast path, when `pinned_sha` advances, `source_hash` is recomputed via `hash_file` so the stored pair stays consistent (check_stale.py:120).

shim-adds-no-new-api.text: The file defines no functions, classes, or constants of its own; its only runtime artifact is the imported namespace.

shim-and-origin-are-distinct-module-obje.text: Monkeypatching `reasons_lib.repair_premises.<name>` does not affect `reasons.repair_premises.<name>`, so tests must patch the origin module.

shim-binds-identical-function-objects.text: Because the star-import in every `reasons_lib` shim binds the same function/class objects (not copies or proxies), any monkey-patch applied to `reasons.api` (or any other canonical module) is immediately visible through the `reasons_lib` alias and vice versa — there is no encapsulation boundary between the two namespaces.

shim-binds-symbols-by-reference.text: Exported objects are the same objects as in the canonical module (`is` identity holds), but rebinding an attribute on either module does not affect the other.

shim-creates-independent-name-bindings.text: `reasons_lib.cli` and `reasons.cli` are distinct module objects sharing the same initial object references, so rebinding an attribute on one does not affect the other.

shim-cross-tree-edge-constrains-review-i.text: Because `reasons/api.py` imports `reasons_lib.review` and `reasons_lib.review` imports `reasons.review`, the effective import graph has a cross-tree edge; `reasons/review.py` must not import names from `reasons/__init__.py` at module level to avoid circular-import failures.

shim-defines-no-all.text: The shim does not declare `__all__`, so further wildcard re-exports scan its post-wildcard namespace rather than a curated list.

shim-deletion-blocked-by-test-and-intern.text: Deleting the `reasons_lib/` package without first rewriting imports in ~20 test files and the internal `reasons/` modules (`api.py`, `pg.py`, `verify.py`, and others) will cause `ImportError` in those consumers.

shim-does-not-copy-canonical-all-attribu.text: The `reasons_lib` shims do not set their own `__all__`; when `reasons.<module>` defines `__all__`, the star import copies the listed names but not the `__all__` attribute itself, so `reasons_lib.<module>.__all__` is normally absent.

shim-does-not-forward-private-names-or-s.text: Star-import semantics prevent `reasons_lib.cli` from exposing underscore-prefixed names or submodules such as `reasons.cli.argparse`.

shim-does-not-redeclare-all.text: The `reasons_lib.metadata` shim does not define its own `__all__`, so `from reasons_lib.metadata import *` exports all non-underscore names present in the shim and can diverge from `reasons.metadata.__all__` if that list contains underscore names or omits non-underscore names.

shim-emits-no-deprecation-warning.text: Importing from any `reasons_lib.*` module produces no `DeprecationWarning` or `PendingDeprecationWarning`, so downstream consumers receive no programmatic signal that they should migrate to the `reasons.*` import path.

shim-exports-only-public-names.text: Because `import *` skips underscore-prefixed names and honors `reasons.network.__all__` if defined, private names in `reasons/network.py` are not accessible through the shim.

shim-fails-fast-without-fallback.text: If the canonical `reasons.X` module fails to import (missing dependency, syntax error, circular import), the `reasons_lib.X` shim propagates the `ImportError` or `ModuleNotFoundError` unmodified with no try/except, no fallback, and no additional diagnostic context about the forwarding layer.

shim-forwarding-audit-is-inconsistent-wi.text: The shim forwarding-import audit returned zero matches even though `reasons_lib/__init__.py` contains a matching `from reasons import *` line.

shim-forwards-to-canonical-module.text: `reasons_lib/review_premises.py` contains exactly one statement, `from reasons.review_premises import *`, re-exporting the canonical module's public names.

shim-has-no-error-handling.text: The file has no `try/except`; `ImportError` from `reasons.mcp_client` propagates unchanged.

shim-identity-guarantee-is-object-identi.text: For every public name `N` in a `reasons` module, `reasons_lib.<module>.N is reasons.<module>.N` evaluates to `True` (object identity, not mere equality); the shim adds no wrapping, proxying, sub-classing, or transformation.

shim-import-failure-is-immediate-and-unw.text: If the target `reasons.<module>` fails to import (missing dependency, syntax error), the `reasons_lib` shim raises the exception immediately at module-load time with no `try/except`, no `__getattr__` fallback, no deferred-import guard, and no additional error context wrapping.

shim-import-failure-propagates-as-canoni.text: Importing the shim raises exactly the exception from `reasons.review_justifications`; there is no `try/except` fallback.

shim-import-is-eager-and-unprotected.text: Importing `reasons_lib.cli` fully imports `reasons.cli` and propagates any of its import-time exceptions, with no try/except in the shim.

shim-module-object-is-distinct-from-cano.text: A `reasons_lib.<module>` shim is a distinct module object from `reasons.<module>` (separate `sys.modules` entry, `__name__`, `__file__`, and `__doc__`), even though re-exported class/function objects are identical.

shim-namespace-rebinding-does-not-affect.text: Rebinding a name in a `reasons_lib.<module>` shim (e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr("reasons_lib.repair_premises.foo", fake)`) affects only the shim namespace; code inside `reasons.<module>` still resolves its original module-level name.

shim-preserves-object-identity.text: For every public name N re-exported by a `reasons_lib/` shim, `reasons_lib.X.N is reasons.X.N` evaluates to True (object identity, not equality), so monkey-patching, `isinstance` checks, and identity comparisons behave identically through either import path.

shim-preserves-object-identity-but-not-b.text: `reasons_lib.mcp_server.X is reasons.mcp_server.X` holds for public `X`, but `monkeypatch.setattr` on the shim does not affect the real module.

shim-propagates-exceptions-unchanged.text: The `reasons_lib/` shims contain no try/except, logging, wrapping, or error translation; any exception raised during import of the target `reasons/` module or raised at call time by a re-exported function propagates unchanged to the caller.

shim-propagates-import-errors.text: This module has no error handling, so failures in `reasons.llm` propagate as import exceptions.

shim-reexport-surface-maps-to-reasons-cl.text: The names available from `reasons_lib.cli` are exactly `reasons.cli.__all__` when defined, otherwise every non-underscore module-global of `reasons.cli`.

shim-reexports-canonical-module-path.text: Symbols re-exported through `reasons_lib.mind_service` retain `__module__ == "reasons.mind_service"`, so pickles created via the legacy import path reference the canonical module and do not depend on the shim surviving.

shim-reexports-retain-canonical-module-a.text: Functions and classes re-exported through a `reasons_lib` shim retain their original `__module__` value from `reasons.<module>`, so introspection and tracebacks show the canonical module path rather than the shim path.

shim-requires-reasons-check-stale.text: The shim has a one-way dependency on `reasons.check_stale`; any import-time failure in the canonical module propagates to legacy importers.

shim-star-import-auto-tracks-canonical-e.text: Because every shim uses `import *` (not a curated `__all__` list), any public symbol added to `reasons.X` is automatically visible through `reasons_lib.X` without editing the shim, and any symbol made private (`_`-prefixed) in the canonical module is silently dropped from the shim.

shim-star-import-exposes-transitive-publ.text: When a canonical `reasons/<module>.py` lacks `__all__`, its `reasons_lib` shim re-exports every non-underscore name in the canonical module’s namespace, including names imported from other modules, so the shim’s public surface can be broader than the canonical module’s intended API.

shim-star-import-leaks-incidental-import.text: Because the shim uses `import *` and defines no local `__all__`, non-underscore names imported at top level by the canonical module (such as `json` or `FastMCP`) also become attributes of the `reasons_lib` shim unless the canonical module defines `__all__`.

shim-star-import-respects-target-all.text: If a `reasons/<module>.py` file defines an `__all__` list, the shim's star import will respect it (re-exporting only listed names), which can silently break `reasons_lib` consumers who previously relied on public symbols not included in `__all__`.

shim-target-must-not-import-its-own-shim.text: To prevent circular imports, the canonical module that a shim re-exports (e.g., `reasons/review.py`) must not import from its own `reasons_lib` counterpart (e.g., `reasons_lib/review.py`); the one-way dependency `reasons_lib → reasons` must be preserved for every leaf module pair.

shim-uses-noqa-f401-f403.text: The star-import line carries `# noqa: F401,F403` to suppress unused-import and star-import lint warnings, and removing it would break lint checks without affecting runtime.

show-cli-output-contract-includes-depend.text: `tests/test_cli.py:TestShow` asserts `show` output includes `Dependents: b` and `Retract reason: Fixed in PR #1`.

show-commands-renders-example-with-2-spa.text: The `show` CLI command prints an `Example:` header line followed by every line of a multiline example indented by exactly two spaces; the `Example:` section is absent entirely when no example was set.

show-omits-example-section-when-absent.text: CLI `show` emits an `Example:` section when metadata contains an example and omits that section entirely when no example exists.

show-renders-example-section.text: The `show` command emits an `Example:` section when an example exists and omits it otherwise.

show-tests-define-cli-output-contract.text: `tests/test_cli.py:TestShow` asserts `show` output includes `Dependents: b` and `Retract reason: Fixed in PR #1`.

single-cli-entry-point.text: The only registered console script is `reasons`, pointing to `reasons_lib.cli:main`; all subcommands are dispatched internally

single-justification-removal-is-blocked.text: `remove_justification` raises `ValueError` when a node would be left with zero justifications; `convert_to_premise` is the sanctioned alternative.

single-node-api-raises-permissionerror.text: API functions that target a single node by ID (`show_node`, `explain_node`, `trace_assumptions`, `trace_access_tags`) raise `PermissionError` when the caller lacks clearance; collection endpoints silently filter instead.

sl-and-cp-stand-for-support-list-and-con.text: In Doyle's TMS terminology, SL stands for Support List and CP stands for Conditional Proof.

sl-cp-docstrings-differ.text: `reasons/__init__.py:11-13` defines SL as all antecedents IN and CP as assumptions consistent.

sl-justification-is-conjunction-of-inlis.text: Redundant with `sl-justification-semantics` proposed above, which captures the same claim more concisely.

sl-justification-is-disjunctive.text: A node is IN if *any* of its justifications is valid (disjunctive semantics); `_compute_truth()` short-circuits on the first valid justification rather than requiring all justifications to hold.

sl-justification-is-sole-summary-cascade.text: The summary's truth-value propagation is entirely mediated by a single SL (Subsumption Link) justification whose antecedents are the covered node IDs; there is no separate watcher, subscription, or imperative link mechanism.

sl-justification-references-only-in-file.text: The SL justification's `antecedents` are filtered by `claim_by_id` membership, so a claim depending only on pre-existing network nodes gets `justifications=None` and is imported as a premise.

sl-justification-requires-all-antecedent.text: An SL justification is valid only when every ID in its `antecedents` list is `IN`.

sl-justification-requires-all-outlist-no.text: An SL justification is valid only when every ID in its `outlist` is `OUT`; missing outlist nodes count as `OUT`.

sl-justification-semantics.text: An SL justification is valid iff ALL antecedents are IN AND ALL outlist nodes are OUT; a node is IN iff ANY of its justifications is valid (conjunction within a justification, disjunction across justifications).

sl-outlist-asymmetry.text: Missing antecedents invalidate a justification, but missing outlist nodes do not — this asymmetry enables "believe X unless Y" where Y may not yet exist in the network

sl-outlist-requires-all-outlist-out.text: An `SL` justification holds only when every antecedent is `IN` and every outlist node is `OUT`.

sl-outlist-validity-requires-all-outlist.text: An `SL` justification is valid only when every antecedent is `IN` and every outlist node is `OUT`; any single `IN` outlist node invalidates it.

sl-param-is-comma-separated-node-ids.text: `add_node()` encodes SL justifications as comma-separated node IDs in the `sl=` parameter and outlist nodes in `unless=`, mirroring the TMS (SL, OL) formalism directly in the API signature.

snapshot-requires-active-subscribers.text: The write path computes before/after truth snapshots only when `write` is true and `pubsub.has_subscribers(db_path)` is true.

snapshot-requires-subscribers.text: The write-path snapshot is skipped unless `write` is true and `pubsub.has_subscribers(db_path)` is true.

soften-repair-metadata-targets-successor.text: The `soften` repair branch writes `repair_action=softened` on `sup["new_id"]`, not on the original `belief_id`.

soften-writes-metadata-to-new-node.text: The `soften` branch sets `repair_action=softened` on `sup["new_id"]`, not on the original `belief_id`.

source-and-source-hash-are-additive.text: `source` (+50) and `source_hash` (+25) are independent truthiness checks; a node can receive both.

source-chunks-must-be-a-mapping.text: Both formatting helpers call `source_chunks.get(...)`, so callers must pass a mapping keyed by premise id; `None` raises `AttributeError`.

source-correction-achieves-resource-effi.text: Source-grounded lifecycle correction with tripartite operational assurance — externally controlled, internally self-correcting, and query-resilient — achieves these guarantees within resource-efficient bounds spanning the full operational pipeline, ensuring correction mechanisms never exhaust the system's computational budget.

justifications.label: Tripartite assurance and resource efficiency are co-achieved — comprehensive correction does not come at unbounded resource cost

source-deleted-result-nulls-new-hash-and.text: `source_deleted` results set `new_hash` and `source_path` to `None` while preserving `old_hash` and `source`.

source-deleted-result-preserves-old-hash.text: A `source_deleted` result preserves the node's `old_hash` and `source` values while setting `new_hash` and `source_path` to `None`.

source-deleted-results-per-node.text: If multiple IN nodes reference the same deleted source file, `check_stale` returns a separate `source_deleted` result for each node.

source-governance-loop-is-dually-grounde.text: The closed source-integrity-governance loop is both dually grounded (resting on two independent evaluation chains — purity and uniformity) and fully deterministic (governance determinism emerges from minimality through source integrity and is preserved by exception safety), achieving both epistemic independence and operational predictability from independent foundations

justifications.label: The source-governance loop achieves dual grounding and determinism independently — grounding from evaluation chains, determinism from minimality

source-grounded-correction-has-tripartit.text: The system's lifecycle self-correction — concretely grounded in fail-safe source integrity verification with governed output — operates within a tripartite assurance framework providing external control (bounded interfaces with defensive ingestion), internal self-correction (contradiction resolution and staleness detection), and query resilience (graceful degradation across all access paths).

justifications.label: Source-grounded governed output (depth-7) combined with tripartite assurance (depth-6) from independent chains shows concrete source integrity feeds into a comprehensive three-dimensional assurance framework

source-grounded-correction-produces-gove.text: The system's lifecycle self-correction — concretely grounded in fail-safe source integrity verification — feeds into a governed output pipeline that is authorized (access-tag gated), bounded (token-budget constrained), and CI-ready (deterministic with nonzero exit codes), ensuring that source-level drift detection translates into actionable, permission-respecting output

justifications.label: Source-grounded self-correction (depth-6) detects problems while output governance (depth-5) ensures those problems are communicated through authorized, bounded, automation-friendly channels

source-hash-is-sha256-hexdigest.text: `hash_file` and stored `source_hash` values are SHA-256 hex digests of file content.

source-integrity-and-governance-form-clo.text: Source integrity enables lifecycle governance by unifying determinism, exception safety, and lifecycle management into a single pipeline, while lifecycle governance achieves gap-free source coverage — forming a self-reinforcing closed loop where source integrity grounds the governance that in turn ensures no source verification gap exists.

justifications.label: Source integrity enables governance AND governance ensures gap-free source coverage — bidirectional reinforcement

source-integrity-grounds-lifecycle-self-.text: The system's lifecycle-spanning self-correction is concretely grounded in fail-safe source integrity: the end-to-end source pipeline (convention-based path resolution, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing, comprehensive staleness detection, CI gating) provides the verification mechanism that makes maintenance-time self-correction practically achievable alongside creation-time exhaustive derivation.

justifications.label: Abstract lifecycle self-correction is grounded by concrete source integrity — source hashing and staleness detection are the mechanism that makes maintenance-time correction fail-safe, not just theoretically complete.

source-integrity-is-deterministic-and-ar.text: The fail-safe source integrity pipeline — from convention-based path resolution through collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing to comprehensive staleness detection — operates within the same deterministic, architecturally-grounded lifecycle framework as all other system operations, ensuring source verification is both predictable and structurally safe.

justifications.label: Fail-safe source lifecycle + deterministic grounded lifecycle → source integrity anchored in deterministic architecture

source-integrity-is-fail-safe-determinis.text: The source integrity pipeline achieves triple assurance from two independent chains: fail-safe operation (convention-based path resolution returning None on missing files, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing with additive backfill, comprehensive staleness detection) combined with architectural determinism (grounded within clean layer boundaries ensuring predictable state trajectories).

justifications.label: Fail-safe pipeline properties combined with architectural determinism grounding

source-integrity-loop-is-dually-grounded.text: The closed source-integrity-governance loop is itself dually grounded — the governance half of the loop rests on two independent semantic foundations (evaluation purity and edge-case uniformity), so the bidirectional feedback cycle between source integrity and lifecycle governance remains sound even if one grounding chain is weakened.

justifications.label: closed loop + dual grounding = robust feedback cycle with independent semantic foundations

source-integrity-spans-hashing-through-d.text: Source integrity forms a complete end-to-end pipeline with no gap between measurement and verification: collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing with additive backfill computes integrity markers without overwriting existing hashes, while comprehensive staleness detection with CI gating and nonzero exit codes consumes those markers to catch all source drift.

justifications.label: Hash computation (depth-1) and drift detection (depth-2) are independently sound; combining reveals the complete pipeline from source file → hash → comparison → CI signal with no missing link.

source-integrity-unifies-determinism-exc.text: The source integrity pipeline achieves triple assurance from two independent chains: the source-to-TMS path is deterministic (convention-based resolution, collision-resistant SHA-256) and exception-safe (fail-safe across both TMS and source lifecycle domains), while lifecycle governance uses that same deterministic source integrity to drive staleness decisions and belief currency management — source integrity simultaneously serves pipeline correctness, failure recovery, and lifecycle governance.

justifications.label: source integrity serves pipeline correctness, exception safety, and lifecycle governance simultaneously

source-lifecycle-is-fail-safe-and-gaples.text: The end-to-end fail-safe source integrity pipeline — from convention-based path resolution through collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing to comprehensive drift detection — feeds directly into gapless lifecycle management, ensuring every source material change on disk is detected, surfaced, and managed through the full belief lifecycle without gaps.

justifications.label: The source pipeline provides detection (what changed) and lifecycle management provides response (how the system adapts), creating complete coverage from disk to belief state

source-path-fallback-uses-tilde-git-repo.text: resolve_source_path falls back to ~/git/<repo-name>/... when a node's repo is not present in the repos mapping.

source-path-format.text: Source references use `"reponame/relative/path"` format; `resolve_source_path` splits on the first `/` to look up the repo key in a `repos: dict[str, Path]` mapping.

source-path-splits-on-first-slash.text: resolve_source_path extracts the repo name by splitting a node's source string on the first slash.

source-paths-use-repo-alias-prefix.text: Node source paths follow a `repo-alias/relative-path` convention where the first `/`-delimited segment is a key into the `repos` dict that maps aliases to filesystem roots, decoupling belief source references from absolute paths.

source-pipeline-is-end-to-end-fail-safe.text: The complete source integrity pipeline from path resolution through hash computation to staleness detection is end-to-end fail-safe: convention-based resolution returns None on missing files rather than raising exceptions, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing backfills additively without overwriting, and staleness detection catches all drift with CI-ready exit codes — no stage in the pipeline raises exceptions on adverse conditions, and each stage's output gracefully feeds the next.

justifications.label: Adding the resolution stage to the existing hashing-through-detection pipeline completes the end-to-end fail-safe property from first path lookup to final CI gate

source-resolution-is-convention-based-an.text: Source path resolution follows a convention-based repo-alias/relative-path format and returns None on missing files rather than raising exceptions, providing safe path resolution for the staleness checking pipeline.

justifications.label: The two halves of the source resolution contract — format convention and failure semantics — combine to define the staleness pipeline's input layer

source-to-tms-integrity-is-deterministic.text: The complete integrity pipeline from source files through TMS truth maintenance is both deterministic (convention-based path resolution, collision-resistant SHA-256 hashing, uniform pure evaluation) and exception-safe (fail-safe source resolution, contradiction-triggered backtracking, challenge-to-justified recovery) — no failure in either source verification or truth maintenance can corrupt system state or produce unpredictable outcomes.

justifications.label: Source integrity and exception safety are independently deterministic across their domains; combining shows the full pipeline is deterministic and exception-safe end-to-end

source-tracking-is-collision-resistant-a.text: Source integrity tracking uses full 64-character SHA-256 digests with exact string comparison for collision resistance, and backfills hashes additively without overwriting existing values — ensuring high-fidelity drift detection with no accidental data loss

justifications.label: Three independent hash properties combine into a single integrity claim — collision resistance (full digests), comparison fidelity (exact match), and operational safety (additive-only backfill) are three axes of the same concern

source-truncation-caps-at-30k-chars.text: `read_source` truncates content at `MAX_SOURCE_CHARS` (30,000) and appends a `[... truncated ...]` marker.

source-type-absent-means-key-missing-in-.text: The `source_type` key is entirely absent from `node["metadata"]` when never set (not present as null or empty string); downstream consumers must check for key existence rather than truthiness or null-check.

source-type-is-closed-four-value-enum.text: The valid `source_type` values are exactly `"code"`, `"document"`, `"self-description"`, and `"derived"`; any other string passed to `api.add_node` raises `ValueError` with a message matching `"Invalid source_type"` before any DB write occurs.

source-type-omitted-when-absent.text: When no source type is supplied, `show_node` returns metadata with no `source_type` key while `list_nodes` returns an empty string.

source-type-roundtrips-through-markdown-.text: A node's `source_type` survives `export_markdown` → `parse_beliefs`/`import_into_network` into a fresh `Network`.

source-types-closed-set-of-four.text: `add_node` validates `source_type` against a closed set of exactly four values: `"code"`, `"document"`, `"self-description"`, `"derived"`; any other string is rejected.

sqlite-network-meta-contains-schema-proj.text: The SQLite `network_meta` table contains at least `schema_version`, `project_name`, and `created_at` rows.

sqlite-only-commands-are-filesystem-llm-.text: The ~21 SQLite-only CLI commands fall into three categories: filesystem-dependent (hash-sources, check-stale, add-repo), LLM-powered (derive, review-beliefs, detect-contradictions, ask), and bulk import/sync — all requiring either local file access or load-entire-network-modify-save semantics incompatible with PgApi's per-operation transaction model.

sqlite-only-commands-guarded-by-require-.text: Commands that touch the local filesystem, Merkle hashes, embeddings, or LLM-specific workflows call `_require_sqlite` (or the equivalent inline `REASONS_PG_CONNINFO` check) and abort if PostgreSQL is configured.

stale-and-out-claims-are-retracted-after.text: Both `STALE` and `OUT` statuses route through `network.retract(id)` immediately after `add_node`, and both increment `claims_retracted`.

stale-beliefs-import-as-out.text: Duplicates existing belief `staleness-information-survives-binary-truth-model`, which already establishes that STALE beliefs map to OUT with stale_reason metadata preserved end-to-end.

stale-imported-claims-can-recompute-to-i.text: A STALE claim imported by `import_agent` as retracted can propagate back to IN during `recompute_all()` because its imported justification is satisfiable while the agent is active.

stale-is-export-only-label.text: `STALE` is an export-only label; the underlying node remains `OUT`, and `export_card` counts it as `OUT`.

stale-label-takes-precedence-over-out.text: A retracted node whose metadata contains `stale_reason` is labeled `[STALE]` (not `[OUT]`) in the export header, and the stale metadata fields (`stale_reason`, `superseded_by`) are rendered as additional bullet lines.

stale-maps-to-out.text: STALE status in `beliefs.md` is mapped to OUT (retracted) in the network; there is no distinct STALE state in the TMS data model.

stale-maps-to-out-on-import.text: Nodes marked `[STALE]` in beliefs.md are stored with truth value OUT during both initial import and subsequent syncs

stale-premise-can-support-dozens-of-deri.text: A single stale premise can support dozens of derived conclusions in the belief network.

stale-result-reasons.text: `check_stale` uses two distinct reason codes: `"content_changed"` when the source file exists but its hash differs, and `"source_deleted"` when the file is gone from disk.

stale-status-maps-to-out.text: Claims with `[STALE]` status are imported with `truth_value == "OUT"` while their `stale_reason` and `superseded_by` are stored under `node.metadata`.

stale-tag-maps-to-out.text: A `[STALE]` markdown tag imports as `OUT` and is subsequently counted in `beliefs_retracted`, not `beliefs_removed`, on an unchanged re-sync.

staleness-checking-is-comprehensive.text: Staleness checking detects all nodes whose source material has changed on disk

justifications.label: Completeness breaks when a source file is deleted — the node silently passes instead of being flagged, creating a false-negative gap

staleness-checking-is-comprehensive-v2.text: Staleness checking identifies nodes whose source material has changed, limited to those that have both a non-empty `source` field and a non-empty `source_hash` field; when any such stale nodes are found it exits non-zero, making it usable as a CI or pre-commit gate.

staleness-gate-catches-all-drift.text: The staleness CI gate detects all forms of source material drift without false negatives.

justifications.label: The conservative read-only checking with CI exit codes provides strong detection, but silently skipping deleted source files and 64-bit hash collision risk create blind spots

staleness-gate-catches-all-drift-v2.text: The staleness CI gate provides a conservative, non-mutating check for source material drift limited to IN nodes, with detection applying only when both source fields are present.

staleness-information-survives-binary-tr.text: Despite the TMS using binary IN/OUT truth values with no distinct STALE state, staleness information is preserved end-to-end: stale beliefs are mapped to OUT on import with stale_reason metadata, and the compact output surfaces this metadata for OUT nodes — so downstream consumers can distinguish intentional retractions from staleness-driven ones.

justifications.label: Metadata carries staleness semantics that the binary truth model cannot express, from import through output

staleness-is-conservative-ci-gate.text: Staleness checking is designed as a safe CI gate: it never mutates state, only checks IN nodes, requires both source fields, and exits nonzero to fail the pipeline

justifications.label: All four properties are necessary for CI safety — mutation would be dangerous, checking OUT nodes wasteful, missing fields a false positive, and zero-exit a silent pass

staleness-is-surfaced-despite-binary-tru.text: Staleness information not only survives the binary IN/OUT truth model (via metadata-based preservation through import and compact surfacing) but also emerges as deterministic, uniformly-structured, machine-parseable CI output with conservative non-mutating semantics — no information is lost between the TMS representation and the external consumer.

justifications.label: The binary truth model threatens to erase staleness nuance, but metadata preservation at the representation layer and deterministic output at the interface layer jointly ensure full-fidelity staleness surfacing.

staleness-output-is-ci-pipeline-ready.text: Staleness checking produces deterministic, uniformly-structured, machine-parseable output with conservative non-mutating semantics and nonzero exit codes, making it directly consumable by automated CI pipelines without wrapper scripts

justifications.label: Deterministic structured output combined with CI-gate semantics yields pipeline-ready staleness checking

staleness-results-are-dicts-not-exceptio.text: Both `check_stale` and `hash_sources` report problems (missing files, changed content, deleted sources) as list-of-dict return values, never raising exceptions — designed for batch audit operations that report all problems rather than aborting on the first.

staleness-uses-full-sha256.text: Staleness detection compares full 64-character SHA-256 hex digests via exact string equality, not truncated prefixes or fuzzy comparison.

star-import-binds-snapshot-not-proxy.text: Names are copied at import time, so rebinding a name in `reasons.review` afterward does not change `reasons_lib.review`'s attribute, though mutation of the shared object is visible through both.

star-import-does-not-forward-private-nam.text: Names beginning with `_` in `reasons/repair_premises.py` are not accessible via `reasons_lib.repair_premises`.

star-import-drops-private-names.text: Any `_`-prefixed symbol in `reasons/import_agent.py` is unreachable through `reasons_lib.import_agent`, because the wildcard import filters underscore names.

star-import-excludes-underscore-names.text: Names beginning with `_` in `reasons.llm` are not re-exported by this shim unless explicitly included in `reasons.llm.__all__`.

star-import-excludes-underscore-prefixed.text: Because all shims use `import *` rather than explicit name lists, any symbol in the canonical module that begins with `_` is not forwarded to `reasons_lib`, automatically preserving the private/public boundary without additional gating.

star-import-guarantees-object-identity.text: For any public name `X`, `reasons_lib.<mod>.X is reasons.<mod>.X` evaluates to `True` (same object reference, not a copy), so monkey-patching a function in one namespace is immediately visible through the other.

star-import-is-time-bound-copy-not-live-.text: The `from reasons.<module> import *` in each shim copies name bindings into the shim's `__dict__` at import time; if a module-level name in `reasons.<module>` is subsequently re-bound (e.g., `reasons.pubsub.some_func = new_ref`), the `reasons_lib.<module>` namespace retains the original reference and does not see the re-binding.

star-import-shim-provides-automatic-forw.text: Because every `reasons_lib/` shim uses `import *` with no local `__all__`, any new public symbol added to a `reasons/` module automatically becomes accessible through the corresponding `reasons_lib/` shim without any code change to the shim file.

star-import-shim-skips-underscore-names.text: The star import in each `reasons_lib/` shim does not re-export names prefixed with `_` unless the source module explicitly lists them in `__all__`, so private module-level attributes in `reasons.*` are invisible through the `reasons_lib` alias.

startup-performance-uses-lazy-loading.text: Both the API and CLI layers defer importing heavy modules (derive, compact, ask, asyncio, Storage) to function bodies rather than module top-level, minimizing import-time overhead for CLI responsiveness.

justifications.label: Cross-cutting performance pattern — both user-facing layers share the same lazy-loading strategy independently

static-version-0-22-0.text: pyproject.toml declares version 0.22.0 as a static, manually bumped project version.

step-counts-schema-is-step-specific.text: `counts` keys differ by step (`entries`/`proposed` vs `accepted`/`total_beliefs`), so consumers must select steps by `name` rather than assume a uniform schema.

sticky-retraction-survives-recompute-all.text: A node with `_retracted` metadata stays OUT even when `recompute_all()` re-evaluates the entire network — sticky retraction is a durable pin that only `assert_node` can clear

storage-atomicity-is-destructive-with-se.text: Storage achieves write atomicity through full-replace semantics made safe by selective preservation of externally-managed rows and implicit transaction rollback on failure

justifications.label: Full-replace alone would destroy external data; preservation alone wouldn't guarantee atomicity; rollback alone doesn't specify the strategy. The emergent pattern is "destructive atomicity with a preservation carve-out" — a specific persistence strategy that is more efficient than incremental writes while remaining safe for externally-managed state.

storage-connection-enforces-foreign-keys.text: `Storage` opens SQLite with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, so insertion order must put nodes before their tags/sources/justifications and deletion must clear children first.

storage-dependent-index-not-persisted.text: The `dependents` reverse index is not stored in SQLite; `Storage.load()` rebuilds it from justifications by calling `network._rebuild_dependents()`.

storage-derives-counter-from-existing-no.text: When loading a database without the `network_meta` table (pre-fix schema), `Storage.load()` derives `_next_nogood_id` from the max ID of existing nogoods rather than defaulting to 1, enabling backward-compatible upgrades

storage-enables-sqlite-foreign-keys.text: `Storage.__init__` enables SQLite foreign key enforcement when opening the database connection.

storage-fts-is-derived-index.text: The FTS5 full-text search index is rebuilt from scratch during every `save()`; it is a derived index, never the source of truth.

storage-fts-rebuilt-on-every-save.text: The `nodes_fts` full-text index is deleted and rebuilt from scratch on each `save()`, guaranteeing consistency with the `nodes` table at the cost of full-reindex overhead.

storage-fts-table-rebuilt-on-every-save.text: The `nodes_fts` FTS5 virtual table is dropped and recreated on every `Storage.save()` rather than incrementally updated.

storage-fts-uses-porter-stemming.text: The `nodes_fts` FTS5 index uses Porter stemming on node ID and text.

storage-handles-schema-evolution-via-try.text: Missing tables from older database versions (`repos`, `network_meta`) are handled by swallowing exceptions during `load()` rather than formal migrations — a backward-compatibility substitute that silently degrades.

storage-init-schema-backfills-legacy-tag.text: When `node_tags`/`node_sources` are first introduced, `_init_schema` copies `metadata.access_tags` into `node_tags` as `access:<tag>` and copies each node's `source` into `node_sources`.

storage-init-schema-is-idempotent.text: Storage._init_schema uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, making schema initialization safe to run against an existing database.

storage-is-fully-production-grade-across.text: Both storage backends achieve fully production-grade operation — concurrent access optimization (WAL mode, derived FTS5 indexes), equivalent safety guarantees (atomic isolated mutations through backend-appropriate mechanisms), and multi-tenant isolation — when both backends provide complete API coverage.

justifications.label: Concurrent-access optimization and backend-agnostic safety together yield production-grade storage, gated on PgApi reaching full API parity with the SQLite backend.

storage-justification-order-preserved.text: Justifications are inserted in list order and loaded via `ORDER BY rowid`, preserving the ordering that determines which justification is evaluated first during truth computation.

storage-layer-is-backend-agnostic-and-sa.text: Both storage backends provide equivalent safety guarantees through backend-appropriate mechanisms: atomic isolated mutations (context-managed load/save for SQLite, per-method transactions for PgApi) and safe hypothetical reasoning (write-flag gating for SQLite, transaction rollback for PgApi), making safety properties independent of backend choice.

justifications.label: Backend-agnostic atomicity plus backend-agnostic what-if simulation establish a uniformly safe storage layer

storage-lists-as-json-columns.text: Antecedents, outlist, nogood node sets, and metadata dicts are stored as JSON text columns rather than normalized join tables, simplifying the schema at the cost of individual field queryability.

storage-load-assumes-valid-json.text: load() does not defend against invalid JSON in text columns; it assumes save() is the only writer and always writes valid JSON.

storage-load-bypasses-add-node.text: `load()` assigns nodes directly to `network.nodes` and calls `_rebuild_dependents()` afterward, deliberately skipping `add_node()` to avoid triggering truth maintenance propagation during state restoration.

storage-load-bypasses-propagation.text: `load()` constructs nodes directly into `network.nodes` rather than calling `add_node`, so truth maintenance propagation does not fire during deserialization.

storage-load-does-not-validate-json.text: Storage.load performs no validation on loaded JSON columns; malformed JSON raises json.JSONDecodeError and propagates uncaught.

storage-load-reads-tables-in-dependency-.text: `Storage.load()` reads nodes first, then justifications, then nogoods, repos, metadata, and propagation log to reconstruct the network.

storage-load-rebuilds-dependents-index.text: Storage.load assigns nodes directly into network.nodes and then calls network._rebuild_dependents() to reconstruct the reverse dependents index.

storage-load-trusts-stored-state-without.text: `Storage.load()` does not validate that antecedent node IDs exist, truth values are valid, or justification types are recognized; it trusts the database contents written by `save()`.

storage-migrations-use-alter-table-not-f.text: Schema evolution in `Storage._init_schema()` uses `PRAGMA table_info` to detect missing columns and issues `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` inline, plus data backfill from `metadata_json` for pre-existing rows — no Alembic, no versioned migration files, no migration runner.

storage-newness-is-file-existence.text: `Storage` computes `_is_new` from whether the database path exists, not from whether tables are empty; `network_meta` seeding only occurs on a newly created file.

storage-no-connection-pooling-or-retry.text: `Storage` uses one SQLite connection per instance and has no connection pooling or retry logic for `SQLITE_BUSY`.

storage-no-partial-load.text: `Storage.load()` either returns a complete `Network` with all state or fails; there is no streaming, lazy-loading, or partial deserialization.

storage-nogood-counter-persisted.text: Covered by existing `all-identifiers-are-durable-across-persistence-boundaries` which states "nogood IDs survive save/load cycles via the network_meta table's high-water mark."

storage-old-schema-compat.text: `load()` tolerates missing `network_meta` and `repos` tables via silent `try/except`, supporting databases created before those tables were added; `next_nogood_id` is derived from existing IDs as a fallback.

storage-optimizes-concurrent-access-and-.text: The storage layer optimizes for both concurrent access (WAL mode enables non-blocking reads during writes) and full-text search (derived FTS5 index rebuilt from scratch on every save guarantees consistency), making the persistence layer production-ready for multi-reader workloads with search capability.

justifications.label: WAL mode and derived FTS5 are independent optimizations that together enable concurrent searched access without consistency trade-offs

storage-persists-network-log-entries.text: `Storage.save`/`load` persists the network log, including at least one `"action": "add"` entry after adding a node.

storage-persists-retracted-truth-values.text: Retracted `OUT` truth values persist across `Storage` save/load.

storage-preserves-nogood-node-order.text: Nogoods survive `Storage` save/load with the exact node ID order preserved.

storage-rebuilds-dependents-index-from-j.text: The `dependents` reverse-index on nodes is not stored as a separate table or column; `Storage.load()` recomputes it by scanning justification rows, so after a round-trip the index is always consistent with the actual justification antecedent lists.

storage-rebuilds-fts-index-on-every-save.text: The nodes_fts full-text index is wiped and rebuilt alongside the nodes table in every save() call, so they cannot drift.

storage-representation-exposes-no-explic.text: Based on the observed tests and schema searches, ANY is expressed by multiple SL justifications rather than a stored `mode="ANY"` field.

storage-round-trip-preserves-dependents.text: Covered by existing belief `persistence-round-trip-is-lossless` — dependents are part of the persisted state

storage-roundtrip-preserves-network-stat.text: Saving and loading through `Storage` preserves nodes, truth values, justifications, nogoods, logs, and node metadata.

storage-roundtrip-preserves-node-source-.text: Node `source`, `source_hash`, and metadata dictionaries round-trip exactly through `Storage.save`/`load`.

storage-roundtrip-preserves-outlist-labe.text: `Storage.save` and `Storage.load` preserve `Justification.outlist`, `label`, and evaluated truth value across a SQLite round-trip.

storage-save-dedups-sources-by-node-and-.text: On save, external `node_sources` rows are restored only when no in-memory node already produced a row with the same `(node_id, source)` pair, preventing duplicate source references.

storage-save-deletes-and-reinserts-all-r.text: `Storage.save()` deletes all rows from every table and re-inserts the full network state in a single SQLite transaction, with no incremental/diff-based persistence.

storage-save-exceptions-rollback-transac.text: `Storage.save()` contains no explicit try/except; any `sqlite3.IntegrityError`, `OperationalError`, or disk-full condition propagates to the caller, and the `with self.conn:` context manager rolls back the entire transaction, leaving the database in its prior consistent state.

storage-save-is-delete-rewrite.text: `Storage.save()` deletes all rows from every table and reinserts the entire network inside a single SQLite transaction; it never diffs or upserts.

storage-save-is-full-overwrite.text: Calling `Storage.save()` a second time on the same path completely replaces all prior network state (nodes, nogoods, log); it does not append, merge, or upsert — the result is equivalent to deleting the file and saving fresh.

storage-save-is-full-replace.text: `Storage.save()` deletes all rows from every table before re-inserting the entire network; there is no incremental or differential update path.

storage-save-is-structurally-total-but-e.text: The save operation achieves structural totality (complete replacement of all network tables: nodes, nogoods, log, justifications) while deliberately preserving externally-managed annotations (node_tags, node_sources) — "full overwrite" applies to the TMS core but not to cross-cutting metadata managed by other subsystems.

justifications.label: Two-part semantic definition — "full overwrite" without the external-preservation nuance is misleading (it would imply tags/sources are lost), and "preserves external writes" without the full-overwrite context is misleading (it would imply incremental save). Both are needed for an accurate description of save semantics.

storage-save-persists-propagation-log-an.text: Storage.save persists the propagation_log and repos tables in addition to nodes, justifications, nogoods, and network_meta.

storage-save-preserves-external-writes.text: `Storage.save()` snapshots `node_tags` and `node_sources` rows *before* clearing all tables, then re-inserts them *after* the network-derived rows; this preserves tags and sources added directly to the database by other modules (`add_tags()`, `add_source()`) that bypass the in-memory `Network` object — a regression here silently loses API-added metadata.

storage-schema-defines-six-tables.text: The SCHEMA constant defines six tables: nodes, justifications, nogoods, repos, propagation_log, and nodes_fts (an FTS5 virtual table).

storage-tests-manual-close.text: Test cleanup detail, not a production invariant.

storage-tests-manually-close-connections.text: Each test calls `store.close()` after assertions, but not inside `try/finally` or a context manager.

storage-tests-target-reasons-package.text: This test file imports from `reasons`, not `reasons_lib`, so it does not directly cover the duplicate `reasons_lib/storage.py` implementation.

storage-trusts-stored-truth-values.text: `load()` trusts the stored `truth_value` without re-running propagation, making the database the source of truth for node status.

storage-uses-json-columns-for-lists.text: Antecedent IDs, outlist IDs, nogood node sets, and node metadata are stored as JSON text columns rather than junction tables — acceptable because the code always loads the full network, never queries relationships via SQL joins.

storage-uses-wal-mode.text: SQLite connections enable WAL mode on initialization, allowing concurrent readers without blocking writes.

strip-belief-metadata-is-idempotent-on-p.text: `_strip_belief_metadata` leaves plain belief text unchanged and only removes markdown structural elements such as headers, status lines, and separators.

strip-frontmatter-avoids-yaml-library.text: `strip_frontmatter` in `import_beliefs.py` deliberately avoids a YAML dependency, handling only flat `key: value` scalar pairs; nested structures produce silently corrupted values rather than raising an error.

strip-frontmatter-incomplete-header-fall.text: `strip_frontmatter` returns the original text and `{}` when a `---` header has no closing separator.

strip-frontmatter-is-total-never-raises.text: `strip_frontmatter()` is a total function: on any input (including malformed, unclosed, or empty frontmatter) it returns a `(body, frontmatter_dict)` tuple without raising — malformed input yields `(original_text, {})`.

strip-frontmatter-parses-simple-key-valu.text: `strip_frontmatter` returns `(original_text, {})` without a `---` header; otherwise it parses simple `key: value` lines, unquotes quoted scalars, and leaves numbers as strings.

structural-modifications-exhaust-topolog.text: All structural modifications to the belief network — additions, retractions, replacements, and bulk operations — both exhaust their effects through complete bidirectional graph traversal (reaching all transitively affected nodes in forward propagation and backward retraction) and converge to stable states with network topology fully preserved (all antecedent and outlist references correctly rewired)

justifications.label: Bidirectional traversal completeness (depth-5) guarantees no affected node is missed while topology-preserving convergence (depth-5) guarantees the graph structure remains consistent — together they ensure structural modifications are both exhaustive and stable

structural-modifications-preserve-most-i.text: The system's two structural modification mechanisms have complementary selection criteria that both converge on preserving the most important beliefs: deduplication retains the node with the most dependents (maximizing structural impact), while contradiction-driven retraction removes the least-entrenched premise (minimizing knowledge loss).

justifications.label: Convergent preservation principle — each mechanism independently encodes the design intent that structural changes should minimize loss of important beliefs; dedup protects by keeping the most-connected, retraction protects by removing the least-entrenched. The conclusion holds if either mechanism is present.
